Fantastic lore and world design, combined with the most fluid combat mechanics I've seen from an rpg. Lots of variety in combat, from sneaky beaky assassinations to juggernauting bosses and summoning a meteor to crush and burn your enemies (and annoying NPCs!). You can craft your own gear which can basically turn you into a demigod, and make potions that buffs almost whatever you want. Choices on how you play the game are varied to say the least.
Main story is like every other Hollywood movie; very well produced but rather bland, but that just means you don't feel bad playing the sidequests, which are the very opposite of bland. Super well written and varied, all coming together brilliantly to expand the world. The two DLCs are - like the main story - predictable, yet very well made.
NPCs talking over each other sometimes, some bugs and uneven difficulty are the only cons. Some bosses will plow through you as easily as you plowed through its minions leading up to it. Save often.
All in all, it's the most immersive game I've played to date. Well worth the money if you enjoy learning about the world you play in while butchering most of its inhabitants.

As promises, I played the game again after this latest update. The developers did fix the bugs I experienced prior. However, it appears that the ship of opportunity has sailed for the developers.
To really kick this review into gear, let me start by saying this game that only offers PvP with no form of NPC or combative AI is a huge mistake. This game is international based, yet the entire 30+ minutes I flew in circles and I never ran across a single player on any map. This game is a barren wasteland of nothingness. Literally a total waste of time.
Next, this game is loaded with microtransactions. Now I get it, dev's have a right to earn funds from their product, I agree with the idea but they're doing it horribly wrong. For starters, this game offers NOTHING different, unique, or new in comparison to other PvP competitors. Sure, you can argue the basis of content that your fighting on dragon back but, there needs to actually "be" another player to fight. There is no one most of the time. So that argument is not only invalid but impractical. The prices for their products are incredibly high and there is no incentive to even contribute to this community of developers. Every single action has been a step on the wrong foot in the wrong direction by the dev's and this path may not be capable of recovering from.
Lastly, the final nail in the coffin of this review. You see, this is solely a PvP game. When a PvP game doesn't work, people will go to the thousands of other options out there. If a solely PvP game is gonna last, it needs to be good from the start or have some super stubborn Dev's who are willing to take a net loss early on. So, lets compare this game to another highly celebrated PvP game:
* Team Fortress 2 for the longest time was a pretty much just a PvP based game before the release of Man vs Machine. the game offered loads of different maps and combat strategies with a range of diversity FROM THE START. All characters and maps were unlocked from the very beginning.
By locking out all of the dragons and map types for a game and group of developers that have NO reputation what so ever the developers have completely locked out any possible redeming features. I'd try to get my profile to level 3 to try out other maps, but no one plays. If I can't play against anyone, I can't level. So definitely no redemption here.
As I said, neat concept and there are a load of opportunities with this idea, but at the end of the day this product was so buggy and incomplete with sooooo little content it's turned out to be a total waste of effort and time. I see there are a lot of people who wrote positive reviews, but when you take the time to read the reviews there is nothing sufficient stating why the game is good. People by nature like to positively rate something if has an idea they like associate with the material. In this case, dragons, flying, pvp, laser guns. All popular topics fused into one unique, though incomplete concept. Thing is though, pretty much the majority of all of these positive reviews have less than an hour of play and I doubt most people take time to spend initial gameplay to analyze and study the game before dedicating time to playing.
What this says is the idea has merit, people "want" something like this, but Dev's, you gotta fix your micro transations and a LOT more content and fast.
Best of luck, over and out.

Trine 2 is a beautiful game. Like, this game came out at around the same time as Skyrim, and just look at the difference (Billy Mays here). The visuals are amazing, and at almost any point in the game you could take a screenshot of wherever you're at and it would be fit to serve as a background. Unlike Trine, Trine 2 has quite a bit more puzzles, and is less reliant on combat than Trine. There's also a huge difficulty spike near the end of the game, that seemingly comes out of nowhere... also, the expansion "Goblin Menace" adds some really difficult levels on top of that. All in all it took me 14 hours to beat the game and the DLC. I don't like Trine 2 as much as the original Trine though, because Trine kind of had an interested plot idea of this vibrant high-fantasy world that had been abandoned due to some evil yet unknown until the end of the game, which was something I thought Frozenbyte did a great job with and I wish they would've kept that feeling in Trine 2, but they went in a "save the damsel in distress (because she was being held captive by her sister)". Anyways, Trine was 9.5/10, Trine 2 is 8/10. If you like puzzles moreso than combat in these types of things, you'll probably like Trine 2 more.
Trine is just such a colorful, fun series. Highly recommended with friends.

This game is fantastic (but probably only with a gamepad). If you're looking to play old school Smash, it's close but not an exact clone by any means. This is a good thing! Don't worry. It does have the same combat style to sate your Nintendo cravings, but comes with some interesting changes. Without grapple's and with cool mechanics like wall jumping, weapons, and a charge + aim mechanic for thrown items (or weapons) it has a good feel. The movements feel smooth and reactive, and rarely do I feel like I can't control my character. When I attack each move feels appropriately powerful and the feeling of being over-powered is well countered with the real threat of other players, all while not feeling too splashy/twitchy/spammy/gimmicked combat.
What surprised me most was that you can throw money at the dev's all you want, but you won't be winning more matches. However, characters ARE locked behind a pay wall (not including the very reasonably sized roster of cycling free playable characters called Legends), but you can simply save in-game currency to get the characters you want. In-game currency accrues somewhat slowly and the cost is somewhat high, so don’t expect to own all the characters after a day’s play but a new character for every few hours of play feels fair for the penny pinchers like me. That said, tossing $20 for all current and future characters is honestly not unreasonable, and frankly I could see even myself buying it. (TO BE CLEAR: if you don't want to pay any money, you won't suffer for it in matches!)
As is, in beta, I would say it's one of the better game's I've played in recent memory and definitely worth your time. Active dev's and progressing this game further is icing on my Brawlhalla cake.

TL;DR don't waste your money or your time. This game is almost nonfunctional.
Initial reaction: Premise seems good! Maybe like Recettear but with slightly worse graphics and more in-shop functions?
Attempt 1: Open game, keyboard controls are laggy and confusing. I accidentally buy too many items to sell and don't have enough gold to buy display cases, so I have to restart because the game will not let me continue. Ok, nbd, I'm three minutes in and maybe a controller will work better.
Attempt 2: NOPE, controller is vastly worse: less responsive, more confusing bindings, some functions that are just straight up not there??, and few appropriate tutorial prompts. I give up. This game is super broken; glad I got it in a bundle and not for full price.

Achievement hunters beware: This game takes at least 90+ hours to 100%, simply because there are achievements where you have to just sit there and wait. One cheevo is to have your shop open for a year, which IRL is 90+ hours... Other achievements are all pure grind, and are completely unreasonable.
Kill 1k thieves, where you see a thief every few minutes, will take forever.
Sell 20k items. You sell a few items a minute, maybe more once you get further in the game, but it's just so pointlessly boring and grindy.... If the achievements get reworked (or just the bad ones deleted), I will change this review (which I have seen happen in the past thankfully!).
As I'm playing further into it, I'm realizing there's some pretty game breaking bugs, like the automatic systems for restocking (which end up being REALLY necessary, and quite broken). First hearing about Brawlhalla:
FINALLY! Smash for PC where I won't suck so much because I'll be using a keyboard instead of a controler. Now instead of pressing combinations of buttons I'll be able to just push the button I need to do what I want!
First Playing Brawlhalla:
This game is somehow harder to control than Smash, HOW IS THAT POSSIBLE?!?!?!?
What is wrong with Brawlhalla:
1) The game doesn't even try to say that it isn't Smash for PC with achievements, the only differences are the controls, the names of the characters, the art style, the fact that it has an achievement system, and the device you play it on. They even have the Smash announcer voice say the name of the character you pick.
2) The controls are more confusing and impractical than Smash's controls. As a PC gamer, the Smash controls are hard for me to use, so I suck at Smash, which is a great game. Lots of players understand these controls which make sense to them. But while Smash has controls that follow a logical order that most can understand and use, this game has no rhyme or reason to which buttons do what, and to carry out actions other than moving, you have to press 2, 3, or even 4 buttons at once to complete simple tasks such as midair movement. These buttons don't even make sense in how combining them causes them to do what they do.
3) There is no originality in the charecters.  Each character has 2 weapons they can use, but there are only 3 different weapons in the game, excluding the 2 items players can pick up: spike balls and bombs. Those weapons are Sword, Gun, and lance.  Firstly, the gun's range is about the same as the lance, so there's no real point to the weapon.  All of the characters have a combination of 2 of the 3 different weapons. It's like playing smash except the only available characters are Falco, Fox, and Captain Falcon. If you actually play the game, you'll see that there are also axes, polearms, Dual Swords, and hammers. But these are the exact same as the sword, gun, and lance, just with different images. This is the developer's lazy way to make it seem like each character is unique instead of actually spending 5 minutes to actually make them unique. But I guess I'm asking too much. 5 minutes of their lives to make the consumers keeping their jobs and income alive actually happy? That's just crossing the line. [For those of you who don't get it yet, I'm being sarcastic.]
4) The game just sucks. I could elaborate even MORE on how much this game sucks and why, but I've already wasted 5 minutes of your time that you could have just seen that this is a negative review and moved on, and 5 minutes is a lot of time, ESPECIALLY if you're a developer of this game. There are some pros, though. The controls have no basis in logic, but do seem like a lose translation of the Smash controls, which don't translate well, but still make it easier for Smash players to learn and play with. The art is creative and the game concept is in high demand. I'm not saying it's worth $20. To me, it's not even worth the desktop icon. But if you're a competitive Smash player looking for a perfectly balanced 100% skill-based online competition, than this is the perfect game for you. If not, than you will probably still enjoy it if the 4000+ positive reviews vs. the 320 negative reviews are any indication.

Holy crap. They finally brought Empires to PC. I'm still in shock.
The short version: it's good. You can take over all of China, now, using a turn-based (every turn is a simulated month) system. It's a little repetitive, because you will take over a territory, rest a month, and then an enemy army will invade that territory, so you've now played the same map twice in a row, and sometimes that twice becomes three or four times before you have a chance to move on.
That aside, I don't have any serious complaints with it. It's slightly different in many ways from the regular Dynasty Warriors series, but the ability to strategize and take over regions is the largest change. There's less of a focus on pick-ups/power-ups in this game, and your generals can all be assigned a specific number of troops for each fight, but for the most part it's the same combat and characters that long-time fans of the series will recognize. There are strategems that can be selected before battles that give your officers special moves to employ. You don't seem to have direct control over these, or when they happen, you just pick what you think would be most advantageous for the map in general, and roll with it.
As a port, it doesn't have the widest range of graphics enhancements, I wouldn't call it "next-gen", but it looks better than ps3. I didn't have any problems with the porting, and my x360 controller worked fine.
The inlcusion of a character edit mode, and the DLC for costumes for older games (especially, for me, DW3) make this a must buy for fans and a great (although the strategy parts can be confusing at first) place to start the series for newcomers. Very highly recommended.
Edit: After playing a while I noticed the enemies will pop in and out some, but that's something the series has been known for. There's also, inexplicably, no autosave, so save often.

Mankind Divided is a love letter to DX1. I say this because DXMD improves upon the key Deus Ex things from Human Revolution, namely giving even more options to solve things, having vastly more to explore and capturing the atmosphere of the original even better.
DXMD is a very good continuation, perfecting the artistic vision, gameplay with augments (and without!) and pulling no punches with the locations, story and lore content. Prague as a city hub in the game is very much alive, and the themes and cultural nuances feel great to experience. A lot of care went into making this, that much is clear. From architecture to inhabitants to futuristic versions of local street environments, it shines as the best bunch of areas in the whole franchise. Along your exploration of all the densely packed stories, oddities and secrets, you'll be accompanied by amazing music once again. It's all so great to experience because it's truly the full package.
Side missions are amazing, I'd say the main meat of the game is simply enjoying Prague and doing the side missions. That's what I did for 30 hours, the remaining 16 or so went into the main missions. After completing the game, I felt good about it all, because there's so much in there, I know that I missed a lot of things, so jumping back in for another playthrough will also be enticing to do. This is a game for Deus Ex original lovers, because it has the same kind of replayability. Human Revolution was good, but this is so much better, trust me. Just lower your expectations for the ending, Human Revolution had a pretty final feeling epic climax of an ending. Mankind Divided has an ending that makes you realize this amazing dense pack of stories and missions was just an opening chapter for much bigger things to come. The ending isn't bad, it's just not an epic blockbuster movie type of an ending.
I recommend this game to anyone who loved the original DX or Human Revolution, Mankind Divided has found its place among my favorite games of all time, it rivals the original because as a whole, it's a goddamn beautiful game experience. Extra strong recommendation if you love reading ebooks, emails etc. for lore content, and exploring every nook and cranny, stopping to smell all the scifi flowers of augmented strife.
Extra note, Breach is a very entertaining separate game mode that Mankind Divided has, where you play as a hacker, delving into virtual simulations (same-ish gameplay loop as the main game, stealth, gunplay etc.) to hack and uncover corporate wrongdoings and secrets. It has a nice story element to it, via said hacking jobs and characters related to them. Very neat.
Get out there and crawl in air ducts, knock out guards, jump balconies, hack terminals. Because those conspiracies and corporate secrets won't solve themselves!

I've been playing Brawlhalla for a while and decided I would do a review on it. And my opening thoughts are: It's like Smash Bros. for the PC.
I got the game for free from a Beta key giveaway from Alienware, so I had no reason to NOT try the game.
So after a pretty quick download I get into the game and I'm greeted with full controller support and a smooth title screen, everything layed out in good spacing. I decide the first thing I should do is head into training and mess around with a few characters. They all have two weapons, most carry a heavy and light weapon, however, some like Lucien carry two lighter weapons. These different combinations make for unique playstyle across each character. I decide to head into some online matches and see that there's a daily mission for playing as Lucien or Teros, so I decide to go play with Teros the Minotaur for a while.

There is little to no lag in matches with the occasional disconnect (even though the other person could have simply quit because I was never disconnected from a match.) The also have a good disconnect system, where the other player is swapped with a usually-easy-to-beat CPU. The rating system seems to work well and has put me up against evenly matched players.
Pretty soon after, Jake got the game, and we got into Team Battles a lot (Which makes up most of the footage you see here.) While the enabled friendly fire was annoying at first becasue we didn't have it on while practicing, we got used to it, and this created some very interesting strategies.
While some nerfs and balancing patches need to be made, the developers are making these patches very often and it keeps the gameplay feel fair and responsive. Overall the gameplay gets a 9/10.
The graphics in this game look great with amazing animations and colorful, easy-to-look-at objects and characters. Overall, this game simply has some 10/10 graphics.
Onto the roster and microtransactions. The roster is ever-growing and cotains fun to play awesome characters. What characters you can play online is rotated each week in a League of Legends style. This is where the in-game coins come in, you don't have to pay a cent for the characters, it's 100% in-game money and they even give you one of your choosing for free. Buying a character means you have them unlocked forever, and over time every character can be bought and unlocked. The Mammoth Coins that you have to buy with real money are ONLY used for cosmetic upgrades and won't affect gameplay whatsoever. The developers did microtransactions right and I love it.
With overall great gameplay and microtransactions done well. Brawlhalla is a great game if you're a fan of the Smash Bros. series, or just fighting games in general. With few problems I can easily give this game a 9.5/10.
EDIT: Dropping the score to a 9/10 because the lag can be REALLY BAD in some matches. I literally lost against an afk player because every time I tried to hit them I simplay lag teleported straight off the edge.

I really wanted to love it.
RWBY has honestly become one of my favorite Animes of all time. (Cue in pitch forks and angry weebs, telling me its not "True" Anime) The fight scenes are unprecedented, the characters are awesomely designed and develop well alongside the story, it can be downright hilarious at times and it even had an unexpected turn in the middle of the last Volume (At this time of writing, that would be Volume 3) and crushed us emotionally without anyone really seeing it coming for the most part. And with all that, it also came along with some of the best music i probably heard in my life by Jeff Williams and Casey Lee Williams. Quite Frankly, RWBY is one hell of a phenomenon and i doubt i'll be falling out of it anytime soon.
However, with that being said...from day one, something about this Officially licensed title was off. Just to clarify, i had the game during its Early Access stages and played it alittle bit after i heard the complete version was done. Regardless, there just isnt that much to this game and it hurts me to look at a RWBY product and say "it could've been more" as it really couldve been. Im highly aware that it was made in house by Roosterteeth themselves and there wasnt a whole lot of people making this. But if that was the case, i really feel like it should've been delayed. Hell, i think it being on Early Access was too much in of itself but im even more disappointed that the complete product feels almost as empty.
I will say, it isnt all bad. Graphically it represents the show flawlessly. The cast as always does excellent voice work for the well estabilished characters and ill admit, those moments when your taking on dozen of Grimm whilist the shows soundtrack plays along has lead to some epic feeling moments. But everything else feels like its just lacking. For instance, the story. One thing that really bothered me pretty much on the spot, was the complete lack of cutscenes. With this beautiful graphic engine, you'd think they'd go the extra mile to make new scenes of Team RWBY interacting with eachother or something of that sorts. To quote Ms.Rose herself...Nope! The game is pretty much told in calls/text and thats really about it. And even if one could tolerate that, they pretty much made something rather forgettable out of it. RWBY has a rather deep and interesting lore going on and rather than building upon that, its just a mish mash of Dynasty Warriors type horde fighting and some rather dull boss fights. One thing that actually had me hyped before release was the reveal of a whole new villian. But ultimately, he just ends up being completely irrelevant. To the point where i doubt he'll have his name tossed out in the show anytime soon.
The combat is abit of a mixed bag. As far as the official release goes, its significantly improved over its previous versions. You get 3 Attack Buttons. On an Xbox Pad, X is your fast attacks, Y is your strong attack and any combination of X+Y will lead to combo variants. RT is your ranged attack and there are a few other things like Contextual team attacks, Counters (Which is done with B), Rolls (Done with LB) and a finisher (LB+RB). I greatly appreciate the changes made from pre to full release. The combo gauge for obtaining things is gone. Rather, Specials are obtained naturally through combat and a leveling system is where you'll obtain points to boast your characters. And the new additions i mentioned do help vary things...but my problem is, you spend the entire game pretty much moving forward and then horde killing. This would be abit more tolerable if the combat had more going for it. Its fun at first, but you begin to realize that you'll use the same combos over and over, and without the ability to unlock new ones, the tedium will creep up fast. The developers probably realized this and hence added the ability to swap characters after a chapter is completed. And while thats nice, every character has about the same amount of combos and it literally takes about under 20 minutes to see what a character is capable of. Considering that Team RWBY is the only playable characters at the moment and that the game is only a couple hours long, that means that the game is going to become an endurance test rather than a fun coop experience. Speaking of which, Coop...yeah, you'll need it. I cant really say the game is hard, but the...um "Single Player" experience is atrocious. If you opt to play Solo, your going to be facing huge hordes of enemies by yourself and its shows the worst of the game pretty much right off the bat. And the coop is abit underwhelming. It can produce some pretty cool moments but nothing ever really feels designed for it really. Your never asked to open things together or have a specific character do something that only that character can do. Its basically the same linear and repetitive experience of Solo, except less tedious due to being able to rid grimm much faster.
I imagine to some, this review is pretty nitpicky. Some would probably tell me not to complain about a 20$ game. Well, there are ironically better coop games for 20$, a great example being Left 4 Dead, and in general there are just way better games at this price point. Im a die hard RWBY fan expressing my disappointment with a game that really had allot of potential going for it. I seriously wanted to love this game like i do every thing else related to RWBY, but i cant. Even if one did get past the linear, Repetitive level design, there just isnt enough content to warrant having this game. I honestly hope that we see a truly realized RWBY title. Perhaps a Platinum styled game, or hell maybe a game like Ubisofts forgotten Naruto Rise of A Ninja; A Hybrid of Open World, Exploration and Arcade Fighters, while allowing you to relive moments from the show. But who knows, perhaps im aiming abit high.

I would find it very hard to give this game a positive review, unless of course you like being endlessly spawn camped, playing on wildly mismatched teams, and having the game devs constantly "tweaking" the game to make it more (not really) "playable".
Let me first bring up the un even team issue. For some unknown to me reason , most of the new players of this game start playing on the American faction. In my experience in the game ( over 1k hours atm) this seems to be a constant. So if you want to join and you are new try the Soviet side. I cant for personall reasons play or reccommend the Nazi faction. When you play this seems to be one of the largest problems, if you have experience most of your team won't. The game match system to keep the teams even fairly balanced in staged matches seems hopelessly broken with teams loaded with players with large in game experience vs. teams with very little. This is to be somewhat expected in the war mode of play but not in staged.
If you like to play as a tanker you can, not really sure how you start this now, I've had a tanker character from beta when you just switched (it does cost in game credits) from an infantry to a tanker and start working your way up. Being a tanker can be fun at times but the inconsistency makes it tough. Then of course there are the AT clowns. We regulars have alot of names for them, rambos, commandoes, you get the idea. If you are in a tank especially a heavy, you are pretty much hosed. The lowest AT guy (anti tank) can carry mines or stickies, the mines they run up to you from behind place the mine on you and then shoot it, boom your dead. This wouldn't matter too much except that you have to pay for your tank spawns. Now as a high level tanker you can afford this, but as a low level tanker you lose credits, and it can be very expensive. The heavy tanks are especially susceptable to these attacks as they do not move faster than any infantry can move at a walk.
Lets move on to the spawn camping: It does exist in almost every mulitplayer online game but i've never played a game where it is as widespread as this game. Every so often the devs change a few things on the maps to make it more difficult but when you cant leave the spawn in a tank, truck or jeep its a serious problem.
Then I will bring up the devs:  For some reason when the game was in beta we had some pretty good maps with varied terrain and options for a lot of play styles. Yes these maps had some problems but instead of addressing the problems they made entirely new maps! WITH THE SAME PROBLEMS! Now i dont want to bash the guy who made them, they are pretty big and complex with quite a bit of detail but the management team that pushed this, needs to have their collective heads examined.  When you have thousands of players giving feedback about issues there has to be some really common threads, address them. Now for some other reason there are no published stats about the weapons you are using in game. For example how much damage does rifle x do with mod a c and e, or how much actual armor will this tank shell penetrate. Tank shells bounce off targets with alarming frequency, depending on who you are fighting. I would not have issue with this but they seem to not have considered that each shell might hit the tank or may have been aimed so as to hit the armor at 90 degrees for penetration.  For example a german tiger 2 is nearly impentrable from the front or sides even if you hit the sloping armor not at an angle but at 90 degrees. I've hit them myself many times when the first shot will penetrate and every subsequent shot will bounce off the exact same spot. One or two time I could understand but five while that tank is stationary? The devs also constantly tweak your equipment so as soon as you get used to it they nerf it and well its useless.  They seem to do this with most every piece of equipment in the game, tank armor, speed, shell penetration, manueverablity, same with rifles. Don't get used to what you have, next week it will be crap.
The devs have also got some really weird stuff going on with the strategy side of the game that greatly affects gameplay on the first person shooter side. If a general has an Assault Team with low stats (like vision) you cant see the enemy very well while you play, yeah I did say that you might be fighting guys that are very hard to see, likewise if you have a good AT stats your team can destroy the enemy like nothing. It makes for bizzare gameplay.  I do not know if that is what causes so many people who play this to call hacks. Which is also as near as I can tell is also an issue. The devs say that they do anti hacking "sweeps" , sadly they do not do enough. I personally have watched playes on other teams use aimbots to shoot with perfect accuracy planes down with tanks from accross the map when the planes spawned. Wait let me rephrase that, THEY SHOT BEFORE THE PLANES SPAWN, and hit them 95% of the time as they became visible. I'm pretty sure i reported those 2 guys, saw them months later not banned, and was told by another player that "that guy is really good! Hes got a utube channel" to which I replied that he was cheating that I saw it on my own screen that there is no way to shoot that accurately with a tank from that distance.
Soo after that long, rambling review, for the reasons I stated and others I didn't, I can't reccommend investing your time into this game. Its sad that I say this because I am one of many who paid them actual money.

In the end, I recommend it for the shenanigans and warm fuzzies one will get from some of the romantic scenes. Grammar Nazis might not survive the errors that I found jarring though, so to those individuals: Proceed at your own risk.

Enjoyable. Fair range of character options. You can only choose between an elven womon and a human man, but you can also choose some aspects of their background and personality. I played it twice, several months apart, and might play it again sometime.

The bad:
- Not enough drawings. The different characters always appear in the same pose with the same clothes, only their expression varies. It's made particularly obvious by the fact that you're always changing their equipment and it doesn't change a thing on their visual.
- Expensive
- The story is classical heroic-fantasy. Big bad guy, group of heroes, saving the world. Nothing new here.

May be bad/ may be good:
- It's a visual novel. Some players like it, some others just hate it. It just depends of the player.
- A lot of fan-service. Read "a lot of visible skin". Many people complained about it. I personally have nothing against nudity, quite the contrary actually. I admit it's a bit stupid to go fight with huge shoulder plates without protecting the belly, but that's standard heroic-fantasy. The main difference with other titles is that they usually add a layer of fabric, but that doesn't protect from blades either.
The good:
- Even if it's primarily a visual novel, it doesn't forget to be a true RPG. The turn-based combats are nothing new, but they are tactical and work very well.
- The musics are cool.
- Though the story is a bit dull, the writing is very good and the characters are original and nicely fleshed out. It's actually pretty gripping to read.
- Probably the best of all: fan-service for everyone. Females in skimpy clothing ? Check. Males in skimpy clothing ? Check. I think it's the first game where I see such an equal treatment. Also, you can play either as a guy or a girl, and whatever this choice, you can romance people from both sexes. Finally...
I actually really liked the game. It's a bit expensive, but for a game with equal treatment in terms of fan-service, I'm more than happy to pay full price. Especially when the game really is fun.

While Loren The Amazon Princess is categorized as an RPG, its RPG elements are light for those used to something that focuses on combat like most Western RPGs or even popular JRPGs. However for the developers Winter Wolves, who have in the past mostly developed relatively generic visual novels/dating sims, it is much heavier on actual gameplay than its predecessors. This combat is the standard turn-based combat where speed detirmines the  turn order found in many "retro" JRPGS. You can a multitude of weapons and armor for your characters that can be purchased in stores or recieved as rewards in combat or through completion of character quests which unlock later in the game.
The meat and potatoes of the game is in your interactions with the characters in your party and how it affects the story's outcome. The plot consists of a relatively standard high-fantasy adventure where a lowly male human or female elf (depending on the character you choose to play as) helps the title character find her lost mother, getting involved in a war between two foreign races along the way.  Dailoge is more like a novel than the dailogue trees found in most Western RPGs, but at many points in the narrative you can choose a response that affects the protagonist's personality. Most of the options involve choosing to be "joking", "friendly", or "forceful" however there are a few times where you make decisions which change the direction of the plot or you can choose a "romance" option. While there is a large focus on romance with several romancable characters of both genders, it is completly optional to the story and is not forced upon the player. While some of the romance options feel a little creepy, there are a few sappy love stories for those who enjoy that kind of thing.
Overall, I would reccoment Loren The Amazon Priness if you would enjoy a light RPG with a simple but sometimes tear-jerking plot and romance options that (for the most part) feel like they are naturally occuring between characters rather than shoe-horned in pulp forced upon you. If you don't care much about relationships or plot in RPGs or can't stand the art style you can find many mechanically better RPGs out there that don't require you to click through hundreds of lines of text and look at 2D sprites.
If you are looking for simmilar titles from Winter Wolves you could look into Planet Stronghold if you want something with more focus on mechanics than plot or the new game Tales of Avorn: Season of the Wolf for an all-around better RPG experience wich still focuses on narrative set in this universe.

I loved the story elements, particularly the interactions between characters. The RPG system was pretty good, but slightly tedious at times. I appreciated the option to "cheat" your way through the game after finishing it the first time, making it easier to explore other paths and romances.

Here is a rather enjoyable game, if you like VNs, RPGs, and turn-by-turn tactical action.
Characters/dialogs/characterization: 8/10. Well written dialogs, good characterization. Many good dialogs are written to adapt to your every choice.
Graphics: 7/10. Art is good, with a few very good drawings, especially if you don't mind mostly-exposed characters naked under skimpy pieces of armor.
Story/World-building: 6/10. consistent story, but not groundbreaking. The plot works and moves in a logical way, it has some twists, but it is essentially predictable. The world is solid, this is the kind of background you'd expect for such a fantasy setting.
Romance: 7/10. Simplistic/obvious options without surprise (just select 'romance' when you're given the opportunity). Though the option is obvious, the dialogs and characters development are well executed. Somehow, the characters are endearing, which keeps an interest to this aspect of the game.
Equipment/Items: 6/10. There are many pieces of equipment that a character can wear. The many armors/weapons/miscellaneous objects are sometimes a bit confusing as of which you should use to upgrade your characters. The limited amount of money and the limited choice in most shops doesn't help (though you can sell the gems and get more money, as I discovered rather late in the game). So the equipment/armor/weapon upgrades are rather few and far between.
Combat system/progression system: 8/10. Good turn-by-turn combat system, with some depth. The choice about the location is only: front-row /back-row. I wish they'd have taken into account the position: left-wing/right-wing, so you'd be more focussed on the opponent you're directly facing. Apart from this (small) reservation, the system is suprisingly well-done, solid, deep and flexible, while being extremely playable. Well-done!
Overall: 7/10. This is not the game of the year, but you can spend a good time with this one. You can maybe play it a few times: it's not long (about 15 hours for one run) and you can try and play it a few times to get to the different endings. Overall, a rather good merge between VN and turn-by-turn fantasy tactical game.

This game was everything I had hoped it would be and THEN MORE.
Combat:
Fluid, easy to learn. Fun to level up
Weapons:
Lots of weapons, very fun to toy with them all and find a good couple to match your play style
Graphics:
Not bad, it's a tad dated but it still holds a fantasy feel with some kind of cartoonish look, somewhat like what borderlands does.
Smithing:
Fantastic, easy to use, and you can get some amazing kinds of gear from it.
Exploration:
Always fun, loot is rendomized so you never find the same thing in the same place no matter how many playthroughs you do.
Questing:
9/10 of the entirety of the quests in this game are great and the monotonous ones are few and far between. The quests are engaging and informative of the story
General:
The world is magnificent, filled with aweing magical ley sparkles and with a great soundtrack to boot. there are a handful of races but a ton of lore on each. the world is vibrant and always full of life, and it reacts to the changes you've made to the world. Loot is always plentiful.
Roleplaying:
This game is RICH with roleplay potential, you can be a paladin using heals and light magic to do good, or you can be a shady rogue that wipes out a village, you can be the anti-hero mercenary thats in it for the money. this game is chalk FULL of goodies for the common RPer.
Encounters:
Fun and engaging, somewhat dimwitted, but there are a lot with decent AI.
Final note:
This game is worth it, the variety in armor,weapons,and spells are fantastic. The game itself is quite and adventure in a cliche fantasy world that'll be JUST what you're looking for and THEN some. I have yet to beat the game I just keep making new Characters and I've yet to get bored of it. The biggest thing with me is that it not only has to be a great game but there has to be a TON of replay value and this game, even though i haven't even made it to the half-way mark, has TONS and TONS of replay value.

My only complaint is that there's limited storage in your house(s) yet they give you so many neat custom armors and materials to make your own.
You can respec your character to anything you want but you more often then not will have sold off all the items you'd use for a different build simply due to lack of proper storage space.
Aside from that i freaking love this game. The combat system is a blast and the character creation options give you not only the three archtypes (knight, assassin, mage) but you can combine their attributes and pick/choose what suits you.
Think old WoW single player but with 3x as many character attribute options. Best part is that you can change them later on if you change your mind.
It can feel grindy at times after the main plot, it's kind of par for the course for RPG's, you can only dress fetch and kill quests in so many outfits before it doesn't feel new anymore but there's a surprising amount of guild/clan quests that i found to be even more interesting then the main plot. Getting out off the beaten track and exploring pays off here, they placed a ton of neat side quests as a reward for those who prefer to look around.
Runs great. Only one weird bug during a sidequest that crashed the game but i never could get it to happen again. One glitch after 100 hours of game play is a worthy note. The graphics are low spec so you'll be able to run it on basically any machine made in the last 7 years.

Looking at specifically the gameplay and the price tag because that should factor into whether you buy this game or not (its probably not worth at the $10 mark tbh)
Pros
+It can hold your attention for a while
+Some sense of progression through town/shop upgrades
+Pretty cheap most of the time, devs are generous with the sales on the $10 price tag
+One of the few shop management games offered on Steam
+Good game style to just have a pretty peaceful gameplay experience
+No, it isn't a flash game repackaged into a Steam port. It's justa standalone shop management game. These are just facts.
Cons
-Mechanics remain relatively the same throughout
-Price markups become tedious to apply to new products and readjust to all products after each upgrade
-Progression starts to feel less meaningful after a while
-Game inevitably becomes monotone not immediately, but eventually. It's not a triple A game after all
-Steam achievements are really badly executed in this game
-Automation means you can literally leave the game for an hour at a time and still be fine and ready to restock your automated bots. It becomes less of a game then, and more of a blueprint of meaningless optimisation. However if half-automation where you have to pitch in every now and then appeals to you, then all the power to you
Overall 6.5/10, not as bad the negative review spam seems to make it out to be. Fine purchase if you're looking for something new in the form of a shop management game - but specifically not when you are already well versed with shop management games looking for something you've never seen before. Most of the people here are the former rather than the latter: or they have already bought the game, so yeah: Shoppe Keep is worth considering.

Just finished the game today. Very disappointing. As a long time Deus Ex fan, I can only say that this game has no plot. It starts well, but after about 6 hours into it I realized that I’m stuck in Prague, and there won’t be any more locations like in previous games. The city feels very cluttered and full of corridors; you don’t really feel a city – more like a bunch of rooms linked together. The game gets repetitive quickly - the music is the same, atmosphere the same, everyone speaks in a monotone voice and I couldn't care less for ANY of the characters I met. If I ever have to hear "THIS IS ELISA CASSAN REPORTING LIVE" again I would kill myself!
The game is simply boring - once you get all the augs and upgrade all your weapons, you realize there is no excitement left. That new "weapon parts" system is so bad for this game. Instead of hunting for upgrades, you can fully upgrade all your weapons very quickly (using an aug that breaks down useless items and weapons). The smart vision aug is a necessary evil, as the game is SO CLUTTERED WITH CRAP you can NEVER find stuff worth picking up without using your "smart vision" which sucks. What a lazy effort - what happened to good old level and game design? I ended up spending the majority of my gameplay in smart vision, missing on the aesthetics and immersion of the world around me.
Finally, most of my actions had no consequences – without spoiling anything, I shot 3 key characters in the head and NOTHING. Not even a comment. Remember how Alex used to scold you in Deus Ex 1 if you did something horrible? No one gives a crap here.
This is a big step backwards from Human Revolution, and a GIANT step backwards from the original Deus Ex.
Oh, and I won’t even mention the random crashes to desktop.

PROS:
+ It's free!

+ Tried-and-true
game mechanics.

CONS:
- All puzzles are monochrome (white and some color of your choosing).
- The white backgrounds in the game sometimes seem too bright (especially if you're playing in a dimly-lit room).
- Workshop integration seems touchy and prone to freezing. This can be fixed by exiting the game and coming back in, and while this can be done very quickly, it shouldn't happen at all.
- No controller support (although this is a minor nitpick, some other games in this genre do include controller support).
VERDICT: Picross Touch is an excellent introduction to the world of nonogram puzzles. It's free (so no money lost if you dislike the game) and some of its puzzles are as good as those in
, a game that I consider to be the "gold standard" for picross.
Although there are a few minor issues with the game, the positives definitely outweigh the negatives.
If you're at all interested in nonogram puzzles, I'd strongly recommend giving Picross Touch a try.

I used to play the original Gunz-the First Duel.  Those were fun days, until hackers started to ruin the fun for everyone else.  Anyway, GunZ 2:  The Second Duel is not a complete substitute for the original, but it still has the core elements.  I do love the fact that the sniper rifles actually work with scope and everything.  And characters are customizeable "to a point."  I use these terms lightly.  Due to the introduction of character classes, you are limited to buying weapons only ment for your character class.  You can still customize how your character looks with clothes (which don't help your overall stats, you just buy them to look cooler) and if your feeling up to drop some green, you can use store credit to buy some more of the fashionable accessories, like hats and such.  Now, as for the gameplay itself, you can set up private servers for yourself and take on the npcs in the storyline (which I recommend because I don't get decent connection).  Or you can set up a public server and and invite people to join you.  And of course, you can go into other rooms and fight people in Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Gladiadtor, ect.  And as for the players themselves, I've noticed not much has changed.  Many people are still trolls, or they just feel the need to belittle others just to make themselves feel beter.  When this happens, I just exit out of the main chat and just set up my own private server and go do some solo killing.  That being said, I give this game a 6/10.  It's still fun to play,  especially if you remember the good old days of the original Gunz game.  And like any other sequal, it has it's own pros and cons.  But if your looking for a decent shooting game, look no further then here.

I have put entirely too many hours into this game. I've gotten a 100% completed game on xbox and decided to pick it up on PC again years later and I have put in just as much time on this game file as I did on the xbox one. Probably even more, since I've picked up both DLCs instead of just legends of dead kel.
To start, this game probably isn't for everyone. However, it is definitely for me. I have my fair share of disliked pieces of the game, but overall, I love this game and the replay value is obviously fairly high for me.
The gameplay is a lot of fun. I love it to no end. The customization on how to play is pretty endless. Wanna be a rogue? You got it. How about a roguish mage? Totally, yes, you can do that. But that's not enough! you say. I want more! you say. No problem, you can ♥♥♥♥ing crossclass all three archetypes and be a mage/rogue/warrior. Or any other combo of the three classes (or ofc a purity of them if you prefer). I do have an issue with the combat in that it almost feels like a chore as time goes on. You definitely get tired of going through one part of the map filled with just ogres, or filled with just sprites, or threshes, or jottun, ect. It gets kind of old. I would actually say that the mobs in this game are my biggest problem with the game. They are insanely repetitive and boring at times, and the only saving grace is that if you've spent enough time speccing yourself to max levels, you can pretty much just one hit kill everything.
The story and lore and characters are what kept me invested in the game. You definitely have the feeling of already being apart of the world while also being reintroduced to it since your character hsa died and has no memories of life before their death. You get to feel like the real "one true savior", which is always a plus in my book as a narcissist. The main story itself isn't even as interesting as the many towns and people you come across. I spent more time completing faction quests than main story quests. The towns all have their own unique issues for you to step in and solve, and really do keep it interesting as you traverse the map until your eventual final run to the end of the game.
I wish there had been more armor to choose from. You really don't want the cool matching armor sets the longer you play the game since the stuff you craft is immeasurably better than any other armor you obtain. This sort of makes unique weapons and armor sets useless, and honestly, by the time you get half the cool junk you can use, you've probably already had the ability to craft far superior weaponry or armor which is unfortunate.
All in all, this is a very charming game, worth giving a try. Especially if you like RPGs. It's not the top of its genre, but it is a game I love and play all the time. I often come back to it when I don't have interest or energy for anything else.

This game has some beautifully written romance dialogue and a competent RPG combat system with a well-built world and good artwork. Unfortunately it fails at maintaining a coherent portrayal of characters and people are frequently quite stupid in that they ignore obvious alternatives to the current situation. They also run on "RPG logic" in that you can recruit people whom by all means you have no logical reason to keep alive at the time. This game was a pleasant surprise. It's mostly a visual novel game, with some RPG aspects mixed in, and they worked quite well together. It was easy to immerse myself in the game as both the setting and the characters were interesting. The story itself is not enthralling, but it's good enough to keep you playing to see it through to the end. The visuals are appealing, and, like many other VNs, some background images are reused. The music was nice and fitting for the setting. The length was appropriate for the price; I logged just over 20 hours on my first playthrough playing in hard mode. I only unlocked 18 achievements so there is certainly some replay value.
The dialogues are not static, and they can change slightly depending on who you're romancing. There is a "camp" option where you can talk to your party members, and new conversations are triggered after certain events. There's also the option of doing personal side quests where more can be learned about the characters. You could also find yourself in a confrontation if you've romanced more than one of them. Some dialogues are a bit cheesy, but nothing bothersome or cringe-worthy. There are a few grammatical errors/typos, but they're very minor and forgettable. Overall, I enjoyed the game and am now looking forward to trying out the other games from the developer.

My feelings on this game are positive overall, but it's definitely a mixed bag, and I'd be less inclined to recommend it when not on sale. The short version: Loren has a solid story with an unusual narrative frame, charming characters, and fun combat, but is bogged down by writing that feels like its own clunky fan-fiction, and stagnant art that lacks much appeal or variety. I want to like it more than I do, though, because it has a great deal of enthusiasm, and tries very, very hard.
In the game's favor:
-Far and away the best thing in my opinion is the combat, which is run on a fairly straightforward, but well executed turn-based system. While it doesn't take long to figure out the resistances and vulnerabilities of each form of enemy, and the scope of the game itself is fairly limited, the instances are varied enough to keep things interesting, and encourage balanced party rotation at the same time.
-One of the reasons I bought the game was a review that mentioned how unusual it is for an RPG to position the player character as the support of, rather than the story's main hero. It's a unique narrative frame that raises Loren above the ordinary for me, one which I felt granted the freedom to switch up my own playstyle a bit. Being the story's hero usually precludes making narrative sense of being the main healer/squishy support character in the party. Being the hero's bodyguard made trying on that role feel natural, even as the game leaves the door open to play as something else.
-The game aims to be friendly and inclusive to all players, and while it didn't wholly succeed for me (explained below), the effort is praiseworthy.
-The characters are, for the most part, charming, albeit a little bit flat.
-The story is also charming, though it reads at times a little bit like Xena Warrior Princess plays Dragon Age Lite in Middle Earth.
What worked less well, in my opinion:
-The writing itself: while the story and characters felt (for the most part) solid, the prose felt clunky and under-edited, with awkward diction, a handful of spelling errors, and more than a handful of convoluted sentences. The "romance" sequences in particular read like heavy-handed, if enthusiastic, fan fiction, and only a few characters really seemed to have a voice of their own that didn't blur together without the aid of a name tacked above the dialogue.
-The art in the game was close to a deal-breaker for me. Admittedly, I'm not crazy about the design, but my gripe is less with the style, and more that it felt shortchanged. The repeated character, enemy, and set designs, the half-hearted, limited range of expressions, and the overall utter lack of variety felt very chintzy; if you don't have animation available to you in this very visual medium, what you do have has to make up for it in beauty and background. What I found instead felt like a collection of xeroxed paper dolls without any clothes, and with maybe six postcards to pose them against. Potential party members can be immediately identified by their ability to blink, a quirk that is rendered even more bizarre by being the ONLY animation in the game (unless one counts scooting one paper doll across the screen towards another during violent/romantic encounters).
-The art and writing, Part II: I hate bringing this up, because I do feel the game tries so hard to be friendly to all players, but... I started out the game and almost immediately shut it off when I realized that not only was Elenor stuck in absurd midriff-bearing armor (something I hear might be altered by the so-called 'censor mode'?), but every woman I encountered apparently shared the same disregard for her innards staying in. Finding one of the first male party members readjusted my thinking from "Ick, this is a bit too male-gaze-y for me", to "Ah, nope, just generally gaze-y". By the end of the game it was back to "Okay, so it's just *mostly* male-gaze-y", because one lumbering, shirtless barbarian does not balance out the Grand Canyon expanse of elf and nymph cleavage I faced, and certainly it couldn't stand against Jul's prominent, perky buttocks splayed across my screen (shout out to Ye Gods of Great Timing for encouraging my husband to come into the room just then). The writing, too, often felt as though it expected me to be more interested in Loren than I was, even as it provides a variety of other optional romantic interests, accommodating multiple sexualities; providing those options is excellent, but the effort is diluted when it feels the game still expects you to like Loren best. I'll only add that one of the potential love triangles involves a mother-daughter pairing, and leave it at that.
-While I understand that this is an indie project and I want to support it, I wasn't enamoured with the fact that the main game, not content with a large-font, title page ad, introduces two prominent characters clearly intended as party members (they blink and everything!) that are only available with the expansion. It's a cheap move that infuriates players when done by big name developers, and I find it similarly unbecoming in a smaller development.
To conclude (if you made it this far!): I don't know that I'd recommend this to a friend, as I don't have many that share my love of RPGs that I wouldn't be too embarassed by the writing/art to suggest it to-- but I'd travel back in time to recommend it to myself again when it was on sale last month, as good intentions count for a lot, and I did enjoy it enough to finish, cringing and all.

Loren is one of Winter Wolve's best VNs. This game happens to feature a hybrid visual novel RPG component that lends itself to degrees of challenge. However, don't expect something complicated or in depth for that matter. I found the battles to be slightly tedious at one point because I was more into the story.
The game starts off as a rag tag duo of you a lowly servant and your Amazon Princess off to find out the whereabouts of her mother. The game then blossoms into your typical team of unlikely heroes out to save the world from impending evil. We've seen this plot before and it isn't unique in any sense. What I enjoyed was the individual character stories and relationship building. You don't necessarily date anyone in the game but as you spend time getting to know your fellow travelers you get the option to romance a few of them and grow closer as the story progresses.
I've played through this game as both the male and female choices. There are several characters for each to get closer to and all of them eventually have individual quests that you can partake in. So while the story is linear in nature you have plenty of side quests and branching that allows you to deviate a bit in the path you take throughout the game.
One thing I appreciate about this game is it gives equal opportunity fanservice. Sure characters are pretty scantily dressed and there's no shortage of semi nakedness going on you are just as apt to see topless guys as you would see nearly nude females. Also there's opportunity for gay and lesbian romance options. Options, being the key word, if you don't like seeing a budding romance between 2 men you can totally avoid it. Now the Steam version is the slightly censored version of the game in which the characters might wear a little more clothes and show a little less skin. To remove the censor there are a few guides you can reference, it's quite simple. Note that the intimate scenes are tastefully done and everyone wears underwear but aren't scenes that are of the SFW variety. But really, if you're playing this game at work it'll make little difference if your boss sees elf boobs or not.
The writing was well done. I actually enjoyed all the characters stories and dialogue and it was a great reprieve in between all the mundane fighting. After you finish the game once you can unlock the cheat menu to auto-win the fights so you can play this game as a pure VN experience.  With the expansion unlocks an few additional side quests, characters and events adding an extra few hours to your journey. But you might want to play the base game first. Overall I enjoyed this game and think anyone who wants a little more variety in their visual novel would enjoy this.

I really wanted to love it.
RWBY has honestly become one of my favorite Animes of all time. (Cue in pitch forks and angry weebs, telling me its not "True" Anime) The fight scenes are unprecedented, the characters are awesomely designed and develop well alongside the story, it can be downright hilarious at times and it even had an unexpected turn in the middle of the last Volume (At this time of writing, that would be Volume 3) and crushed us emotionally without anyone really seeing it coming for the most part. And with all that, it also came along with some of the best music i probably heard in my life by Jeff Williams and Casey Lee Williams. Quite Frankly, RWBY is one hell of a phenomenon and i doubt i'll be falling out of it anytime soon.
However, with that being said...from day one, something about this Officially licensed title was off. Just to clarify, i had the game during its Early Access stages and played it alittle bit after i heard the complete version was done. Regardless, there just isnt that much to this game and it hurts me to look at a RWBY product and say "it could've been more" as it really couldve been. Im highly aware that it was made in house by Roosterteeth themselves and there wasnt a whole lot of people making this. But if that was the case, i really feel like it should've been delayed. Hell, i think it being on Early Access was too much in of itself but im even more disappointed that the complete product feels almost as empty.
I will say, it isnt all bad. Graphically it represents the show flawlessly. The cast as always does excellent voice work for the well estabilished characters and ill admit, those moments when your taking on dozen of Grimm whilist the shows soundtrack plays along has lead to some epic feeling moments. But everything else feels like its just lacking. For instance, the story. One thing that really bothered me pretty much on the spot, was the complete lack of cutscenes. With this beautiful graphic engine, you'd think they'd go the extra mile to make new scenes of Team RWBY interacting with eachother or something of that sorts. To quote Ms.Rose herself...Nope! The game is pretty much told in calls/text and thats really about it. And even if one could tolerate that, they pretty much made something rather forgettable out of it. RWBY has a rather deep and interesting lore going on and rather than building upon that, its just a mish mash of Dynasty Warriors type horde fighting and some rather dull boss fights. One thing that actually had me hyped before release was the reveal of a whole new villian. But ultimately, he just ends up being completely irrelevant. To the point where i doubt he'll have his name tossed out in the show anytime soon.
The combat is abit of a mixed bag. As far as the official release goes, its significantly improved over its previous versions. You get 3 Attack Buttons. On an Xbox Pad, X is your fast attacks, Y is your strong attack and any combination of X+Y will lead to combo variants. RT is your ranged attack and there are a few other things like Contextual team attacks, Counters (Which is done with B), Rolls (Done with LB) and a finisher (LB+RB). I greatly appreciate the changes made from pre to full release. The combo gauge for obtaining things is gone. Rather, Specials are obtained naturally through combat and a leveling system is where you'll obtain points to boast your characters. And the new additions i mentioned do help vary things...but my problem is, you spend the entire game pretty much moving forward and then horde killing. This would be abit more tolerable if the combat had more going for it. Its fun at first, but you begin to realize that you'll use the same combos over and over, and without the ability to unlock new ones, the tedium will creep up fast. The developers probably realized this and hence added the ability to swap characters after a chapter is completed. And while thats nice, every character has about the same amount of combos and it literally takes about under 20 minutes to see what a character is capable of. Considering that Team RWBY is the only playable characters at the moment and that the game is only a couple hours long, that means that the game is going to become an endurance test rather than a fun coop experience. Speaking of which, Coop...yeah, you'll need it. I cant really say the game is hard, but the...um "Single Player" experience is atrocious. If you opt to play Solo, your going to be facing huge hordes of enemies by yourself and its shows the worst of the game pretty much right off the bat. And the coop is abit underwhelming. It can produce some pretty cool moments but nothing ever really feels designed for it really. Your never asked to open things together or have a specific character do something that only that character can do. Its basically the same linear and repetitive experience of Solo, except less tedious due to being able to rid grimm much faster.

I love RWBY. But this is not a very well made game. It feels unfinished and basic.
Combat is exceedingly simple with very little depth, the upgrade trees don't seem to have anything remotely interesting to offer, there's no tutorial or explanations for features presented, and when you start off you're thrown out into the middle of the woods without so much as a scrap of dialogue to set the scene or story.

If you want to buy this game, do it for these reasons... because you are supporting the developers, because you really like the show and want to fight like one of RWBY, because you like horde games and repetative button pushing, because short story mode games like Modern Warfare and Homefront are what really get your heart going...
Don't buy this game at full price. Don't buy this game if you want more genuine RWBY story telling. Don't buy this game if you hate repetative action simulators.
This game, at its core, is a piece of trash. It started as something that promised to be something akin to dynasty warriors or Hyrule Warriors. Instead, it only has those games in mind when they made it. They had so much potential to expand the storyline of RWBY and give the huntresses some real meat to their backstories. Instead, they pasted together some disjointed "missions" where your goal is always the same... Get from point A to B and defend it until all the hordes of minions of increasing volume and difficulty are all dead.
The leveling system is rudimentary and incredibly simplistic and almost worthless once you learn the different combos all of the girls do. The dialogue is a non-entity, and the storyline is ridiculously shallow.
In the end, this was a waste of money and time and I would not recommend this game to anyone.

I like this a lot. It's just the right amount of slightly silly, coupled with good solid game mechanics, interesting level topology and swoopy flying.
it DOES have a slightly cheap feel, but the myriad features and optimizations that would be required to make a game like this run like the new DOOM does would require a huge budget and a large pricetag.  This is very healthy small studio development at its finest.
everything works, there are a pleasing amount of upgrades that i was able to earn in a half hours play session, there are some people on servers and the UI makes most stuff pretty clear.
the actual dragonfighting is fun! it's slower paced than other flight or dogfighting games and theres a large variety of animations in the dragon characters which make it feel very natural and cool to flap and glide around and do popup attacks and dive in for the kill. a full server would be very awesome.
I would like to see perching and hanging implemented, as you can't land anywhere - your dragon fumbles around until you can flap ungracefully back into the sky.  im thinking of the batman games style drop/snatch attacks here.
also going to moan in passing about
general art direction (it all looks a bit disjointed, get a theme going on to tie it all together)
level art quality (maybe you guys should stylize this thing?)
lighting (black dragons get old fast)
some level topography (the nightworld map with all its tunnels and overlooks is my favourite so far, some of the other levels need more height to be more of a playground for flying)
but omfg dragons! reccomended!

Short review:  Loved this game!  Decent replay value, too - Have completed multiple playthroughs.
*Regarding another review that dinged the game for not being child-friendly: Whatever you may think of the art style and description, the game is definitely aimed at adults.  The romance dialogues can veer into M territory, and even the non-romance dialogue and scenarios (themes of leadership, death, making tough decisions, family, racism, war, etc.) may not be well understood or appreciated by younger players.
Longer review:
I can definitely see why other reviewers were making Dragon Age comparisons.  While I enjoyed the battles and the skill systems, the meat of this game is really in the story and the character interactions.  Luckily, the characters tend to be likeable, and there are romance options for many tastes and preferences.  You also generally have three different "moods" to respond in dialogue - "Joking," "Friendly," and "Forceful."  Choosing enough of one type over the course of the game will actually change how your character speaks and reacts in general, which is really cool.  This means that if, for example, you were to do two playthroughs as the female protagonist, even though her name and appearance don't change, it still *feels* like you are playing as a different character if you make different dialogue decisions.  Also, other characters will react differently to you based on which of the two protagonists (female elf or male human) you choose.
As for combat, it is quite well-designed and enjoyable enough that I did some grinding just for the heck of it, but don't expect twitch-action/3D character models/etc.: The battles are purely turn-based (see the screenshots for an idea) and can be as deep or as shallow as you'd like, based on the difficulty.  On Hard, you will definitely have to pay attention to party composition and tactics, and there are many status effects and combos you can use (or have used on you).
Difficulty is almost completely determined by whether you choose Easy, Normal, or Hard, and seemed to be very well balanced, without any crazy spikes or seemingly unfair fights.  Easy is a total walk in the park, Normal is fair, and Hard is, well, hard.  Luckily, you can change difficulties on the fly (even mid-battle) if you are finding it too hard or too easy (or you want to get the achievements for beating certain bosses on hard without doing a whole playthrough that way...).
Game length will vary based on your investment in the game (how often you visit camp to speak with party members, how many side quests you complete, etc.) and how quickly/carefully you read the dialogue, but if I had to slap a number on it, I'd say 15-20 hours for a first playthrough on Normal difficulty.
In conclusion, I would happily recommend this, especially to fans of turn-based RPGs and/or visual novels.  Also, if you have played and liked other Winter Wolves games, I believe this to be one of their best (perhaps THE best), so you should go ahead and pick this up!

It is a short game, but it is a hassle trying to make it to the end in one sitting. I hope that are able to fix that in subsequent updates.

As it stands, this review is marked as a recommendation, but only because I can't bring myself to downvote something that is so near and dear to my heart. RWBY means a lot to me, and that means I've got a bias towards it. I'll try to get past that for the sake of the review.
Grimm Eclipse, as it stands, is half baked. Sure, you could play it, but for $27.99 CAD (20% off RT? Really?), the game just doesn't have enough _real_ content as of this point in time. The story is interesting, but is crammed into 10 very short, very linear levels, and while it can be difficult, it's not that hard. Horde mode is coming in a free update at some point in October, along with DLC Team JNPR, but considering that many of the levels in the campaign already end with a wave based defend the objective goal, fighting endless waves of Grimm and protecting a objective doesn't exactly inspire excitement in me. And as for the Team JNPR DLC, it might as well be character skins and voices. No JNPR specific storyline, no additional content (at least, none announced at this time), just Jaune, Nora, Pyrrha and Ren.
Going back to the subject of combat, it's woefully inadequate for what the game hopes to be. I've never played a Dynasty Warriors game, but I've seen them, and from what I've seen, most games of that genre tend to have all your moves be good for crowd control, not just one. Those games also tend to be very mechanic heavy. Grimm Eclipse is very light.
Grimm Eclipse was rushed out the door to satisfy a increasingly restless fanbase, the same fanbase which proceeded to blame RT Games for rushing it. Honestly, I'm hopeful that support for the game will continue and eventually we will see it updated to better represent the RWBY name.

“Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons” is an indie puzzle storytelling game done right. It showed us, that how immensely powerful a video game can be, when its game-play and story complements each other so perfectly.
The world is detailed, charming and vibrant, and despite its story being only 3-4 hours long, it takes you through a multitude of environments, every chapter feels fresh, compelling and interesting, and filled with mini side-quests that reward you with achievements and extra contents.
The controls for “Brothers” is pretty unique, you simultaneously control two individual characters to solve interesting, varied puzzles in order to progress through the level, on a quest to search for the water of life to save their father. The puzzles themselves are well thought out and doesn’t outstay its welcome, and despite having strange control scheme, I can safely say it works extremely well a Controller and I personally had no problems with it whatsoever.
The story is what makes Brothers so brilliant, it immerses you into the world almost immediately, during my short but wonderful play-though I've experienced happiness, fear, wanderlust, compassion and profound sadness. I really think that no other means of media can really replicate such a mesmerising experience, it successfully told me a coherent, fulfilling and mature story without the characters saying single word, but solely relies on pure interactive game-play.
“Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons” is incredible, and a game that you don’t want to miss, I had a truly unforgettable experience and I think you will too. Don’t watch a game-play video on the internet, but experience this little gem yourself, you will not regret it.

BAD:
The only problem I have with Kingdoms of Amalur is that you can't level up past level 40, so you can't max out your character's skills, even with trainers and skill books available. That's massively disappointing. You can, however, approach a "fateweaver" and change your current skills if you want to try being good at lockpicking instead of potion making. That's interesting, but I'm still pretty bummed that I can't advance my character any further. A big incentive to complete quests is that you get huge xp bonuses for finishing something, and that incentive is lost without any more leveling up :(
That flaw doesn't completely counter the fact that this is an excellent game. I don't know if I'll keep playing it without the xp incentive, but up to this point I have been as drawn in to Kingdoms of Amalur as I was into Skyrim and Oblivion.

I feel mislead getting this game based on the very positive reviews.
The game is not very good. Average at best. Its greatest failure is actually its best selling point. If you like MMOs which this game was obviously supposed to be - you might like it. Otherwise, there are better choices out there - Dragon's Dogma: Dark Arisen and Guild Wars 2 are two that come to mind as they came out in the same year (2012).
The most frustrating things that made me stop playing:
- Gear: once I discovered crafting, there was no reason to equip any unique item I found as crafting was brokenly overpowered. It's a shame because the unique items look really cool, but I was forced into the trade off of looking cool or having better stats.  Poorly designed system.
- Difficulty: played on Hard and it was still too easy.
- Combat:  mostly liked the combat skills, but overall the combat is lackluster. Auto seeking spells and enemy special attacks that are frustrating to dodge -- my experience was just getting overpowered skills/items and mashing two buttons without any real thought or positioning involved.
- World: quantity over quality. Yes, it's big - too big. Although the environment is beautiful, I don't remember any of the NPCs. The monsters are repetetive. Hundreds of quests which are all repetetive.
- Story: poorly presented, poor dialogue options. Was compelled to skip most of it.
This was a good attempt at a new franchice that never got anywhere as there's no ETA for part 2 of this game, so this is all we have. And it's not that good...
