Trine 2 manages to have everything I loved about the original, but vastly improves everything as well, which is what any good sequel should do. The story, the humor, the visuals. Everything is even better than it already was.
Trine 2 is a fantasy platformer, with three interchangeable characters that can complete different tasks; Amadeus, the Wizard, Zoya, the Thief, and Pontius, the Knight. You can play solo or Co-Op with up to three people.
The game certainly lives up to it's title as a "Complete Story." the story is so fantastic I can't really talk about it, I might spoil something.
The other thing I really want to talk about is the environments. This is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. Every few minutes I found myself stopping to look at everything in the background. The environments reminded me a lot of that "Wizard of Oz" prequel that came out this past year, "Oz the Great and Powerful." They're all so colorful and vivid even on the lowest settings. And I think that's the highlight of this game. I'm usually not one to completely praise visuals over everything else, but Trine's visuals are the best thing about it.
Also take this recommendation of Trine 2 as a recommendation for the original as well. I'd write one, but Tine 2 improved so much I'd probably just end up repeating myself.
This is in the top ten best platformers I've ever played, right up there with games like Cave Story, LIMBO, and the Original Mario Bros. And I suggest you see for yourself what make's these games so good and buy them ASAP. You won't be disappointed.

Mankind Divided is, on the whole, a much better game than Human Revolution. The plot and themes come together in a way that works better with the story of the first Deus Ex, and there's a lot of foreshadowing and setup for it in Mankind Divided - which Human Revolution sorely lacked. You get the feeling of a world that's in a state of total disarray and 10 minutes away from the apocalypse - it really feels like dystopian cyberpunk done right.
The gameplay is much, much better and feels like the best possible rendition of Deus Ex-style gameplay today. It gives you a greater amount of choice in all respects, and there's much more freedom in what kind of person you want Jensen to be. There's also a remarkable amount of variety and some truly amazing moments in the side-quests on offer. And the main quest does a great job of building up a mystery and putting you through some intense beats.
However, the game is much, much too short and the ending is also very disappointing. It seems as if the game was cut into several parts, what we got was more or less half of it; and we'll only get the rest of the story in DLC, which is something that I didn't expect to see from a Deus Ex game. Along with an in-game microtransaction store and single-use pre-order items, and you can start to see Square Enix jeopardizing the franchise's future for short-term monetary gain. Not good at all.
However, Mankind Divided remains a terrific game and a solid new outing in the DX franchise. I really do recommend it, but as much as I want to, I also think it's important for us to vote with our wallets. Don't use the microtransaction store and don't reward Square Enix for chopping up the game into pieces and selling it to us again, later - don't buy any kind of DLC. It's the only way to punish this kind of publisher behavior.

Good Stuff:
Basically builds upon Human Revolution in every way. The combat is improved with better balanced weapons and weapon mods and ammo types. Side quests are more varied and open with entire branches avaliable that can be missed if you don't take the right choices. Augs have a new energy system that takes a fixed ammount for each activation and then lets the rest regenerate meaning you don't spend the whole game on one power cell and the new augs themselves are quite fun. Hacking has been made more varied with extra obsticles and complications along with new software. The single hub in the game is much more detailed and fleshed out than Detroit or Hengsha in Human Revolution. The level design overall is as good as ever. The social element has been expanded and there are more opertunities to handle things through dialogue.
Bad Stuff:
This is a glitchy port. Nothing gamebreaking but it did freeze and crash a couple of times for no apparent reason. There is this one loading screen in the hub that takes forever (I mean minutes) to complete. The story ends abruptly when it feels like its about halfway through. The animations look kinda silly sometimes in dialogue. There are microtransactions but there is already too much om the way of credits and praxis. The game ran well on high settings on my GTX 960 with an i3 (beyond a couple of the freezes and stutters just after loading) but of course that doesn't mean you will have the same experience.
Overall:
The bulk of the game is in the side quests and exploration whilst the gameplay is top notch. I wish Eidos had made a bit more but there is enough content you will miss on your first playthrough that you can easily replay for a new experience and the new game + helps out too. I really enjoyed this game and it will still take you a solid 30 hours to experience most of the content.

THE Rock game. Mechanics-wise, it's basically hack-and-slash in a semi-open world that you can explore in your car, together with RTS matches. The voice-acting, story and aesthetics are the real high-light. I also thoroughly enjoyed cruising around, picking up collectibles, while listening to an awesome Metal Rock soundtrack. The attention to detail is amazing.
The devs thought of everything -- there's even the option to make the game kid-friendly by turning off violence and swearing.
On the downside, the multiplayer is pretty much dead. You can still play solo against bots -- otherwise, your best bet is to find a friend who'll play it with you.
The multiplayer is only the RTS segment. The RTS mechanics are pretty good (at any rate, I enjoyed these matches, even though I'm not a big fan of RTS in general). They blur the line with hack-and-slash, because at any point during the match you can swoop down and fight hand-to-hand.
Some reviewers mention technical difficulties because of the port -- I haven't come across any, personally.
Playing time is moderate (I finished the campaign and found all collectibles in about 21 hours) when you consider the fact that this game was meant to focus on multiplayer to begin with. Due to marketing shenanigans, it was unfairly passed off as primarily single-player.

Wow! I never thought I'd play a game worse than my prior-worst, but Tim Schafer set out to prove me wrong! Let's start with some objective facts about my time in this game (for some reason it's not counting what I did a few years ago, but whatever):
15-30FPS animations with 60-90FPS gameplay makes it look choppy and cheap (not to mention the obscene amounts of clipping).
Doing 3-5 genres and mashing them together does not work well when it's your first time doing most of them.
Now for an actual review. The game starts off nice enough, being basically what amounts to a poor man's hack and slash with a metal-rock theme. Neat, right? It kind of drags on though, and never gets beyond the mediocre/bland range. Then some driving elements are introduced, which are okay, but in fairness it's SUPER hard to screw this up (but they kind of do given how limited you are in driving), and th-wait. What. Things were almost getting interesting, what's this "stage" and "fan" resource cra-
If you thought hack and slash wasn't enough, here's some RTS to get jammed down your throat, idiot! Bad RTS, at that. Imagine having to manually move around the map (at high speed, in fairness) to select a combat point, then go to your damn units manually and tell them to go there, then fly back to join in the fight yourself! "Wow!" you're probably saying, "That sounds like complete garbage!" You would be right.
Except you don't have to imagine it, it's right here in this game. Go nuts, friends - it's offered free so often for a reason. It has Jack Black and some other voices I guess but that's like trying to sell you a turd sandwich because it has a sticker on it. I'm tired of giving Doublefine/Schafer repeated chances, at this point I'm realizing (after having played *many* of their games) they were a one-hit-wonder with Psychonauts.
I've done 3 stage battles (read: RTS components) and I'm done. It's just too damn boring. They wait until you're at the RTS parts before you can even start buying weapon/character upgrades for some idiotic reason, and that's at the point where they have the least impact since your units will be doing a majority of the fighting! I just struggle to find anything good to say about this game, but I'm tired of trying. There are a bajillion better games on Steam to spend your money (and more importantly, time) on, so ignore this steaming pile of crap and move on.

Is RWBY: Grimm Eclipse the best game ever? No.
Does it have the best story and graphics? Not really.
But is it fun to play? Definitely.
I see a lot of reviews slamming this game for what it isn't, and while I do agree with some of the points risen, I like to commend games for what they are. So without further ado, let's get this review started.
Pros:
>It's a great stress reliever and great to play casually.
>While some of the animation is wonky, the fighting animation is beautiful and fluid.
>Great multiplayer with a great community of players.
>Ranking challenges are a lot of fun.
>Different fighting styles with every character, so you get a chance to find one that's right for you.
Cons:
>The story is a bit rushed and the dialogue is long and unskippable.
>Single player is punishing and it isn't possible to get all challenges/achievements when playing alone.
>Ranking has no special perks except bragging rights.
>Once you hit the final rank, there's not much left to motivate you through the game other than playing with your friends.
>The final boss fight is long and tedious. God help solo players on this one.
Things that would be interesting to see:
>Perks for ranking up. Maybe, every rank or so, you gain an extra skill point or your attacks are stronger.
>PvP - Vytal Festival style. While fighting side by side with my friends is fun, kicking their butts would be pretty fun too, I think.
>An option to skip cutscenes and/or dialogue.
>Other teams once JNPR is out. (Crossing my fingers for Team SSSN and the villains.)

I am not a fighting game person. But they've always kinda sorta interested me... not necessarily from a competitive angle (though fighting games can be fun to watch), but from a "this is probably a fun, satisfying, and fast way to spend some time" angle.
Unfortunately, I've always found them to be INTIMIDATING AS HELL, especially when your only real exposure to them is through watching the competitive scene. The idea of playing a fighting game is great (to me, a Casual), right up until the point people start talking about counting frames of animation. It's a scary experience for someone who -didn't- grow up on games like Street Fighter or Mortal Kombat (both were definitely around when I was a kid, but my circle of friends were way more likely to play platformers like Super Mario World or shooters like UN Squadron).
Based pretty much solely on really fantastic word-of-mouth from some reviewers I really trust, I've been looking at getting Tekken 7 for awhile now, and approaching it as a fun fighting game to chill out with on the couch, one that is capable of being approached casually as well as competitively. Thanks to the Steam winter sale, 50% off sounded just right, and I wouldn't be out much if I bounced off it.
This game owns. It's gorgeous, the fighting -feels- good, and the overall polish just makes the game downright satisfying to play. I've had a good experience with online multiplayer so far and have never really felt overwhelmed with it, I guess because the matchmaking algorithm is good. There are a wide array of characters to choose from, from super simple characters that offer a great way to learn the game, to super-complex ones with well over a hundred entries in their move lists.
The single-player content is fantastic as well, and I've had a stupid amount of fun just chilling out doing Treasure Mode (which is how you unlock cosmetic items, of which there are tons) when I don't feel like playing multiplayer. I've played a couple characters and feel like I'm developing a more intuitive feel of the one I chose to focus on (Lars, based on online recommendations). While I still feel like a complete button-mashing newb, I also feel more and more like I'm actually learning how to understand fighting games.
tl;dr: game is beautiful, extremely fun, even when you have no idea what you're doing. It's approachable enough that even a drunk button-masher can have a blast.

Gameplay - This game has pretty different gameplay than most other RPG. You can chose to be a mage/knight/assassin or all 3 together. These are not ingame choices, just my own gameplay experience. There's lot of different class weapons and they don't really strict you to play 1 class at a time. You can chose whatever weapons you want in both of your weapon slots. Good amount of magic casting. The game is also pretty hard since the NPC are not braindead and using same technique will get you nowhere. I like this kind of gameplay. Of course i could not summary nearly half of the gameplay mechanics this game offers but i tell you there's alot!
Graphics - Considering it's a 2012 game, pretty decent graphics.
Controls - Controls are not clunky and easy to access. Really easy and straight forward actually.
Optimization - It's perfect you could say.
World Design - It's really good.
Overall - 9/10 from me.

I bought Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning Collection when it was on sale for, like, 7,99 or something. That must be the best bargain in my entire life so far, because after playing the game for almost 50 hours I think it would've been worth the full price. And I haven't even gotten to play either of the DLC's. This game has a lot of content to offer.
It's not perfect, though. Hardly any game is, but in my opinion it has so much good in it that the major bad things don't feel as annoying as they could. The worst thing this game does is the constant crashing on Windows 10. I experienced this too, but for me doing
and stopping TabletInputService in Task Manager's Services tab solved the problem entirely.
This is one of the games where I actually enjoyed the combat and felt like it was truly fun. It's a combination of hitting, blocking and dodging. Nothing groundbreaking but it's fun and fluid nonetheless. And the finishing moves. Oh, the finishing moves. They're epic.
The class system allows you a lot of diversity and customisation options. You can be a 100% mighty warrior, or become a magic wielding assassin or anything in between. With every level up you get points to spend in Might/Finesse/Sorcery abilities. You can invest everything in one of the three or become a jack of all trades. The best thing is that you can even change your class entirely within one game, you just have to pay a moderate amount of game money but it's still an option if you want to try something else.
This game has a really captivating story, loads of lore and a vibrant world full of things to explore. All the NPC's are voice acted and the map is pretty big. For anyone who likes fantasy, this game is a treasure.
The quests are really fun most of the time, and it's not always the same repetitive 'kill that, get this' cycle many RPG's have, although this game has a bit of that, too, but it's not everything the quests have to offer. Again, the amount of content is huge. There are loads of sidequests, faction-based quests and tasks to do as well as the story quests.
In my opinion, the world of KOA:R is really nice looking, and even though the game is from 2012 the graphics look decent due to them leaning more towards cartoony style, which some people love and some don't like that much. The game can look really impressive in places, but there's nothing we haven't already seen. The downside to the graphics is probably the fact that escpecially the dungeons look really similar to each other. There's not that much unique dungeons or buildings after you've played through a few regions, and the same sprites and layouts are used in so many places.
The crashes (potentially caused by the game's incompatibility with Windows 10?) are the major con this game has. The game crashes randomly after 10-20 minutes of gameplay, which can be a real nuisance. I wrote about what fixed this for me at the start of this review, so if you're struggling with this I recommend trying those out. The crashes happened to me in the demo as well, so I recommend trying to get the demo work without crashing before buying.
The camera can really screw you over in combat. You kind of get used to the weird angles and other stuff after playing a while, but at first it might feel really weird.
If you do each and every of the side quests you might end up leveling too fast and then when doing some quests the foes there aren't on your level. This has happened to me a few times, but I don't find it that annoying, just a bit inconvenient.
If I had to rate this game, I'd give it a 9/10. Definitely worth it, especially if you enjoy RPG games.

This is a game that suprised and well surpassed my expectations.
I know when I saw the name I was sceptical but it actually unfolds really well.  The best thing about it is it has the best parts of an RPG- namely a good story, interesting, well-written characters, and a decent combat mechanic system.  What Winterwolves does particularly well is that this style of gaming with the Ren’Py engine does away with the ‘fluff’ or sometimes superfluous content developers put in to artificially extend the playtime.  Forget wandering around town talking to every NPC or pixel hunting to find quest items, you can fast travel town to town and quests are plot driven.  You can even fast forward bits of story you’ve seen if you don’t want to waste time.  Every minute you play you are doing what you want to do rather than what the game forces you to waste time doing.  You will end up spending the majority of the time unfolding the story, battling and interacting with your characters.
Dialogue choices are somewhat fixed and not customising in that aspect (think Dragon age 2) but it was a sufficient mechanic to drive the story forward.  You will end up making gameplay decisions throughout the game that does impact the world state.  The story may share some similarities and tones to Dragon Age: Origins but still a pleasure to watch unfold.  Combat is very similar to Monster’s Den flash game series and does have an engaging tactical element.  There are 3 main classes (warrior, rogue, mage) with each character having one class skill tree and one unique character skill tree.  Light grinding is all you need to get through the story and difficulty options allow you to focus more on story aspects.  For those who like to grind and get the best gear the option is there but it’s not necessary.  You will end up recruiting and adventuring with a party of 10 characters (DLC introduces 2 more) so there are many combos and customisations you can play with.
The character sprites and visuals are beautiful to look at and despite the simplicity actually works well in creating a convincing setting for the story and there is optional fan service mode.  Sure, there can be a few more backgrounds but this game is a great example of creativity when less is more.  The romance CGs and interactions are fun and rewarding to unlock.  There are multiple racial/gender romance options for each character and I applaud the writer for putting all those in, and for the meaningful character progression gained through these interactions.  Each party NPC will also have a rewarding personal quest.
To accompany the visuals I must mention the lush score that accompanies the game.  The soundtrack is excellent and I never tire of hearing the themes.  The dramatic and emotional moments are particularly heightened with good use of tracks.
My minor critiques are with the player dialogue choices- I’d rather see the 3 options than joking/friendly/optional and they don’t really feel very different.  The romances and triangles are handled well but I’d like a tiny bit more climax and epilogue detail.  Would have liked to see a few more side quests and story elements from the towns and map locations based on renown.  Combat wise it’s a great system but the class skill trees pales in comparison with unique skill trees and perhaps the different weapon types could add different effects (eg difference between single/dual/2H weapon) in terms of range, AoE and damage.
Overall well worth the experience.  My first playthrough was a leisurely 15 hours and there’s room for at least another playthrough plus exploring the romances.

Honest review time!
Pros:
- beautiful graphics
- good story (not great, but definitely more in depth than Fallout 4 for example)
- Black budget augments ffs!
- Wide variety of missions
- Pays homage to Human Revolution
Cons:
- not open world
- microtransactions in a single-player game
- MSAA is broken
Really, that is it. No, I did not mention the Day 1 consumable pre-order bonus issue, because it isn't an issue. So what, we got a consumable as a pre-order bonus. Everything else isn't single-use, and why should we get an eternal bonus in the game just because we gave our money solely on faith? I think we already got enough for pre-ordering
There isn't really anything wrong the games optimization. This game is a "bar-raising" game. This means it's trying to break ground for the next generation of games visually, which is why a lot of us are having problems running the game with high graphics settings. The games looks amazing even on Medium, so I really don't see what the issue is.
I am currently attaining and mostly maintaining 60fps on Ultra (no MSAA) with dips as low as 50fps with these specs:
AMD FX 8350 Black Edition (Stock clock)
ASUS M5A99X EVO R2.0 Motherboard
8GB HyperX DDR3 1866MHz RAM
XFX RX480 8GB Black Edition O/C'ed to 1328MHz
2TB Seagate 5400rpm HD (yes, it's running on my crappy HD, not my SSD)
The games runs beautifully, and is a dream to watch. The pre-rendered cutscenes actually ruin the immersion for me, as there are noticable artifacts, as well as a quite low render resolution of the video.
tl;dr: It's a great game, despite microtransactions as cheats, and the broken MSAA. If you're a fan of Human Revolution, this is a must. If you just HAVE to max out every value for the best visuals, perhaps you should pass, as this is making most high end systems cry.

For the purpose of clarity let me state at the outset: This is a review of the game ONLY. DLC crap, pre-order ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, microtransaction malarky... All terrible, but not a part of this review. You can make your own decisions on how to feel about that, and whether or not you should purchase the game.
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is the next game in the storied Deus Ex franchise, revived in 2011 by Eidos Montral (here for their second round) with the superb Human Revolution. I loved HR then and I love Mankind Divided now. Essentially this game is a refinement of their freshmen effort 5 years ago and it is a great follow-up overall. I will break things down into the parts I thought were excellent, good, meh and bad to help anyone reading this decide what parts of the game they'd like to focus on.
Excellent:
-The stealth gameplay. This part of the game is phenomenal, and Mankind Divided in my opinion stands amongst the greats. Thief 2, Metal Gear Solid 3, Chaos Theory, VtM... The best of the best, MD stands next to them proudly with a more refined version of the already great stealth gameplay in HR. Enemies are much more clever, their routes tend to be more randomised, they can see and hear now like almost normal people and there are a variety in enemy types that can bring some unexpected challenge (there are some who are just as kitted out as you!)
Good:
-Side missions and the writing in general. There are many solid missions here that help flesh out the world of Deus Ex and Prague in specific. Many of them deal with augmentation in some way similar to HR, but it makes sense in context and there is enough regular human drama intermingled to give the people in the story real depth. I definitely enjoyed this more than the main story. Each mission has several branch points as well for how you want to handle it, generally rewarding more thoughtful and thorough players rather than those who just bee-line to objective markers.
Meh:
-The main story. For the first 3/4ths of the game I was really excited about where things in the story might go and how threads could be followed through various "chapters" in the game but ultimately most of it didn't pay off. It serves only as a solid opening chapter, but I will disagree with the many reviews saying that the story felt brokenly incomplete. There was a main villain, organization and pointed threat which are resolved by the end of the game. This being a Deus Ex game of course there is a vast reaching conspiracy going on that isn't really broken open similar to the first game, but it is plainly setting up for a sequel. Know what you're getting in to here and you won't be too disappointed.
Bad:
-Animations and faces. I'm not really a graphics guy (I won't talk about them in this review, I just don't really care) but the animation quality for conversations here just isn't up to par. There are several impactful moments in the game emotionally and the facial expressions and acting just weren't up to snuff. Only a handful of times do I think it hit the mark.
N/A:
-Combat. I only did one playthrough of the game on Give Me Deus Ex + No Alarms + No kills. I didn't get a chance to try out the updated combat system so I can't really comment on it.
Wrapping up:
A truly excellent stealth game and a good, yet not as revolutionary follow-up to Human Revolution. For any fan of the series though or stealth fans in general, I heartily recommend this game, even at full price. The world is excellently built and there are numerous engaging stories and characters to be found within it, and with a superb gameplay foundation to keep the minute-to-minute action enthralling.

I have played all deus ex games, so I think I am a big fun of the franchise.
Overall Rating (max 10)
Graphics : 9
Gameplay: 10
Story: 6.5
Sales team attitude: 2
Music: 6
Should you buy?
If you are a fun of the franchise, the answer is yes.
Otherwise, wait for a month, for the game to get polished.
Graphics
The graphic are really good, no complains. They have not discouraged me from playing the game. The augmentations look very realistic to me. They are definitely inspired for real life prosthetics.
Gameplay
The gameplay is amazing!!!. If you like sneaking your way through, taking down every enemy silently without being seen, hacking every terminal, computer and device you can find, then you are going to love the game!!! It is amazing how much time the developers have made to build every map. There were times, that i felt like there were 5 different ways to get to the final destination. The game encourages you to play in sneak mode and explore, but even if it did not, I would still do it. It really cool how many secret passages there are. And the best part is that you have to discover them. The sneak gameplay is the most complete I have ever seen in all games.
If you like shooting stuff and going fast through maps, then this is not the wrong game for you. This game needs the attitude of the explorer and the patience of a master thief.
Microtransactions.
I understand, why people are getting so frustrated about them, so was I, in the beginning, but the developers have not build the game with them in mind. To me it feels like a trap, setup by the sales team,  for users, who are not patient to play the game. In other words, they are a "legal cheat". You can always use the cheat, but you don't have to. I have spent like 25 hours in the game, I think I am about the middle of the game, and i have so many augmentations that sometimes I wished that the developers did not make the game so easy.
Story.
I think the story definitely needs some improvements. The problem is that it feels that we know the conspirators from the beginning. There is no suspense. It would have been much better if we discovered them gradually.
Bugs:
The original game was shipped with bugs, some of them were even affecting the gameplay. The first two patches fix some of them, thus making the gameplay smoother. It is not the first time I see it. The same thing happened with Witcher. For example the current version of the game is way better than the original one.
Music:
The music is good in general. The only annoying part is Elisa Cassan, the reporter. I mean she is everywhere, it is annoying some times. I don't know If that was on purpose, to show that she is part of the corrupted media, but I definitely want to kill her.
Going back to the roots.
As a conclusion I would like to emphasize on the developers effort to connect this game with the first deus ex game. That happens in all domains, i.e. the plot, the gameplay (multi-tools are back) and music.

Think Perfect World Entertainment. Think RNG and cash sinks.
And unbalanced PVP, with lag, with queue systems that half the time you spent doing nothing until you get into a session.
Melee in PVP is an absolute (even guaranteed) clusterf@!#. Oftentimes you don't even realized that the guy you're trying to hit may be your ally and that most players are using the same character with the same aesthetics / appearance.
Now we move onto the characters. Players can choose from a wide spectrum of characters each with their own playstyles and equipment restrictions (bar a few characters).
I like this part, but what imagine happens when you pit 2 players together, 1 comes with a sword, a slow firing and weak hitting sniper rifle, a rapid-firing but highly inaccurate after a few shots peashooter and the other a mace, a moderately fast-firing albeit slower a few margins, harder-hitting assault rifle carrying more ammo and a grenade launcher for the Lord's sake. Oh, and all the characters move so sluggish that everybody had to perform 'dashes' (double tap for...you know, dash, a la Megaman double tap dashing). Plus stun-lock melee. Guaranteed you'd stun-lock them to all Oblivion and get stun-locked in turn.
PVE. Close to Hazard Ops-style. But you don't stand a chance going Solo and that PVE balancing is so damn balanced, you'd think you're playing PVP but against dumber-than-dumb AI bots. And OP bosses. OP bosses with 1 hit KOs, x50 health bars and are superior bullet sponges. If you run out of Revival Coins (think coins for arcades, Metal Slug etc), don't expect to continue your session, just drop out in less than a set time or get kicked instead. Or pray your surviving teammates lose and get your exp. There's no option to purchase coins while in-game either and you can only get coins by purchasing them via microtransactions or daily log-in rewards. (You don't get them everyday.)
Market. I don't even know why'd they bother with the in-game currency (gold, currency farmed by playing and not real cash). Almost all the items of the same category cost the same. And very rarely those weapons are better compared to the rest. Gives off a sense of variety but you'd probably be disappointed, I know I am.
And let's talk about the lottery system. Players are probably better off with the market instead of this because most of the time you'd get a random timed item that may or may not help you at all which most of the time you'd get a timed version of an item readily available in the market. And you waste your hard-earned crystals and ores.
But if you're lucky, you'd get some of the mostly-coined 'privileged items'. Some looked pretty good, while some just plain look dumb. They even have a black / purple version of Captain America's mask-suit combo.
Graphics. They're okay but just so-so. They focus more on character details and lesser on the maps / background objects etc. Expect obvious mesh clippings, though.
Animations. While they, without doubt, look good, it is only so much good they could do. Animations are slow, ragdoll physics are sub-par, and check those legs out when they gun n' run, they even keep their backs straight up 90 degrees as if they're standing at attention.
Music. They're good, but I get the feeling that they lack drive or motivation. Like most of the time they don't even fit the theme or the situation players are in.
Voice acting. Honestly, I was shocked. They're pretty damn good when it comes to NPC dialogues in Campaign. Sadly, voice acting only kicks in in boss fights (towards the best of my knowledge). Player characters' voice acting? Some are okay, some just sound strained with shoddily imitated accents (Elena with the assault rifles and the noobtube). Not all of the characters speak the same language though. Some spoke English, some spoke Korean.
It lags in PVP, but not so in PVE because PVP groups you randomly with players from neighboring countries or globally. And when it lags, you gonna get wrecked. Stun-locks or group stun-locking, getting sniped off or riddled with bullets while downed. (Yes, you can shoot people doubled over to death and is highly encouraged. Apparently, people losing their footing is a close to sure fire way to donate points to the enemy team). And I think the only way to prevent that is to level up and get that level-specific skill to which that has escaped my mind.
Doesn't matter much, expect things to go wrong even when you've done it right.

Player matchmaking in PVP. Aside from the notoriously, infamously 'queue' queuing system, you'd think they done good with the matchmaking. Nope. I played this game a while back when it was just starting out as a Facebook game, poorly translated and still developing. And even at that point in the beginning, it still had WAY more features in it than this Steam version does. And as I watched it develop, it gained even more features, and became truly interesting, one of my favourite apps.
I haven't played in a while, haven't even hopped back over to Facebook to check if it's still there, but regardless when I saw it was on Steam I downloaded it immediately. Even though I was super confused about the reviews talking about how simple and one-dimensional it is, I had tons of fun before and I am greatly looking forward to seeing what they do on Steam.
So I'm saying this now: don't write this game off as mindless and boring until after they finish bringing in the rest of the features, which I'm sure they will. Right now all you can do is hop on different dragons and go shoot people out of the sky, with almost literally nothing else to change or improve how you do so, but with the full set of features it's a wonderful game with many complexities.
It's no more mindless and repetitive than any other multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) game out there, and since Call of Duty is now a hugely popular series, I'm going to assume that a fair number of people don't find fighting for supremacy and honing your skills and equipment set to suit your strategy for blasting your enemies out of existence to be boring.
Different dragons, different stats, right? You wanna tank, you go ogre. You wanna zip around like NAH NAH NAH NAH CAN'T TOUCH THIS, you go manta. But the equipment, that could all be upgraded, and the stats further specialized. A point to winning and leveling beyond unlocking more dragons. Making enough gold to buy the coolest stuff, getting skins for different looks (leopard spotted Inara, oooh exotic!)
Visually, if you wanted to improve the cooling system for your guns (so you can shoot continuously for longer without your guns overheating and going into cooldown), there would be actual cooling pipes appearing on your dragon's saddle. Need more defence to take less damage? Armour pieces for various parts of your dragon. In the later stages of development that I was still playing during, stat upgrades had visual effects on the look of your dragon, which was so cool in my opinion.
And it really helped that you could focus on the stats that were important to you. I'm more of a CLICK WILDLY AND HOPE SHOTS HIT WHILE FLYING WILDLY AWAY IF SHOT AT kinda player, so I upgraded my shot accuracy (so the cluster of shots is tighter--at base accuracy, shooting at one space would have multiple shots hitting random areas in a cluster, so unless you were right up in another dragon's face you couldn't guaruntee shots would hit exactly where you aimed them, unless you upgraded your accuracy) and my cooling systems, and left my defense and actual firepower to later.
Right now, as a level 3 I saw a level 16 and said "meh, they probably won't crash into the ground by accident, let's go shoot them in the face". With full features, a player with a level that much higher than you is cause to go running for your buddies, because the chances of you taking him down alone are next to nil. Which, yenno, is as it should be in games.
Other features I immediately noticed this Steam version doesn't have yet:
Collision. In the FB version, colliding with another dragon results in both of you dying. You don't get credit for the kill, either, but neither do you get penalized for suicide. Made a game of chicken a bit riskier.
Also, healing spawn points. First few games I went, did my blitz thing, dashed back to spawn almost dead, and then sat there in the light like WHY AM I NOT HEALING WHAT IS HAPPENING HERE?! I don't know if that was a conscious decision by the developers to prevent strategies like mine (though the excitement of a race to spawn point--will the one team shoot down the injured enemy before they get within the safety of the spawn drones?! COVER ME GUYS CAN'T YOU SEE I'M NEARLY DEAD GET YOUR TAILS OVER HERE AND COVER ME-- was always very exciting, especially on the bigger maps) or if they just haven't implemented it yet.
Honestly the only thing the Steam version has right now that I don't remember from the FB version is the different battle modes. I only rememember team vs team and free-for-all. These other modes are neat.
So my final word to you guys: seriously wait to make a final judgement. If you find yourself going "this game was fun at first but after a bit..." stop yourself there, because you've tasted what the game is about... now be patient and wait for the rest of it. IMO, it'll be worth it.

Loren is a fun combination of fantasy RPG and visual novel. The story is well-written and your choices truly influence your experience of the story! This is hands down the best visual novel I've ever played.
I enjoyed it so much the first time on easy mode, playing as the elf female, that I decided on a second playthrough (despite having 100+ other games in my Steam library). Now I'm playing on hard difficulty mode as the human male, making different choices than before, and while the overall story arc is the same, the events and viewpoint are completely different than my first playthrough. And it's such a joy because I didn't know that there was this whole other layer to the game's story until I started playing the second time.
The turn-based combat is enjoyable as well. The battles are way easy on easy mode, and appropriately anxiety-inducing in hard mode. There's lots of cool skills and spells you can learn as you level up.
The conversations at the camp with your party members are interesting and can lead to romance if you make the right choices in dialogue. Gay and lesbian relationships are possible. And having no romance is possible.
Graphics, music, sound effects, gameplay mechanics, are all fine.
I highly recommend Loren for lovers of RPGs and visual novels.

Ladies and gentlemen, I think I have found the most racist game of all time.
Not saying it insults real life races, I mean pretty much everyone in this discriminates against someone. Humans hate elves, elves hate humans and elves that have a slightly blue tint to their skin color, amazons hate everyone who isn't them and female, and dwarves...are actually kinda chill. The fact that out of every 10 people you meet 9 of them are racist is incredibly annoying. I know there's discrimination in real life but I don't really like discrimination in real life, it's annoying out here and it's annoying in the game. Honestly, I wouldn't mind except this seems to be all it tackles (well, this and sexism if you play as a male). Come on, there's a ton of issues out there to address. There's slavery in this game, why don't we deal with that? Morality vs effeciency? Or democracy vs feudalism? Or religion vs skepticism? Or order vs free spirit? Seriously, there's so many things you can use (and a lot of them are a lot less stupid than racism and sexism. This is a bit personal but these two topic really annoy me because of how there is pretty much no basis for either of them, I prefer social issues that are actually morally conflicting).
Combat is repetitive on easy, draws on too long on normal, and is impossible on hard. I found myself switching to easy when random encounters lasted 20 minuets, and switching back to normal when every fight consisted of spam special attack. Either I just suck or there really needs to be an easy-ish mode, more transition between the two.
And the outfits...please, please fix the outfits. We're supposed to be playing as heroes, not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. This argument is rather self explanatory, really.
Alright, now that I've made this game sound absolutely horrible, let me explain why I gave it an thumbs up vote.
First off, there's real consequences to choice. I started two playthroughs (that I never finished because of life), once as a grim human male who was duty first pleasure never, and another as a joking elf lady who used her freegoing words to manipulate others into getting her way. This alone created two almost completely different playthroughs (though it mostly just determined who was racist against me), choosing one over the other opens and closes a ton of doors. I found some choices made during the game created two completely different journeys. Most big budget games don't pull this off.
The dialog is also really great. I noticed this more in my sassy elf than my mideval batman playthough, but the words flow really well and can go from being funnier than most comedies nowadays to really dark tragedies, sometimes it feels kinda bipolar but when it works it works.
Finally, the premise. Make no mistake, this isn't your story. You play an important part, but this is not your story. You are not the main charecter, you are the main charecter's bodyguard. You make sure they can do their main charecter thing but you are not the focus. I LOVE this premise and wish there were more games with it in mind. In this, execution is sloppy at times but overall it does really well making you understand your roll. Lots of people may be turned off by this, even I who love the concept was a bit jealous when Loren picked up the glowing sword, but for me this is a great concept that I'm glad someone took up.
I wouldn't reccomend buying this at full price, but when it's on sale you are obligated to get it out of self-interest. I hope the creater makes more games like this, maybe with a more refined combat system, less sexualization, and more variety in the social issues it tackles.

This game quickly became one of my Top 5 Favorite Games on Steam. It's a JRPG-style game from an non-Japanese indie game company named Winter Wolves. This company is mostly known for dating sims and visual novels, but honestly, I think this game is their best yet. (Although, to be fair, I haven't played all their games yet.)
Important note: The DLC is a MUST HAVE. Honestly, the story would seem very incomplete without it, so if you get this game, get the DLC. This review is also based on having it.
While this is definitely a RPG, the fact that a lot of their games are visual novels definitely shows in the design. There is zero action in the turn-based battles. In fact, they rely solely on pictures to represent what takes place in the battle. For a lot of people, this is a flaw, but for me, I was indifferent to this type of gameplay. What was important was that the game was fun to play.
It took me roughly 20 or so hours to get through the game the first time. This is considered short for a RPG, but it has potential for several playthroughs. Personally, I went through 13 playthroughs, going for all the achievements. It can get a bit repetitive going through the game that many times, but thankfully, the creators realized this; there is a cheat mode that enables "story mode" in which the player automatically wins every battle, which can get you through the game much quicker. Obviously, the game is story-driven, which is a big highlight to me. The story is definitely influenced by Lord of the Rings. I can't blame for that, LotR is awesome. However, there are a couple of races that do not exist in the LotR world that exist in this game. Another 1-up this game has is that there's an even distribution of gender between the characters, unlike the sausagefest that is LotR.
There is a bit of a dating sim element to this game, but you can actually get through the game without romancing anyone (in fact, there's an achievement for that). There are several people the main character can romance, which is what gives the game the potential for several playthroughs. Each one has its own unique effect on the story.
Kudos to the creators for allowing same-sex coupling, which is a reoccurring thing in the Winter Wolves games.
Sort of spoiler-ish, but not really:
There are also a few different ways to end the game. Ultimately, the Death Knight (main villain) is defeated in each ending, but how you defeat him depends on things you do in the game. I looked up which way is canon out of curiosity, but ultimately, it's up to the player to decide how the Death Knight should meet his "fate." There's also a pretty heavy hint at the end of the game that there will be a sequel.
Flaws:
- There are absolutely no people of color in this game. White people EVERYWHERE; there isn't even a NPC that has a shade or two. And no, blue-skinned dark elves do not count. I mean realistic people of color.
- The game could do without so much sexualization of the characters, particularly the women. It isn't really necessary that they be half-naked, especially when they're supposed to be fighting in a war.
- I found one technical error in the game. In each town/village, there's a shop and a fame score. The player can earn fame by doing tasks for that particular town/village. Well, sometimes, if you go to a shop in a town/village that has no fame score yet, it'll re-direct to a previous shop. For example, while I was playing, I went to the elves' village's shop and it was linking me to the Citadel's shop. However, once I earned some fame in the elves' village, it correctly went to their shop. This error can actually benefit the player, so it isn't a huge deal.
Despite its flaws, I definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes RPGs, especially if they enjoy story-driven games and visual novels / dating sims.

Disclaimer:  This is not a Princess game.  You don't play dressup as a Princess.  You don't marry Princes.  You don't kiss frogs.  Before judging, just read the review and give the game a shot.  Also, don't take my short playtime into account, as Steam was bugged for this for some reason.  I have over 15 hours logged into this game.
Loren the Amazon Princess is a roleplaying game with a strong emphasis on storyline, almost in the form of a "choose your own adventure" novel.  It is backwards narrated in a very unique way, going back and "remembering" this epic story of Loren (the main character), and her companion--the character that YOU play.  In case you're confused, you actually play as the main character's companion, not the main character herself.  A very odd concept, but very refreshing.
Throughout the game, you travel in search of your lost mother, the Queen of the Amazons, and the story unveils itself through the journey.  As you are leaving your Citadel for the first time in your life, you find foreigners (elves, dwarves, humans, etc) and other strange folk along the way, often wanting to join your party or asking for help, or interacting with you in some way or another.
Like all roleplaying games, you will gather quests through storylines, complete quests and kill monsters for experience, and level up your party how you see fit.  And your party, while mentioned, consists of members that are multi-classed.  For example, as you create your playable character, he or she can become a Warrior/Hero, or perhaps a Thief/Hero.  On your journey, you may find a Mage/Elementalist, or perhaps a Warrior/Berserker.  This gives you the customization to build your party how you wish, giving a strong complement to your team.  As you level up, you add attribute points into Strength, Skill, and Willpower, and choose feats every two levels.
I will be honest--this game took me by surprise.  It is a fantastic game that sucker punched me right in the mouth, and you will soon find yourself pretty deep into the storyline.  The combat is just unique enough to keep a veteran roleplaying gamer satisfied, as you fight by rows and columns.  Furthermore, the ability to set up camp and talk to members of your party gives the player a very relaxed feel as he or she gets to know more about who they are grouping with.
I most certainly recommend this game, and its DLC, as it has a great storyline, simple, yet fun combat, decent character customization, a fantastic soundtrack, and sets you on a very fun epic journey.  It is for sure a great addition to any gamer's library, and will surely quench the satisfaction from any RPG'er.

In the past, I've seen Picross Touch games and I've been tempted to pick one up, but I never have. After finding this free one, I tried it and I was hooked.
This game is good for passing the time and you want to chill out, or don't have time for a longer, more demanding game, but you also want to play a game that makes sure your brain is still working.
The pros I can say about this game would be that it has plenty of puzzles to do to keep you coming back. There's also an editor mode to create your own puzzles and publish them for others to try, as well as you can try out other people's puzzles and rate them.
As for the cons, I was reading some of the experienced Picross puzzlers' negative reviews to see what is wrong, and I would agree that some background music would be nice. Also, there seems to be the problem of more than one solution to some problems, which I've probably encountered myself, but never fully acknowledged. An amazing game that manages to put more grand scale, action set pieces, and poignant moments in a few hours than most AAA franchises achieve in their entire history.
Brothers is a puzzle based action-adventure game that puts you in control of two brothers on a quest to find a cure for their ailing father. Starting in the town where they reside, you control both brothers simultaneously, one with each control stick, with each having dedicated actions that only one brother can execute (for example, the older brother is stronger so he can lift he can lift heavy objects while the younger can slide between smaller crevices). From the town you traverse the surrounding country side , climb into the mountains, and arrive at your quest goal.
The puzzles tend to be fairly simple, but seem utterly appropriate to the environment they are found in (dodging an angry dog by jumping on hay bales outside of town, figuring out how to free a caged bird in a giant castle so you can fly across a destroyed bridge, etc) and use enough different mechanics / use them differently enough to never feel boring or stale.
Graphics and music are delightful with a light fantasical feel that is somehow also combined with an epic scale to make your travels seem much further and larger than they actually (especially important since the game is only 5 or so hours long).
Finally, the story is a simple affair with absolutely no dialogue (they use a non-sensical "language" the player cannot understand), but use character actions, music, and atmospherics to convey emotion and story points. This is very effectively done and builds a game full of fun, wonder, sadness, and joy in a way few games are able to achieve. Can't recommend it enough.

When I first heard about Human Revolution years ago, I was full of skepticism, becuase it had to live up to one of the best games ever made, and to my surprise, it was incredible.
It had a great story, choices and consequences, and a variety of aproaches you could take in order to achieve your goals.
And now we have Mankind Divided.
I have to admit I had to contain my hype when MD was announced, because by now SE had proven that they "got" what Deus Ex was about and I had a feeling MD was going to be even better.
Guess I was wrong. Kind of.
Don't get me wrong, Mankind Divided is a great game, and if you're only looking for gameplay, then go right ahead and buy MD right now.
But Deus Ex isn't only about gameplay, it's also about a deep and well told story, which unfortunatly, MD sorely lacks.
Here's the main problem with Mankind Divided's story:
You remember that point in the original Deus Ex when you got to the airport after new york? That point when the plot really kicks off and you have all these questions that you want answered?
Imagine if the original Deus Ex stopped right there.
Just "fly back to UNATCO and report back to manderley JC" *End Credits*.
That's Mankind Divided's story in a nutshell.
You'll have plenty of questions and there's a ton of setup for future revalations, but no payoff.
It just stops.
I was sitting and thinking to myself "Oh yeah, guess we're going to paris now! Wonder what's gonna happen next!"
And then I just got a message that says "You have unlocked New Game+".
Really?
I guess what I'm trying to say is that the game stops at the end of the story's first act.
If the next DLC is actually the next hub and proper ending I think I'm just gonna give up on Deus Ex from now on, because it will only show that SE doesn't care about creating a great story that lives up to the Deus Ex name, but only about making as much money as they can from a single game.
"Why sell the entire game with all it's content for 60$ when we can get 30$ more by not giving our game a proper ending?"

Despite all of that, I keep playing, and i sincerely hope that someday soon, Anvil gets this game working properly.

- Make the weapon pick up predictable. There have been many times where I desperately wanted my hammer and I got an axe 2 - 3 times in a row. Shoppe keep has a unique charm about it, owing your own store, completing sell quests, and manage the pricing just right to reduce the risk of thieving jerks. It has a some humorous items, some useful like growing weed seeds and selling the product. It has some automation at the cost of profit.

Overall I do like the silly graphics, the random customer names, and being able to see the customers progress with the gear they equip. It is a little time consuming, but in a relaxing way.
If you do like item shop games, do check out Reccetear as well.

I'll try to keep it as straight forward as possible.
If your goal is to have some fun managing a shop without caring about esthetics and whatnot, then there's a good chance you might like the game, provided you're not looking for the most immersive graphics.
If you want your shop to be as neatly organised as possible without compromising efficiency, then this game isn't for you. I'm the second type... and I must admit, I tried so hard not to care about esthetics, but I couldn't, the game makes it very difficult to organise things as YOU want them to be.
But hey, if you want to have some fun for like 5-10 hours, you might enjoy it, otherwise, the bigger your shop gets, the more annoying the layout becomes, the less you enjoy the game.

What's here isn't that bad of a game. Standard business management sim. Start a shop, sell overpriced stuff to nerds, destroy anyone stealing, buy more expensive things, rinse and repeat. If you really need it, just wait the second game.
tl;dr - Has charms, has issues. Feels like it's missing major in-game management utilities and management games kind of rely on those.
The soundtrack is pretty good, the graphics have their own little charm to them, you can play in the trash and flip off customers, and everyone that tries to steal from you can be reduced to a pile of bones. It's easy to get set up and go through, and doesn't require a whole lot of thought.
It gets monotonous very fast, more than most sims I've played. It seems like days drag on and you'll find yourself jumping around the town trying to find something to do while nothing is going on. You can't move furniture at all, you have to break it, so you waste money, and some placement can reduce AI pathing to spaghetti. Pickup and placement of smaller items can either need surgical precision or hotdog down a hallway. Parts of the UI are just flat out terrible. For the most part, if you want to min-max or like to be anal about your placement, good luck.
Looking at the announcement I can already see that a some of my problems with this game, which were based in management, are going to be addressed in the sequel. But with how this was finished and how "finished" it actually feels, I don't really see a reason or potential incentive for me to pick up SK2 in the future.

Granted I only played it for 5 minutes, but in that time I got stuck in a wall, phased through a closed door and was unable to read half of the text in the build/create menu - presumedly quite an important part of a game called Shoppe Keep.
Think i'm going to give this one a miss.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
It was okay.  Not as good as Smash.
This game can't compete with standard 2D fighting games like Street Fighter or Soul Calibur.  The only use for this game is if you need a good 3 or 4 player game, and I would rather you not look here.
IN RESPONSE TO DEVELOPER:
A member of the development team posted in the comments and asked for more feedback on why I thought what I thought of the game.  I was going to post the following as a comment reply, but apparently those can't be longer than 1k characters.
In no particular order:
1)  One of the biggest mechanics in the game is that there's a universal weapon pickup that each character can grab and it turns into either one of two weapons a particular character has available to them.  A couple reasons I don't like this design decision:
1a)  Any character who has their weapon is always more powerful than a character who does not.  Effectively, you *must* pick up a weapon in order to be viable in combat.  It doesn't introduce player choice; it means I always rush to the nearest unguarded weapon before entering a fight.  I would rather just always have a weapon and never need to pick one up.
1b)  Each character has two weapons.  I usually like one of the character's weapons better than the other.  I would much rather a character always use a single weapon so that I know what I'm getting.  I want to feel like I have mastery over a given character because I have the same moveset every time I play; for example, with Hattori I always discard the polearm because I like the katana better.  (If you want a single character to have different moves, I'd rather see a character with a stance change mechanic; see Nightwing's appearance in Injustice.)
2)  I got really confused when I found out that there were only three heavy attacks:  Neutral, Side, and Down.  I guess this is because keyboard players jump with the up key, so they can't use an up special.  If there's only three, I'd prefer specials on Up, Down, and Neutral/Side sharing the same special a la Smash 64.  Partly, the neutral heavy attacks feel a lot like conventional "up" attacks in Smash.
2b)  Also, there's only two mid-air heavy attacks?  Would it be weird if I wanted to be able to use my ground specials in the air instead?
2c)  Some of the specials seem redundant.  Most specials either move you forward or upward.  The down and right specials seem like they're usually forward-moving; these seem redundant, and I'd rather have the better attack on right and some kind of utility on down.
3)  I'd love to have more projectile options for use while zoning with your opponent.  Right now the only way to get a projectile attack is to throw your weapon, which I do all the time.  If you can't throw your weapon because you take out the weapon equip mechanic (which I suggest), I'd love to see some special attacks built for zoning at long ranges, like projectile attacks or reflection shields.
4)  I'd like to duck through platforms by pressing down+jump, rather than just down.
5)  Monetization isn't a gameplay design thing, so it doesn't make-or-break the first impression, but like, in the context of the Steam economy...  $5 for a character?  I picked up Injustice for $5.  I got Sanctum 2 and all the DLC for $3.20 total.  For TF2, a Rescue Ranger goes for $0.40 on the community market.  I don't know if I'd ever spend $5 on a single character in Brawlhalla when I can get an entire game for the same amount.
Oh, and as for the "It's not as good as Soul Calibur comment".  I play a decent amount of Soul Calibur, and the entire game is about pressuring your opponent to make  a stupid choice and then punishing them for it by countering whatever they chose.  I don't know if the Brawlhalla team is big into 2D fighters at all, but there's a free PDF introduction to fighting game mechanics here:
I only read the first few chapters, but it was an interesting read.
In Brawlhalla, I just want more options for what I can do to an opponent.  I feel like the extent of the game is just running at an opponent and trying to pick an attack that happens to hit them instead of having their attack hit you.

This game is so incredibly amazing!
Let's start before the beginning: the Steam version is censored, which basically mean everybody shows less skin. To fix this, go to the developer's website, download the free demo, enable mature content, play it until the first battle, save and quit. When you open the Steam version, you'll find the save ready to load and everything will be uncensored!
You can choose your main character between a male human and a female elf. You can build their skills and personalities by choosing different answers that yes, will change the story. The choice of the protagonist also affects the romance options, as some characters are straight and gay (although the majority is bi).
It's a story-heavy game, which means you'll read a lot. A lot - and you'll love every word of it. I'm not going to spoil anything of the plot, which is actually decent. The writing is also nice (there are some naive falls, like the use of the adjective 'electrocuted'. I doubt that electrocution is a known process in that world, but whatever). I would have enjoyed some more politics in there, but the told parts were in the right spots.
The characters are great, all have a backstory and motivations, and you can decide to explore them or just have a glimpse. Just so you know, Draco is AWESOME. Loren is so sexist it's borderline hilarious. I like how the trope of the 21st century gal in Medieval fantasy is subverted :P
You have waaaaaay more characters than the 6 needed for your party, but it makes it more fun, you can rotate them. Just remember to keep them with some equip and a weapon because of plot reasons, even those you don't use.
Once you complete the game once, a special mode called 'cheat mode' is introduced to replay just the story. You'll win every battle in 1 blow.
The combat reminded me of tabletop RPGs. It's pretty simple at the beginning, but the more you progress, the more you need to plan each action, especially at hard mode. Normal mode is still pretty easy.
Also... achievements! Soooooo many! And cards, whoop whoop.
I can see my whole family enjoying it for different reasons (and at different difficulty levels... and with censor on ahaha).
I got it in a sale and now I almost regret it, it's worth the full price. The dev is also really involved in the community and it's great to see such dedication and love.
The DLC introduces an optional place, the castle of N'Mar, with lots of bosses (who introduce some interesting moral questions), achievements, a slightly different ending and three optional characters (two of them romanceable!). I did expect a bit more considering the price, but it's a nice addition and definitely great to play.
If you're still unsure, grab the free demo and try it out!

I bought this game and its expansion on the recent sale, and for the price I paid I feel like I got great value for money.
Once I started, the stories and characters were so immersive that I found it very difficult to stop playing. I finished it with the same feeling I get after reading a great book; sadness, that it was over. I very much look forward to more from Winter Wolves in this vein.
The story is a little cliched, and seemed to be a Lord of the Rings parody of sorts. You have an aged wizard guiding everyone to resist against the upcoming of a dark lord, a deathknight of animated armor that happened to have more than a passing resemblence to the ringwraiths. The hero had to unite many broken kingdoms that needed to come together to defeat said knight (although that's a common trope to this fantasy setting anyway). There are the amazons, though, with a few undead here and there, so it's not all bad. The bright part of the story is that the protanist was not in a special position before the story began, and was instead a slave.
Any unoriginality in the story, however, is completely forgivable considering the dialogue. For a text-heavy game (the sound effects were just there to replace silence), the text was easy to read, and the game does it brilliantly; I was captivated from the start, and every character had a distinct personality that remained consistent throughout the entire game. Through their personal stories, you can come to relate to every one of your party members, and most of them are done well.
The romances were well done, with each of the two selectable protagonists (male human or female elf slaves/servants) having a variety of suiters to pursue. The romances only lightly effected the plot, however, and the effects of these personal relationships were only felt during minor plot points. The game could be played without romances at all, which may be odd considering it markets itself as a romantic novel.
Loren The Amazon Princess shines in its dialogue and characters, but is not without its flaws. The typical "Joke, Friendly, Forceful" dialogue options were a jarring experience. They didn't give you any indication at all as to what you'd actually say, which introduced something completely unpredicatable in a genre where the one thing that should be relatively predictable is the progranonist. It was easy to work around (scroll up to go back, or save/reload), but doing it this way was a strange decision from the designers.
The combat was extremely easy on normal, but that may have been because the focus was on the story. The turn based system with combos was interesting enough to survive the whole game without getting too boring.
The graphics were well framed with the plot, but the backgrounds were heavily reused, and the game could definately have benefited from having more of them. It was easy to forget where we were based on any particular background image.
All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed and recommend this game to lovers of visual novels. There are plenty of 'they lived happily ever after' endings, as well as one or two not so happy, and if you allow yourself to fall into the characters, a definite sadness when the tale ends and there's nothing more to read.

For the purposes of this review, I will start with this: As an occasional but relatively infrequent insomniac, I played this game from start to finish over the course of the night and through the morning not because I had nothing better to do but because I had to know how things would end. There is no higher honor for written fiction than that feeling of "just one more page", much like the videogame equivalent "just one more level". I say written fiction because while you can argue back and forth about whether visual novels are games (in my view they are), the highlight of Loren The Amazon Princess is still narrative over gameplay.
But unlike many if not most visual novels, there is an actual game here in a game mechanics sense. Fittingly for such a high-fantasy oriented story, it plays as a hybrid between entirely literary visual novels and an RPG. Do not expect the depth of a dedicated RPG. That is not to be found here.
Despite that there is still a commendable level of depth considering it's status as a hybrid. Equipment, level ups, stat points, skill trees and varied character classes are accounted for. Technically the only class choice you have the power to alter is the chosen player surrogate (there are two available) at the very start of the game, but the various party members have distinct roles and flexibility within those roles even if say, the dwarf chick will always be a bow-oriented type. Character forcing does occur at times for narrative reasons, but the game ensures that even characters you don't use often will be of relatively close level to your mainstays. The player surrogate and the titular Loren are often but not exclusively required members, but that's not a huge deal out of a party of six at a time when the roster fills out.
On the narrative front, people often compare this to Dragon Age Origins. That isn't entirely accurate. The theme of uniting different peoples to face an overarching threat is present in both games, and there is a character much like Morrigan. Other than that, it's mostly that both are archetypal fantasy stories.
Make no mistake, Loren is not a narrative you seek out for surprises. Anyone with decent familarity with fantasy novels will find little to shock them. A poor writer would let that result in a boring story, but thankfully the developers are not poor writers. What the writing lacks in surprises it more than makes up for in quality. A well rounded cast with believable motivations, genuine character development, and some damn quotable lines make this a visual novel you don't want to miss.
Also: if any of that RPG side of things doesn't sound like your deal, don't worry about it. The difficulty options and competent automated options for distributing stats and skill points means you will have to micromanage only exactly as much as you want to and not a bit more. Equipment lacks that, of course, but that's straight forward anyway.
TL:DR; BUY IT ALREADY.

First off I would like to say that this review is not supposed to be negitive, it's supposed to be a reflection of my own experience with the game and how I thnk the game could improve. Before I continue I want to say that I had a VERY fun time playing this game and I would most certainly recommend this game to anyone who has played smash before at either a competitive level or casual level because it is not only a very similar concept but it also feels very fresh and new with the addition of weapons that change your moveset completely! This alone sets it appart very far from smash while also keeping the core of what makes it fun which I think is very nice. With ALL that being said here are some gameplay mechanics that I think should be added and why:
-Short Hopping
Reason: It is really hard or sometimes even impossible to approach with an ariel with a lot of the time your options being to either Dash attack or to jump wait a long time then use an ariel. And that to me doesn't feel like enough options and personally I feel like adding a short hop would give the players waaay more options in terms of an ariel approach and ariel movement which I think could enhance gameplay greatly
-A walk speed
Reason: Maybe this is already a thing and if it is you can call me out for it but from what I can tell there is no walk speed, Which is very annoying when you are trying to approach without using a dash attack or turning around for a Strong attack. But then again im not sure how this would work for keyboard so idk you could add this if you want but it wouldnt change that much it would just be nicer
-Fast Falling
Reason: It feels very hard to get back down to the ground when you're up in the sky so adding this would give people more options when wanting to get back to the stage. And who knows maybe people could add it to there combo game example being: Dash attack then Short hop into forward air then Fast fall into maybe a Strong attack. I have played a few tekken games in the past and been a fan of the series for a while now. This entry is certainly the most impressive both in terms of graphics and mechanics.
Story mode was a disappointment for me personally especially as most characters' stories have been reduced to a one-match cameo (kind of like an after thought); the Mishima storyline is nothing innovative either, we have seen it all before basically. Arcade/Ghost mode gets stale and easy quickly, once you notice the patterns and strings that the AI usually commits to.
However, what Tekken 7 lacks in single-player, it more than makes up for it in Online mode. Most of the people online are up for a good slugfest and the online play runs pretty smoothly, apart from the odd match now and again; it is pretty addictive. The cast size is generous and diverse; accordingly there is much to learn, not just in terms of learning the combo strings and set ups but also counters and punishments to each character. It's one thing knowing the moves of a character but another thing entirely reacting to them, it is challenging but the mind games are enjoyable if not a bit frustrating sometimes. I have learned a lot more in my 200+ hours with Tekken 7 than my entire Fighting games experience before it and I still got a hell of a lot more to learn. It is currently missing some of the the legacy characters but hopefully they are added soon.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking to improve their skills or just enjoys a good fight.

Missions quickly become stale and stressful, and while heists are a way to swoon you into thinking that you'll be able to fund so many ill minded activities, they usually end up being a carnival of salt for you and your friends the third time you fail the heist due to some aspect that requires ridiculous amounts of experience in the game.

Even with this system in place, exploiters run rampid in nearly every online server, and the only way you are truly, 100% safe is through the single player. I have seen so many toxic players, people who take the game waaaay too seriously, and those who abuse the power they can receive through higher cost goods that most players dont have access to. Ascender is a 2D platformer in which you control a small robot tasked with finding components to bring back to your maker.
Naturally this means a lot of platforming your way around town running errands for various locals.
You pick up a double jump and grappling hook ability early in the game, allowing you jump higher, swing from hooks and pull boxes around to press buttons and build steps, something we've all come to expect from a modern platform game.
In the beginning of the game you only have space for one of those abilities at a time and it suggests you will have to choose which abilities you need. In practice once you have passed the beginning you will quickly pick enough upgrades to use these and other abilities together. I thought it was a potentially interesting mechanic that was never really used. It is possible this matters more later in the game.
You can also have a speed upgrade which you will need, you are a little on the slow side until then. A tracking device that beeps when you are near something collectable. An ability that allows you to see things that you couldn't before. Presumably there is at least one other ability, but I didn't get far enough to find that.
The various locations are of a decent size and are different enough that you do feel you have gone to another part of the city and consistent enough to know you haven't gone too far. You do have a map of the location you are in but not one of the wider city. It's big enough to forget the way, but not big enough to get properly lost. The quest menu usually shows you where to go but not necessarily the best way to get there.
You are free to wander around looking for things to collect and talk to people, they all seem to have something unique to say, if not always interesting, some will give you quests which you can complete for some sort of reward. Mostly these are collecting or delivering something at a location that isn't always easy to get to, with some fairly easy puzzle solving along the way.
Progressing in some quests may open up other areas or other quests or give you some upgrade or reward that makes another quest easier but other than that you are free to do them in any order. I do not know if any of them are actually optional.
There is a day/night cycle with the background and lighting (with an indicator in the top left), but this didn't relate to one quest being blocked until tomorrow (in the hospital), tomorrow must have been triggered by some other quest, although I'm not sure which. On the subject of lighting, there is also occasional rain and an awful lightning effect that makes the background white and the everything else black. Only in computer games does lightning make things darker.
Up to about 60% or so completion I'd say it was a nice game. After that (specifically
) the precise timing and jumping aspect increases in difficulty. Which depending on your view is either a good challenge in what has been a fairly relaxed game to this point, or an unwanted if not entirely unexpected increase in frustration.
I don't have the patience to continue for now, that probably tells you more about me than the game. I'd say the game (so far) was good enough that it deserves a look from someone who likes and is good at platform games.
I didn't encounter any bugs in the Linux version.
Play with a controller, there is no proper key mapping, only a set of presets for flat qwerty people with weird hands.
The English text could benefit from a proofread, the grammar is a little strange in places but it is fully understandable and should not distract from the game. (Having said that this review will now be full of mistakes.)
Worth playing.
