Mankind Divided provides a ton of improvements over its predecessor. From new augmentations, a more nuanced storyline, and new game modes, everything I loved about HR has been tweaked and enhanced in MD.
The level design has been vastly improved as well, with different playstyles being truly represented in every mission. You can be a hacker, pacifist or go in guns blazing and you are no longer penalized with less xp. It genuinely feels good no matter what kind of playstyle you choose now, which is a far cry from the problems of HR.
For those worried about microtransactions within the game, they are literally just praxis kits and in-game credits for those people that aren't willing to explore the city in its entirety. You are not at a disadvantage if you do not purchase these items, because the game was designed assuming that you haven't.
If you really are interested in getting all of the augmentations in a play through you can always play through with New Game+.

Okey... Time to begin the review of this game.
If you had visted my profile, you will know that this game is the game where I put most of my hours in. The thing about this game is that you have to grind... and grind... and grind... to get anywhere in this game. The game is the the product of Reto-Moto. If you do not have any idea who are them let me enlighten you about them. Who here knows the Hitman series? No one? That is weird. Well that is probably the result of writing the review alone. Alright so no one in this room knows what am I talking about. So Reto-Moto is a small company whose team mostly consist of people from IO Interactive the same company who made Hitman 2016. Okey everyone understand me? If no one raise there hands i will continue. Okey no one? Lets move on than.
Graphics:
Really nothing impressive. It used to be more bland (more on the other side of the contrast bar) but because of that my potato could run it at about 30 fps (in an open area). Now the game is more vibrant (for example the grass is more greener). So overall 7/10 (sorry Reto-Moto)
Gameplay:
What do you expect... Space Lazers from Nazi Germany? Of couse not. (Seriously were you expecting that?) Well as much as Reto-Moto tries to make the game as historically accurate as possible, I still do not get their weapon choice. For example, the new heavy class fighters. They added the ME 410 which was a mid-war development plane while in contrast a update before they added the O-52 Owl. Which a bit of background info is a outdated plane when the war start. See the technology difference? Well all be it the two tier difference between them but there is a possiblity they will meet each other in the sky. It is also not about the planes but also the guns the biggest gap in the technological difference is between the c47 pistol which served the first world war to the second world war and the m1/m2 carbine which only served late into the second world war. All be it that one is Carbine and the other is a pistol. But other than that the guns are reletively balanced. So well done Reto-Moto. 8/10 (minus one point for being exclusively multiplayer). Well this is an after thought, Because the game requires a lot and empasis on A LOT of grinding, minus one point for that (so sorry Reto-Moto) 7/10.
Community:
The community (unlike most exclusively multiplayer games) is actualy supportive. So yeah 10/10 (well done Reto-Moto for supporting the community)
Historical Accuracy:
Well only for games who tries to be historically accurate. Ok since you can actually alter history [so in a way Mother Russia can take over Britan (yay)] i will not actually rate this section.
So overall
7/10 (for Graphics)
7/10 (for Gameplay)
10/10 (for community)
Rounds out to an average of
8/10 (well done Reto-Moto)

+ It runs well
+ It comes with a lot of puzzles

- The puzzles are too symmetrical in many cases and can be solved often through guessing

Even though it looks like the cons outweigh the pros, due to the game's price tag and competent execution, it is a satisfactory time sink if you're interested in picross.

After 31 hours of gameplay,
Picross Touch is not perfect, but it's not a bad game. With a few changes it could have been better, but it gets the job done. Here are a few things I observed while playing the game:
- Some of the puzzles have multiple solutions, but those who have enough patience can see their mistakes and correct the errors. Still, it's not good to have puzzles that have multiple solutions, especially for the casual players who would probably just skip the puzzle(s) they can't solve.
- Some of the puzzle pixel art looks very amateurish in design. Not as polished as Nintendo's offerings that I have played to completion, such as Mario's Picross, Picross 2, Mario's Super Picross, Picross DS, and Picross 3D (I don't have a 3DS to access the eShop picross games). Most of the puzzle art looks like it belongs on the iOS app store.
Personally, I would ask the developer to work on a few things to polish the game (make sure there aren't multiple solution puzzles, fix up the art). One minor thing I would like to see is a quality-of-life feature like fading the number after filling partial cells and marking an empty space, instead of the usual fading all of the numbers after filling in the complete row. One major addition would be workshop support, as adding a level editor for user made levels would expand the game even further.
Hopefully, more picross/nonogram games appear on Steam, whether they are from this developer (or others), as picross/nonograms are my favorite logic puzzles to play with.
I did notice the ambiguous solutions, but enjoyed it nonetheless.
If you like puzzle and logic games, this game is for you. Hundreds of levels to keep you busy in your free time. I hope there will be new added levels and steam achievements in the future.

OMG.... Yes.  Simple easy goodness.  Choose your own adventure at its purest.  This game "is like an onion", it don't look great but omg is it good and what are all these layers?!  And like being on a quest with an ogre, there is no hand holding.  Well..maybe just i tiny bit ;)
Basically its an iron-age mercenary survival simulator.  Rogue-ish, it'll knock you down but don't give up cuz you're never out. My most successful playthrough started with me being beaten and captured 10 different times within my first week of being a freelance merc, then many more times the following weeks.  Then i escaped ran to the nearest city, happened to be a tournament in town, and i won it betting all my money on myself.  I then bought a bakery and have been a successful bussiness owner since, with two more shops in the works.....thats right, my story has evolved into 'Conan the barbarian bought a bread store' lol.  I travel the land 40 deep (ragtag group from all nations) buying bread supplies and killing people for money, ima badass breadmaker and adoring every second of it.
The graphics are from the late 90's but that's when i was coming up so i have zero issue with that, especially when there's hundreds of units on the field going berzerk and there's not even a hint of a blink of lag with settings at max.  The biggest turn off of PC gaming for me is lag, so i cherish games of this magnitude that run (period).
This scratches that Skyrim itch like when you scratch your back with an actual back-scratcher, nailed it.
DEVS wish i could outfit my units not just the named mercs but that just may be a way of making their leveling up more meaningful, so maybe answered my own lol.
As i said in essence its kind of a simulator so it can be 'grindy' even though that word has no real meaning any more.  The grind is the game and you do it almost however you want.
Combat is third person and surprisingly satisfying even though i normally hate mouse combat controls.  Although it does have that downfall of mouse control that is it can be over-intuitive to the point it feels under-intuitive with the micro direction changes from moving a mouse.  But everything else overshadows this to a point that I can't call it a negative.
Overworld travel is done with small markers on a huge map with the 'you move the rest of the world moves' dynamic, if you're standing still its paused.  It reminds me of traveling in Fallout 1 except you can see how the map looks and you can see others moving around you before you encounter them.
It successfully cuts down one of the worst grinds in video gaming, the in-town grind.  You just hit tab to go to the town menu and instant port to where you want to go like shops or your own business haha.  There are still important quest givers in the streets but as soon as you find them and talk to them you hit tab and jump to wherever you need to go from there.  The towns are minimalist so don't expect Fallout or Skyrim level of visual social interactivity, there's a handful of roamers and the rest are 'quest givers' or potential 'quest givers' or shop owners.

"What is your name, boy?"
"Garrett."
Garrett is a thief. Not just any thief, a master thief trained by the masters of illusions and wisdom known as the Keepers, and he's about to be embroiled in an ancient war between the Hammerites and the Pagans in a supernatural tale of sneaking, stealing, and trechery.
One of the first stealth-'em-ups, Thief: the Dark Project is an immersive, powerful, and unique jewel in the crown of its creators, the infamous Looking Glass Studios.
Beating this game took me like 12 years, and it's still as good, as the first time i watched my brother playing it.
An ageless testament to good game design. To date, Thief Gold is the best stealth game I've ever played.
One of the best stealth games out there. Some mechanics in this game are not seen in games today. Instant Classic

Take a deep breath. Look around you. You're Garrett, the master thief, and your instincts and cunning are all that keep you one inch ahead of the cruel hand of the law. You're the best, you steal that which can't be stolen. You reach into myth and claim your destiny... but in so doing, you learn that some stories are all too true, and there are some prizes that should never have been taken. Step into Thief Gold and become engrossed in the original stealth experience, where every sound is an enemy, every light is a threat, and everyone else breathing is a possible witness to your crimes. Hide in the shadows, step carefully, and always keep your wits about you, for you never know whether the next lock is standing between you and your riches... or sheltering you from something you can't escape.
Thief Gold may be dated by modern standards, but its gaming experience has stood with me ever since I played it. The levels are regularly an hour in length if you take care to search for everything, and the dangers both myriad and convincing. Never have I been so guarded in how I move in a video game, but every sound, every shine of light, all of it can make the difference between staying stealthy or being spotted. You can knock targets out or choose to remain in the dark without hurting anyone, this is before the modern Thief so there's no actual reward for ghosting it outside of bragging rights. But every level has its own self-contained story, and creeping around the City shows you so many sides of city life, in the estates of the rich and the hovels of the poor. The story takes extraordinary turns as well, with every name carrying a lot of weight, and every place rich in history.
I implore you, give this game a try. Whether you're a hardcore stealth gamer or you just like playing in the dark, this is one game that will pull you in and have you creeping around in no time.

First of all a little warning: this ain't the same like Legend of Grimrock, an other indie title where you can set up a party. You don't move the characters yourself here. It's more like the Eador games, in terms of gameplay. With the exception that this is a rpg (eador is strategy). So expect here alot of interactive pages instead of a world where you can move yourself. It's more a visual novel with some mechanics (like equip stuff).  If interactive pages bothers you and you rather want to make the action yourself, then skip this game.
Loren is at first sight an interesting game. Rather then the hero itself you take the role of a servant (or more a slave actually)
That will be either a human male or an elven female. After you have chosen one of those you then choose a class. A little complaint here. You can choose between warrior or thief. No option of chosing a mage, which is a bummer.
You can then go to the castle or shop already, but main thing is the saving of the queen. So you soon leave. That's where the story begins then. It is divided into acts. You first begin in act I and the mainquest is saving queen karen. There are sometimes also some sidequests and you will also run into random encounters (which i know myself from neverwinter nights II). You also meet other people on your way and some of them will join your party. A good thing i find is the choices you have to made. At a certain moment you got into trouble and 2 partymembers offer each a solution. So which way do you go?
The choice changes how the story will continue. You will encounter this more.  Often there is also an option of how you will react on a situation. You then have the choice of joking, friendly and forceful. Sometimes also romance, which happens often at places where a bed is (tavern for example). It reminds indeed a bit to the later action games like Mass Effect.
And although it are only 3 options the outcome is different. I don't agree that this is tedious. It's just part of the game. That it doesn't always turn well makes it more interesting.
Going to the next destination goes through a map, which reminds to neverwinter nights or the king's bounty games. But here you also have the option to going to a camp. At the camp you can talk with your party, including your master. This is actually very similar to the taverns in NWN or the campsite in Dragon Age:Origins.
The combat here goes in turns, much like the King's Bounty games, only you don't have here a field. Instead just a page.
There is one thing that bothers me. The claim of being hardcore and keeping old school rpg's alive with this game is a bold claim and also not true. Don't get me wrong, Loren the amazon princess is quite a fun game. But it's not the same like alltime classics as Planescape:Torment and Baldur's Gate. it's even not the same as Neverwinter Nights or Legend of grimrock.
It ain't much hardcore. Still, i don't think that casual players will like it, as it ain't casual either. You have to think sometimes, especially when it comes to fighting. And probably casual players don't like numbers and that you have to allocate them.
If it's worth it's price? From what i see so far i think so. And it's cheaper here on steam then on the site of the developer, which ask €5 more. I think €19 ain't bad, if you keep in mind that Eador: Master's of the broken world is also around that price and managing games like Football Manager from sports interactive cost even triple the price, while that one is just spreadsheets.

Much like a Japanese visual novel, Loren the Amazon Princess is an RPG with a wonderful story and an emphasis on pursuing romance. Most of the game involves clicking through well-written dialogue and making the occasional choice, but there is also combat; the turn-based battles function like a card game, as there are no 3D models or complex animations. The result is fast and rewarding, with no boring excesses like grinding or waves of enemies. The excellent soundtrack, gripping story, and memorable characters make Loren the best game of this style that I've ever played.
(Rating: 8.5/10 "Excellent")

Overall, this is an enjoyable title — not the bestest thing ever, but certainly decent. The story is typical sword-and-sorcery fare (demon lords, bickering humans and elves, prophecies, etc.), but most of the time, it's still engaging enough to keep you playing. The characters are a mixed bag; some of them are actually pretty interesting, some of them are forgettable. The writing is also mixed. The dialogue tends to be snappy and organic, but the narration can get seriously cheesy.
The combat is . . . OK, I guess. Mixing characters and builds can be interesting, but things get a bit tedious after a while.
My biggest issue with this game is the price. It's not a bad game, but there just isn't enough content or variety to justify a $20+ price tag.
(Edit: I used my Steam version to unlock the demo version. Steam didn't log my playtime in that version, but I put plenty of hours into the game.)

The game isn't bad. Let's be clear about that, but it has some flaws that detract from it's fun factor (for me anyways).
The graphics are good - about what you'd expect for this genre of game.
There's a lot of story. It's not badly written, but it's not best seller material either - again, about average for the genre.
I do like that there are places where the plot diverges - I haven't put in enough time to see if it's just a case of B then A, instead of A then B, or if it's a permanent change to the game.
My main complains with the game have to do with the combat system .Since that's the main point of the game other than the story, I consider them pretty serious issues.
First, I'll explain the skill system. Each "skill tree" consists of 6 or 7 skills, each of which has 3 levels and some skills require other skills to unlock. Each character has 2 skill trees available. Every character has one of 3 basic class trees (mage, thief, warrior) and their own class tree of unique skills.
Some skills seem almost pointless. Others seem very counter intuitive.
Example of a pointless skill - from the basic class FIghter tree.
Power Strike (Lvl 1/2/3) - activate to do (15%/30%/45%) extra damage but lose (10%/20%/30%) speed for (3/4/5) turns.
So at level 1 it does 15% extra damage but you attack 10% slower for 3 turns. So each turn will take 1.1 'time' than normal.
The 3 attacks take 3.3 'time' to complete to do 3.45 'attacks worth' of damage. Sounds like a *small* bonus. But activating the skill takes about 0.33 'time' of an attack - so it's actually 3.63 'time' for 3.45 'attacks worth' of damage. In addition it costs you stamina to cast it. Also, if you use any of those turns to do something other than attack, you're just taking a slow turn with no benefits.  These type of skills would have been much more useful if designed as single turn attacks with a smaller stamina cost.
A skill that seems counter-intuitive
The Archmage tree is basically 5 (6?) elemental types. Each skill is an AOE attack with a chance of a status effect (burn for fire, freeze for water, etc).
As you increase the level of the skill, you DECREASE the damage the attack does but you increase the chance of the status effect kicking in.
At level 1 - all the skills do 300% base damage and have a 10% or 30% (depends on the status) for the status to take effect.
At level 2 - it's 250% damage and 20 or 40%
At level 3 - it's 200% damage and 30 or 50%
Again, it's not that combat is awful,  it's just many of the skills seem.. less useful than they could be.
Perhaps I wouldn't be so critical of the skill system had I never played Monster's Den and Monster's Den:Book of Dread - free games on Kongregate that use the same combat style but with much more interesting and varied skills.
The other problem is grinding. Each town has 3 grind battles available. As far as I can tell, each of these battles is always the same with zero variety in creatures (so fighting undead in the dark elf town means 3 skelly fighters, 2 skelly archers, 1 necro... never 3 archers or 2 necros and an archer.. never ANY variety.
I don't know that I find the story compelling enough to complete the game when the combat system is so.... static and repetitive compared to other games I've played with the combat system.

After playing Loren the Amazon Princess, I had to read the game description again and laugh. The game promises vivid characters, a strong plot, and meaningful decisions but delivers none of the above. A demon lord, who looks like someone traced a picture of Sauron off a Lord of the Rings DVD box, wants to take over the world. You must convince each race (elves, dwarves, humans etc.) to fight the demon by completing a task for them (killing something.) It's the plot of Dragon Age without the nuance and well written dialog. Writing your own "backstory" consists of choosing whether you were a stable slave or a castle slave in order to get either thief or warrior stats. Customization is extremely limited. For instance, the thief talent tree is 20 different ranks of inflicting a status condition on a staggered enemy. Overall this was a simplistic and boring game with simplistic and boring characters. It feels unfinished, since they clearly meant for the player to be able to choose to be a mage and they made the romance option nothing more than pressing a big button with the word "(romance)" on it. I can't help but think that this is a placeholder for real dialog that they never got around to writing. Don't let the word "novel" trick you into thinking that there is a good story to be had.

Actually pretty good, for what it is. It has very low system requirements, and it runs on unity.
Graphics and Aesthetics
Graphics are good considering its low system requirements (My broken PC can run it!), but some textures are a bit eh, and animations are lacking in "umf" especially when you fire rockets and kill opposing dragons. The plasma lasers feel as they should, though a sound for them colliding with a dragon would be cool, instead of just numbers popping up. Rockets and Plasma Balls feel kinda eh as well.
The game is very colorful, and has a wide variety of dragons, which homage some familiar tropes (Such as the tyrannosaurus-esque Tiamat dragon, and the European starter dragon), as well as homaging familiar dragons in movies (The Fury and Ogre dragons in particular look like 2 particular dragons from How To Train Your Dragon, though only vaguely).
Story
Literally nonexistant, not even little bits of flavor text for each dragon. Not important, but would be nice to see!
Mechanics
Flying is fun, though going up and down feels a bit slow, and the flying can be quite sluggish at times. (Good luck zipping around corners, even with a fast dragon!)
The combat options are lacking, 1 machine-gun esque weapon for each dragon, an option of a Plasma Ball, Rocket, or Rail Shot for a secondary weapon, and 2 accessory slots for things like mines and things to restore your cooldowns. Each dragon also has its own unique "ultimate" ability, which is the only difference between dragons aside from their stats. Each can equip the same weapons. It feels kind of boring, honestly. More variety in weapon types would make this much more fun. The cooldown time for using your weapons feels too restrictive, and all the dragons have the same cooldowns. The actual combat, however, is fun and intuitive, which is what really matters for a game this simple. Zipping, dodging, and dogfighting another dragon can be quite fun.
Misc criticisms
In TDM, theres no indicator telling what is an allied dragon or an enemy dragon. Friendly fire is on. This need to be fixed.
Not enough players, but this will change with time, as its a very new game.
The progression system is kind of pointless, really.
Overall?
Reccomended, especially for free! I advise the devs to start building some new weapons options for the dragons, and refining their movement system.

I've been a big Picross fan since I first played it on my DSi. This game is great, especially when you consider the price. I finished all the puzzles, and while some of them seem to be a bit lacking in the logic to solve them, there was only one that gave me real trouble (from memory, #146 in the 15x15).
A few of the puzzles do have multiple mathematically correct logic soutions, which I found a little annoying, but not annoying enough to make me stop playing.
The game runs smoothly, and I found no issues or bugs with it (apart from the aforementioned logic issues.)
The only suggestion I would make, is to add the ability to undo more than one step. Sometimes I'd need to backtrack to figure out where I went wrong, but you can only undo the last move, so in those situations, I often found it easier to just restart the puzzle.
All in all though, for a free game, this is great. I would love to see more puzzles added, as it's a great little time waster whe you just have a few minutes to play :)

This game is downright addictive. It makes you think logically to solve the puzzle, but not so hard that it's frustrating or impossible. My favorite feature has got to be trying to guess what the picture is going to be before I finish the puzzle. The simplicity of Picross Touch makes it a relaxing/casual-gaming, break from my favorite RPGs.

A lot of reviews have pointed out that there are some levels with multiple solutions. Yes, they exist, but you are usually left with only 2-6 pixrls that fit multiple ways. By looking at the picture you can get most of the puzzles right the first time. Even if you can't, it only takes a couple of seconds to go through the variations.
Plus, it's a free game.

Now that I've solved every puzzle, I do wish there were more.  Some of the Hard puzzles I think were maybe a step too hard, but maybe I'm just out of practice.  Good way to spend a few hours, and can't argue with the price.

The RWBY series has been my favorite animated series in a long time. From the day the first episode came out, I wished for a game to come out. When my prayers were answered, I immidiately bought the game. Although I have not had the time to play through the game repeatedly, like I wish I could, it had been enjoyable. Needless to say, I am more than impressed, and I cannot wait for many new things to come.

I would like to start with a little disclaimer: I haven't played the game all the way through and I've been playing one character mainly throughout my experience. The experience might be different with other characters, and the game might have some features hidden away later in the game, but I don't think I'll see them.
I love RWBY. I like the show, its animation, its characters and especially the soundtrack. So I really had my hopes up for this. I bought it during early access to try it out with friends and to just see what it was all about. But after playing it for a while I just don't feel like continuing.
For starters, the gameplay is extremely repetitive. Combat is basically just clicking the same button (yes, button... singular) and gets boring really fast. There's a normal melee attack, one ranged attack that's useless, and you've got a special attack. But like I said, you'll just be mashing the same button over and over again. It's no fun and it doesn't get any better.
The story is garbage. For a show that's got pretty good writing otherwise, this is pretty sad. Speaking of which, the voice acting isn't even close to the quality that the actors deliver in an average episode of the show. It's essentially just a bunch of one-liners that doesn't contribute to the game at all.
Another problem I have with this game is the horrible camera. I constantly find myself in some sort of blind spot where I can barely see my character, let alone anything around me.
The soundtrack is pretty much every instrumental track from the show. That's it. A few exceptions here and there but still.
Bottom line, I can't recommend this game. If you're a big RWBY fan, you'll probably just be dissapointed to find that this game doesn't really add anything to the otherwise intriguing storyline that's going on in the show. If you're just looking for a hack-and-slash game, you can do better than this.
Now what I'd like to see, if RT Games ever makes something else related to this franchise, I'd like to see a real fighting game. Think Street Fighter but with the characters from this show. That's something I'll look forward to. In the meantime, save your money for that and go watch the show (again). Just don't play this, you can find better alternatives.

Brawlhalla is an amazing experience for anyone wanting to try out an indie version of super smash brothers. The cast of characters feel unique and each one has their own abilities. However in all of the praise Brawlhalla has been getting, people may be blinded by the current flaws this game presents. It features a set of stats for each character, which isn't unheard of, but also includes a variety of enhancements that can change the characters stats drastically. This provides inconsistancy with characters and makes playing the game more of trial and error than learning every character's strengths and weaknesses. Although this system is not in play for online matches, they intend to allow the enhancements in further patches, closer to release. This isn't the only thing that proves to be an issue; ranked 1v1s are also on the negative side of things. The current elo system makes it difficult if not impossible to climb higher in rank. You lose about the same amount of points that you gain, making the system favor getting wins over actually doing well. In addition to that, the matchmaking for ranked needs a bit of tweaking to suit more people in general. Currently, one of any rank can be matched up with people as high as 3 tiers above them. (Ranks go as Bronze 0~5, 5 being the highest, Silver 0~5, and so on.) This means someone in Silver 4 can easily be paired with a Gold 1 and vise versa. In a system where the difference between any two tiers are the amount of wins, this can be overwhelming. It is true people with greater skill level can stand their ground and potentially beat higher opponents, but that is in far too few cases.
Overall Brawlhalla is a wonderful game and I recommend anyone try it out, however I do not recommend trying to 'climb the ranks' until release, as we don't know what to expect until the game is complete.

For those who don’t want to read a full review, let me just cut it short by saying; If you liked Human Revolution, consider this game – if it ever goes on sale for 50% off or more, I’d recommend it in a heartbeat.
Deus Ex mankind divided is a masterpiece of design, mechanics and unscripted systems that allow for all manner of interesting interaction between the AI and the player character throughout. It plays host to arguably some of the best level design this year – with many really solidly put together levels and a fantastically detailed city hub that acts as a backdrop to multiple side-quests as well as a jumping off point for the main story.
The game takes roughly 25-30 hours to beat whilst playing casually and completing side-quests as they are handed to you. Rushing the main story would likely only run up to 10~ hours but I wouldn’t recommend doing that for reasons I’ll go into later.
The city of Prague is incredibly detailed and very dense, easily one of the best looking environments so far this year – the old 18th & 19th century architecture work with the new-style of angular, geometric buildings of tomorrow to create a city that feels like it has character and a fully fleshed out history of its own. The detail is not just for show, either, there are multiple paths into almost every building that accommodate for any theoretical play-style a player character may choose. Vents, breakable walls, hackable objects, physics objects and environmental puzzles are liberally placed around the city. Verticality is also important, multiple access points across multiple levels and a small but interesting sewer system allow for traversal across the city in a non-standard way for those who take certain augmentations. Right up until the end of the game I was discovering new things about the city hub and finding new loot. I’d defiantly recommend you go into your first play-through blind (without online guides) and turning off the objective markers comes recommended as it helps prevent objective tunnel vision and allows you to really think outside of the box.
However, not everything is perfect in this game – there are a number of minor technical issues, at the start I’d often spot my framerate dip below 60 in wide open areas or if there was a lot going on at once, even on a 980ti & i7 Skylake machine. At the very least I’d make sure you are on the latest drivers and switch off/turn down MSAA as that seems to be the greatest performance killer if you run into problems but after adjusting my settings the game is remarkably well polished for a PC port.
My second greatest criticism of this game has to be the main plot, which is a real shame considering how solid the games mechanics and design is. The story often feels janky, almost confusing at the start and time is not afforded for proper character introduction or development for the supporting cast. It feels like you are plonked in the middle of a plot-line without any real context or explanation as to how you got where you are. One particular point comes to mind, after the tutorial mission you arrive at a train station, meeting a character whom Jensen apparently already knows – however the player has never met this person. This leads to an awkward moment where we are expected to accept that we know her despite knowing nothing about said character. This drew me out of the story a bit and I couldn’t help feel like I may have missed a cut scene or something by accident.
In general, I feel that the side missions are often much more engaging than the main plot and I would highly recommend not skipping them as continuing the story can see some of these opportunities pass you by.
My final, and possibly biggest gripe with Mankind Divided has to be the excessive microtransactions for in-game items. For some completely inconceivable reason, Square Enix thought that a fully priced singleplayer title should have microtransactions. In my opinion that’s plain ridiculous and many will choose not to support this game or this company for that reason alone, and I respect anyone who chooses to make that decision. However, the balance of the game does not seem to be affected by the ‘shop’ and I was able to comfortably play through the game whilst ignoring the shop and its contents entirely and so it’s existence does not affect my personal recommendation as it seems to have no bearing on the game beyond a small ‘Shop’ item on the main menu screen.
Overall I really enjoyed DX: Mankind Divided. It’s mechanics and design are top notch and I would recommend this game for anyone who loves solving environmental puzzles and unravelling the complex environment that have been set up despite the lacklustre story.

It took me 26 hours to complete this game with both the storyline and ALL sidequests (at least those currently known and 2 that are currently not written about anywhere) done, plus quite a bit of time spend exploring.
For a 49,99€ game, that's pretty okay-tier, so you won't hear me complain about that aspect. What is an issue for this game is the bells and whistles around it. The possibility of microtransaction seems to put everyone on edge (although I'd say that you can simply ignore that if you don't want to buy them, no need to get upset about an option that you CAN use but not have to) but more so the DLC. Or the lack of DLC I should say. Yes, if you bough the digital deluxe edition or the season pass, it's quite some extra money for rather little pay-off. The DLC missions are pretty short and the extra items really aren't required in a new game. So yeah, 30€ for that is rather steep but hey, who knows what Eidos will throw in later down the line. I wouldn't mind a 'missing link'-like DLC for those who have had the patience to wait a bit longer. Just because it isn't announced doesn't mean it won't become reality.
As for the game itself: lengthy, lots of exploration, pick your own playstyle and an enjoyable story. Sure, it's nothing too fancy and yes, Adam seems a bit bland (I think it was pcgamer who put it as 'what am I doing here-Jensen' which seemed pretty spot on) but overal I enjoyed it during my tour through Praque.
It's a tenner cheaper than No Man's Sky and you'll get more fun out of a single city than a quadrillion planets/10

People will tell you this is just a Super Smash Brothers clone for PC, but coming from a person who got it back in 1.0.5, it is actually pretty different and tons of fun. Keep in mind the trailer is outdated and at the time of writing this (August 2015, patch 1.15.1) Brawlhalla is still in closed beta. You can get a free code at
but you'll be missing some sweet costumes.
The menus are very well laid out, the only tweak I would make is that Exit Game is in Options instead of on the main menu and the main menu needs a bit of noise at the bottom.
The cartoony artwork combined with the sounds and the character diversity are amazingly done. All the map layouts are balanced (Exept for Titan's End) and the character choices are great. Bear vs cowgirl, minotaur vs knight, it's amazing the amount of work that Blue Mammoth Games does.
Each character (called Legends) starts out with an unarmed moveset and if you get a weapon pickup, your character will get one of their two assigned weapons each with three signature moves that only they have. Also, each character has their own stats. This means all the characters will be vastly more balanced but still feel different.
Brawlhalla is great as a first fighting game. Each character has 11 unarmed moves and 11 moves per weapon, 6 of which are unique to them. This is much more understandable than the ~20 moves Super smash Bros. has, where no characters share the same two moves.
This is also a great game competitively, don't get me wrong.
The Compettitive and casual communities are great. You can get advice from the best by hanging out in their streams and I think that's amazing. Raidhyn is our main guide maker, so go to his youtube and twitch. We also have our fair share of memes, more f which are created each day, but if you don't care about that, it woln't be waved in your face.
Bottom Line: This is one of my favorite games of all time and it keeps getting better. Tons of fun with friends, and go get it now. Go to Raidhyn's youtube and Twitch to get better, and see the reddit thread for helpful links to help you get started!

Tekken 7 for the pc is a stable and decently done port.
+The gameplay is fluid and precise, it feels like they've done nothing but improve on the previous itterations of Tekken.
+ Great appearance customization options, certainly the best ive seen for a fighting game in recent years.
+Online is active, and the game has a dedicated fanbase.
+Good sizable cast of characters, some new, some old.
+A good game to play if you want to get into Tekken
-The story mode is flashy and cool to look at, but nothing to really write home about
-This game, like other Tekken games, has a sizable learning curve
-New content for the game has been slow to come out so far
In any case with Tekken's good sized dedicated fanbase, Tekken 7 shouldnt be going anywhere for years to come.

Now and then you get into a turned based fight and although presented in a simple form, they can be very entertaining.
At certain points you'll get the opportunity to choose a branch, or different angle, concerning the story and developments. Attack, sneak, laugh, cry, start a romance have some wicked hi-res HD hardcore porn scene.. although, no that last one is not in there. Which is actually a good thing.

This game goes against everything I have come to be taught as a gamer. Games to me are supposed to be engaging, fun, entertaining, interesting, adventuresome, often meaningful. RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a Co-op 4 person Spectacle Beat 'em up. It has actually a great concept but was made poorly. The game has next to now actual skill needed to win, you just spam the best of like 3 combos to win. I think after playing this game and watching it develop through its first few months. It is a good time to write a review.
Highly fun game with some innovative and highly entertaining modes, a good shooting system balanced by the comically bad melee, which in fairness is being constantly worked on. Great regimental community, lacks toxicity, Public servers with in game voip can be equally hilarious/disgusting. A fun game with a lot of replay value + dedicated dev team who seem to really care about the game. Large potential, one to persevere with.
To begin:
This game has a dedicated and growing development team that seems to really care about the community, are wonderfully polite and responsive to queries, and have an excellent ethos. What they have already achieved given their size, and lack of producer is really nice and they have been a joy to interact with.
The game itself, can be an absolute blast to play, whether alone or with a regiment. The public servers provide some great, spontaneous moments, owing the natural RP potential of the game, and the ingame voice chat, which adds another entertaining, if at times irritating development. People spamming Drum and Bass in a Napoleonic Wars game doesn't do much for immersion, though provides some hilarious moments none the less. The public provide moments of genuine teamwork, co-operation and friendliness, which is very welcome.
The community, compared to that of Mount and Blade Napoleonic Wars, lacks some of the inherent competition and therefore potential for toxicity. Regiments have on the whole have been great to interact with, hosting a large variety of events and servers
There are some excellent modes, including the naval siege modes and naval modes which add some fantastic variety, and a lot of re-play value. The classic siege and battle maps are pretty good, though more need to be added. A map maker would be a huge boost, and allow the community to aid the replay value of the game. Though, consistently released maps do alleviate this problem to some degree. The current factions and units highlight the potential, with some good looking classes, with some interesting stat differences, new factions being released, and classes such as cavalry if it comes out will further improve matters.
The melee sadly is still pretty rough at the moment, and needs a lot of work. Though it does have some potential. The shooting, with bullet drop turned on, requires genuine skill, though some class balancing is probably required. The artillery needs some changes, including moveable artillery, to stop the monotonous repetition of people instantly aiming for cannons at the start of the round and blowing them up. Alternatively development of the carpenter class to be able to repair them. These features I'm sure will be added in time. The Naval combat is great fun, and naval sieges provide something different, with destruction and explosions galore.
Performance has improved over time, though that is often due to people spending money on better server hardware. Administration is getting easier, with more functions, though a proper in game admin panel would be great. Graphically the game can look fantastic, bar a few hilarious textures, such as lightning. The dynamic weather along with day/night cycles is awesome and provides great potential for more scripted events/ campaigns. Running events has gotten progressively easier and more rewarding, with higher population counts and lower ping, after being stressful at times, particularly in the aftermath of launch.
Overall, this game is a great prospect, for £15 it is, im my admittedly worthless opinion, cracking value and I've already earned my money's worth several times. This game will require perseverance, which given the nature of video gaming, and immediate demands of players, is a difficult prospect, but I believe efforts will be rewarded. If not. Meh. I've had a great time already.

Firstly its the exact same feeling and sounding game as Human Revolution the graphics are marginally better but nothing new or special but framerate wise it is optomised and runs rather nice.  With a game like this though the story and interaction with other people (NPC's) should be where it shines but unfortunatly it falls flat firstly the voice acting is terrible especially from your boss Jim Miller there is simply no effort of any kind put in when he's speaking he just simply rambles on.  Other people are not much better David Sariff still talks to you with such suprise and i swear he loves saying your name out loud, its always ADAM, ADAM, just to make sure you know he's talking to you and then theres the stereotypical foreigner that always misses simple little words during sentences so you can identify that they are a foreigner "i will meet you by bridge" instead of "i will meet you by the bridge" it makes the game feel so tacky that their still trying to run with this.... well joke if you will.
The world is just like Human Revolution and you can walk the streets and enter the sewers etc and although there are plenty of NPC's around and plenty of places to see it feels so damn empty due in fact to the limited scripts these NPC characters have and they will belt out the same couple of lines over and over and over again until you leave the area, if someone is being arrested in the square then that SAME guy is still being arrested 1 week later in that same spot still belting out the same lines again and again, then theres the TV's stuck to walls literally everywhere with the same 10 - 15 second news report from Eliza Cassan playing over and over again like the people on the street, also you have the anti aug types walking around that will take a vieled verbal jab at yourself being augmented and that they dont like it then theres the checkpoint police that want to constantly check your license and will also insult you aswell but as the voice acting is terribly woeful it feels more like an insult from a primary school kid calling you a stupid head in the playground and not some government official with a shotgun giving you a piece of their mind, there is so much aparant animosity towards augmented people and there is supposed to be this tremendous hate between augs and non augs but it never feels hostile or if anyone is actually on edge about it all theres no random attacks in the streets from pro human or aug groups it feels as if im walking through San Angeles from Demolition Man everyone has been pacified to the point where their to polite to even yell.
Enemies and stealth gameplay are no better as enemies will walk their strict patrol route muttering the same few lines again and again and usually spouting out secrets and concerns like "i hope they changed the code on the safe" and "i hope nobody is listening to me right now" and just like Human Revolution you can pick up a box to hide behind and inch your way closer and closer to them without them realising something is going on, the enemies in this game are simply obstacles to get around like the civilian NPC's and cops their not aware of the environment that they are in and simply move back and forth from point A to point B and even when they spot you its still "hmmmm what is that" even though your in line of sight.
I will finish it as i have started but im going to give it a thumbs down rating, IF you enjoyed Human Revolution then pick up a copy you may enjoy it for what it is because its not much else.

Overall the game is good. But at least in my eyes the game could be vasitly improved. My thumbs down is geared towards players who have never played the series before, or haven't played since it's inception (like me, last one I played was tekken 2).
The game lacks any sort of proper tutorial to teach players how to play tekken, this hurts badly when playing against better opponents who know how to cancel moves and movement options, when the game never states either of these are possible at all. When other games in the fighting genre have been doing things better for half a decade. If you're new and not playing with friends, I don't recommend this game in it's current state, it will be an exercise in frustration.
Online mode is extremely poor, lobbies only play one match at a time, a full lobby of 6 players could have you waiting up to 15 minutes between each match (if you lose). While other recent games have lobbies where you can challenge other players while waiting, or even train. You cannot do that in lobby mode or tournament mode.
Tournament mode is busted and frequently hangs. If anyone leaves the tournament even after being eliminated, the pot shrinks. This is not the biggest issue, as often the tournament will just hang and prevent anyone from even playing. Or disconnections will occur and kick players out of a lobby, not even during a match. The tournament mode is overall poorly made. The rewards are nice, but when playing with friends it's again an excercise in frustration.
Netcode for itself is solid when connected to a low ping player, I don't have complaints about that.
Story mode, at least to me an outsider of the series, is really just a poorly told joke. As in it presents itself as being knowingly absurd in it's plot lines. But plays off events in the story as entirely serious. And the story ends up being just like an awful summer blockbuster. And I just ended up skipping the cutscenes at ever chance I got.
Overall if you're new to the series or returning after a long break. I do not recommend the game, and if you fit that criteria and have no friends who play it, I do not recommend it in the slightest.
It has solid gameplay and decent online, so if you know tekken it is worth grabbing at a discount.

My friend convinced me to give Heroes & Generals a try, and since it was free I figured I might as well.  I've played a few WW2 FPS games before, so I figured this might be some fun.  However 2.7 hours in I am already seeing quite a few shortcomings of the game that are quite discouraging for a newcomer to the game.  In no particular order, these are my criticisms of Heroes & Generals:
Maybe one of the more glaring omissions from this title is the
lack of a tutorial for new players.  Though the controls are mostly what you'd expect from a title of this sort, some things weren't clear (such as how to go prone).  Rather than getting a basic training mission where a new recruit can learn the basics of gameplay or practice with the game's equipment, you are thrown right into the meatgrinder.  Make no mistake, it
a meatgrinder of a map where you're up  against more experienced players potentially with better equipment from the get-go.  Not the end of the world by any means but definitely not the best way to welcome someone trying Heroes & Generals for the first time either.  From reading in the forums, it seems there may once have been a tutorial in the past but it was removed.  Why this is the case I cannot say, but it is certainly quite headscratching.
Even
equipment that a new recruit might have such as a melee option like a shovel or knife has to be unlocked.  Other FPS titles will give you at least one other method of fighting besides your primary weapon but not this one.  Superior weaponry being something to aspire to is fine and a way to encourage the grinding necessary to accrue enough in-game currency to unlock.  Basic equipment that would add balance to the game for a new player being the same thing is ridiculous.  Add to this that it appears one would have to grind for hour upon hour to even have a
and we've got a title that is very unwelcoming to new players.
.  Not really the game's fault, but because there aren't as many people playing it these days you're stuck waiting for quite a while to play a match.  I'm lucky if I can get into one after 5 minutes of waiting in the lobby, and times closer to 7-10 minutes are more likely.
Even if you forgive the shortcomings of a constant grind to even get basic equipment and waiting forever to get into a match with a rifle and a prayer, something else rather odd has turned up.  As a new player it's not even weaponry you have to unlock.  You can't even
in the skirmish maps, they're locked.  Why?  What on earth would motivate the game's designers to limit the new players necessary to keep interest in a title alive in such a silly way?  Whatever the reasoning, this means that you're limited to going in on foot from spawn points that are quite far from the battlefield.
Considering all of these points, is the game worth a try if you're new?  It will really depend on if you're willing to grind for a very long time to be able to make things fun.  As things stand right now you get thrown into a match with no idea what you're doing from the get-go, don't even have a melee option to turn to and have to unlock everything from that melee option to riding a gosh darned bicycle in bigger maps.  You don't get all that much in game currency from the matches you're able to get into after long wait times, thus eroding at a willingness to keep on trucking until you get enough to do something useful.  It's not pay to win, but it
very limiting, discouraging and brutal for someone who's just getting started.  If you have the patience to wait it out and grind up to getting better things, and you have the free time to put toward this title despite its many shortcomings, feel free to give it a try.
In its current state, wherein a new player is so severely limited and unsupported in efforts to learn the game or even stand much of a chance to have fun, I can not reccommed Heroes & Generals.  This is especially true with superior titles available out there which allow
options in matches beyond a single weapon and which allow for easier learning of the game.  Heroes & Generals in its current form seems to hate new players and is so infatuated with 'grind to unlock' that it will erode your patience.
I don't mean to harp on the same things over and over, but the fact that you have to grind endlessly to be given the
to use a shovel, knife or
pretty much says everything you need to know about Heroes & Generals.

I got curious about this game when I saw the idea of fusing RPGs and visual novels.  Though I've seen the mechanic a few times, "Loren" seemed to focus on doing "more" with both of its parents.
I can't call the game an insta-buy at $19.99 -  it's going to depend on wether it's for you.  Me, a person who likes his RPGs with loot, skills, story, and choices (and now and then likes a game that you can sit down with for 30 minutes or 2 hours), thinks he got his money's worth.  It is definitely a replayable game as well, so if you're the kind of person that likes to try different endings and plots, then that's a plus.  I found a full playthrough is about 10 hours (winning unlocks  cheat mode)
"Loren" is the story of an amazon princess who's mother vanishes, presumed dead, and promptly gives up her queenship to find her.  She's given a single slave to help her - that's you by the way - and very quickly you're necessary as Loren is essentially a niave, unsubtle, combat machine.  Very quickly Loren and your chosen hero/heroine (who you do get some customization of) end up caught up in wars and intrigue, and collect a ragtag bunch of somewhat familiar characters.  So it's off to battle orcs, lizardmen, demons, and more because the world's problems are a LOT bigger than a missing queen  . . .
The game mixes visual novel style branching storylines and classic "Camp" dialogue with point-and-click maps and classic RPG combat.  It actually balances all of these pretty well - most events are "bite sized", combats don't drag on for long, and there's a pleasing level of detail in things like equipment, character development, and battle strategy.  If you're an accomplished RPG player you probably won't find "Normal" too hard, though there are moments that will push you - you do have to pay attention.
The best part of the combat and character building are how different factors interact - Status effects are a big part of the game, and soon you'll be trying to figure the best way to put your foes off guard.  Classes are meant to work together, especially in boss battles - and every character is "dual classes" with a generic class and a specialty class, adding a nice bit of customazation to the usual trinity of Warrior-Mage-Theif.  In short you're always "this basic class and . . ."
The story is the big selling point, and frankly, "Loren" delivers a giant heaping helping of common fantasy elements and characters that we're all familiar with (perhaps too much), but then actually goes the distance to add little personal details that bring the characters and events to life.  Sure the prose has a purple tinge, and some elements border on stereotype, but it's fun and you'll find a few surprises - you actually get a nice amount of character backstory if you dive into it, as well as interesting romantic complications.  There are parts that will definitely pull at your heartstrings, and I found myself geniunely liking some of the cast.
So a buy?  I'd say if you like your RPGs with story, want a good RPG you can play in short bursts or long sessions, and if something a bit experimental like this appeals, go for it.  I think this is also a game to encourage, because the fusion is quite satisfying - and I'd like to see more.

I wanted to like this game, I really did. It's another lesson in the fact that, in the wake of Greenlight, there's an increasing number of sub-par games on Steam. First things first, I've played a few visual novels - Analogue, Hate Plus, and the school-related one by the same author. Those were all great.
Loren has long, boring conversations evident immediately from the beginning. The story and dialogue reads like someone's sexual fanfiction with the rampant sexism that seems to be portrayed for laughs or as of no consequence and blatant relationships that feel less like hero and loyal servant (like Frodo and Sam) and more like bizarre dom/sub sexual fetishism. If that isn't enough, this is where Loren, the titular hero, seems incredibly naive up-to-and-including the fact that she doesn't know who her city's nearest neighbour is.
The writing is so cringe-inducing that I didn't even get to try the combat system. Avoid, avoid, AVOID.

Thoughts:
Good artstyle (The male and female main characters bug the hell out of me, but everything else is good) for the setting. Detailed and generally fit the personalities of the characters.
Music is really impressive - esp. for a indie title - props to the team on that front.
Gameplay is a subjective matter - I grew up with old school games, so I was fine with it being portraits and skills; but what did bother me was poor/limited item selection; I didnt feel there was enough variety for gearing up - as an example, I spent the whole game with me theif using the default chest armor becuase nothing else was worthwhile for speed - despite searching shops hundreds of timesonly to see the same cycled selection of choices (randomly).
I liked most of the characters personalities; or the thought put into them - though "my" character was a annoying waste of space - you give me dialouge choices - then proceed to shove values/feelings done my MC's throat - regardless of my choices; made the MC feel very spastic and hollow.
which leads me to my main gripe - this COULD have been a epic story; but I felt the writer was too excited or in a rush to finish; the narrative is grotesquely melodramatic and unpolished. If he or she took their time to tell the story properly or with more depth - and with less melodrama - this had a real possiblity to be high up in my ranks.
That, and foreshadowing - the writer seemed to feel the need to tell the reader what was going to happen multiple times, prior to the events (at least four times, to my count). "little did Loren know she would be blah blah blah" "The world would soon realize blah blah blah" Seriously? let the reader find out - don't spoil your own story.
I can tell alot of time and effort went into this, and I repect that - and I like alot of the game - but the poor writing is a strong negative for me; you know its bad when the script makes you cringe.
EDIT: After having completed a second playthrough, I am willing to mark this as "reccomended" - the above flaws still stand, but I discovered the writer improved with time (or as he/she progressed in the tale) - party member quests were fairly short but well-written, and the romance sub-stoires were palletable.
And finally - the subtle-to-see branching options gave me a new respect for the title - and how the dev was more or less good about acknowledging any past choices, and how they affected future outcomes (afew ere missed here and there, but more or less thorough).
so yeah, I'd sayn its worth the money  - I uninstall this game feeling satisfied at thee content - even abit wistful.

First Impressions:
Loren the Amazon Princess is  a "fantasy epic combining intricate turn-based battles with a heroic tale of overcoming evil", as the Steam page says. The game played more like a Visual Novel to me, but the game had an RPG-esque system, so it's not totally a VN.
Loren the Amazon Princess follows the tale of Loren, an Amazon Princess (who would've guessed?) searching for her missing mother. The game plays heavily on the story aspect, and that's not a bad thing. I certainly enjoyed the story thus far. If you're expecting a lot of gameplay, you might want to look elsewhere. The game has a skills, inventory management, and even battles, but about 80% of your time will be spent reading the dialogue. The game even delves into romance later on, if that's your kind of thing (heh, heh).
The combat in the game is all turn-based and is a bit unique, certainly unlike any other turn-based mechanic I've seen. The combat is split into "rows", with your primary fighter up front (up to three), and your others behind them (also up to three). This also applies to the enemies, of which there are plenty. You can max out your party at six players, which I've yet to do, but would love to just to try it out in battle. There's also skill and inventory management, something which should be expected from any adventure-based RPG. Nothing too special with these systems, but at least they're there.
I'd recommend Loren the Amazon Princess for anyone looking for a heavily story-driven RPG or maybe those looking for a VN with some RPG-esque elements.

In all seriousness, however:
This game plays, to an extent, like a visual novel; most of your interactions with the world are done in the format of such. I believe that making the general dialogue options nonspecific is bad; they seem to be trying for an Alpha Protocol thought process with the choices, but succeed mostly in making it annoying to pick what you actually
to say. Romances feel somewhat shallow, and have clearly marked options for getting them; there's no gameplay influence if you do or don't pursue people's affections. Party quests are just a free item for a character.
Combat is mostly in the realm of "serviceable"; there's no pyrotechnics or fancy graphics, and I feel like the growth is too slow at times. At endgame, I wound up with most characters being early 20s, and I just felt like, in general, I was blowing points on just maintaining diversity, not actually improving my characters. There's too much of a "Right Way To Build", in my opinion, and character options are disappointingly limited; your protagonist will -always- be the party healer (and if you don't build them for that, unfortunately, you're crippling yourself), regardless of if they're a Thief or Warrior.
Despite all this.. This is a fun game. I wouldn't pay full price for it, but I consider my time enjoyably spent, so far.

I'll admit the game is entertaining and I'm probably going to finish it to see how the story turns out.  However, if I had it to do over, I would have waited until the game was under $10 before I bought it.  Nothing about this game justifies it's price tag, the gameplay elements for each class consist of about 8 powers that you can put skills into that basically just make most of those eight powers better.  And even the eight powers, in some cases, are just variations of each other.  For example, the rogue has four powers that all basically do the exact same thing but just apply slightly different damage types.
As far as dialogue options go, you basically have 3 (sometimes 4) dialogue options for each situation,  Joking, Friendly, and Forceful (and sometimes Romance).  I'm not sure if the dialogue choices make a big difference as this is my first playthrough and am mostly choosing the friendly options.  However, it is a bit annoying that the actual things you'll say aren't shown before you say them.  The game suffers from Mass Effect syndrome where you might choose a dialogue option and the actual option isn't even close to what you wanted to say.  The good news is, you can use the mouse scroll wheel to backtrack and choose different options, but this can get annoying if you find yourself backtracking every other choice.  If the game gave more indication of what impact dialogue options had on the story, I would prolly enjoy this gameplay aspect more.
If there was more to the gameplay, I might be willing to recommend it.  But story alone is not enough to justify the amount of money the devs are asking.  If you don't really care about gameplay and just want a nice, relaxing (and somewhat simple) game you can sit back and enjoy and don't mind spending the $20, then this is the game for you.  However, if you're like me and like a good mix of gameplay and story, I'd wait until the price goes down a bit.

Short version:
-ride a wild motorbike demon
-You can hear the music still playing from your car when you get out, surround sound

-battles provide a good challenge

Long version:
The writing is overall pretty good, but all the jokes about metal and music culture in general are what make it stand out. I laughed the whole way though. And that's just the script. The game itself is really well done. I was a bit skeptical of how it could be an "action/real-time strategy hybrid" but it is exactly that. Most of the game is actually open world ala GTA style, but the parts where you do battle (through the power of metal, of course) actually go into a sort of real-time strategy mode where you're also part of the action. You have to make and upgrade your army, you can fly around and just command your troops from the sky or jump down and fight with them. There's not a huge emphasis on the "strategy" aspect (it's basically just capturing the nodes in the center of the battle area for resources), but it is very well integrated. You need to pay attention to your army to win battles. Also the battles are actually challenging. I was a bit surprised cause I was expecting to just blow through them, but a few I had to attempt a couple times. There's also all kinds of stuff you can do between battles to make your army more powerful. Without spoiling anything, you can explore the world to find things that increase your stats, or complete quests and spend your points on upgrades at the metal forge.
I also recommend you play this game with a controller. It's really designed for it. I prefer mouse and keyboard for almost anything but this, use a controller. Controlling your character basically feels like a platformer and the rest of the time you're driving. Vehicles are a big part of the game.
Also this game rewards you for exploring with upgrades. And you should explore. A big part of what makes it so enjoyable is just the world they made. It's artistic and you can't help but smile as you drive around. Don't make the same mistake I did and blow through the capaign as fast as possible. I found myself wishing I'd taken my time and enjoyed how cool the land of metal is before finishing the game.

This game is everything that an RPG should not be.
The story had barely and meaning, and failed to even get me to care about this world and its inhabitants. Moreover, the world feels like a generic RPG world, brining little to the table that has not already been established. When I was running around the various levels, the enemies and enviroments were dreadfully repetative. The bosses of this  game are uniteresting and can only be beaten by a slow and painful grind. It took me and 2 other guys almost half an hour to defeat a single boss, and most of that time was spent waiting for mana to regenerate. When we finally beat him, the loot was abysmally boring. Each piece of gear is stupidly generic and useless. When compared to other games such as borderlands, the loot is utterly worthless, with the only changes practially being a 1% increase in damage, while bringing nothing unique or interesting in the 2 different looks per piece of gear.
If you can manage to get through all of that, the gameplay itself is chaotic and difficult to follow. The majority of my time was spent spamming the mouse and tapping keys on my keyboard, all the while half the screen is taken up by useless text, and the other half an epileptics worst nightmare. The art style is slightly charming, however once a fight begins there is just absolute chaos and you have no idea what is happening. I still dont even fully understand how my character works.
The character classes are downright dreadful. The only real difference that is present for most of the game is how characters deal damage, with just a different weapon ability. You should not have to wait for 10 hours to unlock an ability that actually gives your class something noteworthy.
When it comes down to it, Torchlight 2 is a garbled mess of RPG and other genres slapped together, offering little to no innovation, and overall being a generic dungeon crawler.
The only good part is you can have a pet.

I really, really wanted this game to be good. I love RWBY and after the recent decent into darkness of season 3 and the upcoming season 4, i am excited as ever for it. But this game is so bad. I can barely call it a game.
I actually got this back in the Early Access days, when it was cheaper, and i can say that since then not much of the game has been improved.
GAMEPLAY
RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a Co-op 4 person Spectacle Beat 'em up. It has actually a great concept but was made poorly. The game has next to now actual skill needed to win, you just spam the best of like 3 combos to win. There is a counter that doesn't always work, a weird team attack system that actually took me a thrid of my first playthrough to actually figure out and honestly, i found that i could beat the game by spamming one move. The gameplay is not fun, and very repetitive, They throw in Ranks, but it resets your characters level every time you do it so it's honestly not worth it. Not to mention that there is next to now variety in the game.
STORY
There is no story here. Random bad Guy Number 1 is experimenting on grimm, go stop him. That's literally it. And that is so aggravating. RWBY is a well written show, and because this game WAS made by Rooster Teeth, i have to wonder where all those writers went? Did Monty just write the entire story out for them to use, because that's kinda what this game makes me feel like. The characters have no personallity, besides the once in a while one liner or pun or sarcastic comment, which each character only has like 3 of.
GRAPHICS & MUSIC
The games looks are really the only thing that spring to mind about this game thats good. The game is gorgeous and colorful, but is very empty, which kills the awe of it. The music is good, but it's just a bunch of instrumental stuff from the game, which is a little frusterating. I want to hear Red Like Roses lyrics! That's some of the best part of the song
OVERALL: Really this game is mediocre at best and give me an impression of no effort, or they wanted it out as soon as possible. Honestly this game feels the same as it was in Early Access and thats what bothers me. It feels like the game is not finished and its so frusterating that it won't ever be properly finished. With the rumors of JNPR being paid DLC i can confidently say, DON'T BUY THIS GAME, for the full price. If you want a short, dumb, mindless grindy game, this is for you, just please, wait for the price tag to lower. This game is no worth $25.

Picross is a logic puzzle game. Picross puzzles are also known as hanjie, nonograms, or griddlers.
I would not call myself an expert at picross, but I do really enjoy a good picross game, and have bought and completed Picross DS, Picross 3D, and all of the "e" series on the 3DS eShop.
For experienced picrossers, this game features about 50 5x5s, about 130 10x10s, and about 180
15x15s.
Unfortunately, Picross Touch is not a good picross game. As other reviews have mentioned, this title commits the cardinal sin in logic puzzle games - multiple puzzles that I played had more than one possible solution (Easy Puzzle #51 has three solutions, for example) but only one of the solutions is recognised as "correct".
Additionally, the visuals are drab and lifeless, there's no music at all, the largest puzzle size is only 15x15, there's no hint systems in place for newer players, the numbers on the left and top of the puzzle don't grey out individually, and there is no timer to keep track of how long it takes you to solve a puzzle.
If you've never played a picross game before, I suggest you don't start here.
If you're a fan of picross, there are better picross games out there, as well as old-fashioned puzzle books that you colour in with pen/pencil.

Fan of the series, big fan of RT and most of their content, was super-psyched about a video game adaption since the concept and themes would adapt very well to a God of War or Devil May Cry-style hack n' slasher. That said, the (I assume) final product is very... Ehhhhhhhhhhh...
The mechanics are very DMC-inspired and for the most part work fairly well, although a combo list would certainly be very welcome since the game doesn't really explain that you need to insert a heavy attack into a light attack chain to make a combo. Actually, a general tutorial would help a lot since again, the game doesn't explain what things like a Team Attack is or how absolutely vital countering is. Not to mention the controls menu can only be viewed in-game for some stupid reason. I'll go into the menu to find where the dodge is mapped to and get brutalized by what looks like Phanpy from Pokemon going through an emo phase.
The environments match the aesthetic of the series very well but there's barely anything in them. Just a token amount of scenery, the occaisional group of crates and a marker pointing to the next combat arena. Put some♥♥♥♥♥♥in there, a shrine, a cave entrance, a big tree, anything. It feels so empty and plain. Obviously you need some space for the enemies but they only come at you in groups of 5 or 6 in single player anyway.
There's no personality to the characters anymore, save for the occaisional quip during and after combat which becomes VERY annoying when you've heard the same one 10 times in one session, and the story is pretty laughable. There's clearly effort here, but for it's overall quality and at the price it is now, I just cannot reccomend it. Get it when it's on sale and if you literally have nothing else to occupy your time with.

Well, I gotta be honest with this one.
First off, I only come to this game's store page only to see the negative reviews, as literally all of them are correct with everything they say.
Secondly, the patches fix almost nothing, or things you can't even see compared to what the game is. I know you're trying your best to make the game better, but even if you patch all the bugs in the game, it will still be A) Boring and B) Repetitive.
Now, let's get straight to the point:
- EXTREMELY Boring, specially if you play in Single Player. I've tried both Single and Multi-Player, but it was the same experience, only that you get the pleasure of clearing waves faster on Multi-Player than doing that on your own.
- Controls are really simple, but still lack a lot of polishing on how they play.
- One starting weapon, one ranged attack (that is completely useless) and an ultimate attack (that isn't good enough for a lot of things). You get nothing else, just these. That's it.
- All enemies play the same, but there's one or two bosses that play different and take longer to kill (though, as from I've read, the final boss is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to deal with).
- On the whole game, you only do three things: Kill randomly, kill to advance, kill to defend.
+ Upgrades help, even though some of them are not that useful, it still helps (except for ranged attacks).
- Ranged attacks. Does anybody even use them?
- No pause screen in-game, either Single or Multi-player. This is really bothering.

+ Weiss.
That sums up the gameplay, now, let's talk about the story.
- Really lacking. It's just "go through this area and kill enemies", aside from some things that are just... there.
- It makes no sense. A little bit of it does, but still. You randomly appear on this spot? It's never explained, you just did, get over it and defend that spot that I want you to defend, just because I say so and it's good for us.
Nothing left to say about it. The story makes you unable to care about it and that's it.
- Dialogues are really, REALLY annoying, at least for me. I know you're tough and all, but you don't have to remind me that in almost every single area with the same line. At least a variety would be nice.
- Voice acting is... poor. Already said enough with the dialogues, but it's just true, they need a lot of work. A lot of it.
- The music is the same, over and over. Throughout the maps, all you hear is a constant loop on your ears that will stay there. It is from the show, and I know it has a lot of good tracks, but the tracks placed in the game easily get repetitive and boring the more you hear them.
The OST in the game is poor, and makes it unimportant to the game. But as I said before, the game needs a lot of work other than just being rushed to 'please' fans with a 'full release'.
+ Sceneries tend to be nice. Even though they're empty, they're still nice to look at.
- How it's always the same animations makes me feel sick, not in the terms of anger, but visually sick.
- You'd love to go to this place? Too bad, YOUR area is this one. You can't go in there.
- There's a ton of places in where you could easily find a way around other than getting something to cross the path, but then again, you jump so low you wouldn't even reach them in the first place.
tl;dr It's good to look at on your first minutes in the game, but then, you feel like you've seen all of it.
The developers need to complete the game, other than fix minor bugs that aren't really important. I know you care about the fans, that you like the show and community a lot, but sometimes, you have to care more about your work to keep those fans happy. Between Early Access and Full Release there's almost no difference, just some maps and some enemies re-designed very simply, this shouldn't happen on a Full Release, even more if you're going to raise the price of it.
I've spent only an hour to it, and probably wont touch it again until the DLC comes out, but I must say that by reading the reviews of the full release and by just spamming the same attacks over and over in the same events again and again, you get a very clear idea of what you're playing.
I like RWBY, I really do, but this isn't worth the $24.99 at all (I got it on the sale, luckily). If the game is re-made or at least get a REAL full release, then things might be able to change.
But for now, it's just a boring, repetitive, rushed game of Hack N' Slash with the title of RWBY on it.
