In the small genre of stealth there is only a handfull of truly great games. Not only is this game one of the original classics but also one of the best(including the 2nd&3rd) if not THE best. The game takes place in a world that is a mixture of gothic fantasy, steampunk and, sort of 1600s- 1800s Europe. No guns though! But that's a good thing. this world includes all kinds of monsters, creatures and different types of humans. Most humans are designed to be a hilarious sort rather than serious. Events and lore are explained in 4 main ways: from cutscenes that have a awesome and beautiful 2D art style. Letters and books. The main character also comments on things himself, his name is Garret and has a witty sarcastic sort of tone and is a joy to listen to. And finally you can listen to other people talking both to themselves and others to learn things provided you are sneaky and dont disturb them. The writing is suberb and really adds to the game, you actually want to listen and read. The voice acting is brilliant both the serious and humorous. Even the monsters sound awesome and some cases horrifying. The game and two sequels are full of atmosphere, the music, the sounds, the lighting is all done so well. Still to this day have some of the best sound design. At many points this game feels like a horror game which many "actual" horror games cant even say. The guards will sometimes go off on a tirade about random stuff which adds a lot of charm and shows how much fun the developers had making this game. There's also a few different factions you meet, the Pagans who are nature worshipers, very occult stuff, the Hammerites basically medieval Christians and the keepers who i wont say anything about. Very interesting and different all of them.
Now onto the meat of the game. The level design and the gameplay.
So in Thief before every mission you will get a overview of what will be in store and then have the ability to use the shop where you can buy all sorts of things using the money you collected in the last mission so it helps to be a perfectionist and get most of the loot. You can even purchase tips if you think you will need some help. The game has several difficulties, i highly recommend the highest for all 3 games. It wont be insanely hard for you, just gotta be patient and plan out your stealth. The levels are fairly big and have many paths, they're also quite varied so you won't get tired of them. When it comes to your gear, you have a blackjack for knocking people out, a sword for combat which you'd prefer to avoid, it's not like dishonored, Garret is no amazing superhero. You also have a bow with standard arrows, along with some magic ones, water arrows for putting out fire, fire arrows for destroying stuff and killing, and moss arrows so you dont make too much noise on harder surfaces. You go through the mission always looking for the main objective but depending the place Garret will also mention other things you might want to check out, grab, or do. Sometimes will find bonus side events or objectives while looking around. It all works really well! When it comes down to it, just explore a cool level full of thick atmosphere and steal things! Even today the game itself looks fine, levels have a pretty and interesting art design. Although the Ai at times can be stupid and very easy to exploit which i only recommend trying after playing at least one time legit.
Overall the game is a fun, memorable stealth game that feels like an adventure, sometimes fantasy, sometimes horror. And has huge replay value. I can't recommend this enough, they truly don't make them like this anymore. And if you like this one i recommend the 2nd and 3rd game. Thief 2: The Metal Age and Theif 3: Deadly Shadows. They change some things in those games but the core writing and gameplay is there.

My main issue with Shoppe Keep is, that after those 20 hours, the game doesn't end despite you as a player exhausting all of its content. See, at the beginning there's a lot to do, set up your shop, sell items one after another making just a few extra gold off of everything you sell, send your champion on an adventure so he can bring you back more items to sell, place more stalls and shelves, clean up mess the customers make and fend off annoying bandit attacks, craft special goods, level up and assign new skills. However, doing all this would be unsustainable in the long run, since the more items you sell, the longer it takes you to handle managing your shop. That's why the game offers a lot of mechanics that simplify the process. Buy little robots that almost automatically place your goods on stalls and fend off thieves for you. Get carpets so you no longer need to clean after your customers. Buy a pub and gain steady income and after a few weeks, gold become completely irrelevant. As the game keeps going, you find yourself idling around in your shop, since it presents you with all its content at the beginning and it never adds anything new. It's exactly the same at day 1 as it is at day 100, only at day 100 you already have all the skills, your bots have pretty much infinite amount of goods, there's nothing to upgrade, nothing to buy, no reason to send your champion out, no reason to do anything at all.
So why is there no ending at that point? Why is there no goal? Why didn't they add any new content to keep the player going? Well, because the game is abandoned. The developer "finished" the game and moved onto developing their VR game, leaving it as it is, buggy, eventually stale and boring, with no ending at all.
You'll never finish it. It will sit in your library forever and there's no way for you to 100% it, as some of its achievements are bugged or a huge pain to get - like the one that requires you to have your shop open for a whole year (basically play for 90hours ish - with the current content... uhh...). Another achievement is developer only - unobtainable. Another one or two are simply bugged and you'll never get them. I actually tweeted at Shoppe Keep's developer a few months ago, asking them to at least fix the achievements if nothing else. They replied asking which ones are bugged, but never responded to my reply, so I bet they don't really care.

I used to play a lot. And I mean A LOT, of the Original GunZ. So I had high expectations when playing this game.
Was I disappointed? Yes.
Was it so bad I would stop playing it? No.
The original GunZ had a few things that are missing in the new one. First off, what I see as "K-Style" in the game, appears to be I would say not really "K-style" as it is so easy and oddly ineffective. The ineffectiveness comes from the fact that many people are just running around shooting you which is way more effective here than it was in the first game. Also, classes are an intresting thing I didn't find myself as happy as I should've been. The original GunZ didn't have classes; so if you wanted to be a grenade launching maniac with a shotgun and a pair of dual katanas, go right ahead. Here you're restricted to the weapons your class is alotted to. Such as a Sword, SMG, and Sniper rifle for one class, or a Mace, Assault Rifle, and Grenade Launcher for another. Also, many of these classes I find to be a tad broken. By broken I either mean overpowered. Max, for example is just a running Pain Train that can flamethrower you in seconds before you can even defend yourself. Like you'd have to be extremely lucky to avoid a flamethrower Max. Plus Max's weaknesses, can only count in games such as Team Deathmatch. Max in Team Elimination? Better hope you hit first, because you can't parry or block if he does. And it's not only Max, some characters have a sense brokeness in one way or another. In particular, Wayne's wide range stunlock whip, or Rose's stunlock High damage Rocket Launcher.
This next line was supposed to comment on the how screwed you are if you're ping was too high, but then again, Maiet is based in South Korea, so I'll cut them a little slack, as much as I hate lagging in EVERY GAME.
Another annoying thing I found was the Campaign. I remember the Old Campaign as being a fun round for a few games that you could've done yourself. I always used the old Campaign as a way to practice my "K-Style" when none of my friends were on. Now, Campaign is a gamemode I just can't play anymore as it is next to impossible to complete on your own. The First Level is still isn't done for me. And the fact that it is has a time limit, really makes it unecessarily challenging for those who play Campaign on their own, like me. Additonally, Campaign for me was fighting Goblins, Lizards, and Skeletons, that was more interesting than fighting a bunch of soldiers who can't fight seem know which end of the rifle is the shooty end.
As much as I complained and ♥♥♥♥♥ed about the crap above me, I'll talk about why I still play it.
Apart from experiencing good ol' nostalgia, its still the same challenge I had when I first started the Original GunZ. I still get the same feeling of acomplishment when I knock a Max into the air and headshot him so I can charge up my Q to kill the Loli and Gay Cowboy infront of me so I get the triple kill. Its that odd sensation of doing something so impossible that lets me come back. As much as I would like to see more players play this game, knowing the steam community, I'd prefer not have an entire army of Max's up against me in a Team Elimination.
The only changes I'd make is probably fix the broken characters (Max, Wayne, Rose), and see what you can do with the Lag issue. If I'd add anything, I'd add Island and Prison from the Original GunZ map. On top of that, I'd like to see Colesseum changed so that it matches more closely to its original counterpart. (I want my old pitfalls of death back!) But if I were to reccomend this game to anyone, it'd be Koreans, people who played GunZ: The Duel, and people who play games like Guitar Hero, DDR, and other timing based skill games.

While it's not the same glitched, K-Style, ButterFly GunZ:The Duel we all knew and reminisced about from our gradeschool days. GunZ 2: The Second Duel is such a great continuation.

Thoroughly enjoyed playing this in local co-op mode with a friend.  It's in early-access currently and some areas like the menu's do show this.
Fantastic that the developer has made the decision to make this online co-op, some of the puzzle solving will probably require some form of communication between players to be most efficient, e.g messaging at the minimum, VOIP as a preference.  Obviously for couch play you can shout at your mate when he doesn't do the right thing at the right time!!
The game itself and the mechanics involved really are great fun and it's teamwork all the way!  The game involves you and your partner switching between characters (a large one and a small one) to progress the level via obstacle style puzzles.  After the first couple of levels changing forms can result in the death of your team-mate which can lead to some hilarity, if you swtich forms whilst your large team-mate is standing in deep water making him take the small form and thus being submerged and drowning!!
The optional challenges also involve completing the level in set times and the Gold times are set at a level where both players are going to have to operate as a very smoothly oiled machine.  Any mistakes and you probably won't make it, but really satisfying when you do!!  Also there are stars to collect with one bunch of them hidden somewhere secret in each level.
Highly recommend this if you are looking for a puzzle-platformer with co-op mode.

Preface: This is coming from a guy who has played Tekken his whole life.
If I could give this game an informative review, I would, but, as I'm not a curator, I'll just say positive. My first big issue with this edition of Tekken is the strange roster. Don't get me wrong, this is one of the most interesting casts we've had in a long time, however, that doesn't change the fact that a lot of characters are missing, and they took their distinctive playstyles with them. Furthermore, there are DLC characters that have meters, as well as one base game character with a meter. If you're anything like me, you played Tekken because it didn't have meter, and felt complex enough on its own to not need one. Regardless, I can look over that.
My second complaint is the idea of rage. When you boil it down, rage is a reward for loosing. If you're getting your face kicked in, worry not, because you'll earn rage, granting you control of the space! Hooray for loosing and playing poorly!
Although I have issues with this version of Tekken, it is still Tekken. Although it's not the exact same as every other Tekken we know and love, this one isn't terrible. I guess I recommend it, but, let’s just say I'll be abandoning this once SCVI goes live.

So im just going to start by addressing the micro transactions. I dont really pay attention to the big store button as it doesnt effect my gameplay. My vote is purely on the game in its current state. We're voting on the game not the choices of a greedy publisher; and seriously who cares if they sell praxis and credits- if you honestly need to spend money on those to progress in the game you're bad.
ie: Who gives a negative review to a product if the the irrelevant part of the product was bad? like an amazon product thats good, with a mess up in shipping gets a bad review?
That being said I continue my review, and if you are a deus ex enthusiast there is stuff to be said:
PROS:
+ The hand crafted alternative ways of handling situations are far better in this than HR (vents)
+ It feels like stealth has a lot more options this time around with the new Augs
+ Game is Beautiful
+ Voice work is well done
+ The models are much better this time around
CONS:
- Story is lackluster, kinda just sad
- Not really a con, but the microtransaction (its not p2w, its more like pay to cheat)
- The mouth sync is god aweful
- Mouse Sensitivity
- ONE MAJOR CITY, Deus ex is about traversing the globe hunting down the conspiracy, even HR knew that with the places you would visit. In this game you are stuck in 1 and 1/4 cities (Golem is a linear doom 3 kinda map)
- Weird bugs, a lot of people have all kinds of bugs. Mine was going into the shooting range crashed my game.
- 1.5 bosses
- Story seemed to be chopped off right at the end as the conclusion came so fast i was expecting more. (see DLC for the whole story I guess...)
Pro's and Con's aside, after beating the game, I can say the game leaves a .. 'bad taste in your mouth' kind of conclusion. HR was far more wholesome as a deus ex product/experience and maybe the dlc will be the missing parts of what the game was meant to be. But for now I can recommend this game (when it goes on sale), purely that is still a good game, just not what my expectations were of a deus ex product.
All in all I would give it a 7/10 good, not great. Which merits a recomendation at a lower future price.

I'm 28 hours in and I only just left Prague for the first time after thoroughly exploring it, doing all the side missions I could find, hacking everything, and generally just being a severe completionist type poking my nose everywhere and KOing more people than necessary to ensure I could safely run around danger areas to make sure I didn't miss anything.
The game has only been out for 5 days and yes, it was inexcusably buggy on release and still has many issues to resolve.  The release was _clearly_ rushed by whomever had the final decision, and it is suffering a lot of poor reviews as a result.  They should have waited a week or two to fix the bugs, sometimes broken/confused AI, rare crashes, and occasional unproofread text with typo/grammar issues which are clearly unintentional (some are intentional as spoken in the voice of a character).  The five or six splash intros ought to give you an idea of how many people had their hands in the pie, so I imagine it was a bureaucratic mess.  There are a few other minor issues, but those cover the major ones I think.
My PC specs are Win10 Pro, i5-4670K 3.40GHz (no OC), 16GB RAM, GTX 970, and a decent SSD.  I optimized the game in Nvidia experience and have had _zero_ slowdowns and I have very fast loading times; 30 seconds max the first train I took, usually 15-20 seconds on all trains after that.  Loading from main menu takes about 10 seconds and from quicksave, about 3-4.  Game has run at 60fps for me consistently so far throughout all of early-game Prague at very decent settings; geforce turned off some of the more intense lighting effects but largely everything else stayed at high settings and AA got boosted to make up for some stuff being downgraded.  I'm either one of the lucky ones, or people suffering from performance problems are a vocal minority.  Dunno which it is.  I'm sure it'll get addressed before long in any case.  This is why I usually don't buy games until they've been out a long time with plenty of patches, but I've loved Deus Ex since the original and had to go full fanboy on this one and saw the day 1-4 bugs in all their glory.  Although if it was really bad, I would trash on it, like Invisible War was trash, and more recently Fallout 4 was trash.
I believe have had four CTDs in my 28 hours, which isn't too bad for a rushed release, and the save system is abusable to hell and back so you don't have to worry about losing progress unless you never learned to backup often.  You can save as much as you want so long as you aren't in a fight.
It seems clear to me that they put a huge effort into level design in this game, with Prague outclassing anything I remember in HR.  There are just so many little human touches to the area(s) that it's clear they spent a significant amount of time on this, perhaps at the expense of some bugs which they felt were of less importance in the long run as they can't really go back and revamp levels, while they can patch bugs.
I feel that they made a better effort to make all of your augs useful pretty consistently, which I don't really remember HR doing quite so well.  You will run into many more areas where a wide variety of augs will come in handy and it won't be a huge problem most of the time whatever you have chosen, although if you're playing stealth and/or completionist, some become much more of a necessity than others.
The inventory system leaves a bit to be desired... hopefully they can streamline the UI a little bit in that regard, but it's been very manageable so far for me.  I rarely ever go into my main inventory at all except to sell or store things.  Really, the inventory wheel is all you need most of the time.  The hacking UI needs a KB&M upgrade, however.  It's pretty clunky and you can't zoom out enough much of the time.  It's not terrible once you get used to it, but it shouldn't take quite so long to get used to it as it does and perhaps needs some more customization options so you don't click on the myriad popped-up buttons you don't intend to.  There is a huge amount of hackable stuff, so this problem presents itself quite often.
The microtransactions are totally unobtrusive and hidden in a little shop menu.  It's very obnoxious on principle, but I can deal with it.  If someone wants to spend extra cash to OP their character in a single player game, whatever.  It's multiplayer games where that stuff is really inappropriate.  It's worrying that it might become a precedent, but that's hard to foresee especially given the backlash microtransactions always present, as seen in many of the negative reviews.
In conclusion, having played all the Deus Ex games many, many times over the decades, I don't feel like this one has sold me short so far.  I think there might be a little bit of rose-tinted glasses effect for HR (and some others even), although that was an amazing game and I haven't played it in a couple years.  I just don't remember it being _that_ much better than what I've run into in MD so far.  It's possible (and probable) that MD won't be able to match HR's story, but that's a pretty high bar to meet in many ways.  But if things keep up, and especially if good patches keep coming, MD will surpass HR in many other ways.
I'd say if you have a good system (try to have recommended specs), buy it now and deal with some relatively small issues, or else wait six months or so and get it on sale after its had numerous patches.  Either way, I think it's a solid game.  Or wait and see if they do a directors cut in a year or so.  In any case, game recommended.

RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is chock full of addictive fighting gameplay. Combo's (and their respective counter), special abilities, skills, etc. Whatever you'd expect out of this sort of game is pretty much there. Landing combos or countering attacks is satisfying and using your ultimates and other abilities is as well. Each of the four characters differs slightly and has different potential on the field to support one another. Scrounging for artifacts and experience orbs is part of the fun all while you explore through different familiar areas of Remnant. Playing with your team is really a joy.
New enemies -
- that seem unbelonging come into place, with glaves, machine guns, and grenade launchers. It's a jarring disruption in the flow of the gameplay as players are forced to try and hit extremely slim counter windows, suffer through long unescapable enemy combos that can instantly kill if more than one of these enemies attacks a player, and a bothersome repitition of these enemies area after area when they feel as if they should be part of a boss fight. This keeps going on, and eventually rooms become smaller and smaller until you reach wave fights and the final boss fight. The final boss fight -
- is incredibly underwhelming and tedious, with only one mechanic to attack it and no change in the flow of battle to challenge the player. In my personal time playing I have not had a teammate or myself become incapaciated to the boss. Besides the repetetive and boring nature of the fight, the music pauses before it's loop, and really doesn't pump the player up enough for a "final" boss fight.
Besides the fluidity of the game, there are challenges to unlock new abilities. While the abilities that span all the characters are easy enough to get, the character specific challenges are almost unobtainable. It takes several runs to complete them, (Each run being about two hours, depending on how fast your team is, and if you're alone, thats a whole different story.) and once you see what they are, you'll wish you hadn't grinded for six or seven hours just to unlock them.
It gets worst.
With the Official Release has come a ranking system. Once the player achieves some goals, they'll be able to prestige. This is absolutely not worth the shiny little number that appears beneath the players portrait. Essentially, prestiging resets the entirety of your progress. Now, this could be expected of a prestige system, but typically in other games a player who prestiges is able to retain their achievements, challenge unlocks, etc. Points, abilities, and level resets are just fine, but once the player sees that they must redo all the far fetched challenges to unlock the abilities again, the sensation is incredibly discouraging, and squashes any satisfaction gained from prestiging after all the player's hard work in the first place. Some of the challenges are in fact reasonably achievable. Killing a hundred Grimm for Blake's team attack mastery was no issue, but killing four hundred Grimm for an ultimate mastery is really reaching for the stars, especially since you'll be hitting prestige before you're even able to unlock the ability.
Despite the wildly unobtainable challenges, break in fluidity after Forever Fall, and incredibly poor ending, RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is still absolutely fun. It's satisfying to play the game if you can ignore the challenges, story, and grind. If you buy Grimm Eclipse, come in looking for fun and not diffuculty.

I really wasn't expecting much, being a beat em' up title, but I was genuinely pleased with the end result. Before going into the review I will say two things though.
1. I haven't attempted multiplayer
2. I've only just completed the first level
3. I've only played as Yang
When it comes to gameplay, this feels like the type of game that would benefit greatly from having a more free-flow combat system, like the Batman Arkham series of games. It also feels like it tries to emulate that, with a dodging and counter mechanic, but I don't really see much a point to countering half the time, when I can just finish my combo and dodge. To that extent, the game may give the illusion of not having enough challenge, but it can really catch of guard (even in the first level). While it started off slow, with enemies dying in one combo generally, it picked up and I found myself dying 4 times before completing the first level. It's nice to know the devs kept that in mind when making the game, because challenge is as essential to the beat em' up as enemy diversity. Speaking of which, I'm not going to comment on that, because I've only played the first level. That being said, there were 4 types of enemies.
Going into the actual fighters, I feel that it's a bit misleading to call Yang's 'ranged' attack a ranged attack. I found myself missing constantly just by not getting close enough. And even when I did get close enough for the shotgun particles to land, it didn't do much damage. Even at close range. I found that it was essentially a useless addition, because her other combos can space, stun and just generally **** up the enemies. I'm hoping that this doesn't apply to Ruby and the others, because (to my knowledge) they actually have proper ranged weapons in the anime.
I didn't like the leveling up system much. Mostly because, it didn't actually feel like my character was getting much of an upgrade, until I got the initial upgrade to the ultimate. The trees need to be added to, and branch off maybe, to add a little bit of player choice and depth to it.
Graphics wise, I couldn't tell much of a difference between the various settings (ranging from potato to ultra). Of course, having 'Bloom' enabled made the game look much more fantasy like, but that was all that can be said on the graphics. It kind of looks like a happier version of World Of Warcraft. Or a smoother version of Dungeon Defenders (1). Which, mind you, isn't something I have a problem with.
The sounds in the game are alright. The starting enemies didn't make many, and the background music didn't really add much to the play. Like with any beat em' up, I wish there was a button to turn off unneccessary grunts. Their alright at the beginning, but they get annoying very quickly.
That's all I have to say on the game. Over-all, it's a fun beat-em'-up with quirky humour and a knack for letting you beat the **** out of the enemy. Which, in my opinion, gets it a solid 7/10. My opinion may change as I play more, but for now, I'd recommend grabbing a group to play it with.

I was running out of new things to do in under an hour. Adding new inventory to my store isn't "new things to do," either. It's just higher-priced/more varied stuff for customers to hopefully buy.
You might think I hate the premise of a shopkeeper game, but I actually love the idea, and there's a game I
recommend at least reading reviews on: Recettear. It's not a perfect game, but it's cute, has a really good economy, and I was internally fist-pumping and whispering "Yes!" excitedly when I made fantastic sales to customers in-game. My only advice is to make sure you have plenty of physical inventory instead of just raw cash, because it's easy to lose, and you lose all your money when you gameover, but you keep all your inventory! It's kinda like a new game plus that you'll have a much, much better chance of winning. It's a nice game!

Five years after Tekken Tag Tournament 2, Bandai Namco gifts fans of the fighting game genre with the long awaited
. This time PC gamers are finally able to enjoy it on their beloved machines as well.
Tekken 7's main story takes place right after the events of Tekken 6 and focuses on the Mishima Bloodline. Most of the story is told through in-game cutscenes, while some moments are simply images with dialogue. There's a total of 14 chapters, a special chapter and one episode for each character. Unfortunately the story is rather disappointing, the character episodes way too short and their endings were propably the
in the series. The arcade mode is with its 5 stages shorter than in previous games. In Treasure-Battle mode, you fight against an endless amount of opponents and gain money as well as customization items for each victory you obtain.
What makes Tekken 7 a great experience is fighting other players online. Ranked Battle Mode is for achieving a personal ranking and online stats, Player matches are the same as Ranked Matches, but without any ranking or Leaderboard placement involved. You can also join and host Tournaments with up to eight players.

I like to start this review by giving LootCrate a shoutout... I would of never heard of this game if it wasn't for getting this gem in the form of a product code through LootCrate. If you never heard of LootCrate, Its a mounthly subscription box with that comes with all kinds of goodies.. Shirts, Toys (Pop Figures), mouse pads, and some random things randomly every month...
Now on to this game.. If any of you ever loved playing Smash Bros at all.. Any of them.. This game is for you... Its not as great graphicly, But the style more then makes up for it.. It is a beautiful game with great sounds and music.. Anyways, This game controls exactly like a Smash Bros game does.. Every button is a move, and every diretion with combination of the buttons is a move.. Sounds basic, but basic in this form is great.. Anyone can pick up this game and do every move each toon has to offer.. I don't like to have to download and memorize move sets for each toon of a game.. I want to pick it up and play.. Don't get me wrong, the Mortal Kombat style of game play is great, but this games being simple to learn is one of the many things that makes it great..
There is enough toons in the game to fit your style, and each one right now has 3 move sets.. During gameplay you will start off bare fist.. As I said, every button and every direction with combination of button is a move.. Then you have 2 types of weapons that drop.. One is normaly a light weapon like a 1 handed sword, other is a heavy.. Each weapon style also has it own set of unique moves.
For the devs of this game.. There is more we can improve on.. Just as some of the Smash Bros games had.. I would like to see Tile Sets to be able to make my own Brawling Zones (maps)... This would be simple to add and gives something for the community to build upon the game, and get together to share content..
Overall, I rate this game a 4 of 5.. And its a solid 4.. One thing holds it from being a 5 and thats the level making aspect.. I would love to see this added in game.. Not a tool you use outside the game that can be hard for players to learn... Point Click and Plop.. Level is done, using the tile sets of the game.. This being said, you can even add where you can buy tile sets, just like you have with the skins..

I must admit that this is the first Deus Ex game I've played longer than a few minutes. That being said, I was a bit suprised at how cinematic this game was. Guess from a far it seemed like Deus Ex series was mostly an above average FPS with a bit more emphasis on the story lines (It's not). So this game is a breath of fresh air for me and it even managed to pull me away from Doom and Project Cars. The game looks wonderful on very high and ultra settings and the story is mostly good...Not great. Music is excellent and very relaxing. Most the characters are entertaining and the moments where you do have to battle really feel organic.
As far as the graphics go... I must've been spared the headache I keep hearing so much about. Running an FX 8350 with an R9 390 (minor overclock on both) and outside of the whole MSAA thing (Direct X 12 will hopefully help a bit come September) I have had no issues running the game on very high settings with all the other bells and whistles on and still get somewhere between 50-55 fps on average. Turning off MSAA altogether can get the same 50-55 fps on ultra settings. C'mon Direct X 12, just get me another 8-10 fps and we have a deal.
All in all, very cool game. Adam Jensen's voice bothered me in Human Revolution, but seems to have finally grown on me. The game did seem a bit daunting at first with all the options, upgrades, side missions, buttons, weapons, etc... but the game won me over, and I tend to think most games nowadays are too mediocre to bother finishing. But I can really see the effort and detail and this game succeeds because of it.
8/10... If Direct X 12 bolsters the performance even a little, then I give it a 9.
***Update after about an additional 20 hours and Direct X12 Beta***
After a bunch more time under my belt, here are some things that stand out.... On the positive side, the ability to play the game over again with all the goodies is pretty cool. Batman Arham City did the same. I still enjoy the scenery, especially at night. The gameplay is very polished now that I am very familiar with the buttons.
On the negative side... The occasional crashing is kinda crappy. Though the developers have been pretty fast with the patches. So I can't be too mad about that. Direct X12 beta gave my fx 8350 a slight bolster, but still not enough to think about using MSAA and keeping a 50+ FPS average. We'll see what happens when the real version hits.
All in all, still give this game a great score as is. I am able to use a mix of ultra and very high settings and keep the game at a 50-55 fps average. People who claim that the game blows, and yet still put in 30 hours or more, need a reality check... Break down the 60 bucks you spent into the number of hours of entertainment you got out of it. i've put in 50 hours and can honestly say I got my money's worth and then some. Was this an all time great? No. But for every 1 all time great game, I can show you 50 really awful ones. So calm down and drop the "I got ripped off" or "microtransactions ruin the game" act. You are slap fighting an already lost battle and at least Square Enix had the decency to not go all Mortal Kombat X or Destiny about their micro transactions. And I hate micro transactions just as much as the next guy... but face it guys, we're the minority on the micro transactions debate. If we were the majority, companies would've responded accordingly.

An atmospheric and darkly amusing puzzle platformer where the aim is to deal with the pesky archaelogists digging into your home. Initially you can move through the walls and chomp anyone nearby, and possess boulders to drop on the hapless intruders heads, or chase them down.As you progress through the games a couple of new mechanics are introduced, such as a limited use teleport system to make some slightly more complex puzzles.
As you progress you will also unlock pages from the diary of the lead archaelogist on the site, which exposes their mission and more about why they are here, the impact your actions are having on the team (firstly disbelieving despite all the missing team members), and also as they dig deeper you learn more about yourself (via what they are learning), and what you are doing in this long abandoned city.
Overall it is pretty good - the puzzles don't get too repetitive, and I didn't find them either too easy (once any new concepts have been introduced), or too hard - you get stuck occasionally and have to think your way around the map, but the possibilities aren't endless, so it is difficult to be stumped too long.

The Dweller is a minimalistic 2D puzzle game with some unique ideas. You control an eldritch monster who needs to get rid of archeologists exploring an ancient underground city. Your movement is quite restricted, however, as you can only move through solid rock or by possessing boulders.
The visuals are very basic and frankly little bit amateurish and boring.
The game has no real video options and doesn't support 16:10 resolutions.
The audio is rather basic too, but it gets the job done and sets the mood nicely.
Most of the puzzles are built around your limited ability to move around. You need to kill (or scare away) all the archeologist in each level. To achieve this, you need to carefully manipulate the boulders and make sure you don't get stuck.
As you progress through the game, new elements like teleporters are added in but they don't really add much to the core gameplay. The game has some interesting levels, but overall I felt that the puzzle design was little bit uninspired.
Finally, in the last few levels you are given the ability to freely roam around which makes the game much more action-oriented. Personally I felt that this was the weakest part of the game.
There are a few harder levels but overall I didn't find the game particularly challenging.
The controls are bit strange and somewhat imprecise.
The story is very simple and it's easy to skip some of the story notes as you have to manually access them.
I didn't run across any major bugs, but the way boulders sometimes get stuck on each other definitely felt bit glitchy.
The Dweller is an ok puzzle game with some decent ideas. Unfortunately the presentation is rather amateurish and overall the game is somewhat unpolished. I'd only recommend the Dweller to big puzzle game fans.

Gameplay:
This game can be odd and very hard to pick up when you first start, But it is very friendly to keyboard and mouse players instead of alot of games that need you to have a controller. You just have to use WASD right and left click, and spacebar. Thats it, its very easy to pick up after you realize all of your moves. You dont instantly start off with a weapon. Items drop from the sky such as bombs, mines, spiked balls, and your weapon. Each person has one weapon that will match to another person. You have drills, swords, hammers, and a stick thing. (Forgot the name ;~;) But each person has different stats. This game is early access so everything isn't in play yet. Such as if you were to buy it right now all of the characters would be unlocked, you will have to unlock them later when the game is out of early access, then it will have some free players and for payed players they will have a rotation for that.
Competitive play:
There is competitve game play, there must be in every game that wants to prosper. In this competitive you have 3 ranks so far, Bronze, Silver, and Gold. Each one getting more and more harder people to fight. There are harder moves to do inn competitve, such as dodging, LEARNING your mains moveset, and also learning to fight without a weapon. Some of the people in competitve are very friendly and say GG after a match, unlike others that just leave right after. You will run into the same peoplethat use the same main. This is why you have to stick with your main and be a low teir god.
Casual play:
With competitive they have casual for..casual players. Instead of being 1v1 like in competitive you go in a 4 player FFA. They have all the same moves, items, and rules. So it really isnt different. The same thing goes for the people in competitive, some can be rude and others not. But in casual you arn't going to find the same mains over and over. This is where most people train combos for their main. They can also use training in vs CPU mod.
My Thoughts:
As a person that plays alot of Super Smash Bros. I can really see where they got their thoughts from. You attack people over time and the more they get attacked the farther they launch. But you cant shield, you cant grab ledge, and you cant just roll away and spam projectiles. As some classes have pistols they only fire close ranged. Most sword fighters in Super Smash are like the people with the guns in this game having to wall the other player out. But not like Super Smash they have 2 weapons instead of just one. I find this to be very creative and you can even drop them at any time!.
Why should you buy this?
This game really isnt like some combo crazy game like Mortal Kombat, MvC, or Super Smash Bros. Melee. This game is more trying to get as much damge racked up and is very friendly to new players, as a new wave of them had just come out today becuase of Loot Crate giving out codes for this game. If you like games much like Super Smash Bros 4. This would be the perfect game for you. But if you like combo crazy games you should try and stay away. There is currently another game like this that I'm pretty sure will be less friendly to keyboard and mouse players than last, and has a big learning curve just like Melee, with wave dashing and such.
If you buy this game, have fun with it!

TD;DR: Shift Happens is a great Platformer that makes maximum use of its great and unique machanic. Best played with a friend. You should get it!
Long version:
Shift Happens is a puzzle intense platformer featuring two characters who can switch their masses (One is always small, while the other one is huge). The developers make what is in my opinion the most out of this great mechanic! The puzzles are very well designed, as are the levels.
The singleplayer works surprisingly well. You control both of the characters (one at a time) and have to puzzle your way through the levels. The learning curve is very nice, and in later levels it can get very tricky - which I love!
However, the focus of the game lays on Coop. The devs really understood what Coop-fun is based on! You'll have to play together, think together and coordinate your actions to succeed. BUT: Every player has an own coin-count and you're able to trick your mate and steal his coins. Damn, it can be so fun to challenge your friendship!

"old schooler" passionate of this kind of games, having started to play them since Wolfenstein and Doom, i have to admit that, altough this is a little fps and has nothing special, it is fun enough to give you a couple of hours of entertainments, so, why i gave this game a thumb down ? It's simple, just because of the horrific insane amount of technical problems and issues it carries with him.....
The first serious problem is the frequent number of crashes happening in the game, it happens mainly when you load a savegame or checkpoint, tested on a win7 32 bit, the specs of my PC fully cover the minimum requested but could be that a 64 bit OS with more Ram and more Video card Ram could solve this (can't test right now).
So, this said, even with this problem, i was giving anyway a thumb up to the game, yes, with a low score, but always my feeling was positive, so, what is the REAL reason i am giving a thumb down ? I'm going to explain right now.....
The quicksave and quickload system in the game is totally devastated, BUGGED as HELL.....
I readed the forums and the web and discovered originally the game had just the checkpoints, meaning that if you die between 2 you have to restart all over, this at easy difficulty and for expert players is not a big deal, but for new players and, anyway for everyone, when you play at ludicrous difficulty(the max one) you'll notice that you could die like a Boss even a dozen of times in some special points, so, being forced to restart the whole checkpoint everytime could be very annoying, and here the community asked the help to the Devs who kindly worked on this problem and changed the game adding the savegames in the form of quicksave and quickload (just one slot and no manual saving options).
I have to say that this is extremely useful and save you the life lowering the number of suicides among the players...
But, IF and WHENEVER you load a savegame, many bad things could happen and i will try to add some examples:
Sh*t number 1 : there are, in some points, firewalls or fireballs that shoot alternated and the only way to pass trough is to pass between them, penalty, instant death, so, after a loaded savegame could happens that ALL the fireballs shoot no more alternated but all together making impossible to progress the game and forcing you to reload the whole checkpoint.
Sh*t number 2: There are some secret areas in the game that you have to discover all if you like to complete a map 100%, so, after you load a game, could happen that when you pass trough the secret zone, the game not count it as discovered, forcing you to reload the checkpoint.....
Sh*t number 3: to complete 100% a map you also have to kill all the enemies in the map, now, not all the enemies appear in the zones normally, for some you have to do some specil stuff, for example, some enemies appear only after you picked up a special power up item called God mode, now, after reloading a saved game, happened to me that even after taking the power up item the enemies did not appear, forcing me, guess what ? Yes, to reload the whole checkpoint.....
I could continue with other examples but i prefer to stop here, i just let you know that, reloading a saved game could make no more open some doors, not make appear some enemies, not making any more move essential platforms, walls, various devices in the game, all of these, if you're a completionist  but also if you're not and want just complete the level, forcing you to restart the checkpoint or maybe the whole map.
I think that a game with these problems, altough could be nice at first sight, can't be recommended, so, whenever all of the above problems would be fixed, then feel free to convert my review into a positive one with a score of 69%, but at the actual status i have to give a thumb down because all of this is not aceptable.

I love this game so much already <3
Gameplay:
This game can be odd and very hard to pick up when you first start, But it is very friendly to keyboard and mouse players instead of alot of games that need you to have a controller. You just have to use WASD right and left click, and spacebar. Thats it, its very easy to pick up after you realize all of your moves. You dont instantly start off with a weapon. Items drop from the sky such as bombs, mines, spiked balls, and your weapon. Each person has one weapon that will match to another person. You have drills, swords, hammers, and a stick thing. (Forgot the name ;~;) But each person has different stats. This game is early access so everything isn't in play yet. Such as if you were to buy it right now all of the characters would be unlocked, you will have to unlock them later when the game is out of early access, then it will have some free players and for payed players they will have a rotation for that.
Competitive play:
There is competitve game play, there must be in every game that wants to prosper. In this competitive you have 3 ranks so far, Bronze, Silver, and Gold. Each one getting more and more harder people to fight. There are harder moves to do inn competitve, such as dodging, LEARNING your mains moveset, and also learning to fight without a weapon. Some of the people in competitve are very friendly and say GG after a match, unlike others that just leave right after. You will run into the same peoplethat use the same main. This is why you have to stick with your main and be a low teir god.
Casual play:
With competitive they have casual for..casual players. Instead of being 1v1 like in competitive you go in a 4 player FFA. They have all the same moves, items, and rules. So it really isnt different. The same thing goes for the people in competitive, some can be rude and others not. But in casual you arn't going to find the same mains over and over. This is where most people train combos for their main. They can also use training in vs CPU mod.
My Thoughts:
As a person that plays alot of Super Smash Bros. I can really see where they got their thoughts from. You attack people over time and the more they get attacked the farther they launch. But you cant shield, you cant grab ledge, and you cant just roll away and spam projectiles. As some classes have pistols they only fire close ranged. Most sword fighters in Super Smash are like the people with the guns in this game having to wall the other player out. But not like Super Smash they have 2 weapons instead of just one. I find this to be very creative and you can even drop them at any time!.
Why should you buy this?
This game really isnt like some combo crazy game like Mortal Kombat, MvC, or Super Smash Bros. Melee. This game is more trying to get as much damge racked up and is very friendly to new players, as a new wave of them had just come out today becuase of Loot Crate giving out codes for this game. If you like games much like Super Smash Bros 4. This would be the perfect game for you. But if you like combo crazy games you should try and stay away. There is currently another game like this that I'm pretty sure will be less friendly to keyboard and mouse players than last, and has a big learning curve just like Melee, with wave dashing and such.
If you buy this game, have fun with it!

As a huge RWBY fan, this game actually dissapoints me quite a bit... There are good pieces, however the game is just lacking the depth and length it needs for a $24.99 full on release.
The good:
Co-op
Game feels very responsive and fast.
That's about it....
The bad:
Combat gets very repetitive VERY quickly
Very few enemy types (I believe only 8-9 including the final boss)
Poor leveling system
Only 4 characters (more probably released as DLC)
Abilities feel useless when you find the OP one (not balanced)
Boring, generic story
Combat doesn't make sense.... it almost feels like they were going for the Arkham games style here, but it just feels very wrong. If you ever get into danger in combat, you can just spam air dash to regenerate your health within a few seconds and continue fighting. The only times I died were when I got wombo-combo'd by the androids. The leveling system seems to be not that well thought out either, because it requires you to kill a certain amount of enemies with each ability to be able to level it fully. This either forces you to spam one ability and make the combat even less fun, or ignore it completely and not be able to level any of them fully (we're talking 300 kills with each ability). If you level up your heal rate, you can be full health in about 5 seconds out of combat. Tougher opponents don't feel tough, because 1 move will take 1/4 of their health after you counter their wind-up. This game in singleplayer took me about 3 hours to complete max, and there doesn't seem to be much replayability. I hit level 10 (max level) waaaaayyy before the final boss because the chess pieces you find will give you tons of extra XP that isn't necessary. This game just doesn't feel well polished, as there were areas that it didn't want me to go into, but still could because of the air dash, which ended up resulting in me finding more chess pieces that it didn't want me to have.
As a huge RWBY fan, this game is a let-down, and I would definitely wait until the game is more well polished or more content is added for a $24.99 price point.

Take some of the best metal music in the world, voices/cameos of Ozzy Osbourne, Jack Black, and Lenny ( amongst others) and make an open world action tribute game to the metal god Ormageddon.  Play as roadie Eddie Riggs (Jack Black), who is transported into the world of metal. You arn't alone, you gather the humans surviving and fighting in the metal world and gather a metal traveling tour to rock out your enemies into flame and lighting. Eddie gathers special solo guitar abilities and allies of the metal world while completing missions, opening up special buried metal relics, racing against other car lovers, hunting crazy creatures of metal, and rescuing snakes in this open world. Use fans gained from merchandise booths to summon your metal allies to the field to take out your opponants stage. The only complaints I have is the multiplayer is dead, so no crazy concert battles and the driving of the Druid Plow is iffy. It can be completely touchy and hard and setting the game from brutal to normal or gentle may be necassary.  DECAPITATIOOOOOOOOON!

Gameplay
I was pleasantly surprised when playing this game for the first time, I thought it to be a general action game from what I saw, but in fact most of the combat is done in the form of RTS with the main characters being your General/Hero. I would recommend playing the game on at least medium difficulty as easy wasn’t enough of a challenge me personally.
Story
The world and the story is what truly makes this game a stand out, if you are at all a fan of metal music you will probably find some enjoyment from the games setting and story, with some great cameos and easter eggs. The game is also very much a comedy, with some absolutely badass but stupid moments littered throughout.
Graphics/performance
Graphically the game obviously has a cartoony style, which my turn a few people off, but it looks great and has a genuinely cool style for a metal fan. Due to that style the game ran without issue for me, and should run well on most systems.
Value
To be honest I got the game for free so it’s hard to say I got good value from it, but if you want a truly entertaining game with a good few hours of gameplay then I can recommend picking up the game if it goes on sale.

BrawlHalla is an absolute gem with a lot of potential in it's later versions. However, that does not mean that this game is without flaws. Here is an in depth list of what is positive and negative about this unique PC fighting game experience:
+
not a Super Smash Bros clone. Brawlhalla brings new moves and aspects to the table and is a refreshing experience for a Smash Bros Veteran.
+Each character has a unique playstyle, even if weapons are recycled between them. The signature moves have a lot of variety, and can be used for epic combos.
+Online is slick with little to no lag (I have only encountered about 2 laggy matches throuhgout my hours of playing time).
+Long wait times to get into matches are basically nonexistent. Great job on the devs part.
+Progressive leveling and reward system incentivises playing and making a goal for yourself.
+Gameplay is fun, hectic, and requires skill. No two matches are the same, and the items help pprovide good variety.
Unfortunately, that does not mean that this game is perfect. (Many of these cons will probably change of the negativity will not be as bad as the game progresses through early acces and into the full version)
-The items can sometimes result in cheap deaths. The bombs and mines should spawn in less frequently or the devs should make new items.
-The MallHalla is a good place to buy different things, but the fact that the prices are way too high for cosmetic items, and the fact that there is no way to earn this exclusive currency without buying it, the cosmetics will probably not be bought that much.
-Lightly toxic playerbase. I encountered about 5-7 rage quits and after another match, my opponent was very negative in the ingame chat.
This final section is things that are sort of "meh"

~The menus are sort of disorganised. I wish there was a proper title screen that you got before thrusting you into the menus. Also, the bar of "unimportant" menus, such as legends or settings, should be raised up and closer to the rest of the menu. Finally, I belive that the gamemode menus should be condensed into Couch Party, SinglePlayer, and Online.
~The background doesnt zoom along with the stages. Furthermore, there is a slight lack of stages at this time.
In conclusion, I believe that this game has a lot of potential and I definitely reccommend it for anyone who wants a good brawler and can get over the minor quirks. Trust me, they really are minor. Thanks for reading.

I picked up this game cheap, at 75% off.  Even so, I do not recommend this game.  The reasons why are as follows:
Pros:
- Great artwork, very stylish and colourful.
- Great voice acting.  Every line is voiced.
- Huge number of quests.
- Inventory takes a decent length of time to become full.
- Character customisation is okay.  Not good, just okay.  It gives your fighter/theif/mage/hybrid archetypes, as well as a few appearance options, but not much beyond that.
Cons:
- No mod support.
- There is so much artwork, the game suffers from open world syndrome (too big, too empty).  Have fun running around forests and caves for your whole life.
- Though the voice acting is great, the writing is atrocious.
- Quests are BORING.  Even the main questline is BORING.  The best premise the writers could imagine was this:

Everything else were fetch quests or kill quests with no variety.  For the most part, the quest-givers were mewling wimps.
- Lockpicking "minigame" can eff off.
- Combat is too easy.  You will rarely encounter anything tougher than a mere trash mob. "Reckoning mode" will trivialise the rare boss fight.
- The only difficulty occurs when the combat animations lock you in position.
- Camera is garbage.  I needed to run a 3rd party program, and all it ccould do is change the FOV.  But even this was desperately needed!  Also, in combat mode, the camera feels drunk.
- Music is repetative.
- DLC chest in the first village is pointless.  The epic weapons and armour set are replaced after a few hours.
I am indifferent about the ending and other DLCs, as I don't feel the incentive to finish.

An adequately fun time-waster if you have a couple of friends around with nothing better to do, but it lacks technical depth and diversity. The "weapon system" is interesting at a glance, but it trivializes character choice and simplifies gameplay to the equivalent of a Smash Bros. match where beam swords and baseball bats spawn perpetually all over the stage and can be casually discarded with little to no recourse.
If you're looking for something simliar, try out Samurai Gunn and keep your eyes peeled for Rivals of Aether.

The Dark Project is a classic, a very dated classic however. I remember beating this game when I was much younger and remembering how difficult it was. Thief 1 and 2 have probably the least amount of hand holding that I have ever seen in a game almost to the point where it’s a detriment because the levels are so massive that you would very regularly get lost and it does get quite frustrating and takes the fun out of the game because you spent quite a bit of your time in these games just trying to figure out where you need to go and what you need to do. I never found the hand drawn maps to be ever useful when I played this game, it always just looked like a clusterf*ck and I could never pinpoint where I was so I never used it and always ended up relying on my memory of everywhere I have been in the level to forge a map of my own in my head. Thief has a decent story with a cool protagonist but I was never a fan of the supernatural aspects that the story goes to and that story also reflects on the later stages of the game as well because you will be visiting catacombs, crypts etc. I feel like that takes away of what the core of the franchise is supposed to be which is thieving. There is also just some awful levels thrown in there like the Thieves Guild in particular. The controls and movement are very clunky and the stealth mechanics are pretty basic now looking back but the highlight of this game was always and still remains the levels themselves and how massive and detailed they are and how you navigate them to complete your objectives, that is what still makes this game worth trying out today however as a pure stealth game today I don’t think it’s better than the average stealth game out there right now.

Deus Ex has some good and bad, but if you are cautious enough to read a review, then I recommend this for you. If you enjoyed Human Revolution, then this is more of the same with improvements all around. The gunplay and stealth mechanics have improved, world exploration has more paths and rewards, and visuals are pretty good. The story doesn't have a lot of bite, but there are a handful of entertaining side quests. I have a pretty modern rig, and am able to run on medium graphics preset with good framerate. The tutorial level in particular was more stressful on my PC than the main hub of the game.
There is a microtransaction store on the ESC menu which sells credits and praxis kits for an unreasonable amount of real money. As a result, praxis kits in the main game have inflated costs to try to steer players toward buying them through the micro store. There are items in-game that push players to use the companion app for the game, I haven't tried this because I have no interest in downloading an app just to unlock an item. With that being said, I don't think either the microtransactions or the companion app pieces detract from the game because they are both optional and easy enough to ignore.
Overall, there is some shady business practices that are riding the line between reasonable and ridiculous, but beyond that there is still the Deus Ex game you know and love. If you can put up with some mild hail corporate moments, then buy the game. Otherwise, don't buy the game and let Square Exix know why.
Had a great time playing it. Has a very interesting story, can't wait for the next installment.

Did you like Human Revolution? Then you'll absolutely love Mankind Divided. There's a lot of people complaining about microtransactions. I'm here to tell you... those people are crybabies and idiots.
Microtransactions: The microtransactions are completely unobtrusive to the game. I repeat: the microtransactions are *COMPLETELY* unobtrusive to the game. You are literally swimming in praxis in the game. It even gives you like 12+ Praxis at the beginning of the game to spend. Likewise, much like in Human Revolution, you have the chance to buy two more praxis per "zone" and find two or three more praxis per zone hidden. If you are sneaking around, hacking everything, exploring, etc., you will find plenty of XP to level up and get Praxis. The microtransactions are there for people who want them. I might not like microtransactions - but I have no problem with them as they are unobtrusive.
Performance: Performance, however, is a bit of a wild card. I am running on a 4GB GTX 960, 8GB of RAM, and an i5-2550k @ 3.40GHz 3.80GHz. This is enough for my setup to run the game on High settings. The game seems to have the most trouble when loading an area for the first time. Performance is weird in that, people with GTX 1080s, are reporting bad FPS. That said, I know plenty of people with higher end cards running the game on Ultra at 60FPS. I recommend that, if you are unsure as to whether this game will run on your system, that you turn off a few things. MSAA is terrible. Do not use it. Use Temporal AA. It's good enough and less cost heavy. Likewise, Volumetric Lighting and Contact Hardening Shadows can be a bit of a strain on your system. I can leave them on most of the time; however, as I mentioned before - the transition between new areas or "hubs" causes temporary dips in frame rate every now and then. My recommendation: if you want the game? Buy it. If it doesn't run for you? Get a refund. Though, I'll tell you now - most of your FPS problems will be in the "HUB" area and not the tutorial. Which took me close to 2 hours to get into because I tend to play at a slower pace. Be aware of that when looking into refunds.
Moving past the issues of microtransactions and performance, I'm having a blast. This game is incredibly fun. They've taken Human Revolution and just made it a better game in general. I think I spent like ten hours just clearing the tutorial and exploring the small part of the first "hub" area. There are a few side quests to explore and unlock. Plenty of things to hack, steal, and places to break into.
Options: There are plenty of options in this game to choose from. You have your typical nonlethal options, lethal, as well as a variety of ways to tackle missions. For example: I play Stealth Nonlethal. I typically stun a person to get them out of the way; however, if you manage to sneak without touching anyone or being noticed? The game actually acknowleges your achievement. Certain NPCs will thank you for doing your job, thank you for sparing people, etc.,
Augmentations: They've taken a lot of your augmentations and added upon them. Without going into too many storydetails you have access to a lot of cool augmentations. Anyone remember Trigun? Yeah. Your arm can turn into a PEPS gun and fire a huge burst of energy to knock people down. There's also the TESLA augment which is a longer range stun which can be upgraded to mark multiple targets. Remote hacking makes the stealth game very fun. I got it later in the game, so I'm not sure how useful it is *early* but it lets you disable things. Cameras, turrets, robots, enable wirelessly controlled platforms. Turn TVs and radios on/off. A lot of options. There are even some lethal options. Like firing your nanoblades, and some tanking options. These augmentations are all experimental, however, and require you to disable unused augmentations to avoid glitches in your system.
Crafting and Customization: There is a crafting system in the game. Throughout the game you can find crafting parts. These can be used to craft things like biocells, special ammo for your augs, and a few other things. But you can also use these parts to upgrade your weapons. Now, on the downside to this, I'm playing as a Nonlethal Stealth person right now. The only options available to the Stun Gun and Tranq Rifle, as far as I'm aware, is just ammo upgrades. But if you're using lethal weapons... There's quite a bit more to it. Upgrade the accuracy and such. At any point in the game, you can press Y. This opens up your weapon menu as an actual animation, and you can toggle things on/off. Have you been discovered? Remove your suppressor so it does more damage. Going up against augs or robots? Switch to EMP Ammo. Or hold R to do that quicker, but I like the menu better. It looks cool. There's also options for Fire Rate depending on your weapon.
Story: I have nothing to say about the story. Story is subjective. No one can tell you how you might enjoy the story. I will say: I've played all of the Deus Ex games. It'll never be as good as the original but it is just AS good as Human Revolution. That is enough for me. You are caught up in an investigation into terrorist attacks. It parallels certain struggles in real life when talking about augments. Racism is a huge factor in the game. Prague is basically City 17 from Half-Life. Checkpoints, corrupt guards, etc.
In short: The game is great. You will enjoy it if you liked Human Revolution. Just be careful if your system can't run it.

The Dweller is a Puzzle game about a group of young, daring, and probably attractive archaeologists who gradually fall victim to a monster in a cave. Of course, considering that you're the monster, it provides a neat twist on those familiar with the adventure genre.
The goal of each level is simple: Kill Indiana Jones, to do so you are granted the ability to meld into walls and possess rocks to munch, crunch and generally disqualify them from any upcoming beauty contests.
The game is controlled entirely with the mouse and it all works rather well, there was some performance problems where I couldn't move a rock I was posessing, but a few clicks remedied that and there was never any time where that issue caused me to fail a level. Oh, and there was one time where I somehow managed to posess two rocks at once which was kinda weird.
Basically the game is a bit rough around the edges, and unfortunately the game is rather short. I 100% completed the game in only a few hours and felt that the ending (even though narrative is clearly not a main feature of the game) was weak since how you perform in the final level does not affect the outcome from a narrative standpoint.
The puzzles themselves are well thought out and do fill the player with satisfaction upon completion, and the new game mechanics that are gradually added throughout the game are well balanced.
I feel that if you are uncertain about purchasing the game, wait for it to go on offer. Either way, I garauntee you'll have a good time with this one.

Shift Happens is a cooperative puzzle platformer where you play as one of two creatures that end up sharing the same mass. Since they share the same mass, when one creature is large the other has to be small and vice versa. The two creatures can change shape at any time. Many of the puzzles in the game are designed around this premise. This mechanic is interesting and the developers have created some puzzles that do a good job utilizing it.
While the single player levels are better than I expected, the multiplayer is the best part of the game. I played the multiplayer local co-op so I can't comment on how well the online co-op works. I thought the game did a good job of keeping both players active in the puzzle solving making it that no one player can take control over everything.
At this early stage of early access there are a couple issues that will be hopefully resolved through further development. In around 2 hours I completed all but the most recently added levels. I also found the puzzles to be kind of easy. I play a lot of puzzle platformers though so that could be a contributing factor. As the developers add more levels I think both issues could be resolved.
Note: I received a free review copy of Shift Happens. Other than receiving a free review copy I received no other compensation for this review and it had no impact of the content of this review.

Pick from multiple rifle classes, a captain, flag-bearer, surgeon, carpenter, or musician, and join the war as the British or French. Holdfast is the type of game where you want to be very careful with your shots, because reloading a musket takes a long time and leaves you vulnerable in the process. To compensate for this, most shots will kill instantly if they hit. This means that the most effective ways of killing your opponents are to form lines, or rotate shots with other players. The game is fun, but can be a bit tedious since most of the time you're either aiming a shot, or reloading.
The community makes this game much more engaging. Often when you spawn, people will be forming groups to reinforce current battles, or start their own. When you get a group that actually listens, you can form a solid line and accomplish more than you could by yourself. Also you are guaranteed to hear at least one baguette reference if you're on the French side. You do get some players who enjoy blasting music as loud as possible, but the P key opens up a mute menu where you can look for the green speakers next to names (green implies they are using their mic), find that player, then mute.
There are a few downsides to the game:
1) There is no auto-balancing of teams, which leads to one side having 10-20 more players than the other.
2) Some of the maps are unbalanced as well. There is one map where the French start next to a giant hill, and they will tend to camp that hill and take shots from it the entire game, and they will win because the British have hardly anything on their side of the river.
3) The melee mechanics could definitely use some work. There's a hint of Mount&Blade combat here, but due to most hits being 1-hit kills, nobody tries to use the blocks. Everyone spams attacks and prays. Like the gunplay, your best chance at hitting is to slightly lead your opponent and hope your weapon follows them.

This is a game which, like the 1990s game it remakes, is not designed to be taken seriously.  The shooting action is old-school mayhem and gore-filled, which is what every 1990s first person shooter tried to do.
Is it something you should get?  Absolutely.  It's also quite silly, with a campy "B-movie" vibe that is reinforced with stupid one-liners, absurd weapons, over-the-top voice acting, and scatological humor.  It's like the worst action movie ever made, video-game edition.
The good:  Fast pace, incredibly bloody (if you like that), goofy humor, creative stunts, solid gameplay, solid multiplayer, overflowing with secret areas, hilarious narration, and an unbelievable amount of fanservice.
The bad:  It will take some time to discuss the bad.  It tends to be very specific in nature.
The major contention with the game has to do with the stunts.  Jump pads, egads, and various traps from the 1990s game are all back, and many sections are all about pinpoint movement and platforming, and not so much shooting.  This makes the game strangely similar to Portal, seeing that there is no fall damage.  But unlike Portal, it's easy to screw things up in annoying ways, which forces a LOT of backtracking and restarts.
About rocket jumping--1990s ROTT invented the rocket jump, so it makes sense it would feature prominently here (many secrets require this).  However, this means you're inclined to try this everywhere, and the consequence is that you end up getting stuck in areas the level designers didn't think you would go.  I mean, come on.  This is ROTT!
Also, the linearity of the campaign.  It's a minor complaint because 1990s FPSes tended to be linear.  But because the story isn't threshed out beyond the B-movie script, it leaves you thinking the game could have been so much more.
Last point:  the bosses.  They sure as heck upped the difficulty of the bosses from the 1990s game.  It's a minor complaint, but many of the tricks that you need to win are not spelled out until you've died a million times already.  And the final boss is cheap on an unprecedented level.
I think the good outweights the bad significantly.  But make no mistake, it isn't a 10/10.

Rise of the Triad is a rather poorly made first-person shooter and a remake/reboot of the original 1994 game with the same name.
To begin with, I found it little odd that they chose to remake Rise of the Triad. While the original game certainly introduced a number of new features to the genre, I never found it a particularly great game back in the day. Still, proper old-school shooters are rare these days so I decided to give this remake a go anyway.
The core gameplay is passable but not particularly good. The level design is often rather boring and the enemy designs are uninspired at best. The game also has way too many first-person platforming sections and the controls are nowhere near precise enough for the jumps you are supposed to perform.
Visually the game is not particularly impressive either and the animations in particular look extremely poor. On a positive note the game does have a pretty good sountrack.
The biggest problems with the game are all the bugs and glitches, however. The AI is absolutely braindead and one of the worst I have ever seen in an FPS. It is very common to see enemies and even bosses to get stuck in obstacles and walls. There's a lot of other glitches too and they make the game rather hard to enjoy. Episode 4 in particular felt extremely unpolished and some sections felt downright broken.
With the lackluster gameplay and the high number of bugs and glitches I wouldn't recommend Rise of the Triad unless you are a massive fan of the original game. Everyone else is much better off playing one of the other recent old-school first-person shooters or the actual classics.

Brutal Legend is essentially Zelda with a classic heavy metal theme...add in a tiny bit of very simple RTS thrown in for good measure.  If you like Jack Black, if you like heavy metal (mostly classic), if you like open word adventure games, chances are you'll love this game.  Highly underappreciated game in my opinion!
Graphics <Amazing> - While clearly last-gen, they actually look more than passable on PC and I've been routinely surprised by little details as well as texture work (skin texture in particular looks great).  Animation is average, very "metal" I guess.  But what makes this game shine is the overall grahpical design.  Everything in this game screams medieval metal and it works extremely well.
Sound <Amazing> - The only way I feel like somebody would not enjoy the sound in this game is if they absolutely despise Jack Black and heavy metal.  Not just not enjoy it, but you'd have to despise it.  The soundtrack, voice work, sound of the car, etc etc etc, it's all amazing and compliments the graphical style perfectly.
Gameplay <Decent> - For most of the game, this plays like a metal-Zelda.  There's dungeon like areas, open worlds, vehicles, and bosses. You can upgrade your weapons, having both an axe (as in guitar) that essentially works as your magic, and a literal ax which works as your sword.  Most upgrades change both function and appearance.  You can also change outfits, put on jacket patches, and upgrade your car both visually and functionally.
Where the gameplay takes a bit of a dive are in the RTS sequences.  Best bet for these is just cheese your way through them, they can be a little fun just because of their large scope and soundtrack...but mostly these parts are just areas to "get through".  Don't let them be something you miss this game over though!
Overall <Amazing> - For me, this is a game that just about everybody should try.  I thorougly enjoyed it and I didn't think the RTS areas were anywhere nearly as bad as many people make them out to be.  The soundtrack, the little graphical details, even many of the side missions...tons of care went into this game and it shows.

At its core, Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning is an action RPG with equal parts Skyrim and Torchlight, so much so that I starting calling it KoA:SkyLight in my head. While I have had a good time playing SkyLight thus far, the depth of the quest system and the lore is nowhere near as enjoyable as Skyrim, and the action becomes repetitive somewhat quickly.
After about 40 hours I started simply started speeding through the main quests for achievement hunting, since 95% of the quests boil down to standard ARPG tropes: Person A needs help and requests your assistance, sends you to Place B to collect Items C or kill Baddie D. This *can* be enjoyable, however the inventory system is pretty awful compared to other similar games, leading to a lot of backtracking to sell your junk to the nearest market. And since there are so goddamn many vendors in each town, and I had 700k+ gold after 40 hours, I had to rely on the interwebs to tell me that there are multiple places which sell backpacks to increase the carrying capacity.
The combat is enjoyable, but not particularly balanced. You can run across a specific dagger early in the game in a side-quest which makes nearly all enemies for many, many levels significantly easier, and chakrams are pretty over-powered when it comes to crowd control. This lack of challenge with combat and the ease of finding upgraded equipment makes you feel like God-mode is constantly on after about 20 hours. Couple this with a couple items which each increase your experience gain by ~5% means I might have some difficulty getting the "Out of Your League" achievement on my first play-through.
Overall, I would recommend SkyLight, but with a few caveats. If you're looking for deep lore, complex quests, and an immersive feeling world, then you'd be better off playing Skyrim. If you're looking for challenging and deep combat with good balance, you're better off playing another ARPG. However if you're in the mood for an enjoyable, relaxing, kill-loot-repeat game, then give KoA: SkyLight a look.
