This game starts off as a pretty interesting little puzzle platformer, but ends up packing a surprising emotional punch.  You control both the titular two brothers on their epic quest with one controller simultaneously. The controls can be a little tricky at first, I often had each brother running in the opposite direction to where I wanted, but you get used to it quickly enough and it even becomes a bit of emergent gameplay as you send one brother off into the unknown first, while the other tries to stay close behind. Characters are voiced in a fictional language, so it's up to the animations and tone of voice to convey how each character feels about what's going on, which they do a superb job of. All in all it's a game where all its elements come together to be greater than the sum of its parts. It's short enough to finish in one afternoon, and if you pick it up during a Steam sale it's definitely worth the price of a cup of coffee.

For starters, I've wanted this game very badly ever since I watched a few streamers play it in early access. The "Welcome to Brawlhalla!" intro engraved its way into my psyche. Soon after it came out, I was lucky enough to get the game for free as a beta tester, andI couldn't be more excited. I recited the intro and immediately went into 1v1 ranked matches, ready to enjoy the game.
REAL REVIEW BEGINS HERE:
This is a Super Smash Bros. esc. game with tight controls and an EXTREMELY competitive environment. As recent as the release date of this game was, players have already began to practice their favorite legend and invent new metas to keep up with the rest of the community (which is entirely necessary due to the influx of new players.) Some people may argue that the legends (characters) are too similar. While this may be a valid point, all legends have very different play styles. Special attacks are diverse even when performed by two different legends wielding the same weapon.
Once you've learned all of the basic tactics and general gameplay, you have to get yourself used to an entirely new segmant of the game that isn't as prominant in other Super Smash Bros. exc. games, aerial combat. While legends cannot fly, they get three jumps, and a special attack on top of that. That, coupled with the ability to dodge midair, gives way to a large, aerial segmant of gameplay that makes Brawlhalla much dynamic.
I've begun to ramble so I'll wrap this up. In summary, Brawlhalla is a game that should be bought and enjoyed, regardless of it being on sale or not. Thanks for reading, and Welcome, to BRAWLHALLA!

What is up everyone I hope you are having a wonderful day. Early access is always a risky gamble but here’s one where the risk is literally almost free. We’re tuning into a 1v1 ranked match in Brawlhalla and we’ll kick started it with that.
So far I will recommend this game. However, I do not suggest you buy any additional items at this time unless you are willing to try and be part of what could be the next big "super smash" on steam. ***This game has improved since it's inception*** and has added some major updates to refine and introduce new features. As the big giant blue sign says though, the game is early access.
In short, Brawlhalla is melee with the giant exception most of the battles can be fought in the air and some crazy and odd combos can be strung together. Also, here is a cool feature off the bat : the loading screen to play another online game let's you battle it out with AI's while waiting. Unlike Super Smash Bros. : Melee specifically, the game doesn't have a "fast" feel to the game play. Rather, the game is smoothed out and requires proper timing (and the right button) to deliver an effective blow. The game is played generally in the air but the ground attack specials provide for more than enough umph and entertainment. The challenge to out whit your opponents seems equal at almost all odds. Some players will choose to take a precautious route while others will be willing to sacrifice themselves for a win.
Brawlhalla mimics in it's corridors super smash. It is because it seems as the first reference to come to mind. On the other hand, it isn't as I feel the strategies are really diverse and open to the player. There are character limitations and powers in both games but changing and throwing weapons distinguishes brawlhalla. Getting knocked off the map has become avoidable with all characters. When you think you're dead or when you have no chance, it seems playing fields are almost even all the time. The edge of the map is a different game entirely here from smash. Think of kicking a soccer ball versus a golf ball. Being able to slide on the edges opens up a new dynamic (and possibilities) for both players. It seems as those who simply wait to strike at vulnerable times seem to win the most.
The game is persistent in it's work to differentiate itself from smash. Is this a good thing or bad thing you may be asking yourself? It's neither really, until the game is done then a full judgment can be made. The scoring system seems to play the odds of K/D ratio's while the HUD display simply shows it's awesomeness in the top right (although I wish that awesomeness was a tad bit bigger in sprite size)! It's tough sometimes keeping up with the fights, but the camera does a pretty good job of keeping you right where the action is. In other words, the zoom is definitely on the right track. Multiple game types make this game phenomenal. I can jump online with friends and play a free for all or play some two player ranked. It's actually pretty nice to see considering it's in the state it's in.
There are weapon drops in the game which resembles smash, but unlike smash, you're allowed to throw away your main weapon at any time. There aren’t random weapons like smash but there is some variety. The weapon-drop will drop and can be picked up within a certain time by anyone. Each character is given two weapons consistent of axes, guns, spears, swords and not limited to javelins. In this sense, some characters have preferred fighting choices and when unlocked, can change their fighting stances (which can modify stats slightly but limited to local game modes only at the moment). Items are a nice addition to the game, and do not feel as though they tilt the odds. The longer the player holds the button down, the more umph goes behind the shot. Items include a spike ball, a bomb, a mine, and my favorite, the horn. The horn creates a line of fire across the screen and even delivers another weapon to the position you blew it from. I have to admit that this style of weaponry is actually nice. It's breath of fresh air as it's something new. If you get tired of using this, try using this instead. Don't like this, go back to the other thing.
Graphics resemble those of Castle Storm but there is nothing wrong with that. The art style is nice and again, sets itself apart from smash. Sounds are good, but I would like to see a variance. Make a sword sound like a sword (even when thrown), and make a javelin sound different than a sword when it bounces off the ground. Stages didn't sit well with me at first, but they do change over time. I felt as though they were a bit small, I still do but I can see why they are the size they are. I would suggest adding some levels that are larger and try to stay away from creating every level about the same size. I do like the physical changes that go on in the map, again another + for being different from smash. If you really want to get creative, maybe add certain objects that can explode, upgrade, or slow down players in certain spots (and maybe make them usable every minute or so).
****SEPT 2016 update
Everything is in good shape and the servers have finally improved. Game play is literally feeling in good shape and would maybe even like to see more mini-games? 4v4 local? Anything is welcomed as there is certainly no shortage on skins. I would also like to see the in-game coins be put to some kind of use in the future. Right now, everything seems dependant on Mammoth Coins. Mind you, these are only artificial changes not game re-structuring ones. I wouldn't mind seeing some more maps added in the future as well. They've been adding characters every so often but no new topography! I'm excited to see what the final-release will have in store.

*Sigh*
This is a little bit hard for me to write a review on, because I actually really love this game and I may be more than a little biased. I've followed RWBY since the initial trailers and followed the game since it was just a little fan game that had enormous potential. I'll give it my best shot, here, for anyone who comes across this. Let's go over what I think about all the things that people talk about when it comes to this game.
*Spoilers*
Combat- Contrary to what a lot of people are saying in it being too simple and repetative, I have to humbly disagree, in my opinion. For me, I rather liked the combat. It was simple, easy to get the hang of, and didn't get bogged down with hard-to-follow combos. Maybe that's just my inexperience talking, but I enjoyed it well enough throughout most of it (though we'll get to the parts that weren't so great... later). For people saying that the characters are all the same, I think you might have missed a few things. They are different, but maybe not in glaringly obvious ways. Yang is a heavy-hitter with a slow-firing weapon. Ruby has fast attack speed with upgrades to make her weapon fire in different ways, such as a lightning bolt that zips across enemies. Good for groups of enemies. Weiss' power is with her ability to freeze large groups and fire multiple projectiles that can drain down enemy health incredibly fast once leveled up. Blake is quick and dashes around, as well as firing her weapon a great deal more quickly than the others. Perhaps this was my opinion, but I found nothing wrong with the combat at all. I enjoyed it!
Story- This... was very disappointing. This story seemed like it was going to be very interesting, with the way it was being set up. I was interested! When the last update had them inside the crates of the ship, leading to who knows where, I was ready to see what the villain was going to be like. I was expecting a flawed character. Based on Oobleck's words, it seemed like Dr Merlot was previously admired for his work... only to be contradicted in a confusing manner by Ozpin who never liked him. It would have made more sense if he merely played a role in what happened. If were caught in a twisted moral, as his words saying Grimm were superior were quite interesting. Especially if he had others who felt the same way and helped to cause it with him, souring his image. That would have been interesting. Nope! He was behind it all! Big, evil baddie! This was the story behind Mountain Glenn, for god's sake! Instead of a good character, we got a goofy Dr. Wily (which I called him throughout my playthrough) ripoff who wins the award for most incompetent villain ever. Seriously, he doesn't stand a chance or pose a single threat the whole game. The story was rushed, I believe. Because, it ends with the Deathstalker battle (which I will be getting to) and no clear outcome to Merlot. Did he die in the lab? Did he escape? Why did it end with no explanation? Story was lacking severely and needed more time, especially if it's considered canon.
Performance- There's no two ways about it, this game will chug when too many enemies get on the screen. Especially for slightly lower-quality PCs and especially for those whose internet may not be up to task. Single player is well and good, but it's a lot more fun with people running around. Four people, for me however, is too much on screen to even attempt to play it. Could be just me, but I bet others could have the same problem.
Graphics/Aesthetic- This is really a lovely looking game, to me. Sure, a bit rough around the edges in places, but overall it feels very true to RWBY. The locations are interesting from Forever Fall to Merlot's lab to the beach area around his island. I was always interested in these new areas and glad to play through them. They were very well done. I think the time and effort they put into making these areas unique shows through. The UI is also very clean and easy to follow, the upgrade menu equally so. They add to the charm and I was very happy that the pictures were added, as they give it a much more game-y feel than it previously had. And, to be honest, it all looks good even on a potato setting (which is what I played it on). The voice-acting is spot-on, especially with Yang and Ruby's VA's really adding that spark to give their characters life. I loved their performances and the others are very nice and true to the show. Now... I feel like this needs a whole explanation of it's own...
The Models- You can probably find it somewhere, but I was actually very annoyed with people who reacted so harshly to the model changes. I found them to be fine, Perhaps not the best, but I was pretty much sure they were just testing things out and trying to find their style. I wanted people to stop whining about it and just let them figure it out. I'll admit I was hasty in what I said, there, and I can understand where people would be upset at such a jarring change. I was, personally, not bothered by it. The old models and the ones after the Forever Fall update have merged into what I call a happy medium. It's not quite the old, but they look better than the FF ones initally did. I think they look lovely and are no longer an issue.
Ranking- This... is one of the worst things about the game, purely in the fact that it resets everything. Those attacks you had to kill a boatload of enemies to get? Wiped every time you rank up. Come on, guys. I can see putting you back to level one, but to not have those attacks and abilities continue to remain unlocked (especially with how much you had to do to get them)? I think you know that's more than a little irritating. Especially when the reward is a small badge by your character. I was not happy when I found out that ranking up did this. Maybe fix this so it's less punishing you for wanting the next set of challenges and instead giving an interesting way to prolong the game with said challenges? Just a thought.
Now...
The Final Boss- This boss has no threat whatsoever. And, it starts out fantastic! A giant, mutant Deathstalker drops down and you're amazed! Until you realize it could only hit you if you haven't already played through any of the game. The Deathstalker has six different attacks. Three of them are in close range, which you will never get hit by in a million years. They consist of the Deathstalker swinging it's pincers futily in the air, spinning, or slamming it's stinger down for you to beat up a little bit. The other attacks include shooting blasts that seem to be purposely trying to miss you, burrowing underground and moving around the area in a way you can sidestep easily, and summoning four enemies. All while Dr. Wily monologues. It's long, it's boring, it's easy.
*Closing Thoughts*
So, from most of that, you'd probably think there's more to dislike than to like, right? Well... Yes and no. I, personally, enjoyed my time with this game. I spent many hours with it and didn't find myself bored save a few obvious parts like the lackluster story and final boss. I enjoy these characters and I enjoy having them beat the crap out of some Grimm. It was true to the characters and let you interact with their world a bit, with good gameplay and some moments where you feel absolutely epic playing as them. If you can look past the story and some of the decisions made (as well as the price tag) and are a RWBY fan, I'd say give it a try. If you don't think $25 is worth what you've been hearing about it, wait for it to go on sale. Bound to happen, eventually. I recommend it only really for fellow RWBY fans looking for a bit of action-y fun that does it's job decently. This is just my opinion, however. Look around and see other points I may have missed. See if you think it's worth your money!

thief is not only the best stealth game ever made but my personal favorite game of all time. Before i played thief i was far too impatient to play stealth games and prefered more fast paced shooters. However when i first heard of the original thief games, the art style and atmosphere alone caught my attention and made me buy it on sale just to try it out. That turned out to be one of the best decisions of my life. Everything about this game is absolutely amazing. The story is beautifully told through cutscenes that consist of hand drawn pictures and live actors in silhouettes. The main character Garrett, voiced by Stephen Russell, has such a badass personallity and doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about anything except making money so he can pay his rent and survive. The other characters like Victoria and Constantine are fantastic as well but i don't want to spoil anything so i wont go into detail. The gameplay and level design is very complex and can be overwhelming on a first play through, but if you stick with it and explore you will have one the most rewarding and satisfying single player experiences in your life. Each level in this game(with one exception) is entirely non linear and you have complete freedom to explore and complete your objectives in any order you wish. In the beggining of each level you are dropped in with just your tools, equipment that the game gives you as well as any you bought before hand. You are also provided with a cruedly hand drawn map that only serves as a general guide, and a list of objectives. Its up to then to explore and find your bearings in the environment and complete your objectives on your own with no waypoint markers, x-ray vision, or any other♥♥♥♥♥♥♥shoved in praticaly every modern AAA game made today to help you. The basic stealth mechanics in this game consist of using the darkness to hide from enemies. You have a light gem at the bottom of your screen that shows you how dark you are, so there is no confusion on how hidden you are.  You can sneak past every guard and be a complete ghost or blackjack them all like some crazy club weilding lunatic. However, if you try to directly confront enemies you will stand no chance. Garrett is extremely fragile and can't take more than 2 to 3 hits, so stealth is almost a necesity. Moving on to the sound, it is perfect. the music and atmosphereic sound design in this game captures the dark spooky ambiance outstandingly. This game has the best soundtrack i ever heard and it is hard to find the words to describe its magnificence.
Over all this is a hardcore stealth game that is carried with an amazing story that will keep your attention all the way through and will make wanting more when it ends. This game is dripping with atmosphere that is conveyed strongly with the visuals and amazing soundtrack. I strongly recommend this game to anyone that enjoys stealth games and heavy exploration that doesn't hold your hand.

As a noob to this old school stealth game, It took me weeks to beat this whole game, but I do like the stealth-ness that it has, especially with how hiding within the dark to avoid detection, and that is how the thief games where born until Splinter Cell came along.

I was lucky enough to play this game when it was released. Still one of the best game out there. This game had everything: charismatic main protagonist and villains (Garrett, Viktoria, the Trickster etc.), a great new engine (Dark Engine which featured new alpha blending, texture filtering and lighting techniques... all quiet revolutionary back than). Great game and level design (It was designed to be largely unscripted; events, instead of being pre-defined by designers, occur naturally.) Great gameplay (Thief focused on stealth and evasion from a first-person perspective, and not full frontal action.) Atmosphere (The game takes place in a metropolis called "the City" which has been noted to contain elements of fantasy, the Middle Ages and the Industrial Revolution.) Cutscenes (They were partly animated, partly made with live actors and motion capture technology). Even today the Thief series is the ultimate stealth game in gaming history. The stealth system was very new when the game was released. The player had to rely on the environment to avoid being detected. Shadows could be used to avoid notice; a monitor on the heads-up display (HUD) indicated the player character's visibility level. The player could lean, crouch, climb, swim and run, among other actions. Surfaces caused varying amounts of noise; for example, carpet is quiet and ceramic tiles are very loud. Enemies were reacting to these factors, and players could manipulate these element of gameplay to distract NPCs etc. Go play Thief:TDS than go and play the rest of the series

In a world full of shooters and rpgs there is really only one First Person Sneaker franchise to choose from. And its a shame because they blew the roof off that genre (and while roof blowing is quite good, it left no other contenders to offer a shot at this playstyle)
Thief Gold sets you in a Medieval timepiece where laws of logic apply to everyone in the game. Sound travels. Light illuminates. And, a thief living on the streets can't win a fight against 3 trained guards. So to get far in this game you must understand the logic behind its design. Walking slowly on carpet can help you remain quiet, while running fast on tile floor will awaken the entire house. Crouching in a dark corner can help you remain completely unnoticed by those around you, while standing next to a torch will certainly get you some attention.
In this game you abandon the rocket launcher and mini gun and pick up a bow and sword instead. However, the most effective weapon in your arsenal is a blackjack. When using stealth, you can silently take down enemies. But they aren't dumb. They will notice bodies, blood, or loud noises and often work together when things aren't right.
As a thief you can maneuver your way in the front door, or you can mantle your way up to the roof and come in through the chimney. You can bypass all the guards and leave without anyone knowing you were there.. or you can draw your sword and make a mess of things. The choice is yours. Planning your next move from the shadows is a really nice twist from games that throw non-stop action at you. In Thief you get to truly experience every footstep, every comment, every conversation in the level.
While carrying out your mission objectives you also get to search high an low for loot. Little is more satisfying that the sound of new coin going into your pocket. Before you find that priceless vase in the safe on the top floor, take a look at the servant quarters and find some extra coin. Then head up to the kitchen and snag a golden goblet. Pass through the bedrooms and find a note that may help you understand a secret hiding an emerald dagger.
A single level can last several hours if you enjoy the ambiance, and this game comes with 16 levels of ambiance, thrills, and chills. But once you are finished, visit the mods page, as there are a few hundred fan mods that you can play as well. Some of them containing quality and polish that surpass the original game levels.
The path is set out. How you choose to reach the destination is really up to you. Run through the lit corridor when the coast is clear, put out some torches to provider the cover of shadow, or take down the guards and walk through like you own the place. You can even throw some objects or use some special tools to create a diversion away from yourself.. choice is supreme.
Over an 19 years after release and still, every single stormy night you can find me playing Thief by candlelight. At least until you try Thief for yourself.. then you will be too busy playing for yourself to bother searching *winky face*

Thief is good fun during its first 4 or 5 levels. You infiltrate a series of blocky but atmospheric mansions, crypts, and tombs in search of other peoples' wealth. Each meaningful action is punctuated by cool-headed narration by Garrett, the cynical cutpurse for whom the game is named. I bought Thief way back in the '90s...when it was new...and I couldn't quite remember why I never finished it...aside from the fact that I played all of the story videos off of the game CD shortly after I bought it and spoiled the story for myself.
Well, now that I've put a good 10 hours into the game in 2016-17, I remember why I didn't finish the game back when it was new. Thief is a great infiltration and head-bonking simulator during its early missions. The problems start to arise when the mansions and tombs become replaced with ugly, maze-like cities and horribly-designed "bonus" missions...and the guards you're so used to non-lethally dispatching become replaced with invincible zombies and spell-slinging liches who don't care about your preference for non-lethal tactics...which is all you've been using up until then if you play the game on Expert difficulty. I went from my very thief-like practice of carefully evaluating the layout of a building and the patrols of its guards, sneaking up behind each guardsman and knocking him out with my blackjack, hiding the unconscious bodies in dark alcoves, then making my way out of the manor several grand richer...to feeling like I was playing a completely different game. A game that was about memorizing the layout of a twisted and recursive green-on-brown cityscape while I was either killing (for the first time in the game) or noisily running from some manner of super-strong zombie or projectile-hurling supercreature. Some might argue that this is a means by which the game steps up its difficulty. Even then, a legitimate stealth game would give you the option to avoid conflict if you're careful enough. Being forced to kill things that are literally in the way is jarring in this kind of game.
Maybe I'll warm to the game's completely different mid-game focus after I'm done taking a break from it. Even if I don't, though, a game that you can get a good 10 hours of fun out of for under $10.00 isn't bad in this day and age. Give it a shot and marvel at that sound direction.

Paparazzi started lining up outside my house, taking my picture and asking for my autograph. About the time that I got around to one of my easiest cases, I was hired to find some black mail on someone for a friend of mine. Rummaged through their mail and their trash cans, and couldn't find anything, I accepted it and started to head back to my client, giving them the results. When I got to her house, she was locked away in the cellar doing something or another and her baby, which for some reason was a vampire, was just sitting there in the forty-two degree weather. I picked it up and started to feed the darling child, waiting for her mother. After about a couple of hours or so she didn't come back so I decided to take the baby. I changed her name to Arya and then turned to a demigod that started following me around ever since I moved into this town, and then had her transform the baby into a human, add her to my family, and then make her look more me. Went home and decided to cut my losses on the case, happy to have a new baby. When I got home I decided it was time for a change, and divorced my wife shortly before an earthquake shook my house and this weird portal thing showed up in my back yard. This strange guy game out and explained to me he was a time traveler named Emit and that his time machine just broke. So I abandoned my ex, and carried my new baby around with me as I started to collect power cells lying outside my house that this guy needed to fix his time machine. After it was up and running, the guy traveled back to his home town and I stepped into the portal, following him to the future with my baby.
After getting set up and realized I had no valid money here, I turned to my demigod friend again and then bought a mansion before I started to set up my empire designing robots. I started to get really good at it, and as time continued it became very hard to do this and take care of my daughter at the same time, so I did what any sensible person who stood atop an empire of robots would do. I made a robot, a very special one, and then persionalized it for my dear sweet child of mine. I designed it after an old video game, and named it Legion before I gave it various personality chips, including a modified nanybot chip. After various tune ups I realized that unfortunately Legion was an outdated model, something I had to acknowledge as the empress atop a robot empire. I went through and made my greatest breakthrough, designing an updated robot that I named Legion Mk II, and shortly afterwards I gave him sentience. I also gave him the ability to feel different moods and such, and then gave him the capability to love. I sold all my other housebots because I decided they were outdated and no longer needed.
At this point I went back in time with my baby, and Legion Mk I and Mk II. I decided to keep the Mk I for old times sake. As I got back home I talked to Emit and told him I wanted to do some good for the world. At this point I remembered my ex, who was still living in my house in the present. I took Arya with me on my quest to turn the future into a Utopia before we went back to the future and I continued to improve my empire, satisfied that the world Arya lived in was now the best it could be, and that she was safe with Legion I and II whenever I was busy. I decided to do some exploring and discovered a crashed alien ship, it was pretty cool but at this point I was really home sick. I went back to the present with Legion I and II and Arya, and then decided to move back to my home town.
It was at this point that I decided to head off to University, leaving Arya behind with Legion Mk I and Mk II, my ex left behind in my old town. Not long after I got settled in, I met a plant person. I was a little confused, but didn't really care. I wanted to get my education as soon as possible and get back to my dear sweet child of mine, and I ended up missing her very soon.

For those starting out, best advice I can give is to go through the tutorial. Once you get the idea of the basics, you can start taking steps further in the DM, Control Point (lvl 15+) and TDM matches that go on. This is one of those games where you really have to practice to get use to the 3D motions and adjust to the mechanics. There is no real way around it unless you have played other 3D flying similators. Rage quitting never helps in the gameplay or getting use to the mechanics. When you run into the higher levels, the level really doesn't mean anything other then gameplay time and how many matches that person has been in. Don't be afraid of being in a match with a higher level. You do get better at the game over time. I won't deny it. Before reaching the status I am at now in game, I had a rough ride in the beginning worse then most starting out now. There was no tutorial and the game only had TDM and DM. I had to learn on the fly and my k/d was actually only a 0.03 from the time I was a lvl 1 to a lvl 8. I had help from players that are sadly no longer around and did pay it forward in helping other new players learn up until the tutorial was released. In short, yes the beginning levels are tough but the more you practice and get the hang of the mechanics, the better you do get in game.
Certain dragons do well with specific builds. That I will admit to in this game. Wrong or bad building mechanic does make a kill per death worse for a player pending on the dragon. When you start getting use to the game, you fall into one of five nitches in game. Aggressor, Support, Marksman, Tansverse or Ambusher are the main nitches in game. The dragon used the most is what helps place a player into that specific nitch when in game.
The maps right now are very detailed but don't trying swimming as you'll drown the poor dragon. Sadly dragons cannot swim in this game or the water is an acid. Not sure which it is though.
Pros: Great multiplayer, different dragon and non dragon type of creatures, very well balanced between the dragon types, Huge maps, A nice mix of both day and night, Nicely detailed with the maps
Cons: Still buggy, a few players still "teleport" (lag in and out) somehow across the map making it difficult to shoot at them. There are a few other minor bugs but not serious enough to be an overall issue at times.
Pretty boring and rough movement. Still good for a game made in consumer grade Unlity Engine :)

This is a little bit hard for me to write a review on, because I actually really love this game and I may be more than a little biased. I've followed RWBY since the initial trailers and followed the game since it was just a little fan game that had enormous potential. I'll give it my best shot, here, for anyone who comes across this. Let's go over what I think about all the things that people talk about when it comes to this game.
*Spoilers*
Combat- Contrary to what a lot of people are saying in it being too simple and repetative, I have to humbly disagree, in my opinion. For me, I rather liked the combat. It was simple, easy to get the hang of, and didn't get bogged down with hard-to-follow combos. Maybe that's just my inexperience talking, but I enjoyed it well enough throughout most of it (though we'll get to the parts that weren't so great... later). For people saying that the characters are all the same, I think you might have missed a few things. They are different, but maybe not in glaringly obvious ways. Yang is a heavy-hitter with a slow-firing weapon. Ruby has fast attack speed with upgrades to make her weapon fire in different ways, such as a lightning bolt that zips across enemies. Good for groups of enemies. Weiss' power is with her ability to freeze large groups and fire multiple projectiles that can drain down enemy health incredibly fast once leveled up. Blake is quick and dashes around, as well as firing her weapon a great deal more quickly than the others. Perhaps this was my opinion, but I found nothing wrong with the combat at all. I enjoyed it!
Story- This... was very disappointing. This story seemed like it was going to be very interesting, with the way it was being set up. I was interested! When the last update had them inside the crates of the ship, leading to who knows where, I was ready to see what the villain was going to be like. I was expecting a flawed character. Based on Oobleck's words, it seemed like Dr Merlot was previously admired for his work... only to be contradicted in a confusing manner by Ozpin who never liked him. It would have made more sense if he merely played a role in what happened. If were caught in a twisted moral, as his words saying Grimm were superior were quite interesting. Especially if he had others who felt the same way and helped to cause it with him, souring his image. That would have been interesting. Nope! He was behind it all! Big, evil baddie! This was the story behind Mountain Glenn, for god's sake! Instead of a good character, we got a goofy Dr. Wily (which I called him throughout my playthrough) ripoff who wins the award for most incompetent villain ever. Seriously, he doesn't stand a chance or pose a single threat the whole game. The story was rushed, I believe. Because, it ends with the Deathstalker battle (which I will be getting to) and no clear outcome to Merlot. Did he die in the lab? Did he escape? Why did it end with no explanation? Story was lacking severely and needed more time, especially if it's considered canon.
Performance- There's no two ways about it, this game will chug when too many enemies get on the screen. Especially for slightly lower-quality PCs and especially for those whose internet may not be up to task. Single player is well and good, but it's a lot more fun with people running around. Four people, for me however, is too much on screen to even attempt to play it. Could be just me, but I bet others could have the same problem.
Graphics/Aesthetic- This is really a lovely looking game, to me. Sure, a bit rough around the edges in places, but overall it feels very true to RWBY. The locations are interesting from Forever Fall to Merlot's lab to the beach area around his island. I was always interested in these new areas and glad to play through them. They were very well done. I think the time and effort they put into making these areas unique shows through. The UI is also very clean and easy to follow, the upgrade menu equally so. They add to the charm and I was very happy that the pictures were added, as they give it a much more game-y feel than it previously had. And, to be honest, it all looks good even on a potato setting (which is what I played it on). The voice-acting is spot-on, especially with Yang and Ruby's VA's really adding that spark to give their characters life. I loved their performances and the others are very nice and true to the show. Now... I feel like this needs a whole explanation of it's own...
The Models- You can probably find it somewhere, but I was actually very annoyed with people who reacted so harshly to the model changes. I found them to be fine, Perhaps not the best, but I was pretty much sure they were just testing things out and trying to find their style. I wanted people to stop whining about it and just let them figure it out. I'll admit I was hasty in what I said, there, and I can understand where people would be upset at such a jarring change. I was, personally, not bothered by it. The old models and the ones after the Forever Fall update have merged into what I call a happy medium. It's not quite the old, but they look better than the FF ones initally did. I think they look lovely and are no longer an issue.
Ranking- This... is one of the worst things about the game, purely in the fact that it resets everything. Those attacks you had to kill a boatload of enemies to get? Wiped every time you rank up. Come on, guys. I can see putting you back to level one, but to not have those attacks and abilities continue to remain unlocked (especially with how much you had to do to get them)? I think you know that's more than a little irritating. Especially when the reward is a small badge by your character. I was not happy when I found out that ranking up did this. Maybe fix this so it's less punishing you for wanting the next set of challenges and instead giving an interesting way to prolong the game with said challenges? Just a thought.
Now...
The Final Boss- This boss has no threat whatsoever. And, it starts out fantastic! A giant, mutant Deathstalker drops down and you're amazed! Until you realize it could only hit you if you haven't already played through any of the game. The Deathstalker has six different attacks. Three of them are in close range, which you will never get hit by in a million years. They consist of the Deathstalker swinging it's pincers futily in the air, spinning, or slamming it's stinger down for you to beat up a little bit. The other attacks include shooting blasts that seem to be purposely trying to miss you, burrowing underground and moving around the area in a way you can sidestep easily, and summoning four enemies. All while Dr. Wily monologues. It's long, it's boring, it's easy.
*Closing Thoughts*
So, from most of that, you'd probably think there's more to dislike than to like, right? Well... Yes and no. I, personally, enjoyed my time with this game. I spent many hours with it and didn't find myself bored save a few obvious parts like the lackluster story and final boss. I enjoy these characters and I enjoy having them beat the crap out of some Grimm. It was true to the characters and let you interact with their world a bit, with good gameplay and some moments where you feel absolutely epic playing as them. If you can look past the story and some of the decisions made (as well as the price tag) and are a RWBY fan, I'd say give it a try. If you don't think $25 is worth what you've been hearing about it, wait for it to go on sale. Bound to happen, eventually. I recommend it only really for fellow RWBY fans looking for a bit of action-y fun that does it's job decently. This is just my opinion, however. Look around and see other points I may have missed. See if you think it's worth your money!

My review for this game has gone from, "don't buy it just yet", to, "tentative reccomendation", to "yeah this game is alright" and now it's a straight up "don't buy at all". And here's a rundown as to why that is. The short TL,DR is: not enough content, poor optimisation, too high price tag, doesn't have full controller support, boring.
I am a fan of the show. I am a fan of Rooster Teeth. I enjoy the RWBY community a lot, the show is fun and the fans are surprisingly less cringey than most fanbases. But this game isn't good and the fanbase say it simply because it's a RWBY game that exists and that's good enough for them. For me, simply being something that exists that many people want does not make it a good product.
For starters, the retail price of this now "finished game" is £19 or your regional equivalent. As you can see I have 5 hours clocked on this game, and that's all I want to play. That's a few times through the early access campaignn, and the now finished full campaign. In terms of value for money that's appalling; the game is so lacking in content it questions the neccessity for such a high price tag. Realisticallly if this were £7.99 AND I were a fan of the show, I would consider it a fair price, but nearly £20 is too much.
The combat is dull and there is no tutorial. Now, I don't expect the game to handhold me all the way through, but I would like it to explain some of the abilities and how to use them. Because it gives you nothing, at all and just expects you to pick it up as you go, which would be fine if not for the inexplained team attacks that jjust sort of randomly happen as and whenn the game chooses. On top of this, the game is unbearably simple. Light attack, heavy attack, ranged attack. That is what you get given, and it's just spamming those buttons for ~2-3hrs (that's the full "finnished" length of the game by the way), with no diversity or variation.
You have linear levels where you run from point A to point B because the game says so, then kill some Grimm, then fight some waves of Grimm, then run along a linear straight line, then protect an objective, rinse, repeat. The game offers nothing past that. It tries to do more with some "puzzle" bit, and a cart escort mission, but that's pretty boring also. Which is a shame, I'd have liked to see more than that, or at least make the waves more excciting, but they're not. There aren't enough enemies to to make the outnumbered co-op hoard battlle thrill a reality.
The voice acting is ok, they actually have the full cast now, but some of the line delivery is cringworthy at best. The visuals are nice, the style is the best thing the game has going for it in all truth. The game somehow runs less well now that it's a finished product, nnot sure what the deal with that is. Oh and it doesn't have full controller support. I own a PS4 architecture pad that works with every other game in my library that I've needed/wanted to use a pad for, but not this game.
In all honesty it's not even a bad game, it's just dissapointing. When I lpayed the very original pre-alpha builld several years ago, I was pretty excited for the prospect of what this would bring. It had so much potential to be this great, Dynasty Warriors-esque game set in the RWBY universe with adventure and quests and upgradable characters, loot drops (yeah the original build had loot drops) and a huge variety of combat options. Now RT have put their best offering on the table I don't really want it. If I could get a refund, I would. I feel somehow cheated, paying into the early access and getting this very mediocre experience at the end. It's a real shame, I wanted this to be fun, but it's not. Even with friends it's just dull. It's as if in streamlining the game, they've lost all the parts that would elevate this to a good or even greeat experience.
The worst part is, I fully believe that the crew working on this game poured a lot of love and effort into this project, and if this is what we get at the end, it's a bit more than "very dissapointing"... Sometimes when you buy into a game you have buyers remorse. You pay for something and it just doesn't live up to the expectation. I get this feeling here, except the huge let down has arrived months later annd I feel like I've been strung along for a pretty garbage ride along the way.

I didn't get the game for free, but it was part of the eidos bundle and I didn't bought it for this game. So I got it without any kind of expectations.
Yet, this game really surprised me. I wasn't expecting something this good for a game that old. Except for the graphics, the game aged well.
Be a ghost. That's the main rule of this game. If you don't like stealth game, don't read any further, look for an other game. Otherwise, this is one of the best stealth based game I have ever played. When played on expert, the game is hard. Don't think fighting can be a solution. You're more likely to die. Ennemies are everywhere and are stronger than you. Your best and only armor is made darkness and silence.
Thief was the first game to implements the shadow mechanic. Many modern game still get their inspiration from it. And it works like a charm. Even if the graphics don't look good nowaday, the immersion is still complete. On every step behind a guard, you'll hold your breath in fear that he could hear you. (Speaking of the guards, the voice-actors and the dialogues are pretty great. You'll frequently want to stay at the doorstep just so you can listen. Even when they don't talk about anything useful to you.) You feel a little weak with all those guards around you. And yet, you'll feel the satisfaction when hiding in a dark corner without behing detected or when you turn off the lights in a room a become almost invisible.
You play Gareth. Even if you have swords and arrows, you are better at playing hide-and-seek than to use them. Most of the time, miss with your arrow and the guard will hear the sound of it knocking on the wall beside him. Shoot him in the head and... it might not be enough. This can go bad very fast. Your best bet is to hide until they're gone and, maybe, lure them off and knock them from behind.
You get your living by offering your services as a thief. You clients will ask for "this" object belonging to "that" man or "this" document belonging to "this" guy. You do it and they pay you. Of course, while you're at it, why not picking every shiny objects you can find? It shall bring you a little extra gold. You may also find "more" than what you were looking for... The story gets interesting. But even without the story, we get to appreciate every mission.
On the graphic side, the game is starting to look old. However, it doesn't break the immersion and you'll be able to distinguish things most of the time. Like many old games, the controls are a bit odd compared to what we find in modern games but after a while you'll manage.
The game also run perfectly. No crash, no issue of any kind. As if it was a modern game. If it wasn't for the controls and the graphics, I could say this game was released last year. As for the AI, it's not always great. Sometimes they can be lured too easily, but its not better in modern games anyway.
If you search for a good stealth game. Buy this one. You won't regret your decision.
Personnal appreciation : 8.5/10

I played a bit of Thief (2014) before but I wasn't satisfied with it (the thieving aspect felt lackluster and dumbed-down). I took some notice however to the praise its predecessors have received. I then bought Thief Gold for 1.74€ on sale, a steal of a deal and it can't hurt. I have played the first 3 missions so far (excluding the tutorial) and saved currently on the 4th which I am nearly done with.
I am absolutely astounded how much fun I have and feel kind of sad that the reboot was distancing itself from its roots.
The sound design is great. It's important to consider the sound you make by walking (different surfaces produce different volumes of sound). You also have to listen to enemies which you cannot directly see and it goes along nicely with the stealth mechanics (hiding in the shadows and judging different lighting conditions).
The levels are usually very large and allow for many different approaches. However, they might be too time-consuming. I spent one and a half hour just for the Prison one. I like the slow gameplay of it (it's a nice change of pace with all the fast-paced games we currently have) but it certainly is unappealing for some.
The AI is hard for me to judge. If I move to recklessly, they will either hear me and scout me out that way or see and aleart other guards. They do feel kind of dumb at sometimes but I can't expect a perfect replication of human behaviour. Obviously not from a game from 1998 and it could make some levels a tad too hard.
The fighting is kind of strange and unnatural, but I'm fine with it as you usually don't want to fight at all or head on.
I absolutely recommend Thief Gold, playing a game barely older than oneself is interesting and I'll definitely pick up Thief 2 and Thief: Deadly Shadows at some point once I'm done with this one.
SOME TIPS BEFORE PLAYING:
The game will probably not support the resolution you're using, to fix that and many other issues, I recommend downloading TFix 1.23 (as of this writing). You can find it here:
The Intro video and mission briefings will not be played properly, I fixed it by running "THIEF.exe" in the installed directory as administrator (Windows 7 64 bit). Thanks for the fix to some person on the Internet who mentioned it.
I already mentioned that I'm barely older than this game so using the default controls was very weird. There is a steam guide which includes "Modern Thief Controls", you can find it here.
You should try playing the game at Expert,  it's a lot more fun trying to finish the additional objectives. Difficulty affects only the number of objectives and number of enemies as far as I'm concerned, so your starting inventory will stay the same.
Buy it, it might be challening, but in the end it's worth it.

I’ve been playing shooters since 1995 and own all major titles – BF series, Planetside 2, Titanfall etc., but none of them held me for so long. I’m with H&G almost since beta release and still very excited about it.
H&G is a hardcore and intelligent shooter with deep customization options and realistic weapon balance – aiming and killing is much more difficult comparing to BF for example. Since you cannot “shoot everyone in the head while running” or “camp with a sniper rifle” (recon class is not OP for many reasons) the gameplay requires a cooperation and strategic approach.
The game has its unique style and atmosphere; you feel like watching old WWII movies. You can spend hundreds of hours in game and it will be still SO much to learn, so many builds and loadouts to experiment with. You can become a deadly CQC infantry or a machinegun defense specialist, fighter pilot or a tank driver.
As for the negative aspects, there are certainly here. H&G has NO FACTION BALANCE. The most skillful German faction is being continuously nerfed, their weapon is seriously underpowered now, I won’t wonder if once the developers decide to put off one wheel from their cars to make Germans win even harder.
Some maps (Mountain town, for example) have design flaws which leads to spawn♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and the worst thing that devs (Reto-moto) ignore most of the reasoned suggestions on their forums.
Unfair weapon nerfes, increased repair and weapon prices, bad map redesign and poor faction balance are turning off veteran players. New ones could be overwhelmed by game’s deepness and difficulty but nevertheless I would strongly recommend it to every wargame lover.

The Dweller is a short, semi-physics-based puzzler about being a big angry hungry spirit. It's brief but it's entertaining, and while the story is told exclusively in text dumps it's actually pretty interesting.

It's not particularly difficult (although there are some definite head-scratcher moments) and is really actually fun, in a sense that only a richly charming casual game can be.

Let's address something right off the bat: Does the game have microtransactions? Yes. But they are absolutely not necessary to progress properly and the only advertisement for them is a "shop" button in the main menu. I didn't even know about those before I bought the game and I played for a good 10 hours before I learned about them at all! Knocking the entire game just because there are ways to power your way through it by paying real money isn't very fair.
If they want to be greedy, so be it, it's not a problem as long as they don't create artificial obstacles for those who don't use the microtransactions... And they absolutely haven't done that, so it's fine. As long as you explore and don't rush through the game (which is what you should be doing in Deus Ex anyway) you will find plenty of everything, including Praxis kits for your augmentations. So let's get that out of the way. It pains me to see so many people giving this game a flat out negative review ONLY because they don't like the microtransactions.
As for the game itself, I think it's very good. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoyed Human Revolution in the slightest. This game improves upon pretty much every aspect of the previous one. The gameplay is absolutely stellar, with more refined mechanics for both stealth and gunplay, new augmentations to try and a decent number of ways to tackle objectives. There is a nice amount of stuff you can find by exploring, which feels pretty rewarding and can really keep you from following your main quest for quite some time since the hub areas are decently sized.
In regards to the main story, it's the most disappointing aspect of this game. The story is decently written and engaging, with some pretty memorable moments and setpieces. However, the ending comes VERY abruptly and the game ends with lots of questions unanswered. It really feels like they have cut this game short on purpose with DLC and/or sequels in mind. It's really anticlimatic and quite a shame when the rest of the package is so well done. The stakes never feel quite so high as in Human Revolution and the finale feels more like the end of an act and not a whole story. I'd say that a big part of the most interesting bits of story in this game is found in side quests and exploration. I still got around 36 hours out of the game after doing everything I could find, and I'm all for quality over quantity so I still think this game is worth its full price... But I can't shake the feeling that they have cut many things that could have been here.
Before I am done, I need to talk about how the game looks. Boy, is it BEAUTIFUL! The graphics technology in this game isn't the greatest ever but it's very solid, and you can really feel the amount of detail and effort that went into the art design and the crafting of setpieces and scenarios. It's like Blade Runner on steroids at some points! I am very impressed with how rich and well crafted the visuals are, the game is clearly a huge leap from the last one graphics wise. There are some ugly things here and there such as grainy interactions between the sharpness filter and some faces, or the fact that body animations (ESPECIALLY lip sync) aren't up to par with the rest of the visuals when in conversations... But those issues are easily outweighed by the beauty of everything else.
I ran into some small performance issues at first, mostly because I was stubborn and tried to run maxed out textures with a single GTX 970. But after adjusting my settings a bit and the few patches that have come out, the game runs and looks very well. Your mileage may vary of course, that's par for the course with demanding PC games, but I believe that anyone who has a rig right around the recommended specs should feel confident buying the game.
Again, get this game if you liked Human Revolution at all. That is the bottom line. Despite having a mediocre story that's on the short side, the gameplay and environments still make it very worth your while.

Hello there,
During this review I will be comparing Holdfast: Nations at War to Mount & Blade: Warband - Napoleonic Wars a lot. Seeing this game takes so much inspiration from the latter, and seeing how much I know and played the latter, the comparison comes up naturally. Furthermore, before starting on this very brief review, I would like to let you know that despite my few 11.6 hours (at the time of writing) on this game, I experienced everything it had to offer within the first five hours, including every single map, mode, and even organized events (linebattles). I am aware that this product is currently in Early Access phase, and I will give my thoughts on how the game currently is.
Now I'm not much of a writer so I'll go over this quite briefly, please forgive me for the poor quality of the text. I will start with a list of pros, to then follow with its cons, which will all be based on a comparison with Mount & Blade: Warband - Napoleonic Wars.
-
It is something that is missing from Napoleonic Wars, and for someone who is quite interested in the naval warfare of the era I thoroughly appreciate this feature, however it is still pretty much barebones. The person who holds the helm has entire control of the ship (you just press either W or S to lower or raise some sails, simple as that) and there currently is no animation for the person holding it. I would've enjoyed more a system where the crew actually cooperates to manage the sails, instead of it all being done through the one holding the helm.
There is no way to angle the sails either, making it look even more simple. Each cannon can be loaded with only two kinds of shots: Balls, and chain shots. Balls are simply used to hit the hull of the other ship. Apart from rare cases when the top of the hull is it and is displayed as destroyed, or when cannons or other small parts are hit and get destroyed, there is not much visual damage on the hull. That means, if you hit the hull of a ship with a cannon ball it will probably look as if nothing happened and it was never touched. Furthermore there is absolutely no way to tell how much your ship has taken damage and how more damage it can take. There is no way to repair the ship, and there is no way to bail water. Simply, once it's taken enough cannonballs, your ship will proceed to sink and you'll have to launch the rowboats to get away. I'm not fond of this, a very very simplistic approach.
The chain shots are pretty weird. Originally, chain shots would be used to shoot another ship's sails, filling them with holes, therefore rendering the other ship slower and easier to catch or outmaneuver. In this game, from what I noticed so far (And I might be wrong, even though I used these chain shots quite a lot), they cannot damage the enemy sails. All they can do is destroy the enemy ship's mast completely, but not damage the sails. Because of this, every single naval battle turns into a "Load chain shots, aim for masts, shoot the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of those masts untill they're down and then come in and use balls", which is kind of ridicolous. There is no presence of canister shots either (this is true for land artillery as well).
One last issue of the naval combat in this game is the bad water: It looks like hair gel, and it's always flat. There's never a single wave, on any map. I know I've put naval warfare in "pros" despite all its flaws, but that is because it's still something more than Napoleonic Wars, which must be taken into account, however don't expect the greatest of systems.
-
: Not much to say about this. Far better graphics than what the old Warband engine can give. Well detailed models and textures, everything looks quite good, except for the antialiasing not working almost at all.
-
: Far more rewarding kills than Napoleonic Wars, be it because of all the score numbers displayed on the bottom of the screen when you kill an enemy, or because one of those numbers is in a bright red.
That's it for the pros. Literally everything else Napoleonic Wars does better.
-
The melee combat in this game is structured exactly as Mount & Blade's, with four attack directions and four parry directions, except that this game got it completely wrong. It results in a laggy, clunky mess with attacks and parries having an annoying delay of one or two seconds each time you hit the mouse button; People killing you when their weapon doesn't even touch you, or people killing you when their attack animation is only at the start, or even when you're too far away for them to hit you. The system suffers so much of that laggy delay that each single melee fights turns into a spinning around spamming the attack button hoping you'll hit them. Absolutely horrible.
-
Yes, I know it is an Early Access, but as I stated prior I am reviewing it for what it currently is. As of now, the only modes available are "Army Battlefield", "Naval Battlefield", "Army Siege" and "Coastal Siege" (might've gotten one or two names wrong), the first consists into killing the enemy team as much as possible untill it runs out of reinforcements (sorta like spawn tickets), the second is about sinking the enemy ships, the third  and last one about controlling fortified areas. That's it. The maps are currently very few, both for land and sea battles. Hopefully there will be far more in the full game, but as of now you can literally play every single mode and map in the very first few hours of the game.
-
A huge amount of trolls. If you don't play in an organized event, a linebattle, but you instead play casually on a server, you'll be experiencing people who spams all sort of incredibly loud music into their mics, destroying your ears (luckily you can mute them by pressing P), and most importantly there are trolls who will ruin your fun when trying to play as artillery. There is no 'artillery' class sadly, so literally anyone can use a cannon or swivel gun, this means that there will be trolls trying to steal your artillery piece each single time you get off of it to reload. Or, they'll jump in front of the cannon (with teamkill being disabled on most of the official servers), blocking you from aiming, and they will just stand there for the entirety of the darn game without ever getting bored of tired.
-
Muskets in this game are FAR too accurate, literally every single linebattle is about shooting the enemy line when they're so far away you can barely see them (due to the bad antialiasing as well). It's more like snipers than muskets, seriously too accurate, rendering the linebattles pretty boring. You just shoot that very small shape in the distance, get some kills, run around, shoot at that small shape in the distance, repeat, repeat, repeat untill the round is over. Being guns so accurate and being combat done so far away from each other this pretty much removes any tactical advantage in going for a melee charge, which pretty much never happens.
-
For a game about Napoleonic Wars cavalry units should be an essential part of the game, however cavalry is not in the game yet. I believe the developers said it will come in future (how future? who knows, soon TM) although  I think it would've been far better if they released the game in EA with cavalry being already in the game. Being the melee combat utter♥♥♥♥♥♥ though, I suppose cavalry would turn into a laggy mess as well.
That's all I can think of for now. I would like to recommend this game only if you truly believe in the project and you wish to fund the developers; However, if you're just looking for a game to play and have fun with, it's currently not recommendable. I will be updating this review in future and if, hopefully, these issues are solved I will be fully recommending this product.

There's a lot to hate about Rise of the Triad and unfortunately, there's very little to like.
I played the original Rise of the Triad when it was first released in 1994. It wasn't the
best shooter out there (that would belong to id software's "Doom"), but it was still a
very fun, 90's campy first person shooter that most of my generation fondly remember.
This remake however, does nothing to rekindle the love of that game.
1) Terrible A.I., surprisingly accurate at that. Even at a distance these bots can hit you
pretty consistently. It also doesn't help that you're going to fight the same enemies,
the same models, over and over again with little to no variation or even intelligence
on their end. They'll happily stand there firing away with little regard for their own
safety, making them more glorified bullet sponges than engaging (even less so
challening) opponents.
2) This game has some of the most frustrating and♥♥♥♥♥♥poor level design I've had the
misfortune of playing through (just wait til you get to the 2nd level's "The Room")
to see for yourself. The golden rule of little to no platforming in a FPS is broken many
times in this game, and the result leaves the player so frustrated that they can't help
but wonder if the developer even knows HOW to make good/engaging level design.
(For the record, no, these developers clearly don't know.) There's little to no incentive
to explore the level either, unless you happen to be a 100% completionist.
3) Bugs, bugs, and did I mention bugs? Holy hell are there bugs. From enemies (or bosses)
getting stuck on walls, behind doors, or sometimes failing to spawn, to game crashes,
poor framerate, etc. The game is 3 years old and it STILL hasn't fixed all these problems.
4) There's little impact on swapping between the characters, unless you really care to
hear their utterly abysmal voice acting. Although tongue in cheek, the game tries really
too hard to be funny, and flops nearly every time it does.
If you remember the old game, stick with the old game. If you're looking for a new FPS
to play, there are dozens more to choose from. Much like Duke Nukem, this game had
its place in the 90's, and seeing the crap job its been given, again, like Duke Nukem,
this game should've been left alone.
A remake that is primitive at best and just not fun. Should have just updated the graphics on the original and resold it instead. All the silly fun of the first one is gone.

I like Rise of the Triad, but I also have problems with it. I have had a few performance problems wit hthe game. Randomly my framerate will drop from over 100 to 14 after hitting a switch, where it'll go back up. Mind you I run DOOM4 at 120fps+ 90% of the time.
The game when you're in combat is really fun, it's fast and there's lots of gibs to be had. There's a good amount of heavy guns to be used and the primary weapons are good enough. To further explain, you get a pistol, dual pistols a machine gun all with infinite ammo and one heavy weapons which hits like a truck but has limited ammo.
You get gruel to heal and if you blast it with  an explosive, it makes the healing items hot and heal more. Which is a really neat mechanic to sacrifice precious explosive ammo for more healing- and you NEED to do this at times to keep in the fight.
Enemies are simple but have a number of tricks to ruin your day. They'll dive to steal your weapons, throw nets on you, roll around.
The levels are diverse enough and can be pretty big. Traversing them however is a bit of a problem. The game asks you to do some platforming which is difficult enough but with how the level geometry works its a right pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ You'll bump little bits of wall or column sticking out that entirely negate your jump. Leaving you to try, try again. This leads me to traps and crap, they'll have these spinning traps that go around to cut you up and it can be a pain to get by them. They'll carve large chunks of your health off and they're old school unforgiving in their speed. Crushingly you'll often get gibbed in a second because glitches or something, IDK.
The game's buggy platforming is only worsened when you're on a floating platform, your jump momentum seems to just not be there sometimes and you fall to your death and then the game of course has a few dozen lines to insult your poor gameplay. I think it'd be fair to submit a few video clips mocking the poor platforming implementation, because it's awful. You'll need to abuse quick saves because jumps straight up don't register.
Only comically after your 5th attempt the game just crashes. I think we know who deserves the insults during gameplay here, Apology Software.
MORE annoyingly is you'll be stuck in a room, you see the key through a slot and you have 1 door you know you have to get through and then the key door. What the hell do you do? Uhh...uhhh...............oh, you gotta shoot the Triad symbol on the wall in that room to get into the key room. ................. Old school cryptic.
I've heard people say the game is ugly and the details are awful. Eh, I'd say the visuals are hit and miss, a bit muddy but not god awful. There's far worse on steam. The janky animations are more inline with the original and I'd assume that's what they're going for. Janky mind you, they work well enough to communicate what's going on.
I think if you're looking for fun, retro-LIKE shooters you're better off with DOOM4, Wolfenstein New Order/Old Blood, Serious Sam HD & 3...Or buy real old school games like Return to Castle Wolfenstein, PainKiller, Duke Nukem 3D, etc. This game is not bad, it's not good either it's just ...janky.
Also mind any reviews you've seen online as the game has updated a bunch and has even added weapons and fixed issues.

Game was on my wishlist for a while now and finally got it in the Humble Bundle yesterday.
Man, was I dissapointed....
I, for one, don't mind that there's no real tutorial. I'm an old school gamer and we didn't have many of those back in the day. If you wanted to play a game you had to figure stuff out for yourself. And so it is with Shoppe Keep. Prepare for some reading, since they even added an in-game book for you (instead of a physical one like 'in the old days') so you do get an explanation of the basics of the game.
Why only the basics? Because there are no advanced features. The game is very basic and can be summed up in 4 steps:
-Order itme
-Set on display
-Wait till someone buys it
-Repeat
Next to those 4 things are 3 chores you need to do. Cleaning the floor after customers walked over it, repairing your shelves/tables (I guess customers just throw these around the room? Why else would my sturdy hardwood table be half broken after 3 people walk by...?) and putting back items customers just throw on the ground (people in this town are RUDE!)
Now and then there's a fun part, when, instead of neatly paying for something, a "customer" just grabs an item and runs out. You then have the dilemma of zapping him with a lightning bolt or wacking him with a sword. I myself prefer the lightning bolt, but to each his own.
There are some unlockable features like getting up to 30% more money for sales, less thieves, shelves (yes... these need to be unlocked...) so there is kind of something like progression.
PLAN AHEAD! Remember when i said the game only has basic functions? (If yes, good. If not, see a doctor! It only has been like 10 lines or so!) Well, one of those lacking advanced feature is moving furniture around. Yes, if you buy new furniture you can move it around freely, but after placing it you can't pick it up again. The only way to get rid of i is to 'sell' it for a fraction of it's cost and buy a new one to place. Very annoying... At least you can still see how tall an (for example) armor rack is, even before you unlock it.
Also, the beginning is quite slow. You start with almost no coin, and the only thing you really can sell at the beginning are health potions. You buy them for 10g a pop and have to manually price them to make a profit. And here's another missed oppertunity. There is absolutely no refference on how much you should sell things for. I put all my items at 150% and that seemd to work. But there's no feedback from customers or other stores so you would have to match local prices or things like that. No "I would buy this item if it was less expensive" or "I bought this because it was cheap!" to figure out if your prices are good.
All in all a missed oppertunity.

I fell in love with the RWBY series as soon as it was anounced.
To me, the series seemed to advertise a whole new world with with badass weapons being used in badass ways in badass fights. And it lived up to the hype (At least, until Monty Oum died. But I will not go into a tirade on pre-Oum vs post-Oum).
However, I cannot recommend this game simply because it is not badass. It's not even decent. To put it harshly, it may even be an insult to Monty Oum's reputation in crazy animated fights.
The mechanics as a hack-and-slash is too repetitive with little variety in combos. Now, I'm not expecting Oum-level animations because I understand that is difficult to put into a game. But I was definitely expecting something better. At least something like the Naruto fighting games, where players mashing a combination of 2 buttons lead to exciting visuals and a good amount of variety based on what jutsu you equipped.
I am not expecting the battle visuals to be on the level of those Naruto games either because they where produced by a professional studio with experience in the industry, but at least something flashier to do good to the name of RWBY.
The gameplay itself is also boring. You only fight hordes of Grimm. And not even the cool ones like a Nevermore, but just the basic ♥♥♥♥♥es with stupidly predictable attack patterns.
The fighting mechanics of the Batman Arkham series would be way more fun when fighting these kinds of enemies. But since you cannot easily counter enemies, you end up using hit-and-run tactics and kiting the horde until you slowly shave their numbers down bit by bit.
The few things that I will not complain about are the visuals and the 3D background. Pretty much ripped the models from the show and prettied them up, which is fine by me.
However, the potrait/splash art of the characters are terrible. Those potraits feel like Rooster Teeth pulled a random fan-made picture from DeviantArt.
This game is not worth the full $25 as of 7-11-2016.
This game should have stayed in Early Access until they at least added more playable characters and enemies to fight, or until they revamp the battle mechanics into something better.
