First of all, if you have a way to test this game before buying it (playing it at a friend's computer, for example), DO IT.
In my opinion, you can know if this game's for you by just playing 15 minutes (a.k.a. the first chapter of the campaign). If you don't like it by that point, DON'T BUY IT. The game does not get any better. If you like it but feel like you need more content - like skins or more than four characters with greater variety - then DON'T BUY IT. Other than achievement hunting, there isn't much content at this point in time. If you liked it and feel like you could play and grind hours of that repeatedly, BUY IT, the game is probably for you.
Ahem, now, the review:
The first big problem is that the game isn't worth $25. This is the crux of the whole thing, since the game itself is fun, but offers little things to do. Campaign, ranks and achievements. The game still feels unfinished and there's no content whatsoever.
The core gameplay is really basic. You have Light, Heavy and Ranged attacks, an Ultimate move and a broken counter. You will be mashing the same buttons over a over again. Ever heard of the God of War Square Square Triangle symptom? Well, this game suffers from the same. There are only one or two combos worth doing (Psst, Yang's LLH).
This isn't something "terrible", since it is a hack 'n slash after all. There's always fast-paced action and it feels nice to kick the butts of vile creatures, right?
The thing is that its extremely simple, easy and repetitive. Dying seems like an imposible task, there's no strategy and no variation.
There's almost no difference between the four characters and they all share the same type of skill tree. Sure, Blake is better at making combos, for example, but in the end they all feel the same. The max level is 10, and you will probably reach it before the second half of the game, which means there aren't many skills to choose from. You won't have a "unique" character. In fact, you will probably never use 40% of skills in the game, like the rest of us.
The only game mode is the Campaign. You can play with other people or go solo. The campaign is composed of ten chapters. You can clear it in about three hours aproximately, and multiplied by four if you want to use all characters. This is not "bad", since the game is meant to be replayable. But there's little reason to do so. There are no secrets, no different difficulties, no skins nor anything to unlock. The final boss is a joke, its easy and tedious, more like an ordeal rather than a challenge. There aren't many things to do once you beat it. Except for...
...Achievement hunting. There are 25 achievements, most of them are easy and you should get them in just one round. Some of them are interesting enough, but unluckily they fell short.
The story is bad, regardless of whether or not you're a RWBY fan or not familiar with the series. I would say that you don't need to watch the show to understand the game, but they explain so little that you might feel lost if you don't know the basics of the story. Of course, there's no character development, and the big bad is clichéd and does not have a strong motivation. There are NO cutscenes, so do not expect to see things from the show here.
Once you finish this, the only thing left to do is increasing your Rank, which is the equivalent of your multiplayer level. The max is 10, and it requires you to do insane grinding of objectives and then RESET all your progress, so you'll have to begin all over again everytime you level up. Lazy replayability is lazy. You have all been warned.
And that's the game right now. It's not "bad", but it's not "good" either. It's funny but not captivating enough. Honestly, it feels rushed and unfinished, and there are plenty of bugs. And I really mean it.
Many things are lacking, like more characters, game mods and skins. They'll probably be added as DLC, which only makes this "Full Release" worse. There aren't even any Trading Cards or Badge.
TL;DR:
I've been in this boat since January-February. I've seen all versions and updates of this game. The Early Access process was really weird. Some questionable decisions were made without warning, content was cut out for no real reason and the final result feels rushed. The game is fun, but simple, easy and broken. I'm sure the dev team had good intentions, and the game had potential, but $25 dollars is way too much for such a simple game. Not to mention much needed content will come as DLC, meaning you'll probably have to pay even more.
At the end of the day, you can have fun with it. But unless you want to grind by killing the same enemies over and over and over again, the price isn't worth it.
UPDATE: So, we got quite a few new things during this last few days.
First, the price was reduce from 25 to 20 dollars. I believe this is a much fair price for the game. A good move, quite controvertial, but that's the price it should have cost after the release.
Second, Horde Mode. Or should I say "Defend from Waves" mode, since its not an endurance contest against enemies, but you must protect specific objects from 10 waves of enemies, each harder than the last one. It introduce the use of torrets and it requires the teams to have a bit more of teamwork which the actual campaign never needs. But, then again, its just requires you to defend a position from some waves, basically what you have to do during the first two chapters of the campaign. And there are no new maps; the three locations being Emerald Forest, Mountain Glenn and Forever Fall. But its free, which is a good point, specially since, as seen in my first point, the price was reduce from 25 to 20 dollars. So now a new player receives more content for less money.
Third, and this is the strong point. Team JNPR was released as a DLC. It costs 5 dollars...which I find to be quite fair. Now, I haven't been able to use them since I don't have money to spare right now, but from what I've read and watched, they are better and funnier to play with than RWBY, and presents both a better and a more diverse gameplay. So yep, it sounds like JNPR is a success! Let's see if the hype can survive more than a week, though. But granted, it sounds like a good DLC.
So, you may ask, why is this review still a negative one? We have more content for a lower price, and a good DLC!
Well, the thing is, even though all of this is great, the core game still kinda sucks. This update haven't touched any of the issues previously discussed. The Rank System is still broken and requires waaay too much time and sacrifice. Team RWBY still feels boring, and the core gameplay wasn't polished.
So yeah, the reduction of the game's price was a good move. Horde mode wasn't a great addition, but it was okay. And JNPR seems to be great, but that's a DLC. The Main Game still needs some love. So, even though this update brought the game to a grey area, it still have some ways to go if they want to change this review to a positive one.

Thief is a First Person Game unlike most of the games of this genre. It challenges you to carefully navigate the environment in which you inhabit. Each level had three stages of difficulty, the lowest allows for most of the tricks a FPS player should have, while the highest demands precision in awareness and timing to achieve your goals instead of brute force and direct action. The levels themselves provide interesting opportunities to test your ability to bypass the opposition.
The graphics for this game have aged and compared to the current shine of the triple A titles it is lacklustre, but this does not detract from the playability of the game. The audio still atmospheric enhances the game making some of the levels with the undead almost spooky.
The story of Garret the character you play as provides some interesting twists and turns, while giving context to the levels you play. If you are looking for a game that will offer a different gaming experience then Thief will deliver something unlike most of the offerings out there.

Ever since I could remember, I love stealth games, since I played Splinter cell I love stealth games, just hiding in the shadow and kill your enemies is fun…but being a thief and steal anything you can, is even more fun.
I was pretty impress how this 1998 game still holds up today, the mechanics of this game really stands up to a unique design of gameplay back in the day, you thought  Splinter Cell was the first to use that gameplay style? Sorry, thief snatches up first and became the first to implement the shadow mechanic which again back in the day it was a unique feature in the game. You need to use the darkness as much as possible to hide from guards, while also use your thief’s tools to get through the mission.  Being a thief has its own sweet reward when you go to some snobby rich man’s mansion and just steal anything you can and just feel like robin hood, but this robin hood is all for himself only.
The story I got is pretty interesting especially the extra contents I got from the Gold editions, the silhouette cut scenes were interesting except a bit of the cryptic verses it shows which to me feels sorta pointless. The main character Garret the greedy selfish thief going through missions to do the one thing he wants, money. Indeed, throughout the story all he wants is just to be rich and that’s all, even the shadiest job from just anybody he will take it with no 2nd thoughts as long as he gets his reward which I don’t know if I should find him a risk taker or a fool. Although one part of the story finds me interesting when I was reading the wiki was
The gameplay is fun, smooth, but the button choice is a bit odd, I guess I got used to using WSAD but you’ll get used to the WZC if you put your middle finger at the W, ring Z, and index C. Since you are a thief you aren’t as strong as any soldier so you’ll get a variety of weapons, most weapons does the trick though few I find it very un-helpful. For example the broad arrows is practically use as paper airplanes when killing the enemies, especially if you try to headshot them or surprise them, you won’t get a one hit kill, the fire arrow does more damage but it makes noise which obvious you don’t want that. The noise maker is useless because the broad arrow can just make noises by hitting at the wall. Another item I didn’t find it helpful is the speed potion which increases your speed but jumping up and down is almost the same effect speed. The AI sometimes can be dumb and easily fooled by just luring them and hitting them behind the head, or just rush them quickly when they are behind and just whack them, I did it one mission when all four guards were behind and I manage to whack them all on the head easily. This is why to get the most challenging and fun experience play either hard or expert, but I recommend expert for people who have good stealth experience. Expert will give you the most missions and tell you not to kill anyone which you will think more when dealing enemies if you don’t to use your sword to thwack them. Hard is a good balance for beginner thief series, but never go normal, that is for people who suck at stealth, I grew bored at normal and forgot to turn on expert on different levels, I thought I wasn’t ready for hard but I sure did when I played my 2nd play through on expert, the experience was much different and for the better. Though watch out, because the map at times is troublesome to follow and I know is to reflect Garret’s view of the level, but it can be frustrating when getting lost in a level, maybe provide a cryptic hint might help on the menu screen?
This game keeps you on your toes, it does hold up to be an old classic, the voice actors were great, level designs were interesting especially some missions, and the sound designs at times are great when listening to your surrounding of the way you step. I give this an 8/10 “a gem taker” one of a good first start of the franchise to check it out and see if you can be the next great thief.

Mount & Blade: Warband is a masterpiece. So good, in fact, that I will write my first review.
The Good:
+ Challenging and in-depth gameplay with many aspects (army and town management, diplomacy, and most importantly PILLAGING, WARRING, AND MURDERING FARMERS)
+ Leveling system is in depth and each skill has a good effect in game, no skills feel useless.
+ Epic battles with hundreds of units, castle sieges and bandit raids.
+ Easy to pick up and play, even when you're high.
+ Online multiplayer is good for testing your skills against other players (however don't expect a great deal in comparison to the glory of singleplayer)
+ ASTOUNDING MODDING COMMUNITY - Content from the Steam workshop and other sources gives the game almost infinite playability (Yes, there are Game of Thrones and Lord of the Rings mods).
The Bad:
- After a while (~100hrs), all fighting begins to feel a bit the same. (At this point, if you aren't already into diplomacy and town management you might find yourself getting bored.)
- Potato graphics (Think oblivion without the weirdly gross heads), but they hold up well enough.
Overall:
This game is a work of art. I first began to play in 2016, and could not believe I hadn't heard of the game sooner. As an RPG it is every bit as good as any Elder Scrolls title to date. A wonderful example of what can happen when developers put their heart and soul into a game, and encourage community input through mods. Thoroughly looking forward to the next installment, Mount & Blade 2: Bannerlord!

With today's games eating up tens of GBs of storage and TFlops of computing power, it's easy to forget that the primary objective of gaming is still to have fun. Along comes The Dweller, with bare-bones simple visuals, uncomplicated audio and goofy physics, and single-handedly provides better entertainment than at least 50% of the AAA market. How's that?
First of all, The Dweller scores a mega-hit in the atmosphere department, where the bleak visuals, the moody music (soundscape?) and the to-the-point representation of the game's protagonist work perfectly together to put the player in the mood of an eldritch cave system haunted by something horrible. Only this time the player isn't one of the explorers - he's the something horrible. Our hero is trying to defend his domain from the peeking eyes and hands of scientists, dealing with them rather brutally, while the science team gradually starts to realise that the boulders don't just seem to move behind their backs, the earth swallowing people is not an unfortunate cave-in, and people don't disappear because they've gone for a long walk. While the game itself is a series of puzzle screens, solving them uncovers more and more story fragments. Simple as it can be, but very effective.
When someone creates something as spot-on as The Dweller as his first game, he's either a genius or very, very lucky. Maybe a mix between the two. We'll see how it will move with Villainous' next attempts, but whatever happens later, The Dweller remains what it is - a simple and fun puzzle game with an incredible atmosphere and an excellent sense of dark humour. Highly recommended.

Firstly, if you haven't already, I'd suggest playing Deus Ex: Human Revolution before this as the events of Mankind Divided take place two years later (and DE:HR is referenced a lot). There's an optional DE:HR recap video at the start of the game, and obviously this would also be full of spoilers.
On the more technical side - No running or crashing issues for me at all. Runs continuously smoothly on a NVidia GTX 970, and I've not had to turn down or switch off anything in options to achieve that either. Gorgeous graphics, fun gameplay, engaging storylines, amusing dialogue, and even a degree of closure regarding finding out what happened to certain characters from Human Revolution. Yes, some of the load times are on the longer side, but I expect that with higher-spec games. As a fan of the Deus Ex series I was expecting the worst with this (you know how it is with sequels), but was thankfully impressed.
I can't say I'm a fan of microtransactions (you can buy extra credits / praxis kits etc if you want). but it's by no means shoved in your face or forced, so can easily be ignored (you have to go through a couple of menu screens to even get to that option, and at no point are there any pop-ups to push it). I'm not letting that impact my positive review as I'm here to review the game, not debate/protest ethics in videogame marketing / production (my view is pretty much an each-to-their-own scenario on that - I'm just stating my own opinion here).
I'd happily recommend this game (Who can complain about having MORE Jensen lol) but check your PC specs first!
(Edit: At no point have I said I'm running it on ''ultra'' or with every single setting ''maxed out''.. I just said I didn't have to turn anything off / down to play it, and that's the truth. In my experience, games don't default to every-single-thing-maxed-ultra settings when you first install them, so surely running with everything maxed out would be putting settings 'up'?. Anyway, my point was, is that whatever were the default settings on intstall is what I'm playing it on, and I didn't have to switch off anything merely to get it to function, as some people have stated they've had to do).

Where's the rest of my f##king game?
I paid $60 for this, the least I could get is a fully fleshed out story that doesn't end with most of the plot lines dropped, and more than ONE boss fight (a fight that was as complicated as planting one EMP mine and pressing Q.) Add microtransactions in a all singleplayer game and what feels like a short experience (only about 18 hours after doing EVERYTHING I could in one playthrough) and you get this - a mediocre let down.
At least the combat is decent and it doesn't Arkham Knight itself to death. Oh, and the graphics are good, but nothing really stands out or took my breath away (except the wonky facial animations and terrible lip sync.)
Disappointing, mediocre, and a shell of what it could have been because of corporate greed (Which is ironic, considering what little plot this game does have focuses on just that.) Probably not even worth it on sale, but that's mainly cause I just beat the game and am freshly bitter. Don't buy it, even on sale.

Game is missing half of its story, wait for the "complete edition" before you buy this mechanically competent game for the full experience (will also be much cheaper then).
The games mechanics are the same solid quality as they were in the Human Revolution, in both good and bad:
Sneaking is fun and exiting and yealds the most EXP, meaning if you want to play with all the cool augs you better get them "smooth operator" and "ghost" bonuses.
Fighting has somewhat improved: there are now augs that support more violent playstyle (especially the TITAN-aug) but you can no longer kill people with heavy objects (or at least I wasn't able to) which is a shame.
Weapons in the game are somewhat disapointing (except the new stun-pistol which kicks♥♥♥♥♥.
There's no LMG's or Missle-launchers in the game which is great shame for there finally is areas with big open spaces with loads of enemies where one could effectively use them (either for crowd-controll with EXTREME PREJUDICE or to blow clusters of enemies into paste)
No cross-bows or laser-rifles to spice up the game-play with alternative strategies (such as pinning bodies in the walls with the cross-bow or shooting trough the walls with the laser-rifle)
What weapons we do have are functional but they lack balls: the new battle-rifle sounds like a cheap BB-gun (phft-phft instead of ear-drum shattering BANG-BANG) and the revolver doesn't have the same punch as the old one (also the both "special revolvers" suck just as much)
There is apparently a grenade-launcher in the game but I didn't find it and none of the merchants had one for sale but that's more of a problem with the game-design than the player (for I could found multiple ones in the DE:HR).
Hacking has mostly stayed same from the first one but the interface is more cluttered and it feels clunky to use but luckily they removed the pointless aug to "analyze" the nodes (now there's a hacking program for that and it gets just about as much use).
I was hoping that the big delay they had in the development would allow every aspect of the game be bigger and better. While this is true for technical aspects of the game, the writing and the story got seriously shafted.
I will pass the factoid that they selected the most♥♥♥♥♥♥ending in the DE:HRs "ending-o-matic" (I.E the one were everybody dies) to be canon.
Instead lets focus on the new story that has no subtlety: the main conspiracy is immediately explained to us by our new lady-friend instead of letting us figure it out ourselfs before revealing it for those who didn't take time figuring it out (like the malfuntioning bio-chip element in the first one).
The game just says: These are the bad guys, this is what they want to accomplish, these guys are the patsies for the bad guys and this is why we must stop them both.
Main and side-characters are in no better position: none of them evolve or reveal hidden characteristics: they all stay in complete stasis and just play their stereotypical roles (I.E No nonsence boss stays as trict and our rival continues to be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ trough the whole game).
There are no twists in the story: bad guys stay bad guys, patsies stay patsies and Adam Jensen stays uninterested about the whole ordeal around him. Or maybe there are some twists later in the story.
Too bad that the story ends before the halfway point: Is like DE:HR would've ended after the first visit Hengsha (Is almost like somebody cut the game up so they could sell the rest of the story as  DLC but that would be just silly). This ending makes the "Ending-o-matic" in the first game seem ingenius in comparison: At least the story was properly wrapping up by the time we reached it.
In conclusion: If they had given the game longer development time (2-3 years atleast) it might have become a worthy sequel to Human Revolution but in its current state it leaves a bad impression on both itself and the people behind it.
Better luck next time.

This game. Oh this game.
I had heard some incredible things about this game, so I went into it with high expectations - and yet, I still found myself being more awed than I had ever anticipated. The simple design of the characters and the fact they did not speak in a language the player would understand was a wonderful feature, that added immersion and allowed for full character expression to be conveyed through the raw emotion of the characters and nothing else. You really become acquainted with each brother's quirks and mannerisms through how they interact with the environment around them, and it was brilliant how well one of their skills complimented the other's weaknesses - they were two halves of a whole and I fell in love with their characterisation. Which, considering I could not understand what they were saying, is quite the feat.
The vastly different environments were absolutely breathtaking. From the snow-kissed mountain peaks with the northern lights, to the waterfalls and hills; it was incredible. Even the graphics of the water movement was well-designed, particularly in the rowing boat scene. The simplicity of the character design in contrast with the environments they stumbled upon worked really well and enabled me to immerse myself in this world even more so.
The story was by far one of the best story's I have seen in a video game in a long time. I would never had anticipated the direction this game would go in. From inane wonderings in a rural village and skipping stones, to witnessing the bloody aftermath of a battlefied - this game took all my expectations and threw it out the window with every plot twist. You told this story flawlessly, and by the ending I was an emotional mess considering how invested I became in these characters in a matter of hours. I felt their joy, their sadness and their pain, especially at the end. The significance of even a single button became so poignant and really stood out to me in recognizing how well-crafted this game is.
Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons pushed the boundaries and portrays messages far deeper than what you would assume on the surface. A gaming experience I feel like everybody should have to experience. Truly a game I will come back to relive again and again.

Josiah started jumping eagerly up and down, and then crouching and standing eagerly. Strange lad, that Josiah. In the distance, we saw the French scurrying around in no reasonable fashion, one already charging across the field with his musket held high. The fifer struck up a rousing rendition of "Gucci Gang" by the eccentric fellow Lil Pump and my heart swelled. "Rule Brittania!" I cried! I was met by equally raucous cheers of "abandon ship!" and "YOU CHEESE EATING SURRENDER MONKEYS!" Three chaps got so excited they fired wildly at the French who were still over 300 yards away.

Immediately my fellow footsoldiers started dashing across the field quickly leaving the captain's helpless cries of "no wait guys you're supposed to line up!"
French cannons roared, cutting down three men instantly. This was followed quickly by a volley of musket fire, though only Josiah was cut down. Rest easy, dear boy, jump up and down excitedly in Fiddler's green. As we went, a few of us levelled our weapons and fired. Our mob was slowly breaking apart, men falling to pieces around me. Thrilled by combat, I  raised my bayonet high over my head and attempted a war cry, but I got confused and screamed "Hoist the sails, lads!"
As I reached the French line, I plunged my steel into the first man's belly then turned around. An explosion of pain blindsided me and I fell over. UPDATED 16/10/16
First of all, if you have a way to test this game before buying it (playing it at a friend's computer, for example), DO IT.
In my opinion, you can know if this game's for you by just playing 15 minutes (a.k.a. the first chapter of the campaign). If you don't like it by that point, DON'T BUY IT. The game does not get any better. If you like it but feel like you need more content - like skins or more than four characters with greater variety - then DON'T BUY IT. Other than achievement hunting, there isn't much content at this point in time. If you liked it and feel like you could play and grind hours of that repeatedly, BUY IT, the game is probably for you.
Ahem, now, the review:
The first big problem is that the game isn't worth $25. This is the crux of the whole thing, since the game itself is fun, but offers little things to do. Campaign, ranks and achievements. The game still feels unfinished and there's no content whatsoever.
The core gameplay is really basic. You have Light, Heavy and Ranged attacks, an Ultimate move and a broken counter. You will be mashing the same buttons over a over again. Ever heard of the God of War Square Square Triangle symptom? Well, this game suffers from the same. There are only one or two combos worth doing (Psst, Yang's LLH).
This isn't something "terrible", since it is a hack 'n slash after all. There's always fast-paced action and it feels nice to kick the butts of vile creatures, right?
The thing is that its extremely simple, easy and repetitive. Dying seems like an imposible task, there's no strategy and no variation.
There's almost no difference between the four characters and they all share the same type of skill tree. Sure, Blake is better at making combos, for example, but in the end they all feel the same. The max level is 10, and you will probably reach it before the second half of the game, which means there aren't many skills to choose from. You won't have a "unique" character. In fact, you will probably never use 40% of skills in the game, like the rest of us.
The only game mode is the Campaign. You can play with other people or go solo. The campaign is composed of ten chapters. You can clear it in about three hours aproximately, and multiplied by four if you want to use all characters. This is not "bad", since the game is meant to be replayable. But there's little reason to do so. There are no secrets, no different difficulties, no skins nor anything to unlock. The final boss is a joke, its easy and tedious, more like an ordeal rather than a challenge. There aren't many things to do once you beat it. Except for...
...Achievement hunting. There are 25 achievements, most of them are easy and you should get them in just one round. Some of them are interesting enough, but unluckily they fell short.
The story is bad, regardless of whether or not you're a RWBY fan or not familiar with the series. I would say that you don't need to watch the show to understand the game, but they explain so little that you might feel lost if you don't know the basics of the story. Of course, there's no character development, and the big bad is clichéd and does not have a strong motivation. There are NO cutscenes, so do not expect to see things from the show here.
Once you finish this, the only thing left to do is increasing your Rank, which is the equivalent of your multiplayer level. The max is 10, and it requires you to do insane grinding of objectives and then RESET all your progress, so you'll have to begin all over again everytime you level up. Lazy replayability is lazy. You have all been warned.
And that's the game right now. It's not "bad", but it's not "good" either. It's funny but not captivating enough. Honestly, it feels rushed and unfinished, and there are plenty of bugs. And I really mean it.
Many things are lacking, like more characters, game mods and skins. They'll probably be added as DLC, which only makes this "Full Release" worse. There aren't even any Trading Cards or Badge.
TL;DR:
I've been in this boat since January-February. I've seen all versions and updates of this game. The Early Access process was really weird. Some questionable decisions were made without warning, content was cut out for no real reason and the final result feels rushed. The game is fun, but simple, easy and broken. I'm sure the dev team had good intentions, and the game had potential, but $25 dollars is way too much for such a simple game. Not to mention much needed content will come as DLC, meaning you'll probably have to pay even more.
At the end of the day, you can have fun with it. But unless you want to grind by killing the same enemies over and over and over again, the price isn't worth it.
UPDATE: So, we got quite a few new things during this last few days.
First, the price was reduce from 25 to 20 dollars. I believe this is a much fair price for the game. A good move, quite controvertial, but that's the price it should have cost after the release.
Second, Horde Mode. Or should I say "Defend from Waves" mode, since its not an endurance contest against enemies, but you must protect specific objects from 10 waves of enemies, each harder than the last one. It introduce the use of torrets and it requires the teams to have a bit more of teamwork which the actual campaign never needs. But, then again, its just requires you to defend a position from some waves, basically what you have to do during the first two chapters of the campaign. And there are no new maps; the three locations being Emerald Forest, Mountain Glenn and Forever Fall. But its free, which is a good point, specially since, as seen in my first point, the price was reduce from 25 to 20 dollars. So now a new player receives more content for less money.
Third, and this is the strong point. Team JNPR was released as a DLC. It costs 5 dollars...which I find to be quite fair. Now, I haven't been able to use them since I don't have money to spare right now, but from what I've read and watched, they are better and funnier to play with than RWBY, and presents both a better and a more diverse gameplay. So yep, it sounds like JNPR is a success! Let's see if the hype can survive more than a week, though. But granted, it sounds like a good DLC.
So, you may ask, why is this review still a negative one? We have more content for a lower price, and a good DLC!
Well, the thing is, even though all of this is great, the core game still kinda sucks. This update haven't touched any of the issues previously discussed. The Rank System is still broken and requires waaay too much time and sacrifice. Team RWBY still feels boring, and the core gameplay wasn't polished.
So yeah, the reduction of the game's price was a good move. Horde mode wasn't a great addition, but it was okay. And JNPR seems to be great, but that's a DLC. The Main Game still needs some love. So, even though this update brought the game to a grey area, it still have some ways to go if they want to change this review to a positive one.

In the surface this game looks like a musou with hack'n'slash elements to mix it up, has multiplayer and a story mode to boot.
And yet, somehow, after quite a while in Early Acess it stills feels incomplete, to say the very least.
As a Musou it barely has the luxury to call itself that, with just 5 standard enemies with a 'bigger and badder' version, it barely has enemy variety to keep you entertained and levels that challenge the definition of linear gameplay, with waves and sometimes a escort here and there to try to spice things up, but ultimately failing.
And as a Hack'n'Slash it just is too boring.
It has the basic ideia down, giving Light and Strong Attacks and each character has a trait to their strong attack to mix it up in between them. But is just dosen't matter. You will find youself doing the same combo over and over again because it is poorly balanced and has a very insignifcant upgrade system to boot. And even the traits each characther brings to the table has little matter on the subject and things are so unbalanced that playing anything other then ruby, which has a combo that hits anything in a very large cone ahead of her, is a poor choice.
Not to mention the lack of more character loved by the community. Just taking 4 to the game seems like a waste when there is a gigantic cast, with tremendous potencial, just waiting to be implemented.
And i cannot take this... excuse of a story mode seriously.
Like, it's worse then SFV story mode on launch.
It takes effort to break that.
THE ONE THING it kinda hit the spot was with the beauty of the game overall, on max settings, it looks amazing.
BUT it just isn't well optimized enough for you to be able to enjoy them. NOT TO MENTION the really pathetic excuse of graphics options. It's 2016, just giving 5 options of "Quality" just isn't enough. Especially for a 3D game like this one.
Overall this game is a dissapointing and unfinished mess that only makes itself worthwhile for fans of the animated series. Which is rather unfortunate taking in fact that this game could have brought so much more into RWBY's universe.
A waste of potential, and waste of money, for someone who isn't a fan.

At the core this game was supposed to be a fun hack and slash survival game with RPG elements. It's what the demo was a few years ago and it is exactly what it is now. I have never been under the illusion that this game was going to be the Witcher set in the universe of RWBY. Since I never expected a triple A game, I wasn't disappointed.
With that in mind I can only recommend this game. It is a lighthearted, fun hack and slash game. The replayability is in the different characters that all feel and fight a bit differently. The most fun is to be had when you join up with friends and fight yourself through hordes of Grimm.
People that are looking for a deep and rich game, don't look for it here. People looking for a fun game with a fluid fighting system, you've found it! Enjoy (Y)

I will keep this short. I know I am put off by ten page long reviews designed to make its writer look smart.
This review is to counter the only complaint the negative reviews I have seen seem to have.
A lot of people who have negative reviews of the game say there is not enough content for 25 dollars. That is probably because they have not played all of the content.
With a full team the campain took me about 3 hours. The difficulty scales with the amount of players so take that time as you may.
The reason I say those who claim the game lacks content have not played all of the content is not me telling people to achievement hunt or artificially extend the time they spend playing. I say that because the game capitalizes on replayability.
Allow me to explain: The game, currently, has one campain with four selectable ccharacters, the main protaganists of the show, each character has there own moves and there own skill tree that use to upgrade them as you level up. At least half of the skills in the skill tree is locked at the start, and are unlocked by completing simple and not difficult tasks, for example: defeat this many enemies with your ultimate, or save your teammates this many times.
With this system of locked skills you will likely reach max level before you unlock all of the skills. Meaning, these skills offer both the side goal of unlocking them as well as something new to try on a second or third play through. If you like a certain move you can unlock a skill that makes it more powerfull. You can put together a loadout based on combos or spamming ultimates. And on top of that the game rewards you for experimenting with different loadouts with awards for refunding skill points.
And on top of that. Multiply all that replayability by four when you factor in the fact that each character has there own unique abilities and skills. And once again this is all proven to be the point considering there is an entire ranking system based around leveling up all four characters.
Lastly ever since the game was greenlit the devs have teased other teams and more content. Also a "horde mode" is coming soon to add more gameplay. Therefor more content is definately on the way.
It might feel like it's lacking in features, and lack the polish of AAA titles, but as a first attempt at game development from an animation/machinima studio, it's pretty good.
The whole game content is worth 2 hours of gameplay, but fear not there are already paid dlc´s announced.

An ingenious puzzler that is brimming with originality. It's concepts are fresh, and it's aesthetic evokes old horror or adventure novels, which is not as popular as it should be. It is it's own game, never feeling like it's borrowed too heavily from anything else, which is as valuable as gold in a place like Steam.

The levels are developed expertly around the limitations and strengths of the main mechanic. It seems like there are mutiple ways to solve puzzles and none of them are shoehorned in a-la "take the sewers for the stealth approach, or pick up this mini-gun for the hack-and-slash approach". This is a classic case of a developer making a fun, functional, and tight system of mechanics and letting the game stand on it's own two feet (or ghostly tendrils or whatever.)

1st Review/Impressions:
So far the only thing I'm convinced that this game excels at is CRASHING.  Highly unstable currently.  Just when I begin to enjoy the game play it crashes.  I hope this situation improves in the very near future.

TL:DR
- A great follow up to Deus Ex: Human Revolution, similar mechanics with nice new upgrades and polished features.
- Story ain't bad, nothing fantastic but I did enjoy some of the side missions and their stories. Can feel a little short once you know your way around though.
- This can essentially be a Pay-to-win game with the microtransactions, getting through some parts with extra praxis. There is no painful grind for praxis kits.
- New Game Plus has been shipped this time around, and Praxis, Season Pass content do carry over.
- A problem with Human Revolution was the bosses, well in this there is only the final boss, and it is optional.
My playstyle of Deus Ex: Mankind Divided was:
Other people may differ but this is my approach to HR and MD.
Also, for the Frame Rate issues, turn off:
The game is absolutely gorgeous, the gameplay just feels so smooth and fluid, certainly a step up from Deus Ex: Human Revolution. The cover to cover system is more dynamic, augments providing good means and methods of finding new areas. Hacking has stepped up quite a bit, one of my favorite new improvements. Traversal and ledge climbing feels smooth, still has the Explorer style of gameplay. and the HUD looks well this time around. I like the trick in how they integrated Jensen's new Augments as well, and the system of using them (You'll see what I mean). The Story isn't mindblowing or fantastic, it's good no doubt but I found some of the Side Quests more engaging, One in which answered a question about a certain character from the last game.
The main story as you can tell, After the events of Human Revolution. Natural/Aug relations are at a troublesome low "Aug Event" Pro-Naturals and Pro-Aug bashing heads and of course the usual conspiracy storyline in the background (and the return of a few familiar faces in Deus Ex). Some of the plot points didn't surprise me though, you could figure them out at times, although once or twice I was like "Oh, that's why", and there is some questions left to be answered at the end of the game but obviously we have more room for sequels, A lot of time to fill between Mankind Divided and the original Deus Ex.
I love the dystopian tone it sets, the obvious discrimination and paranoia (Like a problem we face today in reality), police out in force, Augs being rallied around like cattle and Golem city was a cool place to visit. I do like the attitude taken towards Jensen in the beginning and (in my playthrough anyway) see how that develops with NPCs and characters. The conversation interaction has improved immensely, there's more body language exchanged between Jensen and characters which is cool.
As for glitches and crashes, I've only had two crashes with the game, only annoying issue was the Steam Overlay not being able to show up, and when loading into a game using space, it would take you out of cover (bound to space bar) but nothing to lose the plot over.
this was patched out in the last update.
As for the microtransaction complaint, I agree it is silly to put Microtransactions into a Single Player campaign, and further more stupid to bind a purchase to that save game. but hey, it's someone's way of playing and who are we to judge if they're too lazy to get Praxis Points or want to breeze through the campaign with no issues, or have a big wallet.
It can become a
, I can see points where people can just say "Oh I need an upgrade to survive in Electrified Areas/Poison Gas" or "I can just up my Stealth for this section and run through the open", people can get very lazy and rather rely on wits, rely on a wallet.
The grind for getting Praxis points is not bad at all, and with new game+ they will carry over to the new game.
Bottom line with microtransactions is that they're in a LOT of games nowadays (Along with DRM),  being used by players and fans and this is why they're sticking around. We can♥♥♥♥♥♥and moan all we like but it's up to us to ignore them if we're that upset or bothered by them. Don't feed the problem, the game can be enjoyed without a little boost.
Personally, I enjoyed my time with Deus Ex, the story is what it is, obvious what to expect from the ending and it does leave things open for more (obviously being a "Pre-sequel". If you loved Human Revolution, then you will enjoy this. I got 40 hours out of the game, I will be trying out New Game+ at some point and of course the "I didn't ask for this" Difficulty (♥♥♥♥ing memes) so I got my moneys worth I feel. It's not gonna be for everyone but if you like Stealth games and some RPG elements with decision making, then this might be right up your street.

A more polished game than Human Revolution, but not nearly as memorable.
Certainly not more than the original Deus Ex.
It took me roughly 24 hours to beat at a semi-leisurely pace, and with roughly 70% of the side missions complete. If I had to guess, I'd say it should take 28 hours to 30 hours max for a lazy completionist (time included for maxing out all augments).
The moment-to-moment gameplay is absolutely solid. Deus Ex's gunplay is finally on par with its peers, and going loud is a viable (and fun) option. The stealth mechanics are still mostly constrained to Vent Lurking Simulator 2016, but with additional augments and a cover-to-cover system (which admittedly feels odd and out-of-place at first), you can zip around freely outside of the ducts with only a fair modicum of caution and planning. Takedowns are still OP, but some enemies can resist them now, so they're not the one-hit KO they once were. Nonetheless, an overwhelming sense of mainstream permeates this game; not to a nauseating degree, but Mankind Divided certainly isn't as niche (or as intricate) as the original Deus Ex, or Human Revolution for that matter.
Speaking of Human Revolution, Mankind Divided loses much of its predecessor's style *and* substance. Whereas HR had three definite arcs, Missing Link notwithstanding, Mankind Divided only really seems to have one, and the game ends right when things really get going. Human Revolution's focus on gold and black in its art style (or &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥filter," as it was affectionately called), is gone in favor of a more realistic design in Mankind Divided. While this does help the game feel less outlandish, it also robs the game of much of the personality that made HR so memorable. Although Prague looks amazing at night, with police sirens blinking red and blue in the midnight rain, it simply can't hold up against the sleek yellow vistas that truly made HR stick out in the sci-fi genre.
In terms of theming, or, rather, writing, Mankind Divided misses the mark by a massive gap. Gone are the socio-political elements of the first Deus Ex, the transhumanism debate of Human Revolution, and the general question of the proper amount of control required in society that has driven the series thus far. In its place is a rote "Us vs Them" story of Augmented people being oppressed by the world at large. While not necessarily poor in its own right, it's painfully inspired by modern elements in a way that is sure to limit its future relevancy. This game's writing will not be talked about in future years, and it certainly won't be revered as a golden standard, like the original one.
The biggest issue I have with Mankind Divided is that it was almost certainly intended as half of a game, almost a simple third. Without spoilers, I can only say that nothing really gets achieved in its runtime; its position in the Deus Ex series as a whole is completely irrelevant at this point. Bringing Jensen back as a protagonist was *mostly* pointless (aside from absolutely stellar voice work), as much of his prior contacts are mentioned in an aside or two, than quickly forgotten about in favor of the new (and much more bland) cast. The universe that Deus Ex has established with such a superb finesse is mostly ignored here; the scope of both preceding games is ignored in favor of Prague, which, although much more detailed than any hub the series has had to offer, is simply not diverse or interesting enough to even hold a candle to Hengsha, France, or Detroit. Several plotlines are left hanging, with almost zero resolution for them; characters are seemingly forgotten and introduced left-and-right, with little to no development for anyone.
Mankind Divided, as a whole, just seems incredibly unnecessary thus far, and its constant bashing of corporate greed and the corrupt nature of control comes off as ironic because of this irrelevancy. Nevertheless, it was a blast to play, and I don't regret the time I spent with the title. In terms of writing, it's subpar for the series; in terms of gameplay, it's at its very peak.

While I see a lot of people gripe about the microtransactions in the single player, I see this as a minor issue. Annoying, but minor. The upgrade points (praxis) you get throughout the game is abundant, and the real gaming experience comes with not buying them at all. You'll get the hard choices, and you'll need to set a plan for how you want to play to synergize the upgrades you choose. I have no idea how it is when buying praxis kits, but I can't for the life of me expect that you gain the same amount of weight on your choices.
My main gripe is the story. The story is... well... alright. Up until when it suddenly ends. Abruptly. It feels as though Deus Ex: Mankind Divided has a third part that won't be released yet, possibly due to future DLC's. Let me just say that if that is the case, that's some damn poor choices. This is a full priced AAA game, but it feels like a book where 1/3 of the pages has been torn out. When I finished, I was shocked and flabbergasted. None of the major threads had been finished. None of the major mysteries that were set up during the course of the game had been revealed. I sat back, feeling I had finally completed the first henchman in the game. But then I got the end credits (!?).
This is bad and disappointing. Especially bad is the fact that the last cinematic of the game explicitly baits that there's MUCH more to the story than has been released. As a person with a lot of enjoyment of the story (and looking forward to everything coming together in the end), this is a disappointment that I can't for the life of me recommend until it's much much MUCH cheaper.

--- Rise of the Triad ---
Rise of the Triad is the reboot of the classic DOS fps with the same name, in short, ROTT. I loved the original game back in the nineties, both cuz it was s fun game, and, since it was a big technical leap forward from what everybody was used to at the time. Yes I'm thinking of you DOOM and you Wolfenstein 3D.
Pros...
- Nice graphics
- Good controls
- Good gunplay
- It feels like a good "modern version" of ROTT. It felt like the developers stayed true to the original formula and kept the feeling. The mechanics are the same. Also, you select one of 5 characters before you start. The wacky weapons and humor (the little I managed to see from the game at least) is still there.
- Nice music and sfx
Cons...
- It's a real sloppy version. The game crashes all the time.I probably could look for patches/fan patches/hotfixes blah blah and I could probably try some stuff of my own to get it playable. But I have a big backlog of games. Also, I felt that this game was too uninspiring to bother. The few levels I got to play felt very much like a ROTT themed generic shooter at best.
Final verdict....
This version get 3/10 since it doesn't work satisfactory, but I probably would want to give it somewhere around 6.5/10 - if it was stable and playable. Buy @ your own risk.

Certainly played the original a good bit, made some maps for it and was looking forward to this release. Without question, I can give it a thumbs up. Played it before they had fully finished it, before they had steam achievements, etc. Recently took the opportunity to revisit the game and share thoughts of this near-final version. (I say near-final, since this development team has continued to issue so many new things and fixes over the years it's remarkable.)
The game is mostly linear, but not bothersome. There are some well-placed secrets that make it worth poking around. You'll need to get a key or flip a switch to progress, but it's not like other games of the mid 90's where you could get lost, or really had to FIGURE OUT the level. I don't even remember if the original RoTT had any "maze" type aspect to it to be honest, so this may be spot-on in that regard.
This game's levels are completely planned--- WELL planned with health + enemies in known quantities and locations. I like this. I am not as much of a fan of games that employ the "lock you in a room and spawn enemies at you until you're blue in the face" mechanics. I find it to be cheap level design! Some may wonder at why we are gathering coins and jumping impossible heights, but this was the original game. You collect coins because you want a high score! You want a high-score because... 1990's!
The missile, flame & magic weapons are as much of a blast to use as ever, but stick to them. I find the pistols and machine gun to be quite underwhelming in all regards, including the animations in which your victims react to being shot by them. You'll only use them for backup though, so it's not a huge deal.
The soundtrack was done with so much passion, they are truly an audiophile's dream. Games from the 90's were all about the music, the melody, and having a "song" to play a game to. Go old-school and listen to the MIDI versions as well!
The bosses are a challenge and have some interesting mechanics, so much so you will likely have to turn down the difficulty. There are no "circle strafe and win" fights here, but there's also no obtuse boss mechanics where you have to die 100 times (or read online) to be able to win.
Multiplayer still seems alive and well. Subscribe the levels recommended to have in your downloads so you can jump in and get to work. Here, you'll see how fast and intense this game can truly be! It works well and is as intended. There is no progress or incentive to do it other than ... you want to shoot other people. Again, 1990's here.
Now for the negatives and I jot these down so you can make sure you come in knowing them and are not disappointed. In no way did they significantly impact MY enjoyment, but some frustrated me at times:
-Occasional quick save crashes
-Difficult FPS platforming to be found here-- but try to have fun. It really is unique! Quicksave and try again quickly!
-Getting stuck at odd times on doorways, ramps, rocks & misc. objects
-There are random checkpoints, very frustrating when attempting to get 100% level completion! You can turn a corner or step through a door and find yourself locked from going back and exploring. Use the guide in the forums, if you're trying to get the achievements.
-Sometimes difficult to shoot enemies behind railings due to explosive weapons detonating on "invisible walls" making enemies invulnerable. Just jump and shoot down at them to land your kill.

I love RWBY and have been watching since Season 1. I was delighted when my friend bought me the Early Access version. Now that the game is in full release, I thought it would be worthwhile to post a review.
Long story short, the game is not worth full price ($25).
There are some great things here. The graphics are beautiful. The combat looks like the exciting and fluid fight scenes in the show. The character models are very close to their animated versions. Voice acting is superb. The overall design is very true to the source material.
But the cons greatly outweigh the pros. The gameplay is simple, boring, and repetitive. There is no real story to speak of and despite being 4-player co-op there are no real teamwork mechanics. You can spam the attack button and get through the whole game. The characters all play almost exactly the same and there is nothing that makes them stand out from one another. There is very little replayability and the campaign is disappointingly short.
If the game was still in Early Access, I would be a easier on it. As it is, the game is great to look at and play around in as a fan of the show that wants to interact with the RWBY universe. But I cannot recommend it at full price at all if you are considering buying it for the sake of gameplay.

If you've been a gamer for any length of time, then you're no doubt familiar with Rooster Teeth. They quickly rose to prominence in the early 2000's, not to mention pioneered machinima, with their series Red vs Blue. Fast forward to 2013: RT has expanded into the realm of anime with their series RWBY. Overall, looking at what they've done the last few years, it was only a matter of time before they entered the realm of video games. After seeing a fangame based on RWBY, they actually hired it's developer and turned it into a full release. On 12/1/15, Grimm Eclipse was introduced to Steam via it's Early Access program. Does the title live up to the hype one would expect from Monty Oum's international hit, or is it a title that will leave you wishing you were watching the show instead?
Gameplay: 8
Overall, GE does a great job of capturing the fast paced nature of the fight scenes in RWBY. The best way I can describe it is if they started by seeking to make a throwback to old school side scrolling arcade games. Then, rather than do side scrolling, RT decides to have 3D environments with a third person view. From there, they take the combat of games like Devil May Cry and the Batman: Arkham series, make it a bit more simple, then mashed those together with the team based gameplay of games such as Left 4 Dead. Toss that all in a blender and the end result is Grimm Eclipse.
Combat consists of your typical mix of light/heavy attacks, counters, dodges, special/team attacks and ranged attacks. While it's not nearly as deep as the Arkham games, you'll feel right at home if you're fairly experienced with the Freeflow Combat system from those games. While the combat in Arkham is fairly fast paced, it's much better to compare the speed of combat in GE to more over the top games.
As for character selection, you'll have a choice between the four main characters of the series (Ruby, Weiss, Blake, and Yang). Various abilities are designed in a way that makes everyone feel true to the series with no two characters playing alike. Characters can level up from 1-10 and earn skill points to either improve their combat abilities, or passively become stronger in other areas (increased health, team medic for quick revival, increased ability to stun enemies and create moments for team attacks, ect). It has been confirmed by Rooster Teeth that Team JNPR will be added to the game in a future update. This will open up plenty of team combinations down the road, but as of now that has zero bearing on the game in it's current state.
In addition to maxing everyone out, there is a prestige system of sorts in place. Once you meet the requirements, you can reset all progress back to level 1 in exchange for an additional Hunter Rank, as well as a new set of challenges. As of now, it's more of a bragging rights reward/achievement you can show off. However, it's been hinted that the system could latter be tied to unlockables such as cosmetic rewards in a later patch. Therefore, it's something to keep in mind as you play if you're a completionist that intends to still be playing months down the line.
The only real gameplay complaint I have is that while combat is fast paced, it does still feel slightly basic. Heavy attacks end the current combo and it can feel awkward trying to chain in ranged attacks at times. Some players will argue that combat felt better during the first months of early access, but I tend to disagree, as the first build lacked some of the elements we see in games that copy Freeflow Combat. Overall, it felt more like a typical button masher than anything and just seemed to lack depth at that point.
As far as the campaign goes, it's fairly short. Ten levels, roughly three hours. However, do keep in mind that this isn't a full price AAA release, and that it is designed with short gameplay sessions in mind. For it's price, I feel the game is just right in it's amount of content, especially considering it's a bit of a throwback to those classic arcade games from the late 80s/early 90s.
Story: 6
Grimm Eclipse straddles the line between "excuse plot" and decent story. First off, while no prior knowledge of the series is needed, people new to RWBY are likely to be lost in regards to who the characters are, their motivations, ect. Second, the events of the game are canon to the series. The story itself takes place just after Volume 2, but before Volume 3. Overall, there's not much substance. There's no animated cutscenes, likely due to wanting to keep the action moving as quickly as possible. The story itself is mainly told through the various radio communications with other characters. Despite all that, it does expand on some previously revealed lore regarding a Volume 2 location. However, without giving away spoilers, the ending is a little weak. At this point, it's unknown if that will play into future game content, or potentially be a dangling thread left to be covered by the events of the actual series. This likely will be a non-issue to fans of the show, but it could be unsatisfying to those that might just be here to play the game with friends, or who could very well be getting their first exposure to RWBY through this game.
Graphics: 8
Graphically, the game isn't going to blow anyone away, but on computers that have decent specs it captures the look of the show almost perfectly. There's been much debate over the last several months while the game was in Early Access, but it seems like Rooster Teeth finally managed to reach a good middle ground. Maxed out and in motion, the game carries the look of the show. On lower settings, there seems to be a bit less cel-shading, yet the game still manages to look excellent considering what type of game is it.
Controls: 10
Grimm Eclipse does offer full controller support. If you've got a PS4/XB1 controller, then it's highly recommended that you play with one of those. If not, it's still very much playable with a keyboard and mouse. Everything about the controls feels just right.
Sound: 7
Slightly mixed here. Sound effects are a great mix of sounds ripped directly from the show, as well as the types of sounds you'd expect to hear in a game with very fast paced combat. As far as the music goes, it's a bit mixed. While the game does make excellent use of the series soundtrack created by Jeff Williams, for some odd reason they opted for instrumental versions of some of the key songs from the series. This normally wouldn't be bad, but the instrumentals in question simply remove the vocals and do not replace them with backing instruments to replace the lost vocals. For some tracks, this isn't a problem.
is an example of this working well. Even without the vocals, it still sounds amazing. However other tracks have suffered greatly for it.
and
are the first two tracks that come to mind. The first loses much of it's punch and actually has a part with roughly four seconds of silence, and the second just sounds too repetitive.
also takes a bad hit since the piano from that song was apparently on the same track as the vocals.
I do hope that they address the fact that so many of the songs sound "off" at some point. Granted, it's not a deal breaker for the game, but it is a disappointment since so many of the songs in question are iconic to the series.
Final Verdict:
While the game does have some minor issues, for a first attempt in the world of video games, Rooster Teeth does manage to deliver an enjoyable experience. Updates and additional characters are in the pipeline, and honestly I wouldn't be surprised to possibly see additional levels added to possibly act as a V4 to V5 bridge.

This is going to be a very long post so if you don't feel like sitting there and reading all of this because i know its a lot so scroll to the bottom for a TL:DR, Now these are my personal opinons so i dont expect everyone to agree with me. I just feel I needed to post ths to finally talk about this game and to warn future buyers.
Rwby: Grim Eclipse a game that I have been playing since the initial release. I had such high hopes for the game but after the" Forever Fall" update and the whole models fiasco i started to lose faith in RT Games. With the "Butter and Butter" I was starting to gain some of that lost faith back. That was until they stated that the game was going to be released out of early access so soon and that's where i had lost all faith. This game was not complete by any stretch of the imagination and im going to explain why I think that and why I wont be recomending this game
Story
The story is fine it's nothing special but at the end of the day it gets the job done it drives you forward wanting to know whats going on with Merlot. Honestly when they had originally said that they were working with the writter's of Rwby the animated series and the fact that the show would be cannon to the volumes I was hoping it would be something more worthwhile.
Gameplay
Now when the game was in EA I thought that the combat was fine I had actually enjoyed a lot of what they had added after the "Combat Revision" update and like many others I thought it was a step in the right direction. But thats just it. it was only a step in the right direction. I was hoping that by the final release it would have been fully expanded upon and not just "tweaked". At the end of the day im very dissapointed with the combat system as it is not. Im not asking for it to be as in-depth as say a Devil May Cry game but at the very least expended upon with a few more combos and maybe one other alternate ultimate that maybe uses the characters semblance in some way.
Also when I heard that we were getting persistant character leveling I was hoping that the levels would increase but it didn't it satyed at level 10 which seemed like a bad idea to me i was originaly hoping that it would go up to say 20 levels. And with the level increase and the persistant levels I had hoped that the skill tree would see either a change or a re work. Sadly it got neither (from what I was able to tell). I was hoping that with persistant levels it would have been the perfect time to change the skill tree but that never happened and in my opinion it feels lazy. I would have liked to see a new skill tree where at level one you dont have much in terms of combos or abilities and as you level you unlock new combos and new ultimates and passive effects (Ex aura increase abilities and medic skill). The way the skill tree is right now is you either give up more offensive abilites for defensive and vise versa. Im sire that may have been the way it was intended originaly when the game had more MOBA elements but not itjust doesn't fit. I feel you would get a better feel of progression like this.
The new rank system was something that I was looking forward to until I found that when you rank up it resets everything. All the challenges and even stroy progress from what I heard. I wouldn't know because I chose not to rank up because I dont want to grind endlessly to get everything again. Good idea horibly executed.
Graphics
Now the graphics I feel are good for the most part the backgrounds and levels are beautiful (especially Forever Fall). The character models were a point of topic that for a long time angred me but at this point I no longer care that the models have changed. They were changed and it was explicitly said that we would not be geting the old models back. But I tought to myself if these models could be made to look as good as the original by the time the game released i would have no problem with it. But unfortunatly they are not better the the original's. They are for sure much better the the absolutly awful "FF" models but the fact is this is the full release I expect them to either be as good or better than the models we had from the very start. My main issue with them now is that they just dont seems a detailed as the originals. If you add in the rest of the detail fix some of the faces a little more (Yang's is fine) then I will have no issues with them.
The new UI is great a huge improvment no real flaws there.
Sound&Music
Now the muic for is all used form the show which im sure no one would blame you, the muisc in the show is amazing and its amazing here. I goes to show that with the right music it can make something feel so much better and there were times when the music was pumping and I was kicking butt that I felt like a BADASS. My only issue is that some tracks (sacrifice) tend to repeat all to often.
The sounds for the game are for the most part pretty good. My only issue is that closer to the end of the story I find the SFX seem to be quite low. It could either be me or a bug not to sure.
My Overall Thoughts
Now while I must say that I do enjoy this game (mostly for the love of the show) I do feel that RT Games has really dropped the ball on this game. They started the EA development off so strong, comunicating with the fans, allowing opt in betas, telling us what was coming up and their plans for the future. But it all went down hill after the "FF" update. comunication got worse the fans felt like they were being ignored and just in general were not happy they way develpment was going. Once the game was set for a realease I knew that this game was not going to be the RWBY game I was hoping for. When all is said and done this game just feels so lazy, and I hate to say it but with the game sorely lacking content the fact that the developer's want to charge money for team JNPR is crazy. Do you not understand that when you release a game with so little content and then you want to charge for something that should have been in the game it makes you seem so greedy and so money hungry. Its not that im aganst paid DLC I just feel JNPR should be free anything after that can be paid for all I care. I have been trying to have faith in you but its mostly gone. My friend who bought this with me at the same time would always say "They are going to ♥♥♥♥ it up" and you know what I guess he was right. I hate to come off as and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but this is the way I feel and I know im not alone on this. I was hoping for maybe more taunts and I really wanted there to be skins for the game. the alt outfits from volume 2 would have been perfect. Something that you could have done with the skins that would have surprised everyone was add in the new Volume 4 re dessigns as unlockables. Having those would have been amazing but at the end of the day all you gave us was a bare minimum game. It makes me so sad that I feel I need to give this game♥♥♥♥♥♥and a thumbs down bucause of how bug a fan I am of RWBY, but i feel like I wouldn't be a true fan if I didn't express my reasons of why I feel the way I do about this game. At the end of the day I do still enjoy the game and will continue to play, I could go on about the other things that♥♥♥♥♥♥me off but i'll chose to end my thoughts here.
TL:DR
I feel the game was released way to early and the game just feels lazy and the game is already getting paid DLC that it does not deserve. Tha game is not worth the price tag so if you not a fan of RWBY you probably wont enjoy this game and even if you are a fan the low amount of content may have you feeling buyers remorse after just a few hours.

Excellent little title.
While the "game" elements here are relatively light, by way of being short, leaving you kind of wanting them to be a little bit more elaborated upon, the unique character control ideas and truly excellent narrative more than make up for it.
Starbreeze put an interesting spin on what is actually typical 3rd person platformer fare with the simple yet genius idea of two simultaneously controlled characters in a single-player experience. It's a bit of a shame that the small-scale indie nature of the project in conjunction with the game being focused on story means that these sequences are relatively short and take a back seat to the unfolding narrative. This leads to the actual gameplay ideas explored to feel more touched on than fully fleshed out.
While this by no means makes them or the game any less special feeling, if you're looking for a challenge, you might be left wanting.
The actual world presented and the story one is allowed to experience are top notch. While there are no understandable words spoken throughout, the game does a tremendous job of communicating what is going on with the characters to the player and involving the player in it all. In fact, the whole game feels a little more like an interactive experience than a typical videogame by virtue of the gameplay elements working to bring the player into the world to allow them to experience the journey, moreso than serving as a real challenge. That said, it's not that there is no challenge at all; what is there is provided by the disorientation resulting from having to control two characters at once, and this can be quite fun.
The world itself is quite whimsical, yet also reserved in the use of outlandish fantasy tropes. This lends quite a unique and mature feel to what otherwise feels like a game adaptation of a child's fable a la the Brothers Grimm.
Graphically the visuals don't really have much to commend them on. Instead of attempting to go for flashy the developers went for competent. While the game doesn't look impressive, the visuals themselves are adequate and look good. The artstyle itself is not particularly flamboyant or colourful either. Rather, think nordic minimalism. Everything feels lovingly crafted and subdued, nothing is superfluous. This, again, seems to be so in order to allow place in the centre stage for the actual adventure the two characters share.
And what an adventure that is! The game being as short as it is, it's hard not to spoil anything by discussing details, so I won't.
Suffice it to say that the journey that Starbreeze has fit into the rather short 5 to 6 or so hours of gameplay is really quite the epic and one of the best and refreshing in modern gaming in my humble opinion. Do take into account that the shortness of the experience in this case is deceptive as it is packed with content that should be able to truly touch anyone who plays this.
Highly recommended, especially if you're getting this for your kids. This is the best answer yet to the saccharine world of dumb entertainment available to children these days.

I have to say Holdfast Nations at War has to be one of the best experiences I have had in a long time, despite still being in ALPHA.
Firmly set in the Napoleonic era Holdfast Nations at WAR boasts impressive 150 player mega battles split between naval and land based conflict.  The two battle types are understandably separated but both are pretty impressive in their own right.
Graphically this game oozes realism with the smoke from your pistol not only obscuring your view but offering a form of smoke grenade protection from your enemy.  Having said that that; the vast majority of weapons in the Napoleonic era were less about being accurate more to do with best guess judgment, so often standing perfectly still is a pretty effective survival tactic.
With its vast array of authentic classes available, although some are still firmly in ALPHA the overwhelming experience is considerably Simulation (esc) and they have been very clever in the way that they have implemented certain aspects to encourage compliant team based participation; for example the drummers, violinists and fife players all increase your accuracy when in earshot.
Have you ever heard the saying “Safety in Numbers”?  Well this is the era where that saying, and indeed philosophy was introduced.  Overpowering your enemies was often more about sheer numbers than tactical superiority and what’s more in Holdfast Nations at War this tactic actually works and is indeed the most effective approach to dislodge a large military strongpoint.
Individual skill does play a big part in this game and it will take a while to adjust to both the Napoleonic weaponry and tactics in Holdfast.  The basic premise is that these single shot rifles and pistols are terribly difficult to aim accurately and as such are only really effective at close range; so you’re likely to get 1 maybe two shots off during an advance before you need to switch to bayonets or sharp sword and engage in close quarters battle.
When this approach is applied during a massive multiplayer battle the authenticity of the experience is through the roof!  I absolutely loved it!  This era is a fascinating one and for me at least, battles like this seem considerably more gentlemanly and perhaps even more chivalrous than those fought in more modern times.
When you switch to Naval Battles the experience is completely different but still retains that high level of realism.  Unlike land battles sea battles are unavoidably team based and your crewmates and more importantly your Captain, will make a huge difference to not only your successful outcome but also the level of enjoyment you will get during the battle!
Roleplay is something I thought was behind me, I considered myself to be too old too, straight laced and too much of a grumpy old man to be able to comply in such silliness but Holdfast has shown me this not to be the case!  After a while of playing I could not resist joining in with the old colonial TeamSpeak banter and despite feeling like a Pillock I loved every moment!  There are even entire battalions who work together and play entirely in line formation; it is truly a sight to behold!
In Napoleonic times if you want your idiot Captain to turn the ship to starboard so that you can fire your cannon into the broadside of the French ship that is currently tearing large chunks out of the side of your vessel & decimating your teammates, you had to be very careful about how you phrase that request, lest you find yourself getting up close and personal with the ships cat!
Holdfast Nations at war is still in Alpha and by all accounts has been for some considerable time.  This means that certain aspect of the game are missing or incomplete and many changes are likely to occur during the remaining months and perhaps even years of development.  That being said Holdfast is a very accomplished and hugely entertaining game which serves up one of the most authentic Napoleonic experiences to date.
One of the major issues at present relates to Melee attacks; they are at best a little bit hit and miss.  According to the games forum this is one of the major things the developers are looking to address and confidence is high that melee fighting will be improved at some point.  Despite this infuriating melee display there are other issues surrounding the game which can dampen but not dislodge the feel good factor that Nations at War serves up.
Some gameplay alterations also need to be considered; like spawn points for example.  As it stands right now often spawn points are out in the open, often miles away from the objective and can be easily overrun and spawn killing is fair game here.  However the game experience is so good that to be honest nobody cares that much about these issues; there is way too much fun being had and too much enjoyment being shared to allow something like 50 French riflemen surrounding your spawn point and picking you off like fish in a barrel to in anyway douse such a great experience.
Holdfast Nations at war is a tremendous achievement and with future development looking likely to include cavalry this is undoubtedly one title you should look to have in your collection.
P.S:
Whilst sea battles are mostly fought in open sea there are a few variations available.  For the land battles though the game has a surprisingly decent number of maps from snow covered plains to dusty ruins and everything in between.  Each of the land maps has an often sparse but overall good layout and within it the hills and available cover are nicely intertwined.  The game even supports a night day cycle which adds yet another layer of realism and complexity to proceedings.
