"Puzzle Horror"
I'm not a superstitious man, and I've never written a review before. But I cannot seem to shake the idea that if I don't give this game its due, some terrible fate is going to befall me.
My dreams have of late been haunted by visions of dark chasms and gargantuan caves deep beneath the earth filled with ancient sculptures and mystical symbols containing some long-forgotten warning from an ancient civilization. A foreboding certainty from those dreams linger in my mind after I wake: That I must decipher the symbols before it's too late... as if I'm forced to play some kind of puzzle game fraught with terrible meaning. Although I feel like I'm loosing my mind from fear, I'm absolutely certain that I must solve this mystery -- even if it only means uncovering the primordial evil that really lies behind this nightmare -- the Horror dwelling beneath.

I don't play puzzle games, because I find them frustrating. Wut? Me stupid? Me smash!
But this was good.
I bought this game because of its setting; who doesn't want to become a cannibalistic incorporeal monster set loose amongst hapless archaelogists? I certainly do. Especially when I have 2 hours to get my 5 euros back should I prove to be somewhat less deadly to them than a malaria spreading mosquito. And in 5 hours, I finished them all. Well, not all, because some of them managed to run away, but I certainly enjoyed making them♥♥♥♥♥♥their pants.
So, what I want to say: if you play (and love) Doom, Civ6, Skyrim/Fallout4, but basically no puzzle games - just like me - and you want something different, then your 5 euros will be well spent on this.
Puzzle gurus beware! The "casual" tag is totally accurate. My 5 hours may translate into much fewer in your case!

At this point in time, I can't honestly recommend this game to anyone but die-hard GunZ fans.
The P2P connections have been scrapped in lieu of a player host system, which works rather atrociouly for the aspect of fighting against lag; host is at a distinct advantage 90% of the time.
The combat has been dumbed down from the open and evolving styles seen in GunZ 1 (whether it was due to glitches or not is irrelevant, it made for the most unique experience I've seen to date in any game). Even the customization that allowed you to be so diverse in GunZ 1 is gone.
Instead we have a system that begs to be a shooter/melee arena, but has so many poorly integrated RPG elements in it that you end up with neither a shooter nor action RPG.
All that said, this is still probably one of the most unique shooter experiences on the multiplayer market. So if you can deal with all the crap or just like a decent challenge, it's worth a look at.
For myself, though I'll keep playing in memory of GunZ, this game only rates about a 6/10

The wonderful and ingenius second installment of what I think is the best physics based puzzle game franchise. This sequel offers a unique fairytale storybook style in contrast to the dark, somewhat dungeon based original. The game feels more open than its predecessor despite removing items and replacing them with sparce non-gameplay influencing collectibles. This game is packed with impressive, long levels and excellent replayability. Players have to be more creative and conservative as puzzle are not as easily circumvented though solving them is more interesting and visually rewarding. This game is well worth buying at a sale (about $5) and has an equally incredible expansion pack (about $2 on sale) that adds a new chapter to the story and plenty of new levels and skills to play with. I truly recommend fans of puzzle games and casual gamers to buy this game. Also, see my review of the original Trine.

While I see a lot of people gripe about the microtransactions in the single player, I see this as a minor issue. Annoying, but minor. The upgrade points (praxis) you get throughout the game is abundant, and the real gaming experience comes with not buying them at all. You'll get the hard choices, and you'll need to set a plan for how you want to play to synergize the upgrades you choose. I have no idea how it is when buying praxis kits, but I can't for the life of me expect that you gain the same amount of weight on your choices.
My main gripe is the story. The story is... well... alright. Up until when it suddenly ends. Abruptly. It feels as though Deus Ex: Mankind Divided has a third part that won't be released yet, possibly due to future DLC's. Let me just say that if that is the case, that's some damn poor choices. This is a full priced AAA game, but it feels like a book where 1/3 of the pages has been torn out. When I finished, I was shocked and flabbergasted. None of the major threads had been finished. None of the major mysteries that were set up during the course of the game had been revealed. I sat back, feeling I had finally completed the first henchman in the game. But then I got the end credits (!?).
This is bad and disappointing. Especially bad is the fact that the last cinematic of the game explicitly baits that there's MUCH more to the story than has been released. As a person with a lot of enjoyment of the story (and looking forward to everything coming together in the end), this is a disappointment that I can't for the life of me recommend until it's much much MUCH cheaper.

Breaks my heart to say this, but Rise of the Triad is not a good game. If Steam had a neutral vote, I would use that. As it is now, I have to say it's just slightly below the threshold of my recommendation (for whatever it's worth).
The game has mediocre controls and physics, which is terrible for certain levels. Some levels try to be platforming stages, but the awkward physics and movement of your character make precise movements a distant dream, resulting in savescumming and/or frustration. The guns feel extremely weak and lacking in impact, even common enemies can shrug off several "special weapons" much too easily. Getting shot at is also poorly conveyed as the direction the damage arrow points at might not be anywhere near the direction the shot came from, not to mention its very poor job at indicating imminent danger.
Easily the most disappointing thing in the game is the level design. It's all over the place with very hit-and-miss results, having more misses than hits, really. They focused too hard on the "platforming" of the original and favored it instead of shooting things. The bosses were interestingly designed, but poorly executed, especially the final boss. El Oscuro was a terrible fight in the original to begin with and they somehow managed to capture that same fart in a jar while multiplying the awfulness exponentially.
Graphically, the game is pretty meh for a 2013 game and that's literally all I can say about it.
As for sounds and music, the redone soundtrack turns the unique and diverse originals into generic music with pretty much nothing but the same guitar all the way through. The voice acting is plain bad. Hearing the characters talk mid-game gets grating after a while as they repeat the same line for the tenth bazooka you've picked up in the level. Fortunately, there is an option to enable the original soundtrack, though it only allows the generic midi synths and a few tracks don't even loop properly.
Stability is also an issue. Starting as early as the first level I experienced crashes, but they calmed down after a couple of levels. Crashes still happened, but they weren't as common as in the first few levels. There were also some noticeable strange framerate drops in very specific areas, messing up jumps and letting enemies get free shots on you for a split second.
I still enjoyed at least some of my time playing the game, but I'm glad I am done with it
On a side note, the game likes to mock you if you die, which is cute at first, but gets really annoying really fast when the unique voice clips run out. There's no way to keep that from going stale instantly, so it should have never been added.

Completely new review, post XL update.
For those who have not seen the Mortal Kombat X scandal, the TDLR is: Ed Boon personally promised the MK9 / Injustice disasters won't be allowed to repeat, and the PC version will be as polished as the console version. On relase day it was revealed that NetherRealm did not work a single minute on MKX PC, and outsourced it to the most amateur, famous for their fckups hated porting studio, High Voltage. Again. To the same people who messed up MK9 too. TLDR is, it was an Arkham Knight level of disaster again, with over 90Gb of patches that always were a step ahead and 2 steps back regarding performance. Once they even accidently deleted everyone's profiles, along with unlocks and everything, even from cloud with no possible recovery, so Warner decided to give away the unlock everything DLC for free for everyone (optional to install, can be uninstalled separately and it gives your current profile back with your unlocks only). Kombat Pack 2 came out, but not for PC - the game's reputation was so bad (dropped from 15.000 players to 500 and sinking) Warner didn't bother to sell the second paid DLC pack. MKXL came out for consoles, along with a brand new fantastic netcode for online play, but neither Warner, NetherRealm or High Voltage answered to questions - where is the PC support? A few months later Warner announced they drop PC support for MKX, leaving it to rot (what they didn't say is, players already left it to rot a year ago at this point). Amongts others, I too had a detailed review discussing everything you see above in more detail, High Voltage's fckups, and was among the loudest who hated the game and warned everyone about avoiding it.
That changed a year later, in 2016 september.
8 months later out of the blue, a Mortal Kombat XL open beta popped up on steam. Warner didn't do any marketing for it, but XL was coming to PC, with thankfully High Voltage fired from the job and a completely new, dedicated and skilled team working on the port. The resaults are fantasic.
* Massive performance improvements. Easily achieved 60 fps now with higher settings than before.
* No more crashes and instabilities.
* The new netcode is the best I've seen since the 4th generation of Street Fighter, possibly better.
* Free costumes because why not.
* Decent, enjoyable story and varied challanges for singleplayer content. Doesn't make much sense without MK9's story, slightly more with it, but arguably the best singleplayer story in any fighting game to date. Plus Mileena kiss scene.
* Sadly, character selection menu and X-Rays are still 30 fps locked, but the game is smoother than ever. This is by design, X-Rays are basicly rendered videos, but still the drop can be felt.
While the game on sale is a good purchase now for anyone interested, it's real value depends on multiplayer. Everything is given now, to have a thriving online scene - performance, netcode, knowledge. Question is, can the near uprepairable reputatio of the original MKX overshadow XL or not? Will players come back, will new ones join? Without online players, there is no real fight. I recommend you to check out some steam statistics.
Warner and NetherRealm clearly paid for this re-porting project not because they hope for making profit from MKXL PC, after the original X had Arkham Knight level of destroyed reputation, but more likely they wanted restore some trust in NetherRealm's name in the eyes of the PC community, with the upcoming Injustice 2 being seen as "it will be a sh*t port" long before relase. With MKXL, they prooved themselves to be capable of making decent, good PC versions, so I'll give them a shot with Injustice 2 - I'd advise NOT to pre-order it of course. Whatever they'll advertise as a bonus, will be aviable for purchase for a few euros a month later tops.
MKXL update is free for everyone who has Mortal Kombat X, so you may want to pick up an MKX key from a 3rd party store before they disappear and only expensive MKXL keys are on the market. It's extremely cheap, it was for a long time, and even cheaper now (from 3 to 7 euros for the core game and 2-3 more for Kombat Pack 1) because every retailer is getting rid of the old keys. You also get a nice discount on Kombat Pack 2 on steam, if you own the game + KP1.
EDIT: Multiplayer is like beating a dead horse. Roughly 50 players online all the time, 45 of them play on near maximum settings and low fps (effecting your game too since you should be in perfect sync), the 5 others are players with over 2000 games played and you'll stand no chance against them. Coming from over 4000 hours of Street Fighter, in comparsion there is no ground for mindgames and real respectful matches in MKX, because either it's a joke category (low fps / terrible connection people) or russians trying to humiliate you after them knowing, they challanged someone who has thousands of matches less played than them. Singleplayer is an okay experience, playing vs the AI is pointless after that, c'mon it's a fighting game, multiplayer or nothing. And that part, despite all the great changes, is still dead, thanks to Warner and High Voltage. Edited in part comes from 1,5 months of testing it (multiplayer only, 20 hours). Changed the review to NOT RECOMMENDED.

This is going to be a very long post so if you don't feel like sitting there and reading all of this because i know its a lot so scroll to the bottom for a TL:DR, Now these are my personal opinons so i dont expect everyone to agree with me. I just feel I needed to post ths to finally talk about this game and to warn future buyers.
Rwby: Grim Eclipse a game that I have been playing since the initial release. I had such high hopes for the game but after the" Forever Fall" update and the whole models fiasco i started to lose faith in RT Games. With the "Butter and Butter" I was starting to gain some of that lost faith back. That was until they stated that the game was going to be released out of early access so soon and that's where i had lost all faith. This game was not complete by any stretch of the imagination and im going to explain why I think that and why I wont be recomending this game
Story
The story is fine it's nothing special but at the end of the day it gets the job done it drives you forward wanting to know whats going on with Merlot. Honestly when they had originally said that they were working with the writter's of Rwby the animated series and the fact that the show would be cannon to the volumes I was hoping it would be something more worthwhile.
Gameplay
Now when the game was in EA I thought that the combat was fine I had actually enjoyed a lot of what they had added after the "Combat Revision" update and like many others I thought it was a step in the right direction. But thats just it. it was only a step in the right direction. I was hoping that by the final release it would have been fully expanded upon and not just "tweaked". At the end of the day im very dissapointed with the combat system as it is not. Im not asking for it to be as in-depth as say a Devil May Cry game but at the very least expended upon with a few more combos and maybe one other alternate ultimate that maybe uses the characters semblance in some way.
Also when I heard that we were getting persistant character leveling I was hoping that the levels would increase but it didn't it satyed at level 10 which seemed like a bad idea to me i was originaly hoping that it would go up to say 20 levels. And with the level increase and the persistant levels I had hoped that the skill tree would see either a change or a re work. Sadly it got neither (from what I was able to tell). I was hoping that with persistant levels it would have been the perfect time to change the skill tree but that never happened and in my opinion it feels lazy. I would have liked to see a new skill tree where at level one you dont have much in terms of combos or abilities and as you level you unlock new combos and new ultimates and passive effects (Ex aura increase abilities and medic skill). The way the skill tree is right now is you either give up more offensive abilites for defensive and vise versa. Im sire that may have been the way it was intended originaly when the game had more MOBA elements but not itjust doesn't fit. I feel you would get a better feel of progression like this.
The new rank system was something that I was looking forward to until I found that when you rank up it resets everything. All the challenges and even stroy progress from what I heard. I wouldn't know because I chose not to rank up because I dont want to grind endlessly to get everything again. Good idea horibly executed.
Graphics
Now the graphics I feel are good for the most part the backgrounds and levels are beautiful (especially Forever Fall). The character models were a point of topic that for a long time angred me but at this point I no longer care that the models have changed. They were changed and it was explicitly said that we would not be geting the old models back. But I tought to myself if these models could be made to look as good as the original by the time the game released i would have no problem with it. But unfortunatly they are not better the the original's. I was desperately wanting to get a Steam card ever since the game came out. It was the reason I finally bought a game. It was even my first purchased game! (Usually stuck to free to play games.) I absolutely love the RWBY show, but... I have mixed feelings for the RWBY game...
Pros
1.)You can play as the charcters on Team RWBY!
2.) You can level up your characters and unlock cool skills!
3.) You can hear the RWBY characters speak~ (Yang's puns/jokes! Yes!!! I love them~)
4.) So far I haven't seen anything that shows you need to pay to win in this game!
5.) You don't have to worry about your gear being worse than everyone else's gear.
6.) Multiplayer Options. Going solo mode is boring and can get tiring fast, but I found that doing multiplayer mode helps a bit with that.
7.) Speaking of multiplayer runs, the game offers an option to invite your friends to a private one!
8.) The other multiplayer run you can do is the Quick Group option. If you have no friends or your friends don't have the game... (Like me~) You are able to join a group with random people who are also playing in Quick Group.
Cons
1.) Sometimes it's difficult to play in multiplayer since some people rage when new players make a mistake. Of course, this isn't the game's fault, but just be aware that it could happen. (This is true for every game with a multiplayer option though!)
2.) It seems a little repetative and can get boring. All you do is a get a message from your scroll, kill some grimm, have a small break to find artifacts/xp boxes, kill some grimm waves, and repeat.
3.) Limited character choices. The only avaliable characters are the RWBY teammembers. Blake is my favorite character, but I would also love to try others like Pyrrah or maybe even Nora!
4.) Can't costomize your character! I wish I could change their outfits...
5.) No tutoral! You have to figure out what everything does on your own!
6.) You have a low level cap (it's 10).
7.) After level 10 you can trade all your xp for rank 1 which is great, but... I do all that work just to go up one rank? It's a lot of time to level up all your characters to max, but would be cool if they would give a bonus reward (Maybe they could have it so you unlock other characters after each rank. The requirements to complete for ranking up get harder each time and I'd love an additional reward for the effort put in~)
8.) Speaking of the ranks.. There's no real incentive for going up the ranks other than a fancy achievement. (Beacon Graduate is only unlocked after reaching Rank 10!?)
I would recommend this game if you have patience. There will be times you can have issues with teammates or you get bored of doing the same thing over and over. I can't tell you if you would enjoy the game unless you actually try it, though. And I do recommend you try it for yourself and see what you think! (Plus, I'm still new to the game and this is my first review of a game so I can't say I'm an expert at judging.)

I love the world of Remnant.  I love the show.  And I do really like this game.  While there could be a few things changed, like less defending an area for a few waves, they also get a lot of things right with this game.  Team RWBY look like they came straight off the show, as do the Grimm.  They use the very same voice actors (very talented voice actors I may add) and that's how it should be.  The main thing that I love about this game is that the developers actually listen to their fans.  Remember when they changed the character models and people didnt like that?  They changed them back to make them look more like their models on the show.  You go, Rooster Teeth.  I'm gonna give a list of the pros and cons of how it currently is in my opinion.
Pros:
-The game is fun to play solo or multiplayer.  You get to play as anyone of Team RWBY (Weiss is my favorite, Yang my second favorite).  I see that people want other characters in here too, and I'm sure they'll put Team JNPR in here sometime in the future.  Come on..who doesn't want to play as Nora?
-The game looks wonderful even on potato settings.  They put a lot of detail into making Remnant and they do a damn good job.
-The voice acting is godly.  They have the same people who voice the characters in the show, (yes, even Oobleck), voice them in the game.  While I think there needs to be more interaction between team mates, they still can show off their personality with just a few lines.  A few more lines of dialogue for the main characters would be good to have as well.
-Rooster Teeth Games actually listens to their fans.  I already have said that above, but I'll say it again, they're some of the best developers when it comes to listening to feedback.  They don't ignore our opinions and their patch notes are pretty funny to read sometimes you gotta admit.  You honestly can't hate Rooster Teeth.
-Yang's puns.
Cons:
-The combat is a bit too simplistic.  You only have to click or hit a button a couple of times and hit another button to do an admitidly cooler heavy attack.  I have tried all the characters and so far, Weiss seems to be the most helpful out of all of them with her large AOE freezes.  Should give all the characters more combos to do.
-You can't pause single player.  I can understand multiplayer, but you should at least be able to pause a solo game.
-The counter doesn't always work.  There have been several times where I try to counter an enemy, and it doesn't respong and I end up going down.  Please fix that.  It'd be amazing to be surrounded by enemies and if they start to attack, just counter them one by one and then ult.
-Maybe adding a few more enemies would spice things up even more.  Additional mutated Grimm and whatnot.  I'm not gonna hold this against them though.  The Grimm still look like they jumped right out of the show.  Just need more variety.
-While I know this isn't a AAA title, with the amount of stuff in it currently, it should only be about 15 dollars right now.  Once they add Horde Mode and maybe a few more things, then bring it up to this price.  The current price right now on this game doesn't need to be this high.
Things they should do:
-Bring in some different outfits.  Use the alternative ones from the show as well as some unique ones to the game.
-Bring in Team JNPR at least.  Maybe Team SSSN as well.
-More victory taunts instead of just having the one.
-More Yang puns.  She doesn't make enough.
-More game modes and add challenge modes.
All in all, this is still a great game to play with friends and solo.  With a few more tweaks and additional stuff added to the game, it'd be even better.  However I'd recommend getting this game on sale unless you're a big fan of the show.

Excellent little title.
While the "game" elements here are relatively light, by way of being short, leaving you kind of wanting them to be a little bit more elaborated upon, the unique character control ideas and truly excellent narrative more than make up for it.
Starbreeze put an interesting spin on what is actually typical 3rd person platformer fare with the simple yet genius idea of two simultaneously controlled characters in a single-player experience. It's a bit of a shame that the small-scale indie nature of the project in conjunction with the game being focused on story means that these sequences are relatively short and take a back seat to the unfolding narrative. This leads to the actual gameplay ideas explored to feel more touched on than fully fleshed out.
While this by no means makes them or the game any less special feeling, if you're looking for a challenge, you might be left wanting.
The actual world presented and the story one is allowed to experience are top notch. While there are no understandable words spoken throughout, the game does a tremendous job of communicating what is going on with the characters to the player and involving the player in it all. In fact, the whole game feels a little more like an interactive experience than a typical videogame by virtue of the gameplay elements working to bring the player into the world to allow them to experience the journey, moreso than serving as a real challenge. That said, it's not that there is no challenge at all; what is there is provided by the disorientation resulting from having to control two characters at once, and this can be quite fun.
The world itself is quite whimsical, yet also reserved in the use of outlandish fantasy tropes. This lends quite a unique and mature feel to what otherwise feels like a game adaptation of a child's fable a la the Brothers Grimm.
Graphically the visuals don't really have much to commend them on. Instead of attempting to go for flashy the developers went for competent. While the game doesn't look impressive, the visuals themselves are adequate and look good. The artstyle itself is not particularly flamboyant or colourful either. Rather, think nordic minimalism. Everything feels lovingly crafted and subdued, nothing is superfluous. This, again, seems to be so in order to allow place in the centre stage for the actual adventure the two characters share.
And what an adventure that is! The game being as short as it is, it's hard not to spoil anything by discussing details, so I won't.
Suffice it to say that the journey that Starbreeze has fit into the rather short 5 to 6 or so hours of gameplay is really quite the epic and one of the best and refreshing in modern gaming in my humble opinion. Do take into account that the shortness of the experience in this case is deceptive as it is packed with content that should be able to truly touch anyone who plays this.
Highly recommended, especially if you're getting this for your kids. This is the best answer yet to the saccharine world of dumb entertainment available to children these days.

Also, I do not own a controller so I played the game together with my girlfreind and we loved the co-op, maybe that was one of the developer's goals: to get people to actually play a simple and beautiful game together. Nicely thought out.
All in all, the few hours spent with the brothers will remain as a pleasant memory. The game does not have a high replayability rating as it is very linear but there are a couple of achievements to be hunted. It will, however, make you feel something. Sadness or compassion or love, or all three. It is worth to experience it!

Let me start by saying this--I am hugely, deeply passionate for good storytelling and the impact it can have on people. I also happen to enjoy video games. That said, I have played and loved video games that had a deep and emotional story, but were lacking in gameplay. I have played games that had immersive and enjoyable mechanics, but not much of a story. And I have played games that had both a great story and innovative mechanics, but the two felt entirely separate. But never before Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons have I played a game where the mechanics and the story were so completely and brilliantly intertwined to create a more deep and immersive experience.
This game has you controlling two brothers, on a personal quest to travel the stunningly beautiful fantasy land they live in, in search of medicine to save their father. I would describe it as single-player co-op, in that you control both brothers at once. If you play with a controller, each joystick and top button controls one of the brothers. This mechanic of gameplay is part of what makes the experience so immersive--though it can be a bit awkward, you get used to it, and it helps the narrative to pack a bigger punch when, for example, the two brothers have to scale the side of a crumbling castle connected by a rope, and each relies on the other to reach the top safely.
I won't spoil anything, but I will say this--the story of Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is impactful. It hits HARD. It takes turns you don't expect it to. It deals with dark and unsettling subject material, shown through the eyes of children. I haven't cried over a video game since To The Moon (like, not sniffles or a single tear, but open crying), and while I adored that game, this game packs a far bigger punch. This is one of those games that I feel will stay with me for a long, long time.
As far as the gameplay itself goes, Brothers is exceedingly enjoyable. The puzzles are interesting and can be challenging, but aren't difficult. You won't find yourself frustrated or wanting to look up a walkthrough. The controls work well, once you get used to them (that said, I'd highly recommend you play this game with a controller. The keyboard controls are awkward). The puzzles don't repeat themselves. The environments are stunningly beautiful, and encourage exploration, but don't make it possible to get lost.
There are some fun achievements to be gained as a result of exploring the environment as you play.
The music in this game is top-notch. I bought the soundtrack as soon as I finished the game.
All of this being said, I cannot recommend Brothers highly enough. If you care about video games or good stories at all, please, please play this game. Don't watch a playthrough. Trust me, you'll ruin it for yourself. This is a game that is meant to be experienced. The story is between 2.5-3 hours long (I took about 5, but I took my time with it). Please, buy this game, sit down, and experience it all in one go. It's hard to really express what makes this game great without revealing spoilers (DAT ENDING DOE), but I can say this--I cannot imagine anyone playing Brothers and regretting it.
I am so very glad this game exists. While this game is not without its flaws, it is such a wonderful example of what video games can be, as well as what storytelling can be.

Brothers - in which a boy learns how to swim.
Summary: I'm not recommending this game, as I didn't find it to be all that engaging. Pretty to look at, though.
/-- Technical  Elements --/
Graphics: Very solid. They're working with a great engine here and the visuals are extremely nice to look at. Nothing earth-shattering or limit-breaking - all is smooth, soft, and pleasant in terms of tone and contour.
Sound: Also good, particularly the light ambient music. Not really a fan of the strange language used (comes out like babble or moonspeak to me), but there isn't enough vocalization in the game for this to really matter.
Control: Mixed feelings. The game has you playing as two characters simultaneously. Sometimes this leads to two-player mechanics being executed by a single player, but just as often it involves repeating one set of actions with both sticks simultaneously. The twin player concept limits how much action you can actually direct on a per-player basis, and most everything you do comes down to "position stick, hold trigger". Get used to gripping the triggers for extended durations, too; you can't let go of a trigger while climbing, and climbing is a key activity in this game.
/-- Story --/
The story is well contained, with a beginning, a middle, and an end. That said, the story doesn't really go much of anywhere, reducing the ability to "feel" about the game to the moments you recall from the journey. Other games have run with this concept further and in my opinion better while still showing some progression or serious change (Journey among them, oddly enough), but in this game you will eventually teach a boy to swim. That's pretty much the whole of it.
The main dilemma of the story is that your father is sick, but he's referenced so infrequently through the game's course that it's easy to forget he's even out there. Some sort of hook back to the reason for the grand quest might have been useful, though I'm not sure how best to convey that. Ori and the Blind Forest managed whlie still sticking with made up languages, and showed significant progression, too -- but I digress. Point is, there's a story, but I don't find it particularly rewarding.
/-- Value for the money  --/
This is a fairly short game and should probably be hunted on sale. $10 or less is a good mark to watch for. I'd possibly argue for $5 but the amount of work that went into the visuals is evident and is worth some reward.
/-- Closing thoughts --/
I didn't really like the core mechanics very much and think the game would have run a bit better with a solo protagonist. The visuals and sound are solid, but the story is kind of "meh". There wasn't much in the way of engagement for me. I didn't get lost in this title and even felt a bit fatigued playing through end to end.
I don't actually recommend this title; I find it to be pretty average and there are better uses of your time and money. But if you're a hardcore visuals enthusiast, you might give it a try.

While Brutal Legend is a little rough around the edges, it makes sense because it's metal. I don't expect perfection from metal, I expect it to bring that primal feeling when music connects to your soul. In Brutal Legend you play as Jack Black playing a personification of himself in a lovingly crafted world styled after various types of metal music. Part action game, part RTS, all rock.
Pros:
Great story/scenery. Traveling across the world through the different 'types' of metal and just seeing all the clever ways in which Double Fine incorporated metal music into the landscape is so much fun. Running into icons of metal as the story progresses is also a treat.
Music. If you want to just cruise around in a sick♥♥♥♥♥ride and blast metal music as you tour the landscape you sure can. I know I did. What more could you ask for from a soundtrack than the greats?
Character/Enemy design. As I mentioned earlier the scenery was gorgeous, but I especially love the stylization of the characters and enemies. Brutal Legends versions of Ozzy, Lemmy Kilmister, Rob Halford, and more are just perfect. The metal-ized creatues fit right in among the chrome and stone.
Cons:
The RTS bits. While they were enjoyable enough, they were sometimes a tad frustrating, especially some of the later scenarios. Honestly my biggest gripe with them is they just felt somewhat jarring. You'd go along with all this action gameplay and suddenly you're managing little minions in an RTS band fight.
Driving controls. While I did love cruising around there were definitely times where the keyboard/mouse driving controls just felt a bit rough.
Overall I'd give it 8/10. It's not a the perfect game, but if you love heavy metal then I would definitely recommend giving it a go.

I'll start by saying i never expected much form this game, somehow back when it came out the reviews convinced me to avoid it somehow. Even when , at least for me, the Double Fine signature made it all that more alluring.
Long story short, i was pleasantly surprised. I haven't finished the game as of yet, but i can't wait to do it.
Although i was a little bit put down at the beginning of my playthrough because of some minor issues in the end the game grew on me, i canpt exactly put my finger on it, but it did. Maybe the presentation, which is great -
-. You can expect the usual double fine characters that exude personality (had some full throttle vibes here and there), the wacky exchanges and GREAT atmosphere -
. On that part i also felt the need to uncover all the cameos, JUST BECAUSE THEY ARE GREAT. A couple of artists even do more that one character, and some of those are HILARIOUS.
Gameplay wise it's not groundbreaking, but taking into account that it's a 2009 game i think we can cut it some slack and just enjoy the experience.
On the good side I enjoyed the free roam elements -GTA style like map- and the battleground aspects of the game, even if the second was not fleshed out in its full capacity, sometimes it felt clunky but still fun, and it was never frustrating. Combat felt better when having units under your command. This is not a game where you can charge head on into the enemy and wipe out their whole army singlehandedly, i had to learn that the hard way. Even with all the abilities- "solos"- unlocked i had to be mindful of my positioning in the battlefield in order to actually pull them off (that's beacause every  major abilitie is cast with a guitar solo minigame and while performing Eddie would be vulnerable to enemy attacks, so there's no safe way to spam the bigger, more damaging solos. Again, this underlines the main role of Eddie, he's a roadie and he rants all the time on how his role is to make the show, the band, everything and everyone ELSE look good.
On the bad side, as i mentioned before, are some minor, but sometimes annoying points to take into account:
There's NO fast travel option, and it is a big map. As much as i liked roaming through the landscape, sometimes i just wanted to get somewhere fast, I'M LOOKING AT YOU HUNTER. Also The collision detection when running through hills is terrible. That could be forgiven but in a game where you can't jump it can quickly get dicey with the terrain sometimes. It's clearly aimed to just explore certain areas and avoid heavily decorated ones.
Progression also felt a little uneven but the reason for it probably has to do with the use of the -overpowered- DLC upgrades (there was no way to know which  ones where DLC and which weren't)
Don't come here expecting a typical hack&slash, this game it's unique and a bloody good time. After all this time it actually holds up pretty well and totally worth the price.
Metal, Noise, Blood, and Fire! Nuff said!
10/10 would shovel hand again

I think that after two full playthroughs and completing all the side missions I'm ready to write a review for this game. After my first playthrough, I was genuinely disappointed and angry when reaching the end of the game. It was obvious sequel bait, the game didn't feel finished, in fact, the only reason I even knew the game was over is because they flashed "NEW GAME + UNLOCKED" on my screen. However, after having finished the game a second time, I'm impressed with what's there, and it feels a lot more complete than I originally thought it did.
Both of my playthroughs were on the "Give Me Deus Ex" difficulty, and the second was a New Game + continuation of the first, so I had roughly half of all the augmentations in the game right from the start. My first playthrough took roughly 13 hours to complete, and I missed about 6 side missions. My second playthrough was right around 20 hours, and I completed every side mission in the game this time.
I want to focus on the positive first, and outline what I think the game did right. Most important thing they got right are the characters, but even so, a lot of them feel like weaker characters than we got in Human Revolution. Next are gameplay changes, if it was in Human Revolution, it's better in this game, and that's a good thing. And finally the variation of the side missions, they don't all feel like they have you doing the same thing.
Now for what I feel are the features that neither hurt nor help the game. First off, the new augmentations feel right at home, but, I only ever found myself using one of them. And, the story, no, it's not nearly as good as Human Revolution, but it's not as bad as people have been saying, it has some interesting themes in it.
And now for the bad parts of the game. The AI wasn't improved at all from Human Revolution, and, if it was, it doesn't feel like it. The PC port can't get much worse, in fact, I'd say it's *almost* worth Steam giving out refunds. And of course, the business model, one use consumable DLCs, and microtransactions.
Now to focus a bit more on each point I brought up, first off, the characters. While, I do feel like most of them are weaker than their Human Revolution counterparts, there's a few that are just as strong as Human Revolution's best characters. Elias Chikane is the pilot for TF-29, and, in my opinion, he's a better character than Faridah Malik. Otar Botkoveli is this game's answer to Tong from Human Revolution, and again, in my opinion, he's done VERY well, by the end of the game I felt he was more powerful than Tong ever was. And my personal favorite new character, Jim Miller, director of TF-29. Stronger than David Sarif? Maybe not, but he's right up there with him. However, for some of the other characters, they just split up Frank Pritchard's personality and put it into a few other characters. But for Pritchard's counterpart herself, Alex Vega, she's probably one of the more annoying characters in the game. This game offers a lot of choices, and Vega is always telling you to choose the one that you feel is right, but if you don't choose the one that she wanted you to, then she complains about how you're not doing the right thing and how you're missing out on this and that. Not a very likable character, but then again, Pritchard was pretty hard to like.
As for gameplay changes, the new movement system for cover to cover movements is done perfectly, it feels natural and it makes stealth feel like less of a chore. The gunplay also got a few improvements, however with the mouse acceleration in the game it's a bit hard to notice.
The final positive are the side missions, they're all fairly lengthy, well thought out, and the best part about them is how varied they are. They aren't all fetch quests, sure, there's a few here and there, but I don't want to get into too much so I don't spoil anything, just know that they are varied and well worth the time.
Moving onto the neutral sections of the game, first one being the story. Is it as interesting as Human Revolution? No, most of the themes explored in this game can be found in others. But then there are a few, that, in my opinion, almost make the story one of the better parts of the game, but they focus too little on those themes and too much on the much more bland ones. On top of that, the main villain is mostly forgettable, like most of them in Human Revolution. However, this game doesn't have any standout villains like Human Revolution had with Jaron Namir and Hugh Darrow. They're are more like Zhao Yun Ru, at the end of the game you question why they were even in it as much as they were.
The new augmentations are also a neutral aspect of the game, remote hacking is the only one that I found to be useful all the time rather than situational. They all seem to be viable, but sadly you won't be needing most of them, much like the base augmentations.
And for the part that I'll be spending the most time writing, the negatives.

The AI in this game is still awful, stealth in this game is the same as it was in Human Revolution. Enemies have next to no peripheral vision and can only see 10 meters in front of themselves. In fact, stealth in this game is FAR easier than it was in Human Revolution with it's new cover to cover movement. Which, in my opinion, is not a good thing.
Now for the PC Port, wow, it's *almost* worth Steam giving out refunds for this game. 5-6 minute long loading screens that feature Jensen performing the same 3 actions over and over. Severe frame drops, which seem to only take place after 3-4 consecutive hours of play. I only ran into three or four crashes while playing the game, which have (allegedly) been patched out of the game.
Now for the business model, which, is ironic considering how corporate greed has been a minor theme in Deus Ex since the original game. Day one DLC, which is a one time use, once you remove it from your storage it's only ever on that save. Hopefully you're not playing on the "I Never Asked For This" difficulty. And utterly useless microtransactions, in fact, why are they even in the story? I mean, is that why credits are no longer rewards for finishing side missions? So you can sell credits to us for real money? Yeah, how about no.
And now for something that I haven't mentioned yet in the review. The other game mode that ships with the game. Breach mode. It's easily one of the worst game modes in any video game I've played. There's a total of 4 objectives in it: "Download Data" you run up to big data towers and hit 'E' on them. "Collect Data Fragments" you look for little purple diamonds and pick them up. "Eliminate Units" you just kill the required number of defense systems. And "Eliminate Prime Unit" you just have to kill an incredibly strong version of the people you've been fighting. That's it. I've put two hours into this mode and have not completed the first server yet, and there's 3 of them. Oh yeah, your equipment comes in card packs, want a Combat Rifle? You better buy some card packs. Need Armor Piercing ammo for that Combat Rifle? More card packs. Do you NEED firewall key fragments to continue? You need to either go back and grind those missions for unrealistic time limits and score goals. Or you know, buy some card packs. The worst part about it is that they try to give you backstory to the companies and locations that are in the main game. But here's the best part about it, you have to deal with NPCs that communicate only via text, that give you the EXACT same information as the fully voiced and developed characters in the story mode. Breach mode is a complete cash grab and waste of time, just avoid it at all costs.
To end the review, let me put it this way, it's basically Human Revolution. If you liked Human Revolution, you'll probably like this. If you're new to the games, start with Human Revolution, try that before you pay full price for this.

Most bugs are fixed now. The story and the world itself are decent at the very least. I've played close to 30h, and most of this time was spent chasing optional side missions, exploring hidden places, and hacking into computers. The details that you get from this exploration are great and make the world feel more alive and connected. However, a lot of other details are just absurd and yank you out of the emirsission all of the time, which I find really annoying. It just really feels like the developers had no attention to detail or took a lot of shortcuts, but at least the story writters had some sense.
I've got to say the side missions have improved a lot since the previous game. Now they are much longer, detailed, and substantial. They actually feel like some parallel subplot, opposed to a useless errand. Also, from random exploration you occasionally stumble upon clues towards points of interest. POVs in the game are kind of like mini side missions. They are very short, but still contribute to the world and story. You can easily miss a lot of them if you don't actually read emails/pocket secretaries or pay attention to people talking in the back alleys, as POVs don't always automatically show up as an objective. Sometimes you have to check out the place that the conversation is mentioning to get the mission started. I find this to be a cool detail though, as it feels like a reward for taking the time to explore the details.
Adam Jensen's part in all of this is very confusing to me though. I have no idea why the game has him as the main character, besides that he was the main in the previous game. He has absolutely no personal investment in any of the story I've see so far (I am at story mission 14). The main character could have easily been someone totally new.
The character animations have improved and some characters actually feel like actors when you talk to them. Regrettably, the voice acting is quite poor on half of the characters. It's just very monotonous. You get no emotions at all from the characters voice, or the emotions feel very fake and forced.
Overall, I think that whoever likes the first game will like this one as well. However, I am very dissappointed that they I've included micro transactions and that its so obvious that they didn't pay attention to the gameplay and world details. The details of the story are good, but the actual physical world, and the gameplay in it, feel very half baked. Also, the GUI and user-experience makes zero sense on a keyboard and mouse. Hence, why I don't feel like recommending the game.
EDIT: So I just finished the game and the ending is very anticlimactic... Considering the Illuminati are the big vilain, all we get from them is a couple of short cutscenes and a major plot twist after the credits. What a joke, the game finished very ubruptly.
Also, the DLC is a joke... It's a 10-30min mission (depending how much you explore) that adds nothing to the plot. Can't believe I paid for this.

-Disclaimer- This preview was written during Early Access. Brawlhalla is subject to change.
Brawlhalla is a dream come true for some gamers. Fans of Smash Bros have always had to turn to a console to sate their chaotic filled tendencies. Brawlhalla finally brings things to the PC/Mac and makes it readily available to everybody. The combat is fantastic, music well done, each character feels defined. It offers multiple game modes, couch co-op, single player and possibly more on the horizon. Brawlhalla seems like indeed something that did come from the heavens and is here to answer all your prayers. However, like most things that are too good to be true, there is something going on underneath the surface. Perhaps a venus flytrap of gaming if you will, showing you its tasty gaming nectar and then eating you whole. What am I talking about? Let's go on a little journey.
The core of the gameplay is exactly what you want it to be. 4 player brawling action is brought to you with a multitude of character choices. Now unlike that "other" game, these characters aren't perhaps as well known. Matter of fact if you asked me their names, I couldn't tell you. There is the robot guy, ninja girl, alien dude, minotaur man, pirate guy. You get the idea. It's not that these characters are not unique, matter of fact they each look very different and are very well animated. Just for the most part it really isn't that big a deal when you break things down.
Each character comes with a set of two weapons and different statistical choices, ranging from strength, defense, and speed. Now each weapon itself has a certain power set, the rocket lance can blast you forward, the guns obviously have a ranged aspect to them, the hammer is slow but powerful etc. Characters share these items, the only thing that changes is the style in which the power-attacks are presented. While aesthetically this works, your character choice really doesn't change all too much when it comes to combat. I was just as good with ninja girl/sword then I was with pirate/sword. There are some attacks that are very different and then there are some that are exactly the same. The fact the characters are all more or less the same doesn't take away from the game too much. The combat is still fast, reactive, and fun. Just keep in mind the weapon sets are more important then the character flavor itself. Predicting what your enemies bring to table also is difficult because the ability to change your stats, this adds and takes away a little bit from the tactical nature of the Brawl style game.
From there we launch into the levels and chaos ensues. The levels themselves are designed fairly well but nothing too exciting, mostly platforms in different positions. One level did feature moving platforms. I felt the levels need a dose of personality, hazards, traps, something to make them stylized and make them feel like as much of a character as the one you choose. Everything does blend well, the characters feel like they fit with the levels art style and everything flows well with the combat. The game controls easily, but it is probably is preferential to play with a controller, luckily the game does feature full controller support/rebindable keys.
Details of the game are fairly well polished as well. Music is high paced and decent, matching the style and themes of the game, although it is nothing too memorable. Thankfully it doesn't get repetitive. Sound effects are perfect and add that oomph you want when something explodes or when you crack someone really hard. Game modes are varied, although there isn't a story mode yet. You have a tournament mode, online, and even some in-game mini-games. This I liked quite a bit and would love to see it expanded upon. The options menu is a tiny bit lacking at this current moment in development but hopefully that will change.
So everything sounds great right? I would agree with you. Brawlhalla is a well done, action packed, competent game on Early Access. Lacking in bugs and online multiplayer is working well.(If you're US based.) Here is the catch, this is closed beta. Meaning that this game is eventually going to open up to everybody. Which means that Brawlhalla will be Free to play.(FTP) Which means one terrible and dreadful thing exists in the underbelly of this game. Microtransactions.
Mallhalla as its known, is the shop where you can buy all sorts of digital goodies. Now let me say I am not against Microtransactions. IF they are done right. I understand developing a game is not cheap and that there are bills to be paid and families to be fed. I am perfectly fine with everything on sale in the shop as well, all of it is cosmetic. Where Mallhalla begins to scare me is the huge gap between Taunts and Redeem Code. That could easily be filled with Characters, Weapons, and Levels. Which means you could be barred from using a new weapon set or new level, new character etc. There are plenty of ways that could all go sideways. Suddenly this goes from a fun brawl game, to pay me money to play with this toy. That might not be the case at all but it's something that should be kept in mind.
The prices of the micro-transactions themselves are also a bit wonky, if you ask me. Mammoth coins cost anywhere from $2.99 for 60 to $49.99 for 1000. With skins costing on average 140 coins that places the actual retail price at a whooping $7.00. That is quite a bit for a skin.(Although this isn't unusual in FTP games) While prices are not final and may change, this is still a scary example of things that are in the game right now. Start throwing in new characters and new weapon sets. Which undoubtedly will be higher priced then skins, suddenly this is a very expensive game.
Now the developer has mentioned there will be an in-game currency that can purchase the items in the shop. Those have yet to be implemented at this point in development.
Brawlhalla is a promising game, one that I hope doesn't fall prey to greed or bad decisions. It is not a clone of its inspiration and competition. Deviating in some features/mechanics that are for better or worse, Brawlhalla captures that one magic element, fun filled chaos. Giving you massive amounts of replay and letting you play with your friends. The game has a bright future, long as that mico-transaction element is handled carefully and they listen to their community.
I will keep a watchful eye on Brawlhalla as development continues and it moves into open beta. More servers are added to expand the multiplayer. There are still many things that can be improved upon and hopefully those prices change a little bit. The little Smash player inside of me is optimistic, I hope he doesn't get knocked out of the board in one smash.

Builds upon the first Torchlight game in every way.
Played on Windows 7, iMac (2009) Yosemite, and Linux Mint 17.3. Runs great on all three OSes.
PROS:
+4 distinct, versatile, and fun-to-play character classes: Outlander (ranged), Berserker (melee), Ember Mage (mage), and Engineer (heavy weapons and support team).
+Wider range of Pets, which will assist in battle, sell off unwanted loot, purchase needed potions, and can be taught spells.
+HUGE open world, composed of three main areas and tons of side-quests and unlockable areas.
+Looters' paradise. Loot is diverse and plentiful. Loot can also be sold or traded when playing online.
+Fun in single player, with alot of replay value beyond the initial playthrough via NG+.
+Online co-op with up to 4 other players.
+Enemy types are extremely varied, cool looking, and fun to battle.
+Gorgeous graphics and an inviting visual aesthetic.
+Windows, Mac, and Linux versions available.
+Very modest hardware requirements, especially considering the amount of content in TL2.
+A steal at only $20, and often on sale for even less.
CONS:
-Weak story.
-Online co-op isn't as streamlined as other online RPGs.

It's been a while since this game has been relevant to me (or anyone else for that matter), but, while I'm writing reviews, I might as well close the book on this one. I did enjoy RotT for a while, in spite of its best efforts to ensure I couldn't, but looking back at it from a more objective point of view, this was a subpar experience. Let me break this up into some relatively simple points.
+The soundtrack was one of the finest points of the original game, and the same is true here. Lee Jackson's masterful compositions translated quite naturally to metal.
+The smorgasbord of ridiculous rocket launchers is as satisfying as ever to use. Just like the original, the game really only comes alive when you get a hold of some explosives. And there will indeed be ludicrous gibs.
+The powerups are all back, including the delightfully stupid "dog mode", which I've yet to see in any other game.
+Bullet weapons are less boring to use than in the original, though the dual pistols feel useless now.
+There's now an extra weapon slot for magic weapons, though it rarely comes into play.
+The multiplayer was pretty fun, albeit not very populated, and I can't imagine that's gotten any better with time.
+At least they managed to implement manual saves, even if it is only a single quicksave slot. Most games these days offer no such function.
+The General Darian fight was a huge step up, as was El Oscuro, who you are actually allowed to shoot at now.
-The level design somehow manages to be worse than it was before. There was a certain charm in the nonsensical quality of the original, with its maze-like layout and creative use of traps. Now everything is essentially a straight line, with the unique quirks of the old RotT heavily applied to only a few select areas...
-with the exception of the bouncing pads, which are now mostly directional and make up several horrendous platforming segments. Your character's rigid movements, combined with said pads' tiny size, leave very little margin for error.
-Touchplates, pushwalls, and wandering walls are gone.
-Every checkpoint is a point of no return, so missing any secrets means replaying the whole level.
-Reloading a checkpoint will sometimes leave you unable to get 100% due to some enemies not re-spawning or some of your coins being uncounted, but, I guess that's a good incentive to not die...
-Enemies are somehow even dumber than their 90's counterparts, standing perfectly still to repeatedly shoot at you; you'll still get hurt pretty quickly though. Back in the day, hitscan enemies shuffled side to side in a random fashion while occasionally taking a shot at you in-between, but that was still somewhat decent game design, unlike this.
-Level geometry is finicky, sometimes trapping you inside of it, and sometimes being unexpectedly intangible.
-Even on reasonably powerful machines, the game's performance is mediocre at best. Framerate will take a sharp nosedive when the action gets complex, and large levels will often trigger a crash to desktop. This has been a problem from day one.
-Krist was a classic case of "kill him faster than he kills you", NME's heat seeking missles were often instant death, and Snake Oscuro was overly long and tedious.
So yeah. The old RotT definitely was not perfect, and I'd hoped that this would address some of its shortcomings, but it brings its own instead.

A fast-paced FPS that is horribly buggy, not very well optimized (though slightly improved now), and yet somehow great fun.
If you want top-notch graphics, you won't get them here.
If you want polished gameplay and performance, you won't get them here.
What you WILL get here is a crazy, unique experience, that will often kill you for stupid reasons (questionable level design, or the terrible sin of precision platforming in a first-person game), but you just can't help but respect and enjoy it somehow...
Also possibly some of the best music that you could ask for in this kind of game!
Maybe this is mostly coming from my nostalgia for the original Rise of the Triad: Dark War, which this game surprisingly manages to stay pretty faithful to in its oldschool feel and wacky style, but this is the kinda game that just makes you want to endure through the challenging/unfair moments, just to see what weird thing is going on in the next area, and to use the delicious and ridiculous weapons on more unfortunate fools!
Blow your enemies into LUDICROUS GIBS with homing rockets, drunk missile barrages, literal walls of fire, magical baseball bats (yes), and that's not even half of the weapons!
Hunt for dozens of, often well hidden, occasionally dangerous, secrets!
Transform into a god, or a dog, and obliterate all who stand in your way!
There's also multiplayer (no cooperative though), which is unfortunately not very active as far as I know, but every Saturday, developers and players tend to get together for a few hours or something, for a good bit of fun!
So if you want a game to just switch off your brain and play for a while, pick this up on sale and have fun running around like a mad-man/woman, in creative levels full of a variety of enemies, power-ups & downs, traps, and of course, awesome music! (You can even turn it to the oldschool soundtrack, if you're feeling particularly retro)

Completely new review, post XL update.
For those who have not seen the Mortal Kombat X scandal, the TDLR is: Ed Boon personally promised the MK9 / Injustice disasters won't be allowed to repeat, and the PC version will be as polished as the console version. On relase day it was revealed that NetherRealm did not work a single minute on MKX PC, and outsourced it to the most amateur, famous for their fckups hated porting studio, High Voltage. Again. To the same people who messed up MK9 too. TLDR is, it was an Arkham Knight level of disaster again, with over 90Gb of patches that always were a step ahead and 2 steps back regarding performance. Once they even accidently deleted everyone's profiles, along with unlocks and everything, even from cloud with no possible recovery, so Warner decided to give away the unlock everything DLC for free for everyone (optional to install, can be uninstalled separately and it gives your current profile back with your unlocks only). Kombat Pack 2 came out, but not for PC - the game's reputation was so bad (dropped from 15.000 players to 500 and sinking) Warner didn't bother to sell the second paid DLC pack. MKXL came out for consoles, along with a brand new fantastic netcode for online play, but neither Warner, NetherRealm or High Voltage answered to questions - where is the PC support? A few months later Warner announced they drop PC support for MKX, leaving it to rot (what they didn't say is, players already left it to rot a year ago at this point). Amongts others, I too had a detailed review discussing everything you see above in more detail, High Voltage's fckups, and was among the loudest who hated the game and warned everyone about avoiding it.
That changed a year later, in 2016 september.
8 months later out of the blue, a Mortal Kombat XL open beta popped up on steam. Warner didn't do any marketing for it, but XL was coming to PC, with thankfully High Voltage fired from the job and a completely new, dedicated and skilled team working on the port. The resaults are fantasic.
* Massive performance improvements. Easily achieved 60 fps now with higher settings than before.
* No more crashes and instabilities.
* The new netcode is the best I've seen since the 4th generation of Street Fighter, possibly better.
* Free costumes because why not.
* Decent, enjoyable story and varied challanges for singleplayer content. Doesn't make much sense without MK9's story, slightly more with it, but arguably the best singleplayer story in any fighting game to date. Plus Mileena kiss scene.
* Sadly, character selection menu and X-Rays are still 30 fps locked, but the game is smoother than ever. This is by design, X-Rays are basicly rendered videos, but still the drop can be felt.
While the game on sale is a good purchase now for anyone interested, it's real value depends on multiplayer. Everything is given now, to have a thriving online scene - performance, netcode, knowledge. Question is, can the near uprepairable reputatio of the original MKX overshadow XL or not? Will players come back, will new ones join? Without online players, there is no real fight. I recommend you to check out some steam statistics.
Warner and NetherRealm clearly paid for this re-porting project not because they hope for making profit from MKXL PC, after the original X had Arkham Knight level of destroyed reputation, but more likely they wanted restore some trust in NetherRealm's name in the eyes of the PC community, with the upcoming Injustice 2 being seen as "it will be a sh*t port" long before relase. With MKXL, they prooved themselves to be capable of making decent, good PC versions, so I'll give them a shot with Injustice 2 - I'd advise NOT to pre-order it of course. Whatever they'll advertise as a bonus, will be aviable for purchase for a few euros a month later tops.
MKXL update is free for everyone who has Mortal Kombat X, so you may want to pick up an MKX key from a 3rd party store before they disappear and only expensive MKXL keys are on the market. It's extremely cheap, it was for a long time, and even cheaper now (from 3 to 7 euros for the core game and 2-3 more for Kombat Pack 1) because every retailer is getting rid of the old keys. You also get a nice discount on Kombat Pack 2 on steam, if you own the game + KP1.
EDIT: Multiplayer is like beating a dead horse. Roughly 50 players online all the time, 45 of them play on near maximum settings and low fps (effecting your game too since you should be in perfect sync), the 5 others are players with over 2000 games played and you'll stand no chance against them. Coming from over 4000 hours of Street Fighter, in comparsion there is no ground for mindgames and real respectful matches in MKX, because either it's a joke category (low fps / terrible connection people) or russians trying to humiliate you after them knowing, they challanged someone who has thousands of matches less played than them. Singleplayer is an okay experience, playing vs the AI is pointless after that, c'mon it's a fighting game, multiplayer or nothing. And that part, despite all the great changes, is still dead, thanks to Warner and High Voltage. Edited in part comes from 1,5 months of testing it (multiplayer only, 20 hours). Changed the review to NOT RECOMMENDED.

This game is a mixed bag. I marked "Do not recommend" for lack of a better option.
The game has the bones of a fantastic game, but is lacking the meat.
Chances are if you are reading this, you are already a fan of the Rooster Teeth series, so I won't waste time with the character break down.
Here are a few pros and cons of the game:
Pros:
-Characters move and look like you expect them to. They were very true to the series.
-The studio used the original voice actors for the game.
-Simple to learn, but a fair amount of combat depth
-All 4 main protagonists are playable.
-Online community is currently alive and healthy.
-Surprisingly decent netcode. Not many indie studios produce online play this seemlessly.
-Teamwork is encouraged, but not to the point where people feel the need to berate new players.
-Many different ways to build a character
Cons:
-Very short. You can easily beat the game in under 4 hours.
-Despite very standard visuals, the game is fairly hardware intensive. This is one of the few games my computer will drop below 60 FPS.
-No expanded online content. You just play through the single player campaign with up to 4 people.
-Poor online communication structure. No voice chat, and you cannot type during cut scenes.
-No downtime to assign skills in online mode.
-To unlock all skills for some build, you need to have an ABSURD number of kills. We're talking "Play through the game 6 times with a single character" long.
-Hunter Rank up system resets ALL your stats. Ranking up will predictably reset your level, but all the hidden abilities you need an absurd number of kills to unlock also get reset.
-Environments feel a bit plain. Most fight areas are large, flat spaces with little to no cover or obstacles in the middle.
-Very little environment interaction
-No PVP
This game could really use some post-launch patches that include more modes. It would be great to see a "Survivor mode" or a "Defense mode" where you defend an objective from wave after wave of enemies. A PVP mode would be fantastic as well. End-game content is very lacking as well. I'm sitting at 7.3 hours of play time and I've got all 4 characters to max level. 10 short missions really doesn't cut it in today's saturated market.
All-in-all, I wanted an action game that worked well with a controller, and this mostly satisified that itch. I wish there was more content and challenges to it.

I feel like I'll probably be crucified by the more zealous RWBY fans for writing a negative review, but here I go anyway. To preface, Grimm Eclipse is not a terrible game, but what it is is a game that feels rushed out and amateurish. If nothing else, it feels like it needed a lot more work before the developers should have, in good faith, called it a "release version". But they're calling this the final product, and I'm going to review it as such.
You might be looking up at my time played and thinking "that doesn't seem like a lot", and you're right, but what should alarm you is that that's all the time it took me to play through the campaign twice over, along with random quickplay sessions of random levels here and there. The campaign is short. Really short. And that's an even bigger problem considering that that's the only mode that's available right now. Horde/Survival mode should have been a part of the release package, and without it the game feels incredibly content-bare.
But that might be as least somewhat excusable if the campaign was at least good. The "story" itself is a meaningless excuse for the team to be out and about killing grimm, with precisely zero interesting developments over the course of the game. Things get repetitive very quickly, as the only variety comes in the form of the occasional new type of enemy, because you can count on one hand the number of scenarios that aren't just "kill grimm in this area to move to the next area". The level design itself is pretty awful, too, with invisible walls plastered everywhere, and an incredibly low amount of effort put into hiding the "secret" artifacts. But despite all those invisible walls, we still managed to accidentally clip ourselves into walls way more times than should be acceptable. And don't get me started on the level transitions, which have you sit through either ~30 seconds of monologue or have you watch some ridiculously poorly-made "cutscene".
The combat, even if relatively simple, is fun for the most part, but it does have some very questionable design decisions. For starters, all four characters' "ultra" abilities are just slight variations on the same thing: a big area of effect attack, the character-specific upgrades for which are really boring modifiers like "also stuns" or "also knocks enemies away". Team attacks are a great concept that misses the mark in its execution. Your teammate stuns an enemy, and if you're paying attention, you can follow up for a team attack for massive damage! Except that you don't actually have to be paying attention at all considering just mashing the team attack button all the time has no penalty. At that point it might as well just be automatic.
The ranged attacks are also really clunky and almost seem tacked on. Instead of being able to weave melee attacks and ranged attacks together in a flurry of action like you might see on the show, in Grimm Eclipse, trying to quickly switch between the two ends up being horribly ineffective. This is mostly due to the fact that only the third attack of the ranged attack string is worth a damn. Unless you're finishing off an extremely low health enemy, or just trying to continue your combo as you move between enemies, single-shot ranged attacking is pretty much useless. You have to commit to doing the full string or nothing, and that doesn't feel smooth.
(As a much more personal gripe, I was really disappointed with Blake's entire moveset in this game. Instead of using shadow clones to deceive or distract enemies, they only show up briefly during certain attacks to stab the enemy and then disappear. At best you get to leave a shadow clone behind for a second before it explodes. And wasn't it awesome how Blake could use her sword as a sickle and chain in the show? Well, you can't do that in Grimm Eclipse, so forget about it.)
All this topped off with a stunning lack of polish or seemingly much attention to detail at all. Walk speed is out of synch with the walking animations. Picking up items has no animation and just puts an icon over your character's head to signify that they're "carrying" it. No animation for picking up a downed teammate. No animation for pushing buttons. Enemies have absolutely no way to deal with players getting on top of things and will just sit and growl below you. They took it out of Early Access way, way, WAY too early. They added more content without having improved the previous content first. As a beta, the mechanics -worked- but they left a lot to be desired. I feel like it was a publisher decision by Rooster Teeth to push it out as soon as it did.
The characters are too similar. What I mean by this is that they don't play differently enough. I can easily play Yang or Weiss the same as I'd play Blake, with little loss of final outcome. It's kinda just like... ONE character with minor tweaks in abilities.
Speaking of abilities, some seem kinda... useless. Ultimates were designed to be used in times of pure ♥♥♥♥ery, when you were completely surrounded, but more often than not, dodging out was the better option. It killed me more than it saved me.
Weird upgrade system. Blake's ultimates are by far the most useless of the four girls.
Range attacks also seem useless outside of utility, like stunning enemies with Blake, or unless you're Weiss. Seems like a failure from a design standpoint.
Everyone ♥♥♥♥♥es and moans about Destiny and the Division style bosses where they are really just bullet sponges of the same enemy you fought before. It's kinda here as well with the Ursa Majors and the final boss. It's just a slugfest against the bosses with no need for thought.
It's not really a co-op game per say. It's like... a game where people fight in the same area. Interaction, both in dialogue and activity, are lacking. As it stands, everyone just kinda does their own thing, and usually its a mad scramble for XP rather than helping teammates.
It would have been interesting to see a more class based system with RWBY. Yang as a tank (Could have even worked with an Overwatch Zarya type tank). Weiss as a support, buffing teammates. Ruby as a nuker for burst damage. Blake running DPS.
While playing I compared this game a lot to Legend of Korra. A game in the same genre with a similar graphic style, four unique bending forms, both built with lower budgets. Platforming works. Plus with the rumour of PAID DLC for an overpriced game? Sad face.

First, let me start this review with a quick history lesson: Back in the late 2015/early 2016, there were rumors that SE decided to chop MD into pieces, to make it a triology. That the original MD was bigger, but SE wanted to milk the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of it (Because they surely love their episodic crap).
Now is mid/late 2016, and oh boy, you guessed it. Those rumors were partially right. By the time you watch the credits roll you will feel utterly disappointed. The story is quite mediocre and never takes off. The game ends abruptly right in the climax of the game. And you barely get any answers. In fact, the whole game is about Adam being an errand boy. Remember those videos about Adam saying how much he wanted to find out where the Illuminati are, that he joined the Task Force just to find them and so on? Well, that's a lie. That won't happen. Because the game ends in a big cliffhanger, and it never goes in depth into the Illuminati. Not only that but your choices don't matter at all, only to see a small variation of the same ending. That's it.
Characters are forgettable (Poorly developed), it is quite impossible to create any emotional link between them and the player. They are just faces that give you info as you move on. The story lacks the personal motives HR had, Adam is just doing what others tell him to do. And to make things worse, the main villain in this game only appears a couple times during the whole game and only for a few mins. There's never any sensation of revenge, justice or just hate towards him. Only, indifference.
Oh, and remember that augmented guy in the yellow hoodie from the trailer that is so emotive showing us a "human" Adam? The dude that they sold us as a key part of the story? Well, only appears for 5 secs during the whole game. There goes all the emotiveness, down the drain. And don't get your hopes high expecting to see many of your old buddies.
In other words, it doesn't matter what you do in the game, when you reach the ending you are back to square one in terms of plot development. This game does nothing for the core motivation (Find the Illuminati). Worse, Adam doesn't care at all of what's going on during the whole game (Part of the issue is the complete lack of attachment to any character in this game appart from his former boss).
But not everything is bad, gameplay wise the game is superb. Gunplay has been improved, new powers and the environments are not only beautiful but also, there's a ton of hidden stuff on them. Prague is beautiful and feels alive, although, kinda small (And personally, I rather go back to the old DX hub style in different places around the world, not just one city). Basically a HR 2.0 improved in almost every aspect. The port itself sucks (at launch) but I hope nixxes step up their game and fix it.
