PROS and CONS below,
but first with my suggestions for a better, personal experience as a game.
I really think this game missed the opportunity of giving immersive experience that only a medium as immersive and personal as a game can provide.
Controlling the characters felt like I am no more than a random guy clicking and pressing the keyboard,
making me feel completely irrelevant to the World of Remnant, the world that I really would love to dive into.
There just isn't enough opportunity for interaction between the characters and the player.
Fighting the grimms gave me a glimpse of what it is like to fight along our beloved huntresses, but not enough.
My suggestion would be making the player to be one of the professors directly managing the team, assigning missions, teaching them skills, upgrading their equipment, healing or aiding them when they are hurt or in trouble, changing their costumes (which effects their abilities), and many more things that can make the whole experience much more personal and allow the player and characters to shape the campaign story together. It would also be great if the characters have dialogues towards the player.
I want to be engaged and connected to the characters, feeling like I am actually contributing to the team RWBY, and perhaps other teams too.
This is not possible with an anime, but very doable with a game.
That is why I think it is a massive missed opportunity.
Having said that, I still think this is a must have for RWBY fans.
Now the PROS
- The action mechanic feels easy yet very satisfying to use.
Clicking in rhythm is cool, especially with Weiss, making steps and moves in orderly fashion.
Turning the camera around with the mouse movement to aim the enemies feel natural and quick.
- Also the visual of the game is pleasant to look at.
Scenery is beautiful and character models are right from the anime.
- Sound effects are just about right. Nothing too noisy or quiet.
And of course, the sound track is awesome.
CONS
- Some parts of the story didn't make sense to me, such as why Dr. Merlot let the team into his lab so easily. Bad move on his part, and I just don't get why he had to make such a foolish decision. Perhaps just for the sake of the progression of the game levels?
- The campaign could be longer. Much much longer.
The overall campaign does have replay value, playing with others and leveling up each characters.
But there just isn't enough content to enjoy for a longer period of time.
People may get into collecting achievements and leveling up gems, but it feels very repetitive overall.
Now, I personally think the price is pretty reasonable.
I also know that there are more to come in the future.
But that future is not here yet, meaning we have only a half of the game, making it hard to call it a 'full release'.
I really enjoy the game, and I look forward to future updates,
I also really hope that Rooster Teeth realizes the full potential of this game as a medium.
It could be so much more.

I still do recommend this game. I bought within the three hours it came out and have had it ever since. While it has been given negative reviews lately, I still believe that they have come a long way from when it first came out.
First, I don't know what this is about the character models downgrading the actual performance of the game, but for me, somebody with a two-year-old Toshiba, which was a Windows 8 ( now a Windows Ten because it's the only option I had ), with an Intergrated Intel 4 graphics card, it works.. actually quite nicely, even with the 'full release' ( I'll cover this later ).
Could they refine the new character models a bit more? Yes, they could. However, I find the new ones to be much easier on my eyes, despite the 'doll like' faces. The beginning models had a bright glowing to them that was kind of obstructing the features of the models, anyways. Maybe if they removed the glowing characteristic, they could have kept the old models. It was definitely a good change for people who have sensitive eyesight and couldn't sit down to play the game for more than thirty minutes without their eyes becoming sore or a headache. I would like to see an option to switch between the new and old models , though. Mostly so people would stop giving the game negative reviews ( and yes, people are doing this ) just because of the models not looking as 'nice' as they used to. Other than that, the graphics are quite stunning to look at, even if you're playing on 'potato' quality, as the game calls it. They could continue to improve these.
Now onto the 'full release' aspect of this.
I don't think this game was quite ready for a full release and the $25 price. I think they should have kept it at $20, as the range of most early access games coming-out-of-early-access are anywhere between $15-20. I do think they should have waited a few more months, or at least have brought it gradually, instead of all at once in one giant pile. I wasn't able to attend RTX, so the people who did go might say otherwise as they got to see more of the content, but as for how my standing is right now, the ending feels somewhat rushed and the enemies towards the end... well, unbalanced.
As far as the co-op portion goes, the only real issue would be the kill-EXP stealing. If EXP was shared equally when monsters were killed, this would not be an issue at all. However, usually, the person who kills the monster, gets the exp. Unless you're playing with friends, this can be quite an issue, and can force you into single player. That and it feels kind of crappy to have somebody steal your kill after you just pulled off a flashy combo. Obviously you'd still have your Wave MVP EXP which might somebody ahead, but that's usually a component in most team-based games to begin with, and it's not that big of a difference.
Camera could use some more refinement for controllers, I believe. The camera for the keyboard-mouse playing option seems to be alright for me, however. I have played both methods and the one that's more awkward, for me at least, is the controller one due to the camera angles being quite irritating at key points.
Other than this, the game's actually pretty good. I'd recommend it ( and have been recommending the ever living hell out of it since it came out ) to my friends and people who are part of the show. It's definitely got some ways to go, but at least they're trying to handle all of this at once as best as they can.
This is purely my opinion, however, and others may have different opinions as we are humans and we're not all entirely the same. I am grateful that this community is at least somewhat respectful of everyone's opinions and that its.. 'innocence' so to speak hasn't entirely left it. And I hope it stays that way, because we all know what happened to several other games once the squeakers got a hold of them.

Okay, so the game is now out of early access. So what exactly was added prior to release? Unfortunately, all that was added during the "content updates" were essentially map packs. The Forever Fall update added 2 chapters to the game along with a revised combat system to make the game feel a little less spammy per say to the point where I can say it is about on par with most other beat em ups on the market and updated the character models that makes them look arguably worse than before the update for a period of time. Now the new update at the time of release provides us with 4 new chapters to finish off the story, although a bit shallow, but still there nonetheless.
The Good:
-The voice acting for the main cast is pretty much spot on in my opinion, although I'm not convinced of the voice acting for the main villain's performance seeing as he's supposed to be a mad scientist, he kinda comes across as a bit whiny when you get to the "foiling the villain's plan" part of the story and overall feels a bit forgettable in my opinion
-The music is for the most part pretty good
-It's RWBY. Right? Right? Anyone?
The Average:
-Combat has a nice arcadey feel to it, but overall is competent at best. Nothing mind blowing or anything special
-The health system is essencially regenerating health. Technically armour, but when your "aura" is depleted, damage goes straight to health and the game is not very clear on how many hits you can take before kissing the floor. Maybe as a lazy solution to not program health items or something so a lot of the combat involves kiting with very little repercussions
-Story is meh, but it's there
-For some people, there are not enough levels to play on, but then again, most beat em ups recycle the same levels for multiple missions
-The game was not built with Co-op from the start, hence why the feeling of team synergy is absent, just spawn more monsters with more health
-Only 4 characters. Would be impressive if they play very differently from one another, but that's not the case
-Enemy variety is a bit lacking, but to be fair, so is most other run-of-the-mill beat em ups
-Voice lines can get repeated quite a bit and kind of got irritating after a while.
-The overall difficulty of the game is close to casual level, but maybe that's what some people are looking for
The Somewhat Ugly:
-They did change the leveling system from a Dota-style micro progression to persistent leveling and honestly, it's no different from one another other than you now level a bit slower and you can respec your points at any time
-The upgrade system is filled with nothing but passive upgrades. Even if say for example, Blake's Shadow Clone ability upgrade gives you a stunning ability now, you're still playing the same way as before only you can do the same things more efficiently, ultimately feels like they only added a progression system to tick off a check box
-There are no manual difficulty settings
-You cannot pause the game in singleplayer mode for some reason
-The final boss fight is a bloody joke and is easily exploitable with almost no variation in attack patterns during its phase changes
-What is Co-op anyway? Aside from bonus exp, what's the point in revival when you slap on a  respawn timer? You want to stay alive? Kite the enemies until your teammate's respawn timer ticks down to zero
-The $25 asking price during its official release
-Performance can be a bit bad, but I mostly blame the Unity Engine for this being a common pattern across low end machines
-Announcing a horde mode during its early access period and not delivering it to us on release. I know nothing about coding, but I don't know how hard it is to make one for this game.
-Again, almost nothing changed during the 8 months of early access
As a beat em up game, it's competent at what it does and I wish they didn't mention they took inspiration from Left 4 Dead because there is no semblance to it in terms of mechanics and gameplay design at all. It's fun and I don't hate it, but I just can't bring myself to recommend RWBY: Grimm Eclipse at the current $25 asking price due to the game being presented too early during its early access period and its questionable business decision to raise the price for the content that was added during that time. I recommend you wait until it drops back down to the $15 it was asking for during its early access launch or lower and then maybe I'll consider it. It only feels empty to me because it was presented to us in a way where we got the impression it was going to be more than what we got now, almost as if they were possibly making a desperate attempt to make back what was lost. Besides this, there are other beat em up games that are roughly the same as Grimm Eclipse of course and provides more bang for your buck like Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus, Phantom Breaker Battlegrounds, Shank 1 & 2, the Batman games, and so on and so forth.

Worth a buy if you are optimistic about the games future, and only on sale.  25 dollars for 4 characters, about 6 or 7  enemies (literally that many. anything differing counts as a pallete swap with mildly altered attributes)  and combat that starts off fun, if not a bit generic, then devolves into spamming either your ranged attack or your special attack as you get stronger.
The main issue is that, as you get stronger, the enemies dont. The stronger pallete swaps might come in, but their attack patterns are the same, and your health actually regenerates if you avoid taking damage for like 3 seconds, making this probably the single easiest beat em up i've ever played.
The story is serviceable, although you have no idea who the characters are if you're unfamiliar with the anime as no backstory is explained, and there are no cutscenes.
As negatively as i'm painting the game so far, i actually still enjoyed it. The main characters have charisma and are even funny sometimes, the combat is flashy, and it has a very old school feel to it. I grew up on beat em ups like final fight, streets of rage, and golden axe, and this feels like a natural evolution to games like those. No brains involved, mash buttons, dont get hit. Its that simple
No depth in combat, but you may enjoy mindlessly smashing buttons on the same few badguys with your friends for about an hour or so. But NOT for $25. That is an absolute rip off. If you can find it for 10, its a sound purchase.
I'm giving it the recommend on the grounds that the game seems to be getting updated relatively consistently, so theres a shot this could be great instead of just playable.

I finished Dragon's Dogma and needed something else to play, and several lists recommended me this game. I liked the description so I bought it -- spent four hours playing almost immediately. It's a great game. It's got the feel of an MMO without the MMO aspect; its like there should be other people running by me doing their own thing but its and independent game, and I love that. The graphics are beautiful, the sound isn't overpowering, and I actually got attached to some of characters quite fast. Not to mention I recognized some of the voices from Dragon Age (Cullen started talking to me and nearly gave me a heart attack)
I'm four hours in and have barely touched the main story line, have only been running around doing small tasks. That excites me because that means I'll be playing for awhile, which is what I want. There were some minor issues with using a PS4 controllor, as the right joystick is meant to control the camera/lockpicking, but that's easily fixed via using the mouse or increasing camera sensitivity (which I did).
The leveling system is cool, choosing destinies and what not, since I liked in Skyrim how I can learn magic while also being a warrior and sneaking too, and that's the same here. I have magic, carry a sword, and my backup weapons are daggers. There's a little bit of everything regardless of what you want.
It's a shame this came out during the light of Skyrim because it probably would have done much better. But I recommend you get it, regardless of the type of RPG you like, because this has aspects from all of them.

There is an alternate reality in which Trine 2 was never created. In this reality, humans no longer have the capacity to love.
Infants, having no one to care for their well-being, are corralled and raised by Monosynchronous Online Teaching House Environments for Rearing Souls (MOTHERS), where childhood is reduced to random flashing images designed to simulate an active upbringing. While so-called "Educators" --robotic arms attached the walls and ceiling-- pass out meals and clean drool from the white tiled floors.
Through these images, New Humans are taught to queue and await assignment to a corporate subsidiary known by a number only, starting with Corporation 99 and counting down. Each corporation number represents the required brain mass to be plugged in at that location.  For example, Corporation 99 represents those in the 99th percentile for brain mass.
At these locations, humans are plugged into the super computer, WORK (World Organizational Recreation Kiosk).  Once plugged in, their brain power is used to calculate the algortihms used to control the MOTHERS. While each human conciousness wanders the same infinite maze of colored-coded rooms that force them to feel a specific emotion.
Red for joy, blue for anger, yellow for pride, purple for embarrassment, and so on, forever.
This has become existence for mankind. This is existence without Trine 2.

This is interesting and decently exectued. You control two brothers at the same time. The elder is stronger and the younger is smaller and can fit into small places. Each brother is controlled with their own analog stick and trigger button. It forces you in some places to control them both dynamically, which can be a bit challenging, but it's fun to play.
The story is presented implicitly, with the characters using a fantasy language that is not translated. The journey starts with the boys, having lost their mother recently, now setting out to find medicine to cure their gravely ill father. Along the way they meet various friends and foes and cooperate to solve puzzles as they proceed.
It's pretty good. Definitely worth checking out.

Brothers sometimes feels like a homework assignment that someone did for a class on Characterization Through Control Schemes, but to be fair it would get them an A. It's not a "drop everything and PLAY THIS NOW" game, but at only 2-3 hours, it's a nice palate cleanser.
The art direction is beautiful, with excellent use of color and a few really interesting locales to traipse through. It can get overindulgent in showing it off - there's no shortage of angles and setups that exist soley as scenery porn - and it likewise spends a bit too much cutscene time believing that you're gripped by a barebones fairy tale coming-of-age story. But the core is sound, and while it's almost a stretch to call it a puzzle game (they mostly consist of going to the only obvious interaction point and pressing 'use' with one or both boys), it moves at a good clip and doesn't overstay its welcome.

Like no other game Thief holds a very dear place in my heart.  Nothing in my experience comes close to the sense of otherworldly atmosphere as presented in this game. Despite having clunky controls & older graphics, I was impressed with the size of the levels & complexity of the heists. I liked the tone of the game world; the struggle between chaos & order. This game is pretty great when you're not fighting anything, which I believe is intentional.

Do the cutscenes play?  Nope.  Are there some annoying bugs that make it difficult to play on modern systems?  Yep.  Is it better than any modern game released?  Yes.  You take ANY level in this game, nevermind The Sword and Bafford's Mansion, and you have an entire game that is better than most modern releases full games today.  It's that simple.  Stealth, detection of your presence, your awareness of your visibility to your opponents, your realization of levels of detection by voice cues and whether you have a chance of just staying in the shadows all make this games one of the MOST INTENSE battles you will EVER face without ever firing a single shot.  You don't fire fight in this game.  Two blows from a Hammer's hammer and you are done.  No 200% armor, no superhealth, no quad damage, no invulnerability.   It's just you; a mace, a few arrows filled with water and moss and hopefully a flash bomb or two.  It doesn't get more real than this game and you can feel the love and care in every level

Where to start?  Other than their terrible "Augment your preorder" business decision (since that's been discussed to death), here are my issues:
Bugs:  I haven't played a game this buggy since Vampire: Bloodlines.  Movement is just awkward.  You have to jump to get over the smallest obstacle, like stairs and other tiny obstructions.  When you are moving down a slope or up an incline, you will inexplicably start strafing.  The inventory screen wouldn't let me move anything to my hotbar.  Sometimes lootscreens get stuck and you have to alt-tab out.  Sometimes the mouse stops working when in dialog or other screens.  The list goes on and on.
Hacking: My god, hacking.  You can't walk 5 steps without seeing something new to hack and there's about a 99% chance there wouldn't be anything exciting as a reward.  Plus, in non restricted areas, there's no penalty for being seen hacking.  The completionist in me wants to hack everything I see but it becomes the biggest nuisance.  It's also virtually the same minigame as HR, only at an isometric view that makes it difficult to see.
DLC: Making your DLC save locked (meaning you have to purchase it again if you intend to play through the game twice) is something we would joke about in the old days, about how DLC would ruin games, and then it actually happened.  Disgusting business model that will set an unfortunate precedent for other games.
PC performance: I have a pretty decent machine.  I can run Doom, Mirror's Edge Catalyst, Witcher 3, etc. at the highest spec and get 60fps but I can't for this.  If you don't turn off MSAA and lower hardening shadows and volumetric lighting, get ready for 30 fps.
Difficulty:  I'll freely admit I'm not a fan of hard games but this game is just way too easy.  The AI is downright hilarious.

Frankly, I don't see anything The Sims 4 is offering that's better or more advanced than what The Sims Cubed already has. For that reason, I'm not going to bother purchasing The Sims 4, and will instead enjoy the great little time-sink with the grossly-overpriced DLC I already have.
As far as this great little time-sink goes, I'll cover the bad things first: Glitches of all kinds are apparent, from screen tearing to improper model loading to Sims getting stuck on invisible bumps in the carpet. It doesn't look like The Sims Cubed is going to be getting anymore support, either, since EA has decided to publish The Sims 4. Gameplay gets repetitive; even though you get to customize your Sim's appearance, gender, etc, and personality traits and ambitions, these things just don't feel like they have enough of an impact on the game itself. Most personality traits and Life Ambitions merely give you an extra option some radial menu somewhere, but do not actually impact how your Sim behaves or forms relationships with other Sims. Skills are way too easy to learn - you can master any given skill in about twenty minutes real-time if you push your Sim to interact with the right objects or people often enough. This makes your Sim even more bland, as there is no challenge for them anymore. And I wasn't lying at the top: the DLC is grossly overpriced for what each pack adds to the game.
On the other hand, the best thing to say about The Sims Cubed is that it's fun. That's the whole premise of The Sims franchise - to have fun playing god in a world of almost-human-beings. It's voyeuristic. It's vicarious. It's reality TV where you decide what the characters are going to do every day. Each expansion pack adds enough new content to the game to make sure that there's always something new to do. I wouldn't recommend buying The Sims Cubed unless you're also going to spend some money on a few expansion packs, like World Travels, Pets, or Seasons. If you do, The Sims Cubed will keep you playing for a long, long time.

Tekken 7's big story mode is only relevant to long time Tekken fans. Furthermore it borrows from Street Fighter, which feels way off. The arcade stories for the individual characters are generic and much too short. The game is lacking a proper tutorial and practice mode, which is a crime considering its movement complexity. Other than that, ... it's Tekken. Nothing more, nothing less. Every single Tekken game feels like the same game as before. Same clunky and convoluted controls, same animations, same throws, kicks, punches, characters, roly-polies ... No innovation whatsoever (I don't consider rage arts an innovation, sorry).
The graphics may seem good at first glance, on second however the game looks ... wrong. The colors feel out of place, while most characters lack detail (especially in the face). Facial expressions are as good as absent. They are awfully stiff, as are some of the animations. Some even look like performed by wooden dolls. The character customisation is strange. A lot of comical stuff in it as well as a load of dull clothes.
This doesn't look and feel like a 2017 fighting game. You get better overall visuals, smoother animations and controls with much older DOA5, or even Street Fighter V, and Guilty Gear (if you like the art style). The latter is especially interesting if you love stories, delivered in Anime style. No comparison to this ... unimaginative mess in Tekken 7. Sorry, but it's just dull. But, to grant a point: Mary Elizabeth McGlynn ... nuff said.
If you are new to Tekken and love to spend hours and hours learning to master characters, this game could be for you. If you are a die hard Tekken fan, this game is for you. If you are a casual brawler, you might be better off with other titles.

The team aspect of this game is one of the defining features which sets it apart from most other hack-and-slash games. Also, I am a big fan of persistent characters and the hunter ranks as this gives so much more reason for replayability and play-diversity.
Overall, a beautiful first game from RoosterTeeth Games and I look forward to future updates (Horde Mode please :D) and more games from them.

Brawlhalla.
First. It's free. Don't buy it from Steam. Go register for a free beta key on Brawlhalla's website and they'll email you one the next day (I, and many others I know have had this experience).
Second, and more importantly. Great game. Easily the best brawler available on PC and should be a go-to for any Su*er Sm*sh Bro's fan. Regularly updated and improved, and has gotten considerably better even in the last month I've been playing. Local multiplayer, online multiplayer, online matchmaking, solo game modes. NOT pay2win, uses a very Dota-like system for microtransactions that ONLY unlock cosmetics. There's integrated support for about every imaginable controller you can connect to a PC, which is great for throwing together local multiplayer games with friends. gg brawlhalla.
Lastly, and to be expected, the game is still in beta so some of it's features could be improved. For example, though you can queue into online matches with another local player, you currently cannot with another friend playing on their own PC. Hopefully in the near future they'll allow you to make public multiplayer lobbies with your friends, or queue into matchmaking with online (as well as local) friends. Also, there's no real introduction to the mechanics of the game which makes it a bit annoying when you start out (see below). Those are my two primary complaints, but there's still a lot of fun to be had with the game.
Play it. It's free. You'll like it.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
*I mentioned how there's no real intro to the game mechanics when you start, so a few things to know about Brawlhalla
--When picking a character, each has stats and two weapons they can randomly get as drops in game.
--Stats, from top to bottom, are: Strength (how hard you hit), Attack Speed, Defense (how many hits you can take), and Movement Speed
--Weapons are dropped randomly in game, and are indicated by their icons. i.e. Spear, rocket lance, caestus, pistols, etc.
--In scored game modes, points go: +1 for kill, +2 for kill on someone with a streak, -1 for death, -3 for suicide.
--In all game modes, the more hits you take, the more damage you'll build up, making each successive hit cause you to fly further off the map. The amount of damage you've taken is indicated on the top right of the screen around your characters face; white = no damage/hard to knock off map, red = max damage/easiest to knock off of map. The mechanic works exactly like the percentages in Su*er Sm*sh Bro's.
--Light attacks cannot be charged, while heavy attacks can be.
--Dodging is helpful both for avoiding enemy attacks, AND for getting you back on the map; i.e. dodge up/left/right to get the last few inches you need to make it back on a platform
--You get 3 jumps in mid-air. If you get attacked in mid-air, you get an additional jump. You get unlimited jumps off of walls. Keep this in mind when moving around the map.
--That's all the important stuff I remember off of the top of my head, hopefully it's helpful!

My review for Brawlhalla:
TL;DR: It's a great Smash Bros clone, although it's nowhere near as complex.
Brawlhalla is a 2D fighter made by blue mammoth games that as of this review, is in open beta.  The game is heavily inspired by the super smash bros series, but I don't think the developers are trying to hide this. I see this as a pro and a con. Smash Bros is a wonderful series that has no other equal on pc, but I don't feel like this game tries hard enough to make itself different from it's inspiration.
The object of Brawlhalla is simple. Instead of being like Street Fighter, where you attempt to lower your opponent's health to zero, you knock your opponents off of the screen. Instead, their health goes up with more damage. You attack other players with quick, weaker attacks, and slower, stronger attacks, with each having their own button. The controls are solid. It feels less “floaty” than say, Super Smash Bros Brawl, but not as tight as Melee.
You start off with just your fists, but as the match goes on items such as swords and hammers appear, each with their own advantage. Smaller weapons, although weaker, are much faster. They're great for building up damage. Some characters instead wield guns or bows that are capable of a strong ranged attack. The bigger weapons are slow, but strong. They're great for finishing off a foe. Along with these weapons, the game provides mines, bombs and a spiked ball.... things that you can launch towards enemies. The game does a good job at feeling competitive even with the items, even if the variety is lacking.
The map selection is fairly small at the moment, but I expect this to change, since this game as I mentioned before, is in open beta. Although the selection is small, the maps are solid and well made. The settings range from old rusty temples to grassy.... rocks.
As of this review, the game offers 21 fighters called “champions.” This is one place the game falls flat.  Even though this selection is fair, they feel the same. They all have minor differences in stats and all wield the same type of weapons depending on the “type” of character you choose.
Overall, I give the game-play a 7 out of 10.
The graphics are decent, but not mind blowing. The cartoony, mythical 2D art style fits well with the game, even if it doesn't take your breathe away. The low key graphics makes this game very easy to run, making the game more accessible to people with low end machines.  The sound is simply okay. The effects do the job, and the music is less than stellar and forgettable.
I give the graphics and sound a 6 out of 10.
One of my favorite things about this game is the free to play model. It does this phenomenally well. The game rotates 5 champions and switches them out. While you play matches the game gives you in game currency that allows you to buy all of the champions if you choose. They're not very expensive either, so it doesn't feel like too much of a grind. Using real money doesn't give other players an advantage, as it can only be used to buy cosmetic items like skins and taunts.
I give the “free factor” a 9 out of 10.
Overall, I give the game a 7.3 out of 10. Brawlhalla is a good 2D fighter, although there isn't much to it and the variety is lacking. I can heartily recommend this game, given the price tag.

Well, let's talk about Brawlhalla for a sec, shall we?
At first glance it would seem as though it's a PC game going for the style of Smash Bros. On the 10th or so glance, it seems as though it's a PC game going for the style of Smash Bros. But with a few twists that keep it mostly seperate.
First of all is the weapon system. I personally LOVE this mechanic. You start off with your weak melee attacks until you pick up a weapon, displayed on-screen as a generic sprite. When that happens, you get a non-generic weapon. Each character has a combination of two weapons that they can recieve. There's guns, spears, hammers, 1 sword, 2 swords, and a rocket lance. That's right, a rocket lance. Though each weapon is not exclusive to their characters, each character has 2 exclusive moves (1 per weapon) that they can use. Each weapon is VERY nicely balanced, and I'll talk more about that later.
There are also items you can pick up, though variety is sparce. There are spiky balls called Mace-Balls, which you throw at enemies. There are land mines, which you can either throw at your opponent(s) or at the walls and floors. Finally, there are plain ol' bombs that will make you stare in disbelief as you fly off into your doom after some ♥♥♥♥ throws one at you.
Online play. I'm a little... eh about the quality of the online play at the moment. On one hand, it's incredible to wreck people online and tell them "gg" before having all of them ragequit, (Seriously, check out my Brawlhalla screenshots, I have that one in there somewhere) there is a lot of lag sometimes. On one hand, some matches can be as smooth as offline play, on the other hand some can involve unforseen game mehanics such as teleportation and death by "I swear that guy was on the other side of the map .01 seconds ago". Despite this, the developers have stated repeatedly they are constantly working on improving online play. They have had multiple lag fix patches already and more are to come. So, that'll make the game even better.
Offline play is so fun. There's a tournament mode where you play against CPUs to be the ultimate champion. The CPUs are pretty easy themselves, but the challenge lies in not getting killed while gathering many kills to get a high score. There is a star rating out of 5 you get at the end, with 5 being pretty difficult to acheive (SPOILER: There's a practically impossible rating to get that's above 5 stars... No more hints as to what it is) Also, there's local play where you can play with up to four people using controllers, and one person can use the keyboard or keyboard-mouse. No LAN unfortunately. The last thing is training mode. I won't go too much into detail with this, but imagine Smash Bros' training mode + damage per hit shown, visible hitboxes, and hitstun visibility.
The balance. Outstanding. Though this could also be a statement as to the lack of variety, you could almost press random in a tournament match and come out the victor with anyone you got. Of course, it's not perfect. But unlike some other games, which have tier lists from SS all the way down to F or even G, Brawlhalla's tier list is more like an SS to A.
Wait, did I say "tournament match"? Yes, Brawlhalla has a competitive community that even now, in closed beta, is over 100 strong. This is when the game isn't publicly available, and there's over 100 people participating in competitive play. Think about that for a moment. As I write this even, I am procrastinating much needed sleep for a Brawlhalla tournament tommorow.
PROS:
-Great brawler in the style of Smash Bros
-Good offline mode
-Has an online mode
-Near impeccable balance
-Growing competitive community
CONS:

-No LAN play
-I can't come close to beating Raidhyn
-A little empty (Probably just a closed beta problem)
-I have to fight Raidhyn in a tournament tommorow

Easily one of the best stealth games I've played. Though appearing simple by today's standards, the system where you are in various levels of concealment while lurking in several levels of darkness is very well though out and implemented with many ways one can get through a level. It's not uncommon for a player to reach an objective with much more of the area to explore and loot. Very rarely will you find everything in a level on your first go, in fact I never did. AI is intelligent enough to require careful planning at any corner, the abililty to lean and peek pivotal. Listening in on enemy conversations can either be enlightening or just plain amusing, and while their voice acting can be questionable at times, our main characters are voiced superbly.
Being able to save anywhere and any time is helpful, and I'd recommend abusing this system mercilessly. If a guard sees you, escape is definitely possible (unless you're on a difficulty which causes this to fail the mission), but I for one tend to just reload to right before it did, that's just me.
Speaking of difficulty, you can change it at the start of any mission. All difficulty increases add objectives to your missions, sometimes just a higher loot requirement or not killing/being seen, but in some cases you have more side-tasks you must accomplish. Not many games do this anymore, so that was a pleasant surprise.
I cannot praise this game enough, but there is one thing you should know. In this version, cutscenes are pretty broken. There are fixes if you look it up, but I was lazy and just searched them on Youtube between missions. As you get later in the game, they become VERY important to the plot. Don't go through the first five wondering if there should be any like I did!
Now if you like stealth (if you don't, then this is NOT a game for you, it is raw thievery from the shadows), buy this game already. Even full price makes me feel like I paid too little for such an incredible experience!

I remember getting trial versions of this game on older computers and playing the crap out of this game.  It was fun, addicting, and could put you in a daze very quickly.
Zuma Deluxe is a puzzle game where you control a rotating from from a top down view in what looks like an ancient Aztec/Mayan temple of sorts.  There is a track on the screen that has multicolored balls moving through the track.  The objective is to shoot colored balls from the mouth of the rotating frog onto balls along the track.  Once three or more colors are formed together from a ball from the frog's mouth, the balls disappear.  But watch out!  There is an end to the track!  So as your balls move along this track, if you don't lessen the line of the track, then you could easily find yourself in the losers pit.
My big deal is that I have played this game countless times before.  I didn't want to play through every single level ever all over again.  No big deal!  I played the first and second level, and the AI recognized my skill level and asked me if I would like to go to a level more fitting for my skill level.  Nothing makes me happier when a game recognizes my ability to play at a higher difficulty, and tailors itself to that difficulty.
Make no mistake.  This game isn't a serious buy.  If you want something to pass the time, or get bored by the expensive AAA titles, pick up this game and give it a whirl.  If you hate time passing puzzle games, then you might not like this game.  I will never uninstall this title though.  Never.  Not even to make room for Deus Ex: Human Revoution.

I'd have to say that I love this game. I learned the controls in just a few matches. They are simple enough for anyone to use, but have enough flexibility and complexity to pull of maneuvers you'd think came from a jet combat simulator. The health and damage system is adequate, being shot at is a real risk, unlike a lot of other first or third person shooters, where you'd think the character was the man of steel. Unlike other shooters, I managed to make my first kills in my very first match, which was very satisfying. A game that takes too long to offer the player some incentive to play, is hard to continue playing. Time of Dragons is not one of those games.
For the most part, the game is evenly balanced (And the promise of biweekly updates means that whatever tweaks need to be made to keep it fair, can happen), the lack of "upgrades" in the usual sense making combat a test of skill over grinding. The sense of progression is present, and from the start the game offers you the opportunity to test out several of the different dragons, to see which fits your playstyle the best. There are dragons out there for a mix of niches, whether you like a heavy hitter or a swift and agile fighter. (Which appealed to me the most.)
Sure, there isn't much content to this game. But do all games need content? The matches are quick, six minutes each if you join from the start, perfect for when you just want to take a break. But there's enough variation in the Team and Solo deathmatch modes and maps to offer several hours of unique play. No match feels quite the same. The matchmaking system itself could offer more, though it is relatively fair, and again, even a new player can trump the most experienced if they take a well-aimed shot.
For being free-to-play, the game is astoundingly well put-together. It is the first shooter that I've been able to run at full resolution and graphics quality without losing the most precious commodity these game need, framerate. The maps are very well thought-out, with places to hide and ambush and space for an all-out dogfight. The music, unintruding and not distracting in the least (in fact, I would go as far as to say it is beautiful) is quite fitting to an aerial combat game like this,  a refreshing break from the grating "hardcore" shooter music. Sometimes when you're all alone in a match (It happens every once in a while) you'll find yourself just soaring around the map, feeling like the king of the world.
Overall the game shows great promise in what is to come, and great fun in what is already there. I can see myself staying with this game for many months.

This is a game with major potential. Seeing how the devs are still working on it as people are reporting bugs and other things, there's a high chance they're going to exploit that potential.
For now, let's talk about the game in its current state. The graphics are good for now. My PC is pretty low-end but I can still run on the highest settings on the opening screen without dropping frames (however, there is an in-game setting for post effects that makes the game look ugly AND drops your frames immensely, so this setting should be removed or fixed pronto, but just turn it off in the in-game settings for now if you're having problems).
Actual gameplay is very, very...
FUN.
I feel like I could play this game for hours on end without getting bored of it. Time will tell if that feeling will continue, but as of right now, everythings running a smooth course. Graphics, audio, animation... none of that really completely matters if the gameplay isn't fun. And this game's gameplay is straight up, pure, magical fun. I mean the concept itself sounds fun, just think about it! Fire-breathing dragons with missiles and lasers mounted to them? That's awesome! And the fact that it is executed so well in this game makes it all feel incredible.
The only bad things in this game are the bugs and some of the audio. Let's start with that audio. The music in this game is pretty darn cool, but the sound effects are plainly sub-par. They need to be remastered in order for me to feel fully submerged into the game, because otherwise, it feels like there's no reality to this game when those fuzzy, low-qual dragon roars play. Now, the bugs are mostly with the HUD. Sometimes when you're in the options menu, you can't click the accept button. That's one example. There are also collision bugs regarding dragons running into walls even when they haven't even touched the walls. Other things, like certain flight animations, need to be polished and more rounded. But perhaps those animations help with the game's charm. Honestly, I really don't care about charm.
All that matters is that you should give this game a shot. It's got class, fun, and dragons with GUNS on them for crying out loud. It deserves a chance, so try it out, at least for a half hour.
TL;DR:
This game has a couple bugs but it's incredibly fun, so try it!

There isn't much to say about this one. It is a simple but fun game.
You are a dragon, someone strapped some guns to your back and you are off fighting other dragons. The weapons have infinite ammo, but your Dragon only has limited heat capabilities, limiting how much you can fire before your guns overheat and have to cool down.
There are 3 types of secondary weapons: Plasma Ball, Rocket launcher and Railgun (Sniper). And then there are 4 'consumables', which are basically stuff like Smokescreen, Mines (invisible to the enemy) and Cooldown and Stamina injections. Each dragon has their own special ability, such as “breath fire”, “breath toxic gas” or simply “create blinding flash”. Also each dragon has different stats. Bigger dragons are slower with more guns, slower dragons are more nimble with less guns.
That is the entire game. Its an Unity Game, so don't expect to much on the graphic end, the UI is quite simple, but honestly, the flying is fun. The game isn't big and it runs on a potato.
So if you want to get your Dragon on, and enter a team deathmatch or a free for all, this game is great for that. As I said, the flying is fun and its a simple game. Pick it up, jump in and have some fun.
I think the biggest downside to this game is how simple it is. Give it a whirl, its free to play... and I haven't found a cash shop in the thing yet and already have unlocked 3 dragons after an hour.. so.. really.. what are you waiting for?

The game is decently fun, fun enough for me to be able to keep playing until I beat the game on Normal (with a friend). It really has a lot of stuff going for it, but there's one major flaw that makes me not want to keep playing, and makes me not want to recommend this to anyone else.
First, the good. The visuals, sound, and overall atmosphere are great. The different abilities are also quite fun to use. I also was having fun pretty much constantly throughout the game - I never really got to a section where I started to feel frustrated. They give you so many options and ways to avoid hassles like traveling long distances, dying against boss fights, and things like that that you hardly have any reason to have a bad time playing this game, especially if you play with a friend. Playing with a friend is fun - the game is designed so that you get a feeling of teamwork without feeling like you're under a lot of pressure or that you'll let other people down if you mess up. It's cool to have a different set of abilities that you start to gain mastery over while also getting better at working together with your co-op partner's abilities
Unfortunately, the complexity of all of the different classes, abilities, skill point and stat point allocation could be really fun to play around with, but the flaw that makes me not want to play this more or recommend it to others is the way character building works. Without third party tools, you pretty much cannot re-spec your character other than the last few skill points you spent. What if you are a beginner and don't really know how to build your character and you find yourself with a build that seems to not work very well or you decide you don't like a skill very much and want to change your build up? You can't do that. What if you get bored of your current build and want to switch to different abilities? You can't do that. If you want to experiment, you have to resort to console commands and third party tools to reset your skill and stat points. If you don't want to do that stuff, you have to just make a new character and spend a bunch of time leveling it up again (which I personally don't find fun). In a game with such a variety of options, it really sucks to prevent you from easily experimenting with all of the cool content they've created.
Furthermore, you have to allocate your stat points every time you level up, and, from reading various guides, I got the impression that it's actually a bit counter-intuitive how you should spend your points. I initially thought that, if I want a tanky build, I should put points into Vitality, but it seemed like people suggested it's actually better to get all your tankiness from gear because vitality doesn't give you much per the amount of points you put into it. When I wanted to build a DPS focused character, I was unsure whether I should be putting points into strength or focus - I just didn't understand how the different skills scaled and it wasn't obvious by looking at the menus. For example, some abilities say they scale off x% of weapon DPS, but how would I know from that statement whether Focus or Strength will make me do more damage? The fact that it's this unclear combined with the inability to un-make poor stat allocation decisions really hurt the enjoyability for me.
Because of my uncertainty about how to build my character and realization that I wouldn't be able to change things up, I felt like I needed to follow a cookie-cutter build rather than experiment with my own because I didn't want to have to re-make my character. This is definitely less fun than trying out different abilities yourself as you play and learning organically.
So, overall, I had a decent time playing the game but I was honestly kind of glad when it was over, and I just didn't enjoy it enough to recommend it to others.

I ve been playing this game for about 2 years and i have mixed feelings about it. It’s free, the FPS-RTS combination makes it very interesting and addictive because each battle is meaningful and has an impact on the war, it is fun to play with friends but at the same time it has some issues that haven’t been fixed yet that are really annoying.
For the new players this game is just brutal. You choose 1 soldier for 1 of the 3 factions and you get thrown into an encounter battle. ‘Capture and hold the objective’ glhf. No tutorial, no training session to give you the basic idea of the game mechanics and gunplay. There used to be a quick training mission, where you could at least shoot some of the guns, bazooka, scoped rifle and Anti-Air but it’s now removed. Anyways, after a few encounters, 2 skirmishes, 1 town, 1 factory and 1 airfield battle (matchmaker keeps throwing you back to the encounter map for some reason) you get player rank VII which means you will be matched against any player from now on, either it’s another newbie or a veteran (experienced player). So for a while (since the grind is quite a lot) you ll probably find yourself in a disadvantage having to fight against better geared players, tanks and planes. A few encounter battles later you can join the war, extra xp/ribbon boost + underdog bonus, ‘yes please!’. Except now you go against hardcore players/clans and uneven resources. And that’s when most new players give up and go spam forums with ‘everyone is cheating-op guns/tanks/planes’ threads. My point is, I think the new players are not given enough time to learn the game before they reach the endgame (war battles) and they end up leaving when they get stomped by vets over and over again.
Of course you can pay real money to unlock stuff and support the developers, like any other free to play game. Does this make it pay to win? No, you can get everything with in game credits. Buying veteran membership (recommended, if you decide to spend money on the game) or straight up buying unlocks just speeds up the grind.
Now for the veteran players I don’t really know what to say. We ve all seen how the game is going downhill one update after the other :/
Squad system massively limited the usage of special classes, so if you don’t have auxiliary seat in your squad you can’t use any of them, or you end up in some low rank dude’s squad who can’t even give orders
There is no balance in the matchmaking system. More often than not you get in some battles with too many tanks and planes and recons vs infantry and paratroopers, how is this even fun?...
Gunplay got messed up all together in one of the updates with the cone fire changes. Now gun balancing is done by nerfing to the ground whichever gun is performing well at the time
The sound bug of the semi-auto and bolt-action rifles still exists and sometimes happens to full auto guns as well lately which for me it is the most annoying bug because I mainly use sound to spot enemies
The RTS part is completely broken and ignored. The usual suspects start battles with alt accounts or autoresolve their way to victory although they have favorable attack-defense lines in most battles
The community is asking for new maps, instead we get some rework on the old maps, which some were good (mountain town, factory, airfield) and some were just performance killers (town and skirmishes, too much jungle -.- ). Also the cap points went from being tiny and 1 grenade could clear the point to being extremely big and really hard to defend (those roof cap zones are ridiculous…).
Meanwhile in reto-moto HQ everything is working as intended!
Don’t get me wrong, the devs are doing work, and they bring regular updates to the game, be that guns, cars, tanks, planes etc, which are nice but they are not good enough for me personally to keep playing the game and having fun while those core issues I mentioned above exist.
I m looking forward to the new renderer update, hope it comes with a few improvements, but at the current state of the game i wouldn't recommend it.
TL;DR: if you are new to the game don’t go in with high expectations, there is a lot of grind and it will be tough until you start getting better equipment. And let’s hope reto will start fixing some stuff and make HnG great again.

It is amazing how as computing technology improves and new tools such as VR are introduced that consumers continue to pine for 'better' and 'more immersive' games, as though immersion is some ideal we may hope to one day achieve once the graphics are good enough and the gadgets we attach to our forehead become more effective. However, one need only look back to the late 90's, when a developer known as Looking Glass studios was already forging the path for immersive simulators decades ahead of time.
It achieves immersion not with high resolution character models but lumpy primitive 3D figures. It achieves immersion not with 3D glasses or goggles but with game mechanics and level design. Is Thief Gold perfect? Certainly not. The movement physics can be rough and get stuck on the uneven surfaces of the levels. The AI can be frequently prone to mistakes and it is not uncommon for guards to end up stuck in walls. There are also some monster lair levels which have aged very poorly compared to the rest of the game. But the core mechanics, and the world and places in which you are given to apply them to, give rise to a game which gives the player the sense of interacting with a living real world. The sound design should be given its own praise for bringing the square, low resolution worlds to life, as the mere footstep sounds do its job of grounding you in its setting. But even with the blocky low resolution visuals, Looking Glass does an excellent job of bringing to life the various manors and facilities which you visit to life with the proper decorum and architecture necessary to a place which people live in.
It is also impressive how such an old game takes themes such as dark fantasy and steampunk and synthesizes them into a setting which is uniquely its own, and feels distinct from the multitude of midieval fantasy games on the market. It's gameplay is also a unique fusion of first person exploration, stealth and even collectathons, that genre which wholly belongs to the 90's. It is a wonder why item and treasure collecting are not applied to more realistic genres more often, there is something quiantly enjoyable about wandering through carpeted rooms alone but near danger, admiring the oil paint portraits, opulent furniture and elaborate wall patterns, all while enjoying the thrill of robbing the owners right under their noses, taking everything valuable in sight and adding to your bonus in valuables and goods. In some ways, you could look at Thief as the ultimate walking simulator, one with complex and engaging interactions and a fail state, which would already make it superior to all the walking simulators released within the last few years. Eat your heart out, Dear Esther and Gone Home, this is how you do a walking simulator.
In the early days of 3D technology, when it was an exciting and unexplored frontier, game design was more alchemy than a science. Mechanics and genre formats had not yet been solidified, and the routine of 3D game templates was not yet a thing. Games were not yet pigeon-holed into preset genres(fps, third-person action, rpg etc) and the kinds of games that could exist where limited only by what kind of interactions and mechanics that could be made with the technology available. Sometimes to advance the future, it is necessary to look to the past. Looking Glass showed with their games that to make engaging and immersive video games, you need fun and engaging mechanics and interactions, and an interesting enough world to apply those mechanics too. No amount of technology will ever advance the quality of video games if we do not remember what it is that makes video games fun and unique compared to other mediums. If you want to remember what is possible for the future of video games, look to the past and play Thief Gold.

Brothers - A tale of two sons is a little miracle among the vast sea of games. It's so full of clever ideas, exellent exection of said ideas and emotional story that any one of those would be enough. Brothers does all of those things.
You play as two brothers at the same time. How it works is that your controller's left thumbstick and left trigger controls the other brother and right thumbstick and trigger controls the other. On your journey you face various obstacles that you have to solve with teamwork. Basically you are playing co-op with yourself. The puzzles are really easy but the difficulty comes from your brain trying to manage two things at the same time. Brothers is built to be a very casual experience though and you cannot, for example, die by accidently walking over an edge of a cliff. You can die but it needs to be clear mistake from the player. This might happen if you hang on a ledge (by holding a trigger) and let go. Brothers is not by any means a challenging game. It is most of all a story.
And what a story it is! The game does not give you any written backstory. Instead everything is told via visual cues. Neither does it have written dialogue since all characters talk in gibberish. Emotions are told with waving, pointing, shouting and so on. The world is storybook-like and somewhat clichéd but on some levels it has to be so that the player has some idea how the gameworld operates. Story on the other hand really touches some heavy subjects and it will leave you in awe. The ending is story-wise and mechanically just amazing.
Brothers even starts like a storybook. You get a menu and the game has already started on the backround. You don't get to tinker with graphic options or controls, you just begin the tale like you would a book. There is almost no tutorial, basically it just shows movement keys. In some other games this could be a problem but the controls are perfect and, since it's running on Unreal Engine, the game does not demand much from your hardware. No idea how this works without a gamepad it just isn't meant to be played like that. The story takes about 2,5h hours to complete and there is nothing besides it. There does not need to be. Definitely a recommend!
(One idea would be to play this with a close friend or significant other so that one player holds other side of the controller and the other grips another side and see how it goes.)

Never have I ever been so emotionally affected by a game, even though the characters don't speak a language you will understand, you will still laugh, you will cry, you'll be confused and you will be in for an amazing adventure.
You will probably see things in this game that you've probably never seen in a video game... or fiction for that matter, you're in this richly detailed world with so many things going on and different stories being told, but instead of focusing on the world, it focuses on two brothers whose sole concern is to save their ill father (hence the title).
The game play concept is brilliant, note that I didn't say the execution is that great (unless you are really good at multitasking and can control two characters at once) but it probably wouldn't have worked any other way, they made as simple as possible, the analog sticks move the characters and the left & right triggers lets the brothers interact with things. The controls while odd, really do tell the story and there is a reason why this a single player game (though I imagine you could figure out some way to play coop if you really wanted to).
If you want  a game about extreme challenge or combat etc, then this is not your type of game, this game is really about simple puzzles, climbing, some jumping (automatic) and most importantly of all, experiencing the game and its story.
I never really cared about the whole "are games art" thing, it never really mattered to me, but to me, art should have some sort of profound meaning, it should possibly relate to you, after all that is why art is so subjective, it depends entirely on the feelings and experiences of the viewer. If ever I would label a video game art, this would be it, so YES I recommend this wholeheartedly, the game is very short (circa 2 hours), so shut off all distractions, put on some headphones and let yourself be immersed in a fantastic story.

This is an mildly addicting game that could possibly invent a new genre of management sim. However, the execution feels amateur at best and struggled to keep me interested after a few days of playing. I bought this game when it was on sale for $6 and that price was worth it, but I'm not sure its worth a buy at full prince. Since I have to pick either a thumbs up or thumbs down in the rating system, I'm choosing to recommend this game but in reality this is a below average game that would only be enjoyable to someone who is attracted to the very sepcific premise of the game, running a fantasy shoppe. If thats a dream you have, then you'll have some fun with it. If thats never been a fantasy of yours, then this game is more annoying that its worth.
Pros:
+accessible gameplay that lets you jump right in to running your shoppe.
+good pacing, where milestones are achievable but do not feel automatic or guarunteed.
Cons:
-many gameplay mechanics feel untested. Little things like NPCs walking through objects, quests that reset whenever you exit the game, and NPCs throwing the items across your store if they decide not to buy create an experience that isn't necessarily game breaking, but a constant annoyance.
-There is a ever-present attempt at humor that is cute at best, but quickly becomes unbearable as the same bad jokes are repeated over and over and over.
-In-game information is poorly communicated. Important information like store appeal and items in demand are hard to find while apparently useless information like the leveling system (it doesnt appear to matter what level you are, since the skill tree works independently from it) covers the top third of the screen.

First of all, I love the RWBY series and can't wait till Volume 4. The game is another topic entirely. Let me comment that for a small team to create this game is an achievement all of its own. I give props for that. The game is a sad turnout that these guys try so hard to accomplish for the RWBY series. I wouldn't spend my money on $25 dollars on this game. It is sad to say but since the content felt too linear. Here are my major concerns for the game that the developers might reconsider and consider.
Story
-- The story is basic through the first 5 chapters trying to figure out what is going on. The last 5 chapters picks up the story which is fine and all. The story lacks depth on how the world works. Even for them it is hard to come up with a story all on their own in the RWBY universe. It would have been great for the story to be more rpg elements of story teling such as side quests could be hunting trophies for grimm. Throwwing out ideas would at least give them for inisght of what they can do for story.
Gameplay
-- The gameplay on RWBY is lack luster after playing for several hours. The beginning seemed alright, then it was repetitive. I felt that if the team had more resources within their grasp they might as well improved or added on more complex combat system. Dust should be used as an usuable upgrade for semblance and challenges to unlock different combos. Combos should be selective for the player, so the player has freedom to combine different moves. I am spitballing ideas, but it could have been great. Though I feel the team did everything they could, I wish they had more time to give a better combat system. I do think the current combat is fine, though it feels basic. Also, I would love to see Ruby use her semblance of speed, Yang going super saiyan after her aura drops, Blake using her clones in very unique ways, and Weiss for using her glyphs to power up her teammates and summoning. I mean I could go on, but this is what you guys can take into consideration for Huntsman/Huntress combat and skiill leveling. The level up should noto be there, it has been overused to long. Instead, skill leveling like the challenges the game gives for unlocking better versions of the move set. Sorry, again. Geez, my mind wanders.
Music
-- The music is great and awwesome since it comes from the original soundtracks of Volume 1-3. I hope new music content comes available to the game exclusively. Though I hope Jeff Williams has time to give new music for this game.
Though I don't think it will never happen, but I digress.
Interface
-- The HUD is fine though I would love to see their aura health bar shown on the girls to detect aura levels like in the series. You can see aura disappear on the individual such as you see in the show. I would like to see that. I don't have much to say though.
I probably missed few key points on this review, but the cost is not worth it in the long run. True, you have more content, but you can save your money instead. I do feel bad for giving a bad review on the team, but the way the game feels it felt ambiguous and it wasn't unique on its own right.
Overall
5/10. I am being very generous HERE. I would like to see if they can remake the game into something great.

I'm a big fan of detail when it comes to a new IP RPG game and Kingdoms of Amalur didn't disappoint, so much lore and story hidden in this gem. Still kind of hoping that a sequel may be in the works now that the troubles in the courts are over. I like the fact there is so much choice, from mixing up class abilities (even having hybrid classes) to letting the player just do the main story or having many many side quests to tick away at.
Pros: This game has a massive amount of content, although some of them can be the boring errand runs at times, fetch these items, kill a number of these monsters, deliever this letter etc, fully voiced npcs do make these more interesting then many mmos that give you text only. Combat is diverse and smooth, you don't feel restricted to picking one class, theres even a trinity class if you want to use abilities of all 3 (Albeit missing out on the most powerful abilities of each tree). While the game is fairly easy in terms of difficulty, the interesting story counters this easily in my opinion.
Cons: While there are multiple races in the game I would have liked seeing more of the cultures in greater detail much like the DLC race, the main game didn't give the same feel. Some quests can be repetitive and gathering resources for crafting seems pretty pointless once you get hold or create a decent set of armor and a good weapon, the only point is for the achievements. There isn't really punishment for stealing, you can do some quests that would be difficult by just stealing the item from the NPC and paying the crime fee to the guard.
As odd as it seems I thought the side quests with the factions were more entertaining than the main storyline, consequences for your actions whereas the main plot seems unchangable. There is plenty of replayablity in the different classes, one playthrough you might be a powerful mage, another a warrior, another a rogue or maybe one who dabbles in all 3. The different crafting skills do offer that additional incentive to play the game more than once as trying to do all in one playthrough could be draining due to how much is available. Then again you could do it in one playthrough and merely go to a Fateweaver that resets all your attriutes and skills so you can change your class whenever you wish. Do I recommend this game? Definitely, it's a fun RPG with heaps of story and lore to keep you entertained.

Don't be fooled by this turd masquerading as an old school shooter. I never played the old one, but hopefully it didn't suck this badly. I love old school games, like shadow warrior, doom, duke nukem,  but this seems to not know anything that makes old shooters good. Graphics are fine, there is no story, but that's normal in old shooters. The levels are big and long (insert d!ck joke) and the game is decent length. That's about where the good ends.
Let's start with weapons. In old school shooters, you carry tons of varied guns. In this, you can carry 3 total weapons. pistols, which you won't even use most of the first level. A mp40, and a third special weapon. You have to hold pistols and machine gun, but only can carry one special weapon (??). Every time you pick one up you drop the other, meaning you need to blatantly waste the special weapon each time. Only the ones suck. There are like 5 total, meaning like 6 guns in the game. But almost all of the special are just grenade/rocket launcher shooters, which are only usually helpful on bosses and groups of guys. So there is only a shotgun to use on single guys, most of which you fight the entire game, meaning the special weapons are useless. So you can only carry 1 other gun, and its worthless. Yes this means you use the mp40, the exact same gun, for 90% of the game. No you don't get new machine guns to replace it. You use it the entire game, yup sounds fun huh? Then if that's not enough, instead of varied enemies, like in many old games, you fight a single enenmy the entire game. You fight an asian guy in a yellow costume, a black costume, with armor sometimes, and that's it. They use the same character model and just give it different uniforms, that's it. So you play level to level fighting the same 1 guy with the same one weapons......yeah now you'll know why I was bored after an hour. Nobody wants to be doing the exact same thing from level 1 to level 15. There is a melee button but the hitbox is terrible and you will miss people looking right at them, so it's worthless too.
Sometimes levels have basic puzzles. There are a few levels that change things up, and use traps and what not, and that's a fun change of pace. Then the game tries platforming, which is maybe the single worst thing in the game. It's hard to move, and then once you press forward, and hold for more than .1 second, you go flying forward and are unable to stop your momentum. This means landing on single little platforms even just when jumping is impossible because you can never judge where you will land and you either land before or way after. I dreaded platform segments because it is the worst I have ever seen in a first person platformer, good thing they use it a lot right (*facepalm*)
The enemy AI sucks. They stand there and let you shoot them, or just continually roll side to side, or shoot you through walls where you can't see them from across the level. The dying animations are just them standing up with unconvincing red stuff that looks nothing like blood and showing up in the air, then they suddenly fall down. It is the same every time. They don't react to bullets and there seems to be no physics. Then there is the saving. Game has quicksave and checkpoint. For the first time ever in a game, if you get to a checkpoint, and then quicksave later on, quit the game, and "resume game" later, it won't take you to the furthest quicksave, it will actually take you back to the checkpoint, nice programming guys. You can quickload from the further back checkpoint to load further. How dumb. Then if you die you can't press quickload to go back to the quicksave. You have to wait for the game to load up the death menu and you have to click the button to quickload. Another first. Why would I not want to use quickload during my death/menu. That's 2/3 the reason it was invented.
The final straw is boss fights. The game PROHIBITS you from quicksaving during any boss fight or during platforming sections, the two most poorly done and frustrating segments in the game, go figure. Oh but they ALSO don't give you checkpoints during boss fights. This means when most bosses have multiple stages and insta-death abilities, you lose 3-5 min of progress from 1 hit or so. There is one boss where his attack will auto track and kill you. You must hide during each of his attacks. Then you get a second to pop out and hit him, but he flys around so you can't hit him well, then when he stops moving he instantly starts shooting, so you have to hide before he stops. This means you get like 1-2 seconds of shooting before you have to run and hide and wait out his 10 seconds of shooting. Sometimes the game glitches and he can shoot you through the walls. So after doing barely any damage and killing him, the game doesn't give you health, and suddenly he has a new form. You drop down into a new area, and he still has instant kill ability. So I die, and lose all that progres. In one try it instantly forced me off the ledge but he was already shooting, meaning I couldn't get to cover or do anything to keep from dying. So the game made me die, and since I couldn't save between forms, I have to spend 5 min getting back to the form only to insta-die again and repeat. Oh also there is multiplayer but it’s already completely dead.
An old-school shooter is known for having a large arsenal of carry-able varied weapons, fighting varied guys, and fun boss fights. This has you use a single gun the entire game against a single foe, and not be able to save because it say's you can't when you need to, and has some of the worst boss fights ever. Thief Gold - the first installment (an updated version of Thief: the Dark Project) in the cult saga of Thief games. The game was released in the year 1999 and very well received by critics. Surprisingly, even though I am a fan of Splinter Cell and Hitman series, I haven't played Thief upon its original release. Luckily, recently I finally got my hands on the game. Even though the game is not about graphics, I highly recommend installing HD Mod - it looks simply beautiful.
The game is set in a steampunk city called.. The City. Gameplay suits people like me very well. I am the kind of person who likes to crawl around the levels very slowly and sniff every corner. Now, you CAN go through the front door
swinging your sword, but that would be just silly. And, unlike Camelot, The City is not a silly place. Although AI is not the sharpest - you cannot expect a super advanced AI from a 1998 game - you will still face a formidable challenge and your attacks are but a scratch to the enemies.
For a game that is almost 20 years old, the levels are bigger than one could expect. If you like to screw around, it may take around an hour to finish a level. Despite all that, level design is very good.
There isn't much of a tutorial to the game, since the training part covers just really basic things – it teaches you how to swing your sword and use items (like keys to unlock doors). You will have to learn things on the go. At your disposal you have a sword, a blackjack (a tool for pacifists – when you don’t want to kill your opponent, just knock him out), a bow and some explosives (like flash bombs). You probably won’t use your sword too much however. With a variety of different types of arrows available to pass through levels undetected, you will find the bow to be one of the most useful items.
I recommend the game for everyone who enjoys stealth games, likes a challenge or simply wants to remember old times and replay Thief with HD Mod. For those who haven’t played any games like this before – this is great value for your money and you definitely should try it. However, if you don’t like slow paced gameplay – this game is not for you. But I definitely recommend this game. Especially on sale - it's a steal.

Redlight this. An ok job for a 3 person team, but more time in planning and effort in execution of a shopkeep "feel" would be great.
+ Well done with the music! Bit odd at times though.
+ While rather lackluster, having a customisable avatar helps the game feel more personal.
- All the menus are gross.... like what the hell.

- Time skip option... PLEASE. Or at least run the game while alt-tabbed. Would love to watch videos to kill time.
- Really doesn't feel like there's any challenge. Could be improved by adding a charge to delivery fees, so you can't just grind basic items with a 10% increase.
- Lack of incentive for progression is really noticeable. Why can't we start with a smaller shop, and slowly buy our way up to a mega store with employees? Get to a position where we can sit in a chair and watch the money roll in. Yes I know, it's based on ye olde times. But why can't we use modern day organisation? It's what I feel works best with games based in the past - when you use your knowledge of the 21st century to your advantage.
- More than one "type" of tutorial would be nice. I prefer having an npc guide me through basics, rather than reading through the (rather ugly looking) tutorial. Some would prefer listening.
- Hopefully there's a way to advertise your shop later on. Sure I only played a few days worth, but man the lack of timeskip and low customers per day is super frustrating. And remember, if someone isn't interested in the game for long enough to reach that point, they won't experience it.
- Town feels too big, little reason to go outside other than to chase down a thief and visit that dude with the extra stuff. Can sit at the door and kill them instantly.
Not worth the money currently. Wouldn't purchase it for more than $2 USD. A suggestion to make this worth $10 USD is by hiring more people of broader life experiences to brainstorm ways to improve the depth of your game. Revise tutorials and progression, start smaller and end bigger. Work on them menus! Good luck.
