Brawlhalla is going to bring back local multiplayer in a refreshing way that Super Smash Bros has in one way and hasn't in another. The thrill of chaotic brawling between three other players is brought into Steam as a soon-to-be free to play game with the optional microtransations of cosmetic items as well as purchasing in-game coins (there is no system as of yet that allows for awarding coins, which renders the store useless FOR NOW. I have great hopes that this company will be fair with its coin system). Each character has its own unique playstyle much like Smash Bros and the Training Mode is a great place to get a feel for each character and see which you like best. Unlike Smash, each character has their own signature weapons that spawn in the match through the use of "weapon portals" that act much like grabbing an item on the ground. The weapons do not necessarily make your character more powerful. It can be fairly fun to challenge an armed opponent with your bare hands and succeed. However, these weapons do increase the range of your attacks and can be used to create outstanding combos that can lead to some serious beatdowns. The multiplayer is locked at Time Limit Mode for now, but the Couch Play and Single Player tournament allow for stock matches for all you Smash players that prefer lives over time.
All in all, I am fully appreciating the game as is and will continue to support it. I can't wait to see how many more characters, weapons, maps, and other ideas Blue Mammoth Games has in store for Brawlhalla. Great game!!!

This game to me seems like a mix of Super Smash Bros and Awesomenauts, if I had to make a comparison. The controls are good, the character designs are pretty great and the music has a certain feel to it. Each character has 2 special weapons (as of now, I believe, there is a feature in the game to change it, but it doesn't really do anything, maybe it's skins for the weapons) which are pretty fun to play around with and see what character does what moves. There's online multiplayer, local multiplayer and a roster of more than 10 characters, although despite the weapons, and even with the them, they generally share the same movelist, so that might turn you off if you don't like that sort of thing. I CAN recommend it now, with there being a free early access, but if you have to pay then I would wait until they add more to the game. In other words, can't wait to see what they have up their sleeve.

In short: A decent smash bros clone. Early Access.
There are so far 13 characters ('Legends') to choose from, and various skins to acquire. Each character has different damage, attack speed, defense and run speeds. As such characters do feel different -- some are tanky, some are pure glass cannons. At the moment all characters are available to play, this will soon switch to a free rotation with permanent unlocks.
On top of individual stats each can equip 2 types weapons (swords, spears, hammers, pistols). Although the weapons are largely the same no matter who wields them (except the looks) each character has a unique special move per weapon type. Then there are mines, bombs, spiky balls to spice up the match.
In terms of movement you can chain up to 3 jumps, dodge, and wall-jump. Nothing fancy, but the 3 jumps do a lot to ensure you stay on the arena. Look at the screenies -- the arenas are tiny, a few small platforms or a single larger one, few walls to bounce back off. And in a typical smash bros fashion with each damage stage you're sent flying with greater speeds.
So far I had problems connecting to online matches though, couldn't even look for a game because I "lost connection to server" every time I tried. I don't know if it's just general server issues or what.
Akin to mobas of the day Brawlhalla monetises skins (character, weapon), taunts, and unlocking characters (with a free rotation). The currency is Mammoth Coints, which currently come at about $1 per 20.

Honestly, what can I say... I never cried so much in my life. This is not a game for very sensible persons (like me). I just finished the game and I need to hug my teddy bear really long to get over the story.
In terms of gameplay, I actually have nothing negative to report. The controls are simple but can still confuse as you go on in the adventure. The puzzles are quick to understand and can be solved without experiencing much frustration. Sometimes, I think it might be a little bit too easy. There is no part where you can get stuck or that is really challenging in my opinion. Still, I don't see it as a problem since the game is not about feeling awesome after solving a hard puzzle or bypassing a large obstacle and more about telling the story of the brothers. Difficult puzzles would maybe ruin this experience.
The narrative of the story is just fantastic. Even without using an acutal understandable language (the characters in this game speak some a made-up language + there are no subtitles), it is always clear what the characters in the game are saying or what they are talking about (also because they use gestures which helps out a lot). The story and (if existend) the relation of the individual characters is easily understandable.
Sure, the game is pretty short (it took me two hours to finish it without having all achievements) but I think it's the right length. Since the gameplay is simple, you can only do so much to keep it fresh and entertaining. Maybe one level more wouldn't have hurt but I don't think it's necessary either.
All in all, Borther - A Tale of Two Sons is an entertaining, small and also emotional experience. If you're looking for a quick and fun game and you're not the most sensible person out there (*sob*), definitly check out this game!

You might have been strayed away because of the Mixed review you saw on the store page for this game, but you may or may not be surprised that those reviews are not accurate of how the game really is. I will not lie, this game is
. Despite what some of these reviews might say (i.e: pay to win, not fun, unbalanced, op weapons just to name a few) this game doesn't demonstrate almost all of these. I'll start off by describing the "problems" angry players have posted about.
Is Heroes & Generals Pay to Win?: No, it is not. There is a very large difference between Pay to win and Pay to progress. No weapon in this game has an extreme advantage over another, and at the end of it all it was whoever was the more skilled player. However, most of the more luxurious weapons are locked behind ribbons in which you must level. The later ranks of these do take a long time to progress, and this is where pay to progress comes in. You pay with either money or in-game currency, and gain progression without having to gain it in game. (i.e. killing people with your M1 Garand gives you modifications for your gun)
Unbalanced weapons: This entirely relies of the player's point of view of a weapon, nation, vehicle, and whatever else it might be. Is the StG44 unbalanced? Nobody knows, except the person who just got killed by it.
Unbalanced nations: As said before, this relies on the player's point of view of the game. Maybe that player is playing the German nation, and he's getting stomped by the Americans. Most likely, he finds that something is unfair about that nation and he blames his own mistakes on the belief that American weapons are overpowered.
Another thing which is great about this game is that there is something for everybody. Do you prefer standard boots-on-the-ground action with a rifle in hand? Infantry. Do you prefer sneakily landing on enemy players on their own objective? Paratrooper. Maybe you prefer driving a tank, striking fear into the hearts of the Infantry around you. Or maybe you like to the stick to the air, engaging in dogfights with other players and bombing those beneath you.
A major feature in Heroes & Generals is the RTS game. The RTS game controls the ebb and flow of the entire war gamemode which is fought by other players in the action game (FPS). Generals of your nation plan battles out in cities in order to control the entire map, and as a soldier, you get to engage in those very fights planned by the generals. You are the one supporting the outcome of that fight, and I personally think that is extremely cool.
TL;DR - Heroes & Generals is fun, despite all of the people complaining about it's very miniscule problems, as well as their own personal problems of the game. Give it a try!

Now that I've had an honest chance to play Thief I can say that, while it has faults it is still an enjoyable experience. The gameplay is what one could expect from a first person stealth romp, or from games like Splinter Cell for example. You get missions that change in terms of objectives based on your difficulty, kind of like Goldeneye on the N64. In these missions you'll do things that one would expect a thief to do, steal things, lots and lots of things. Though sometimes you'll be busting friends out of jail or other things of the like, but they all come back to the stealth elements of the game. You as Garrett are not much of a fighter, and on the higher difficulties are even tasked with not killing at all, so as such you rely on the shadows above all else. The use of shadows and sound is like I said earlier similar to Splinter Cell. The darker your surroundings the harder to see you, and the different surfaces all make louder noise.
The first of my newer problems arise here though, and it has to do with your enemies. For the most part you deal with local town guards who don't seem like they'll be too much issue, don't be fooled. Every enemy you encounter is deadly, and when they find you they will chase you everywhere. Do yourself a favor, SAVE OFTEN. Keep a close finger on F11 or you'll be stuck in a lot of tricky situations that have the high probability of ruining your missions entirely.
Another issue comes in the form of the game's combat, or the lack there of. Your swordsmanship is controlled based on where you are looking at your enemy, right side for a slash to the right vicea versa. You can power attack with a held click and block with mouse 3. Overall the swordplay isn't terrible, but stacked against other combat engines, even some from the era, it's very lackluster. Your bow is indeed a weapon but it's far more useful as a tool, using water arrows and the like to affect your surroundings. Your bow has a sight, but only with trial and error can you reliably hit a target without prior knowledge about where the arrows will go based on the sight. Make sure to do training and take as much time as you need to figure out your bow's ranges. The opening cinematic shows Garrett nailing a guard in the neck with a well placed arrow, don't do this unless you have to. I say this because every time I've tried to kill someone with the bow I've only ever♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥them off. Even with an assured head shot all they do is stagger and then shove their sword through my chest.
The environments are all really great in game, ranging from castles and prisons to zombie infested mines and abandoned sewers. Wrapped around all these environments is some of the best sound design I've ever heard in almost any game, some of the voice acting witholding mind you. The music is non-existent for the most part, leaving you instead to the ambiance of the area you are in. Guards talk about their days, machinery whirrs & grinds, and ghostly sounds wail in the darkness. Thief's environments steal the show for me, above all else.
One could easily look at the game and pan it for its graphics, and admittadely they're not much to look at. Add to it the animations are a bit stilted and robotic, but admittadely they are pretty smooth all the same. Characters are blocky and have some messy textures at times, but that could be looked past because nearly everything else is awesome. The graphics as a whole are what you can expect for the era this game comes from.
It may seem like I've got nothing but problems with Thief, but like I said I can't help but laud over the environments and atmosphere that is established. It is amazing, really some of the best I've ever seen. The combat may suck, but a swift blackjack to someone's head when they don't see it coming puts them out of commission pretty much indefinitely. If you're playing the game right you'll never have to really fight anything or anyone, so really the combat takes the back seat to a game that is all about the stealth and environmental design of the world. At least that's what I've got to say personally about it.
So grab it on sale or the like, slap the mod on, don't get stabbed, shot, bitten, or eaten, and have a good 'ol time with one of the progenitors of the stealth genre.

While the game has some of the feel of the RWBY series in its speed, it lacks a lot of its charm and energy, If I were to guess, I would say that the developers intended to capture the rush and scale of the first RWBY trailer, but forgets that what really drew the fans in were its lovable characters and how they interacted with one another. Another more obvious draw was the kinetic, raw spectacle and creativity expressed in the fight scenes which made the series stand out; only in a Platinum Games production would you see something more balls to the wall crazy than in a RWBY battle. The lack of either of these elements is the core reason as to why this game fails as a part of the RWBY universe and franchise.
Instead, what we get is a fairly short series of boxed off rooms with a set amount of enemies to kill, empty corridors with little to nothing going on between them and little flash and finesse in the presentation of any aspect of the game, with palette swap enemies and rehashed mini bosses sprinkled throughout this vast emptiness just to give the effect of -something- going on. The enemy aren't even that interesting; the weakest part of the show are the Grimm, whose role in the show is to be that everlooming presence that remind the viewers the world is constantly under threat; instead, it is the personal drama of the characters, the villains and the ultimately the human conflict that vitalizes the show. With the Grimm given the sole focus (outside of a single spoiler character), you'll find it very difficult to feel invested in the story. That isn't to say that the Grimm shouldn't be in the game; there are some very interesting looking Grimm in the show such as the Nevermore, which had one of the best fight scenes in the first season. However, as said before, the game lacks the desire to focus on anything interesting, so for the most part you'll just be dealing with the same three or four types of enemy that can all be felled in the exact same manner.
Speaking of the combat, it tries its best to be an imitation of the Batman: Arkham games, with counter icons and "free-flow" combat with a mix of heavy and light attacks and an "Ultimate". However, I eventually ended up using almost exclusively the light attacks while watching in an eternal panic for the blink and you'll miss it countering system which the enemies WILL spam with abandon and, due to terrain issues, the counters may not even connect and you'll end up ganked by three other Grim, resulting in your untimely and sudden respawn. Although there are four playable characters from the start, I ended up exclusively using Yang for much of the game due to her no-nonsense animation style, which significantly reduced the chance of getting locked in an animation and dying as a result.
So Grimm fails to capture the charm and energy of the series in its combat, but what about the music? Well, it has instrumental variants of the show's soundtrack, which is always a plus, however it's poorly mixed and has absolutely no concept of what "audio looping" is, meaning that the soundtrack rises, goes through the motions, then stops entirely, then starts again. This means that there's a significant amount of time of complete audio non-action in combar situations. Outside of combat, there's some severe audio/context dissonance, with the hype music tooting away during scenes of walking through the again empty corridors. Additionally, due to the overall lack of boss battles in the game they missed the opportunity to play the vocal tracks during the climactic parts of a battle like they do in the show or a good Platinum game like MGR does.
Now, all these problems wouldn't be so bad if it were a fan game. In fact, it started out as exactly that. And I do realize that this is the company's first venture into the videogame market, and for that I do commend them for branching out into new medias. I'll always appreciate Rooster-teeth to go beyond their initial scope. On the otherhand, Roosterteeth also know when an idea is stupid or half baked, so this entire game feels very out of character for them.
But this isn't all bad news. As their first game ever, they could have created a much poorer product. The mechanics are there, and occasionally I was having fun stringing hits together. Visually, it's very similar to the show, and the environments are a perfect match for the show. I'm not too bothered by the change in models close to the end of this games release; I spent very little time looking at my character's face anyway, but I did notie that their heads are all just a little too large. Still, it's hardly notable when you're slicing up grimm. The animation is a little janky at times with the enemy, but the player characters themselves are done very well.
But as I entered the third and what turned out to be final hour of the game I realized that there's so much more that -could- be done, but simply never came to pass. When the final boss came, I thought I'd actually be able to face off against the villain personally; a fight against an equal, a fellow Hunter, would have somewhat made up for the lackluster rest of the game, but my only reward was only more disappointment.
So what can we take away from all this? This game lacks the charm and spectacle that RWBY is known for, and is full of missed opportunities and interesting story that Roosterteeth has become famous for, and I hope, if they ever decide to revisit the gaming sphere, that they try to bring their personality with them next time.
Sorry for the long-ish review, it's 8:30am and I am extremely bored and just a tad disappointed. But even if this game is a flop, I'm still thoroughly hyped for season 4. This hasn't shaken me as a fan of RWBY, but it has dissappointed me as a gamer.

I got this game gifted to me by a generous friend, and was excited to reminisce in nostalgia at the old-school, arcade-style FPS gameplay I expected. I was very satisfied with my gameplay experience.
If you like fast-paced FPS gameplay, score/combo multipliers, making your own maps, and endless bloodshed, then you will really enjoy this game. I played the original, and the remake does fantastic justice to the 90's era of FPS gameplay.
The aesthetics are good - the remade assets provide an updated old-school arcade experience. The game is not graphic intensive, but still provides decent weapon effects like the "god mode" blast and the RPG rocket explosion. The music and sounds are good and add to the intense, speedy atmosphere created by the game.
Controls are typical of an arcade FPS and easy to learn. I tried using a controller, but much prefer the keyboard and mouse combo for this game. There isn't a tutorial, however, the learning curve is minimal (to moderate) enough that one isn't absolutely necessary. You can adjust the difficulty to suit your needs - the hardest difficulty is fairly unforgiving.
Before you begin, you select a character with different specializations (ex: some are faster, tougher, etc). The game only supports one active playthrough at a time, so selecting a new game will overwrite your old one. Gameplay consists of you progressing through levels to the end area, killing numerous enemies along the way and collecting coins if you wish to increase your total score. You will frequently need to find and trigger switches to advance in the level (also spawning more enemies). There are many secret areas for people who like to explore (these also sometimes reward you with heavy weapons).
Something I found very amusing is the reload mechanic - you don't ever need to reload, however, you can reload as often as you like (purely aesthetic). Enemies will have to reload between clips. Sometimes, an enemy may get on his knees and plead for his life. If you spare him, he will most likely attack you once a bit of time has passed (or your back is turned). You can aim down the sights of some weapons with the right mouse click, however, that may also be the secondary fire for a particular weapon (ex: explosive shotgun). As you take damage, you will have to find food to eat, healing you instantly. There is a "god mode" weapon you can sometimes find in secret areas, which give you temporary invulnerability and a powerful blast attack.
True to the 90s era form, you will not regenerate health, there is no radar or waypoints, and gameplay is very, very rapid. Another thing I found very amusing the the lack of recoil - most weapons have a minimal spread. The shotgun has a "camera shake" that occurs after you fire, which I think is supposed to mimic recoil (but is happens shortly after you fire, and seems a bit ridiculous).
Overall, if you enjoy fast twitch shooters reminiscent of old-school arcade FPS games, then you should give Rise of the Triad a try.
Recommend!

+ Mixed classes. By this I mean: everything goes. You want to be a 100% warrior? No problem. A battlemage? Gotchu. Equal parts of Might/Finesse/Sorcery? There's a destiny for that. I was playing a warrior-rogue hybrid charging into everything headfirst with a greatsword. Go crazy.
+ Gathering ingredients is similar to how it was in Oblivion, meaning you can fail gathering a plant if you don't have enough points invested in alchemy. Also, the starting area is peppered with ingredients required for health potions, which is always nice, especially when you're new and don't know how to play.
+ Voice Acting is superb. I'm sure half of NPCs were voiced by a 100 different people. If not, I'm still impressed. However, being a hardcore Dragon Age fan I couldn't help but hear Cullen in half of male NPCs and Loghain reciting me lore bits.
+ Character customization. Especially the tattoo which at right settings could look like a scar.
+ Chickens. Finally, nobody throws me in jail for accidentally killing a chicken or ten. There's even a "Chickens slain" count on your stats page.
- Hard is normal, normal is easy, haven't tried easy difficulty but you get my meaning.
- Stealth system is kinda weird? I was wearing heavy armor but with enough points invested in stealth I could sneak up on enemies and execute them, at least in the beginning of the game.
- Some abilities in your preferred ability tree are kinda useless but you have to invest points in them anyway because the next level requires a certain amount of points.
- Some items stay in your inventory after the quest is finished and you can't sell them. This becomes less of a problem halfway through the game when you have maxed out inventory space and don't need more money than you can find on your travels, but scrolling through 30 unwanted items while looking for a repair kit was kinda off-putting.
- There little incentive to buy anything other than backpacks. By checking every corner I already had good weapons and armor and I didn't need to buy them. Had 5 Million gold by the end of the game, most of that from enemy drops and quest rewards.
- Some bugs are game-breaking. I recommend making a hard save before every main quest. Some bugs make it unable to continue with it thus preventing access to other areas.
- Man Boss can be defeated in about 5 minutes if you stock up on a certain potion, making it easier than common trolls.

At first, I assumed that this game might have been like a certain freeware game known as Build and Shoot, a fun little game that never really did get a lot of attention, but had a lot of fun ideas that make the game quite fun to play. Being able to dig trenches, a small wall, or even a fancy bunker made for an interesting game where the key to winning isn't just shooting people, but being able to build things to keep people from killing you as easily, be it as simple or complex as you desire.
This is not the case here.... All this game turned out to be is a simple run and gun game that provides silly killstreaks ala CoD.. Hell, it is nothing more than Blocks of Duty if anything.. The whole building aspect is utterly pointless in game, because there is no way to shoot over anything two blocks tall, meaning you can't use cover to protect yourself while you reload and fire from it. Heck,  the mere act of building takes ages, and it is much easier to just ignore building all together and just shoot at each other. Even breaking the map isn't fun, let alone the fact that it can sometimes be very easy to fall off said map without warning in some places.
Seems the only building element in the game is for the guns, which of course is easier said than done, since it requires third-party programs in order to fully complete your gun, and even then it could still get denied if it doesn't meet certain requirements.. The guns that do pass, however, are frustrating beasts to deal with.
So, you can't build (let alone even use) cover in a game where you die really easily, the combat is pretty much CoD in block form, and oh yeah, some of the maps suck pretty bad too.. Can it get worse? How about the fact that the community is so small that it is depressing to just think about it?
Really, if you want a fun block builder/shooter game, stick with Build and Shoot, it is free and much funner than this, let alone it probably has more players than this game ever will.. And BaS doesn't even have a large community either, so that is saying a lot.

Believe it or not, I am a professional historian in real life. One with a PhD about French history and working in a cultural institution. As you can imagine, I was really excited about this game. Despite my busy life, I'm playing video games to dwelve into the past, to be immersed for a few hours in this history that I love so much. What is a romantic like me thinking of Holdfast: Nations at War?
It is obviously early days for this game and many features are missing. As it is, we are dealing with the infantry and the navy, but horses and mobile artillery are absent. This is the rule of Early Access Games, something that we signed for when we bought the game. I am pleased to say that Holdfast is already enjoyable. A typical siege battle will let you chose between the French and the British, the latter always being in the attacking seat. While the lack of discipline of a few players is sometimes a problem, the large amount of role-playing fellow soldiers is very often enjoyable. It is not rare to have a good officer screaming orders in an early 19th century fashion while the men shout taunts at the enemy. The last minutes are usually tense, with the French holding to their last precious tickets. Often, a round ends in a large British charge with a bayonet slaughter near the French flag.
Navy battles are also good fun and feel as a different game. After selecting your class, ranging from a sailor to the captain or a violonist, you have a role to fulfil. The crew will usually make sure that guns are loaded and ready to fire while riflemen wait anxiously to shoot at enemy sailors. You need to be patient to enjoy naval battles. Sometimes, the captain will sail for a long time, trying to avoid action in order to follow the best course. But suddenly, the orgy of violence kicks in and there is nothing better than being fired at from two directions and seeing bodies of your fellows flying in the airs.
As you can see, I like this game very much. It is, however, not perfect. Early Access issues aside, maps are not diverse enough and lack the historical touch. I would very much like the team to work on real locations. Why not start with Hougoumont farm or a Spanish village? How about a French city to match the invasion of France in 1814? These ideas could give a breath of fresh air to the gameplay. There are also minor historical details that could be improved but this, unless you're a history nerd like me, won't bother most.
Overall, I would strongly recommend this game. There is nothing like holding the line while the French are melting on you, and having the lad next to you screaming 'come on, you cheese-eating surrender monkeys'!
Ps: I'll update the review to talk about future update.

Thief: The Dark Project or Thief: Gold in this case is one of my favorite games of all time. It's a brilliant piece of fiction and brilliant gameplay wise. It's a bold stealth game set in a fictional world run by Nobles, Peasants, Religious Fanatics, and Pagans. You're Garrett a cunning, sarcastic Thief who needs to pay the rent so instead of doing an honest days work, he steals. He's one of the best stealth characters in video game history. The game is set in a giant fictional place known only as the city, it's a giant cross between the Dark age and the Viktorian age, the art style is dark yet colorful, even for 1998 graphics I still find the art style and graphics appealing and I'd take them over any modern day graphics. I'm serious.
The stealth gameplay is something put together so perfectly in a game. You're not only gonna have to worry about sticking to the shadows you're also always gonna have to worry about how audible you are, given what surface you're walking across. Grass, wood, and stone are a surface you can easily sprint on. But can't jump on or else you'll make too much noise, while carpet is a surface you can jump on and also sprint on. The same can't be said about marble flooring which is a dead give away if you even walk on it. You'll see more marble flooring and more lights that you can't put out, the more you get to the rich and powerful in the game. To call the current state of this game a "full release" is either an insult or blind optimism. As a fan of RWBY, I've always wanted to get this game the second I saw the base version of this before Roosterteeth even picked up on it on youtube. While I wasn't here for the majority of the early access, I did play it through before the update. The differences between then and now are very few. This "full release" is basically just a story mode expansion pack. My problem is calling that a full game. There's still some glaring bugs (like how my camera will randomly try to go back and forth constantly without end until I re-open the game) and combat is still to the point of nauseating with a subpar auto-lock on system and lack of a real lock on, on top of a better-than-it-used-to-be-but-still-horrendous camera. On top of that, my PC isn't the best but it's not so horrible I can't play some graphically intensive games. There's many with stronger graphics, and yet, this one has a terrible framerate for me. The rest is more empty than anything.
As stated before by a number of reviews: the combat is stale and there's next to no variety between the characters. For a hack and slash, I don't have issue with the combos being in a bare-bones state at the moment. You just use weak attacks and hit strong attack after the first, second, or third weak one. This is fine, but aerial attacks are all useless. Counter, in my experience, does virtually nothing. Either it's me and a timing issue or the button is just pointless. I do like the HP system regenerating itself quickly by backing off and getting a skill for it. I'd be more a fan of the ultimates if I couldn't sum them all up as “big aoe big damage” for every character and nothing else.
The story is alright, not spectacular. I won't say anything about it for anyone who hasn't played it or is still getting through it. The scenery is majestic in my opinion, just a little too spacious. The random comments from Team RWBY through levels make the game more lively since otherwise it's mostly silent until you've sprint long enough to find a wave(s) of the same... three enemies.
In this current state, I wouldn't recommend this to anybody. If the devs want to start throwing DLC on top of just grazing over how this game is nothing remotely close to a finished product, they only prove this was a mistake and expect it to live off hype. This game CAN be good and it's not even a total disaster. The idea is there, the design just isn't. Characters “look” diverse, the music is okay, the graphics could be improved but they aren't horrendous, the level up system and skills aren't bad either (though it'd be nice to know the names of my skills. You call a skill Frostbite and don't tell me what it is, why would I upgrade it?). But when I see something labeled “team attack”, and then using it really had nothing to do with being a team, I'm just left confused.
I love RWBY and I can only hope future patches of this game are less built on excitement like the “full release” was. And for the love of God, I pray they focus on making the game far more functional before they start talking about additional content you PAY FOR.
If you really, really, really want this game, get it on sale. 25 dollars is just a mistake you will wholeheartedly regret.

DE is a mix and a meeting of genres, including Fallout, Gears of War, Half-Life 2 and a touch of Splinter Cell and Hitman. Stealth or breach are big features in the game and every move, decision or kill you make effects the game. The game follows the protagonist Adam Jensen (once head of Sarif Industries security) who is now an Interpol counter-terrorism agent two years after the Aug Incident. Due to the incident, a lot of the non-augmented population are against augments. This has caused a major division between those who have augments and those who don't. Due to being repressed, augments have organized themselves and some have even gone as far as to resort to terrorism. This is where you and Jensen come in.
is what one would expect from Deus Ex but a lot shorter. The main story line is decent as it didn't have major plot twists or turns. I felt Human Revolution gave me more of an "oh crap" feeling when it came to certain cut-scenes or scenarios (especially the very last one)! The player can choose to follow the main story line or can take part of side missions and have influence on smaller aspects of the game. Besides main and side missions, there are POI (points-of-interest) that the player can inspect to find NPC's or some sort of materials. I've done most of the side missions before I went onto completing main missions. This is a good idea as you will not be able to go back to certain side missions upon completing a main mission (the game even gives you a warning before proceeding with the story). Doing the side missions will give you more cash to spend and even build up your Arsenal, not to mention score some brownie points regarding your moral score within the game. The side missions do feel a little cheap sometimes but other times can be exceptionally challenging. The main story is good, but Human Revolution left me with a lot more to think about while playing and even after finishing. Anything with a good story will make one think and maybe even relate the story to reality. There are a few times I was caught off guard in some scenematics (think
whereas I found some to be really weak.
is half a step up from Human Revolution. You are stuck in first person camera until you take cover. Upon taking cover, the camera will take a 3rd person over the shoulder view unless you're aiming down your (gun)sights. Everything feels smooth and the action/stealth balance is beautiful. I find it really helps to stick to a certain augments depending on your play style. If you are playing for stealth, you'll definitely have to look at invisibility, remote hacking, improved hacking and a few other upgrades that will make your solo play easier. If you are a breacher, then it definitely helps to upgrade armor (2 types), battery power, gun handling and use of the typhoon system. It is possible to be balanced but it will be difficult in certain areas to do what you want regarding hacking security. What is good theme that they kept was the ability to choose multiple paths to reach a destination. Vents are quite popular but overhead excursions are just as good to keep out of sight. The option of holstering your gun is an effective one as well when dealing with conflict. Police or even enemies will ignore you given you left the scene without any firearms or suspicion. However, if Adam does managed to get spotted the alarm alertness level will go from normal to hostile. The AI is quite smart when it comes to fire fights and will not be afraid to close in on you (depending on the difficulty level). This provides a good challenge and forces the player to either evade or fight back.
So what makes Mankind Divided (or Human Revolution with better graphics, new story and some re-skinning) decent? I'm disappointed with the lack of change but it would be ironic for me to say that the game play is crap. The game play is good, but is just as good (or rather similar) to Human Revolution. The gears of war cover system combined with FPS control makes for some enticing combat. Add some super natural abilities being augmented and it can make for some interesting methods going about a fire fight (or even avoiding one). New abilities have been added to Jensen arsenal to compliment the old ones. Upgrading certain body components will give you certain features, so pay attention! Upgrading the legs will let you fall from any height. Depending on what you want to get out of the game will depend what you upgrade (so better eye sight for stealth or more bang with the weapon abilities). Weapons can also be modified and customized to the players preference. Laser system, scope, silencer and even ammunition type (from electric to armor piercing) can be equipped and changed. I highly recommend keeping your battery and hacking systems upgraded alongside jump and strength for better inventory and ability to lift heavy objects.

Are you a fan of Smash Bros., but for some reason aren’t willing to buy a Nintendo system to play it? Well there may be a solution for you in Brawlhalla. At its current state it’s definitely not as polished as a full-fledged 1st party Nintendo title, but so far it’s a pretty decent brawler with fun (and sometimes frustration) as its core.
As of writing this, there are twelve characters to play with. At first I didn’t see to much of a difference between them, but the more you play you’ll start to pick out your favorites. Each character has different stats assigned to them be it faster speed, higher defense or higher attack. I’m not sure if the sword symbol with the “swoosh” above it is the “heavy attack”, but it would make sense. Defense and speed are just gimmies though as far as guessing what they mean.
I’m not much of a min/maxer  so in Brawlhalla the stats don’t play too much of a role for me unless it’s the speed stat. Damage gets thrown around a lot so defense didn’t really feel super important either. Punch someone enough and you’ll send them flying. Get punched enough and the same will happen to you. None of the characters had visible weight either; everyone was as easy to hit off the stage as anyone else. So what’s the main deciding factor in picking a character? Weapons man, it’s always the weapons. I tend to like the longer range weapons like the spears or lances. The short ranged duel wielding daggers (which seemed to be the coolest looks wise) feel slower than I expected, but I love the swords on Thatch and Hattori. I just “get them” better for some reason. (Read that as: I don’t tend to suck as much with them.)
The main differences in the Brawlhalla cast lies in which weapons they can use the look and reach of their special move. You may be using the same type of weapon and it may look fairly similar, but almost every character has a different looking special with more reach or power (or a nifty spectral bear graphic). It’s those differences that will almost force you to play with all the characters to see if you like how one handles compared to another because that’s really the only easily seen difference. That sounds rather negative, but it’s neat to see the subtleties. At the same time, I’d like to see more differences between characters rather than just the looks and weapon choice. At the same time, I’m still one for looks, so even if a character handles well and has my weapons of choice I still won’t pick him/her if I think they look goofy.
The guns in Brawlhalla come off as rather awkward. I don’t handle them well, but I’ve got a bud that has really shown me up just by having me watch him. To a skilled player the guns are possibly no different from the sword or dual-wielding daggers, but it’s just not working out with me. Maybe it’s that the bullets don’t go very far… but that should be a plus in my book. How many times have you been annoyed by a person that just keeps running away and taking pot shots at you? (Argh… that’s a frustrating memory *calms before table flip*.) I know I’ve been a victim of that. Even with all that “history”, if I play a character that uses guns and end up picking them up I’m more likely to chuck them at someone’s face then shoot them.
There are a number of levels to play on and they are all pretty basic, but functionally sound. There is nothing super complicated about any of them, but they all come off as different enough to be able to pick a favorite if you had to. They even just added a new level recently which manages to be as simple yet still differentiate itself from the rest. As simple as they are, Brawlhalla is just begging to have a level editor included. It would only be a boon to the game even though I’m sure there’s a lot more coding involved in implementing that, but it’s always nice to give the fans some creative license. If there’s one that shines above the rest it could be implemented in the main rotation for everyone. Who knows what the future holds.
“Blah blah blah, single player… what’s there for me and my buds?” I’m getting to that. Let’s just say at its current state I’d say that Brawlhalla is better suited for a local fighter than an online fighter. It’s all implemented and you can go online if you’d like, but the lag is pretty bad at times and it’s pretty usual to see people teleport around. The local play works great (Amazingly impressive if you were to compare it to the online mode at this point) and if you’ve needed a reason to buy more controllers for your PC, Brawlhalla could very well be it.

Brawlhalla is a basic fighter, but has more than enough going for it to justify giving it a try. It’s a blast to play when you figure out how all the moves and characters work. There could be more differentiation between characters, but that may come with time. There is a learning curve, but you don’t have to test your metal against other people. If you want to challenge other players, you can go online and fight through the teleporting lag that happens quite a bit right now. I can’t go negative on this because it is in Early Access and that will probably be fixed. The local multiplayer works fantastically though! You can also have plenty of fun fighting the NPCs and once you figure the game out they won’t give you a headache every time. With simple controls and a fun aesthetic, Brawlhalla is shaping up to be a pretty awesome game.

Thief was a pioneer of its time, turning people away from mindless killing and over to tactful thinking and stealth. In many ways it cannot stand up to modern titles, but it surpasses others still. I find it most challenging coming back to older games to review them. Firstly, there's not many who'd be reading these reviews - most people buying it on Steam owned it at one point and don't really need convincing. Secondly, it's hard to separate nostalgia from honesty. On other words, it's hard picking fault with a game you've grown up with. It's like a sibling - even though they may be flawed as a person you love them anyway. You grew up with them, they mean something to you.
It has been some time since I came back to the original Thief. Last time I played it I was very young and the prospect of being caught scared me so much I barely made progress through the story. Fortunately my older, possibly more apathetic self, now desensitised from most video-game fear by the many horror games now doing the rounds, found progress much easier.
The first thing you must consider is the game's age. Thief came out in 1998. To put that into perspective, Half-Life came out that same year. Games in that era were very much similar - FPS was king. Stealth hadn't really been thought of as a core game mechanic and the concept led to what became a very unique game. Rather than goading the player into massacring hundreds of would-be assailants, Thief flipped the whole playing field on its head. Combat was to be something that should be avoided and feared - it meant you'd done something wrong.
The world created in Thief is rich and deep, even if it isn't overly explored and developed as lore. You get a feel for the various factions and how they fit into the society of the world. From the fervorantly religious Hammerites to the technophobic Pagans and everyone in between, the world is populated with a huge variety of people with different roles in life. This doesn't so much come to mean much over the course of general gameplay - avoiding being detected is key to your success, regardless of if there's a powerful magic user around or just a servant who might royally fudge up your day by running off and telling the guards. All the while you'll be stealing stuff. After all, the game
called Thief. There are also many documents lying around which give valuable information or simply give an insight into the game world.
This brings me to the storyline. Minus spoilers, naturally. Playing as master thief Garrett you'll get pulled into a very nasty and sinister plot, which echoes many a dark tale of evil. Even considering the game's age the story isn't at all bad. It takes you to many different locales from treasure-laden lordly estates to cathedrals and entire city districts abandoned to an encroaching malevolence. Even knowing such evil exists makes the least magical places seem spooky. Thief boasts one of the scariest levels in videogames. "The Haunted Cathedral" still sends shivers down my spine, even in the altered Thief Gold version of the level.
AI-wise the game does quite well, even by today's standard. There are fixed enemy types, as you'd expect, but they each possess certain attributes which determine how they behave. For instance ghosts and apparitions are completely deaf, but are easily alerted to visual disturbance, while beastmen have heightened hearing. As a general rule, any messing about you do (making noises, picking up valuable trinkets from highly visible well-travelled locations) will trigger people to search for you. The more you do it, the longer they look and the more on-edge they get until they find you. The combat itself isn't great, and for me I'd say it was the biggest let-down in the game. The animations don't quite synch making parrying difficult.
In terms of graphics Thief is very basic. It uses the first iteration of the DarkEngine, so all the humanoid models are very edgy and polygonal. The animations are what you'd expect, but they get the job done. The game mechanics are fairly solid and the mission briefs/cutscenes give you enough information to go through the levels with the minimal of guesswork. The stealth system itself is very basic. It measures stealth via light and sound. If you're stood still in a dark shadow (or sometimes a very thin shadow in a doorframe) you'll be completely invisible, regardless of surrounding lights and the sillouhette you'd think would be a dead giveaway. Enemies would have to bump into you physically to detect you.
One thing I should note - Thief Gold is different to Thief: The Dark Project, the original release. Many levels were redesigned, added or removed. In some ways the changes are good, certain things are made easier whilst other things are made much more challenging. It's a mixed bag. Purists will tell you the changes are bad, but you can make up your own mind.

To call the current state of this game a "full release" is either an insult or blind optimism. As a fan of RWBY, I've always wanted to get this game the second I saw the base version of this before Roosterteeth even picked up on it on youtube. While I wasn't here for the majority of the early access, I did play it through before the update. The differences between then and now are very few. This "full release" is basically just a story mode expansion pack. My problem is calling that a full game. There's still some glaring bugs (like how my camera will randomly try to go back and forth constantly without end until I re-open the game) and combat is still to the point of nauseating with a subpar auto-lock on system and lack of a real lock on, on top of a better-than-it-used-to-be-but-still-horrendous camera. On top of that, my PC isn't the best but it's not so horrible I can't play some graphically intensive games. There's many with stronger graphics, and yet, this one has a terrible framerate for me. The rest is more empty than anything.
As stated before by a number of reviews: the combat is stale and there's next to no variety between the characters. For a hack and slash, I don't have issue with the combos being in a bare-bones state at the moment. You just use weak attacks and hit strong attack after the first, second, or third weak one. This is fine, but aerial attacks are all useless. Counter, in my experience, does virtually nothing. Either it's me and a timing issue or the button is just pointless. I do like the HP system regenerating itself quickly by backing off and getting a skill for it. I'd be more a fan of the ultimates if I couldn't sum them all up as “big aoe big damage” for every character and nothing else.
The story is alright, not spectacular. I won't say anything about it for anyone who hasn't played it or is still getting through it. The scenery is majestic in my opinion, just a little too spacious. The random comments from Team RWBY through levels make the game more lively since otherwise it's mostly silent until you've sprint long enough to find a wave(s) of the same... three enemies.
In this current state, I wouldn't recommend this to anybody. If the devs want to start throwing DLC on top of just grazing over how this game is nothing remotely close to a finished product, they only prove this was a mistake and expect it to live off hype. This game CAN be good and it's not even a total disaster. The idea is there, the design just isn't. Characters “look” diverse, the music is okay, the graphics could be improved but they aren't horrendous, the level up system and skills aren't bad either (though it'd be nice to know the names of my skills. You call a skill Frostbite and don't tell me what it is, why would I upgrade it?). But when I see something labeled “team attack”, and then using it really had nothing to do with being a team, I'm just left confused.
I love RWBY and I can only hope future patches of this game are less built on excitement like the “full release” was. And for the love of God, I pray they focus on making the game far more functional before they start talking about additional content you PAY FOR.
If you really, really, really want this game, get it on sale. 25 dollars is just a mistake you will wholeheartedly regret.

This is a tough one. I'm a humongous Deus Ex fan, I loved the original game, and I loved Human Revolution just as much. Those two games had their own problems, but they were still great games as a whole. This however, I don't know.
First, the game runs like utter crap. It just doesn't run well at all. I have an i7 and a 970, and at medium settings at times I was scraping by. Not a crazy powerful, top of the line computer, but it should be able to get by. The game looks nice enough, but man, a lot of stuttering that came and went, poor performance in some areas, occassionally completely outrageous loading times. Cutscenes stuttered too. Sometimes the game ran great. Othertimes, not so much.
Now, gameplay. The game plays pretty well. If you liked the way Human Revolution felt to play, you'll feel right at home here. There are some interesting new augs, but it's difficult to use all of them. I'll avoid spoilers. New augs felt good to use, fairly useful, but it feels like some completely outshine the others. I never onced felt the need to use nanoblade, while remote hacking was an almost invaluable tool.
Now, the problem with the gameplay. The game doesn't give you enough moments to really hit full stride. There are a few times where it feels like I'm having a proper time getting through a mission, and the rest of the time you're in the hub. Now, I'm talking about those "grand" infiltrations. The game very much still sort of leans heavily towards stealth in my opinion, with a lot of negative reaction if you decide to use combat. But those moments in Human Revolution, like the FEMA facility infiltration, and the Tai Young Medical tower climb, were amazing. There's a few others in HR, but MD only really offers a couple times where I feel it reaches that scale, Golem City, and the lab in Switzerland.
It feels like a lot of the time you're kind of just.. meandering, really. Like I said, there needs to be more of those missions where you're really hitting your stride. Really put your guns, and your augs, to the test.
Now the story. I won't say much other than that, it ends abruptly, and on somewhat of a cliffhanger? I believe there are multiple endings, but in the one I got, there was room to move forward with the story. All of the decisions you make in the game basically boil down to Eliza Cassan speaking on TV about the reprecussions of what you did. I wasn't a huge fan. The conspiracy didn't run deep enough. The villains were a little too cut and dry, one person you kind of don't know what's going on with, but others you definitely know are either good, or bad. This is Deus Ex! I want to feel like I have no idea who to trust. Remember in the original game when you found out UNATCO were part of the conspiracy? Yeah, I want that.
There are some other things that kind of bother me. The facial animations flat out suck. They just don't sync up, they don't look good. It's the current year. The game looks beautiful. Why do non-Jensen faces look like they belong in 2007? I mean, Half-Life 2 was doing way better facial animation than this.. in 2004. Also apparently they used mocap to animate the bodies when people are talking. I don't believe that somehow. All in all, dialogue always felt kind of awkward. Like two robots that don't know the other is a robot trying to convince each other they're human, but also don't really know what humans are like that much.
One more things, this game has microtransactions. It is a full priced, singleplayer game. What the ♥♥♥♥ are you doing, Square Enix? I already gave you half a years salary for the damn game, and you want more? There are other things I've heard about the microtransactions, like them only applying to your current save, and no others, but I can't confirm, as I'm not giving them another dime.
I'm going to go with a pass on this one. It's 60 bucks. The game should work properly. It crashed on me a few times, and always at the worst moments. The story was lackluster at best. The environments didn't really ever give me a chance to stretch my legs. The setting was kind of just annoying overall, honestly.
Would pay 30 bucks for.

It's not so much that I don't recommend Shoppe Keep, rather I recommend that you "wait and see."  I'm not sure about you, but I only tend to buy early access games when and if they're released, and I rightfully expect them to be some type of finished - at the very least with all the features in place and certainly all the serious bugs wiped out - but this game just isn't there yet.
It's not well-optimized.  The graphics chug resources, and I know of at least one option (show edges) that makes the game look like♥♥♥♥♥♥  The music is sparse - one song per phase, at least until you unlock the vinyl player.
The game, essentially, is capitalism at its finest.  You earn money mostly for the sake of earning money.  You can add more displays to the shop, buy tiers of gear to sell to the four classes, knock out walls and get more rooms --- all for the sake of earning more money.  If you're super-casual and just like to see a number going up, this is the game for you.  If you wanted any serious sense of development, or investments, or customization, or really anything interesting to do WITH that money - you will be sorely disappointed.
The game represents a "bad grind", as in "Hey, this is gonna take forever and there's not much to actually achieve."  The upgrades take a LONG time to get, and are almost entirely lackluster.  And for the money that you make, there are gold sinks everywhere.  Knock out a wall to get another room?  10,000 gold, which is perfectly reasonable.  Knock out the next wall?  100,000 gold.  Next wall after that?  250,000 gold.  Those are not typos.  Even the robot you buy to help around the shop, for some reason, consumes gold per minute, and since his scripting is a little slow it can take anywhere from 5 - 15 seconds for him to get going.  The Champion you hire frequently won't break even with the loot he brings back.  Plants in the garden grow very quickly, and if you spend literally a minute or two away from them, will rot in the ground ruining the entire crop. They added an NPC with special displays that start at 175,000 gold.  Ultimately there are only completely boring massive gold sinks to throw your money into.
One serious gripe I have is that should you find non-unique class items and put 'em up for sale, but haven't unlocked that tier of customer yet - it's an EXTREMELY remote chance that they're going to sell, because they're technically part of an upgrade.  That means all the cool blue-grade stuff you find in trash-cans or from your Champion just sits inside a frigging box until you unlock that tier of customer.
What the game really needs is an in-depth crafting system.  It doesn't have it.  Imagine a shop that you customize from the ground up, selling items that you make yourself.  That would make most people blow hundreds of hours on the game.  Instead, you have 28 crafting recipes, and if the trial-and-error isn't enough, it will take weeks of in-game grinding to get the KP for both the cauldron and the grinder.  It's not a bad start, but is a complete snoozefest, mostly thanks to the KP system.
KP (Keep Points) is how you unlock skills, perks, and items in the game.  You make sales, they go up.  The formula is never explained properly.  Sometimes you'll get a few in a day, sometimes thirty.  It can take weeks of in-game time to unlock certain elements of gameplay, like the Champion.  Quests exist (sell x number of y), but back when I had started they weren't working.  This translates to a LOT of days of looking at the same stock in the same places, with only the "hot items" to break up the monotony.  At the time of this writing I have 35 hours in the game and have maybe 60% of the upgrades, at least all the important ones that change the gameplay.
The updates to the game are frequent, seem to be at least once a month.  This is good, because the game still has bugs, like items getting stuck in the floor when they're dropped by thieves, and the game badly needs more things to actually do.  I don't know what's planned for the future.  The game pretty much defines "Charming, mindless, casual" rather than the "Involved, in-depth, customizable" experience I was looking for in a shop sim.  Maybe it'll get there someday, maybe it won't.  If it goes down to five bucks again, go for it.  Otherwise, wait and see.

Amazing. I'm 43 now and have seen a lot of games, but few have had this level of quality. You can downright feel how much blood, sweat and tears has been put in this title. Whether it's the accurate animations, the picturesque surroundings, or the matching sound & music - nearly every single detail is made with so much love and carefulness, it will sometimes simply take your breath away. Do yourself a favor and take your time to explore what this game has in store for you, especially since people and animals usually react individually to the brothers. I really enjoyed this tale of two sons, right from the touching opening sequence until the remarkable, courageous ending.  Besides Diablo III and Torchlight i'ts the best title I played in the last couple of years.
However, there are some minor things worth criticising. First and foremost, and as indicated above, this game is primarily about exploring its beauty. Brothers may be considered an adventure, but if you place importance on brain teasers, you are at the wrong place - the difficulty is mild, to say the least, the solutions are almost always obvious and easy to accomplish. In adition, it's too short - cutting corners, you can replay the game within less than an hour. In single player mode you tend to confuse the controls of the brothers, as you instinctively want to control the one who is currently located on the left side of the screen with the left analog stick, and vice versa. And last but not least, the camera won't rotate in every situation, which is out of all reason, but hey, worse things happen at sea...
The bottom line is: Don't miss this game. It's worth every penny.

Note: I originally insulted the engine in this review, after further reflection I don't think the engine is actually that bad. Semi-destructable walls and passable lighting effects definitely make it better than what I originally described as a Doom 2 engine. Really the failings rest in level design and content creation, as well as over-all direction. I'm beginning to suspect that much like the original game, it's only salvation is multiplayer.
I bought this game on pre-order because I'm a sucker for nostalgia. I actually bought a four-pack, cause I used to play the original with my friends in highschool at lan parties (on Pentium 1s, 33mhz woot). I suspect I'm exactly the market they were shooting for, someone who has fond memories of what was always kind of a lame game with ridiculous weapons. Decades later, this reboot is redefining what I consider lame. The enemies almost appear to be sprites instead of polygons, their animations are attrocious, they have a hard time following you from one room to another, and they have a tendency to spring back to life post-mortem from time to time. The pick ups are all over the place, ugly nonsensical tokens, just like the original. Really, so many bad aspects of the original game which were at that time stunted in the name of performance, are now lovingly recreated in the name of nostalgia, making the game seem intentionally terrible. The voice acting makes me cringe, just to think that they asked actual people to lend their voices to this monstrocity. There's a lot of what appear to be inside jokes for the developers, no one else could possibly find them amusing, and that kind of applies to the entire work, this whole game feels like an inside joke that we're all standing outside of. Of the four copies I received, my copy is the only one that's been played for more than minutes. I suppose we should salute our thin skinned developer, so few people have the courage to really push games backwards.
P.S. - You know what people really love? Colored Keys. Can't get enough of them.

This game was a struggle to justify at its 10.00$ price, and now it's 2.5 times that.   The combat is shallow (there's literally four combos for character, a ranged attack, an 'ultimate', and a roll), very few enemy options, and repetitive enviroments. What's worse is the game is 'balanced' around co-op, so many enemies (even early on) will two-shot you and it'll be game over, where as in Co-op your allies (in theory) could revive you from cheap kills.
Perhaps the worst part is a non-working counter system.  Certain enemies have big, really damaging wind-up attacks that can be interupted with a button press... but the range this works from is not defined well.   And,  let's say you're just out of range to do it, then you're stuck in a blocking animation for no reason and will die.  Or if it takes long for your canned dash to reach them, they'll do the attack anyways and kill you.  Similar issues exist for the 'ultimate' attacks (which lock you into an animation after them which will cause a quick death).
All in all, this game could have been interesting. It could have been fun. But it's not.  The basic combat is heavily flawed, wonky, and just doesn't function how it should.   But that's not why I'm returning it.  On top of these issues, it doesn't play well with multiple monitors (I had to turn extra ones off beforehand); for a really good game, that's fine, I'll do it. This isn't a good game.
Save your money until its eventual 80 or 90% off sale.

So, RWBY: Grimm Eclipse. A game that started as a fan project and should have stayed like that to not lower its reputation. A fan game that had a "proper" team behind it but forgot the "fan" aspect since not much feedback was accepted and no future changes were proposed before they started the work. A game that had potential but most was wasted thanks to bad decisions, greed (early release) and a bad choice of engine (should have been unreal engine 4) but manages to redeem some wrongdoings in certain departments.
Lets cut to the chase:
The game is a co-op hack n' slash game based on a very successful show called RWBY. But does the game have a soul?
Gameplay: 4/10
Time for a bit of history. Back in Dec 2015 release r0.30 existed. The gameplay was very fast paced, and you felt like a god (do note this only included the first easy half of the story) after cracking combos between melee and ranged one after another and also using your "special" pool (you could select one of three ultimates which would later become combos with the full release). After that the gameplay changed to a slower, more combo oriented system, and the player had their ultimate. The ultimates should have been more powerful, yes, but the main complaint is the counter system. Grimm have this F key on the top of their heads when you should counter them. Originally the system didnt have a delay so you could spam the F key and jump from one enemy to another. Later on the system became kind of clunky considering the AI is poor and F bombs (i mean the key) appeared everywhere. Since the game rushed its release, its very obvious that during the final chapter the developers said "♥♥♥♥ it, lets just give them a load of high-tier enemies one after another", this could have been challenging but currently is frustrating since balancing is way off. Buy hey, not all is bad, there are some small quests to do like pressing this, destroying that. Thats about it really. 4 players online, maybe you will survive. Alone, nope. The final boss felt like i was battling chapter 1 Grimm all over again it was that easy. Before the boss the player has to survive waves (again, *yawn*) and the final wave of the 4 took 20 minutes to beat. The difficulty is Dark Souls tier, and then im presented with a cute green scorpion. The leveling-up system is nice, but could have been a bit more detailed. A nice addition would be various ways to complete a chapter, the A to B can get repetitive.
-Combat needs a bit of improvement
--AI is♥♥♥♥♥♥ college level.
--Balance pls
-Can get repetitive due to the waves
Story: 8/10
Not gonna spoil anything but imagine a hack n' slash Sonic Heroes albeit with 4 peeps and the same style mastermind.
The idea behind it is brilliant, connecting certain things from the show to the game, but cutscenes between chapters made by the animation team could have made the story clearer, specially when you try to speedrun the game and could have made the game feel a little more "natural" for example: Seeing what team RWBY did inside a container and planned and talked about. Banter basically.
-Player could get a bit more background
++Interesting concept
Graphics: 6.5/10
Time for more history. Back in the glorious r0.30, the models of the characters were exactly the same as the show models. Later on they decided to remake them from scratch. Originally it didnt turn out well but they improved them over time. They still arent an exact match (inconsistencies can be seen, some more obvious than others). The model change which was uncalled by the community (a bit like brexit) was due to "performance issues" but the performance didnt improve and actually got worse on the release version r1.0. Considering people love the characters, there are quite a few buyers that will buy the game for the characters (like me) so yeah the show models were better hands down.
The artstyle of the game is very similar to the show (apart fom the above mentioned) which is good. And the maps are nicely detailed and have nice nooks and crannies.
The best part of the graphics is the HUD, honestly, good job! Needs a size slider.
--Meh models
+Nice hud, could do with a size slider
+Art style similar to show
+Level detail is adequate
Sound: 9.5/10
The soundtrack is absolutely brilliant and captures the mood of the game. Sound effects arent bad either, some could need a bit more punch.
++Sik trax bruh
+Nice effects
Fun: 7/10
I am a social beast, I love multiplayer and teamwork even more. Get a brilliant team and you are in for a ride. The wild ride can struggle to keep up at parts due to the issues mentioned above, but if youre ito L4D2, Portal2 or team-oriented games this may be for you. Singleplayer, as stated before, can become frustrating at later chapters.
++ Co-Op
-Singleplayer is frustrating
+Friendly community
-- Issues stated previously
Value: 7/10
The game started at 15€, back in December 2015.(I purchased for this price) Now the game is 23€ and its a bit expensive considering the fact that additional characters will come as DLC, but some free content was promised.
The "sweet spot" would be 20€ considering the content, above mentioned, general polish of the game and workers wages.
-A bit expensive, wait for sales.
-DLC plans already
+Possbile free content
Performance: 7.5/10
Inb4 &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥rig" comments.
I have already mentioned performance issues before, so lets delve deeper. In my case the game ran the best back in r0.30 (yes, with the show models). After the new models were introduced a bit of stutter was noticable and framerates dropped. The framerates were fixed with a hotfix but the stutter was still present. Guess what, r1.♥♥♥♥ing0, runs like a half-dead donkey. Framerates are lower and the micro-stutter is still present. Personally I get the feeling that Unity was a bad engine choice considering the AI and the map size. But hey, Rust runs better and the world is massive. Think how long Rust has been in early access. Think about all the time the developer had available to know the weak points of the engine and provide workarounds. Think about how quick this game has exited early access.
-Performance worsened but still runs OK on a 2013 800€ rig as to be expected on ultra. Could be better.
Hope this helped with your purchase. :)

A great single player game. Very interesting missions, detailed and fun storyline (without being overly complex) and a perfect balance between casual and hardcore, meaning almost everyone can play this game to completion.
For the first time in the series, you play as 3 protagonists, and can change between them as will. Not only you'll see they doing their own (funny) things when they aren't active, you'll be able to appreciate 3 different sets of side missions for each character. In the story missions, however, you'll be able to play with all 3, changing them in the middle of the action. Sometimes, this can lead to some amazing cinematographic scenes, where you are controlling a car with one of the characters while the other is sitting on the side of the road with a precision rifle. This means there's some strategy involved in some missions. Nothing very complex, just like most GTAs.
And BTW, nothing in this game is deep and complex. But the game doesn't feel shallow either. In fact, R* found the perfect balance. This feels like a casual game sometimes, but can feel like a hardcore game if you want. Most missions can be as easy or as hard as you want just by trying different tactics, and you can even SKIP difficulty parts IF YOU SO DESIRE. And just like GTA 3 and Vice City, most missions can be finished in different ways, you are free to find out the best tactics to beat each mission. In this aspect, the game is WAY better than GTA San Andreas.
Also, the game is PACKED with side activities. Mini-games, side missions, random events (that may or may not involve your playable characters), LOTS of stuff to see and do and a huge and detailed map to explore.
Great graphics (WAY better than the console versions, BTW) and a fantastic soundtrack complete the package.
GTA 5 is not a perfect game. There are some weird flaws here and there, like cars that appear out of nowhere (not as frequent as the older GTAs, at least), some missions that could be a bit more detailed, flying controls are HORRIBLE, etc. But none of the flaws really ruin the game al that much.
GTA 5 is fun. No matter what you are doing there, you'll have fun. Even when you don't feel like doing missions, you can just kill some NPCs to call the police, hop into a car and run away from the cops until you die (or they give up). There's always something fun to do here, and not only the storyline huge, there's enough content to keep you busy for hours! GTA 5 may not be the best game ever, but may be one of the most fun ones.
Highly recommend this game. ^^
(BTW, the game has an online mode, but I don't care for online, so I can't comment on that.)

Thief - The Dark Project was the first game I ever purchased for PC. I am happy to see that it is now able to be incorporated into the Steam Library of games. To this day my daughter, who spent many hours on "dad's" lap watching TDP with her sippy cup, is still a fan of the Thief series. Obviously this game has a lot of memories, and also a lot of meaning; so I won't even try to be objective...
Thief Gold is not an enormously fast moving game, so if you are the type of player that wants to "knock 'em all dead" and hurry up and finish, I'd think you would dislike Thief Gold. It takes time. Waiting out guards, finding loot, and at times failing and dying. If you're not familiar with Thief Gold, you may want to save often.
The graphics are not bad for '98, and keep in mind that you don't fix up a '67 Thunderbird to look like the modern Mazda version of Thunderbird today. Thief Gold is a piece of gaming history. A landmark for patience and problem solving in the gaming world. So... put the super graphic modern games on the shelf of your mind, and step back in time to an era when you were able to overcome the developers design in your own way!

I bought this game on january 1 when it was on sale, and played it quite some time.
Player base
The first week I played this game there was always a server with at least 6 players online.
But a week after the sales I had trouble finding a server with 1 player online.
Every time Guncraft was on sale, there was a peak in the number of players online but a couple days later they are all gone.
Gameplay
I like the fast-paced gameplay and no recoil or bullet drop, but the custom guns are overpowered.
When you make a custom gun, you get points that you can spend on damage, firerate, accuracy, ... if you spend all points on one ability it gets overpowered. The thompson (custom gun, downloadable through steam) is by far the most overpowered gun in the game, it has the best accuracy of all guns, increadably fast fire rate and high damage. That's why all the noobs use that gun.
The heads of the player are bigger than their body, so headshots are way too easy.
And if that's not enough overpowered things, you have the vehicles. Vehicles should make this game, but sadly they break it.
Community
This game has a very small but fun and noob friendly community.
Shout-out to Redcorpian, Zusheqiel and turbozack for keeping the community kind of alive.
Updates
Short: None
More in-depth: When you ask the developers of Guncraft when a new update will come out, their answer is "soon". But their interpretation of "soon" differs a lot from most peoples interpretation. From 1 january until now we had no big update. For a long time they were saying that a big "thing" would come, but it turned out to be the Humble Bundle sale -_-
They also made some block packs so they can make some more money before the game finally dies.
Gamemodes
There are some nice gamemodes that I haven't seen in other games, but sadly there is nobody to play these gamemodes with.
I had hope for this game, but not anymore (like a lot of people). If the game is on sale again and you can convince your friends to buy this game, you should buy it and you can have a lot of fun. But otherwise, don't buy it.
