Kingdoms of Amalur is a game that I sadly do not recommend. It lacks depth and immersion to justify playing this game for an extended peroid of time. The storyline is dull, the npcs are forgettable, and the world is just outright boring. While the concept behind the lore is rather unique, there's nothing to draw you in, to make you invested in the story or even your own character! To help visualize, Kingdoms of Amalur is a MMORPG without the multiplayer. The only redeeming quality is its combat. Combat in this game is among one of the most entertaining that I have ever played in any RPG, and has that "easy to learn, difficult to master" aspect to it. However, after minutes of gloriously decimating your enemies, you would likely become bored, and exit the game. If this game is on sale, and if you think you can overlook these flaws, then by all means, get it, but in my eyes, this game is not worth buying most of the time.

There was a lot of hype in my circle of friends and colleagues when this game first launched years ago. They praised the combat system and the ability to forge your own character class as you go along. They lived in the world of Amalur and it's bright, colourful forests filled with magical creatures and countless NPCs needing your help. They urged me to give the game a go so I can experience it's wonder for myself...
...and years later I decided to do so. In fact, I gave the game 3 chances to grab me. The first time I finished the tutorial section and stepped bright eyed into the sunlight, I was immediately overwhelmed by the sheer amount of dialogue to work through when approaching characters. Life was busy back then and I had other games vying for attention, so I gave up and shelved the game. A year later I decided to pick it up again and continue from where I left off. I skipped through the dialogue to get to the "fun" parts of the game, but it felt a little empty without the context of why I'm breaking crates or hunting down rogue leaders. I promptly shelved it again.
So, I attempted it again 6 months later and decided I'll persist. Sadly, it was in vain. I progressed quite far into the game this time around and managed to finish roughly 60 main-, side- and faction quests. The game never managed to immers me in it's world and I really became irritated with the sheer volume of flat dialogue the game insists on throwing at you. The choices I made felt inconsequential, the boss fights were just dances of dodge-hit-dodge and spamming whatever special abilities I managed to unlock at that point. Crafting felt useless as the items I managed to loot from the game world was sufficient (bordering on over-powered) and I never felt any need to spend the copious amounts of gold I managed to hoard.
I really want to recommend this game, but it felt like an absolute chore to play and I didn't enjoy a single minute of it.

Gunz 2 is a above-average sequel to a stellar game, Gunz The Duel. A lot of the mechanics are the same or have been polished and there have been some changes done to try and balance things out. There's a new co-op mode which is far superior to the "Quest" mode in the last game, which took hours of grinding and several minutes of research in a lobby to be worth your time.
Also I personally like the class system, it helps you know what to expect from each person you're facing.
Now onto the negatives. This feels like a beta. A closed beta, at that. There are a plethora of bugs, host errors, lag problems, and probably other things I havn't encountered. They aren't usually gamebreaking but there are some. The "store" to purchase outfits, weapons, etc is barebones. The original Gunz's store had, in a rough guess, 50-75 items, not including different gender items. when I first played it. This has two for each weapon and three outfits per character. It's also microtransaction heavy. It takes about 10-20 matches to afford the "cheap" weapon upgrades or outfits and ten times that for the other items, that have no benefit besides "I look nice".  Everything else relies on "reward crates" from winning normal  or ranked pvp matches to get ores or crystals to gamble for temporary items or the 1 in 200 chance of a permanent.
All that having been said, I enjoy this game. I think it's great for the state that it's in and I remind myself that while Gunz was a better game when it launched, it didn't have near as many features or game modes. It didn't have separate characters with entirely different animation and weapon sets. It didn't have co-operative multiplayer at all, that came years later. Give this game a chance and if you find issues with mechanics being a little off or a couple bugs...remember this. It's nowhere near a finished game. It won't be for years yet, if Maiet is still the company it was.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who wants to play a quick online game, either pve or pvp, that has a low entrance level but a steep learning curve later on. And we havn't even found the mechanic exploits yet like we did with the original yet that made the combat so much more. =P

I have been waiting for this game since it first cam to early access. And, while the game could have used a bit more polishing before release, it has alot of content (especially for a 10 dollar game). It starts out very slow, however if you wait out the first few days by selling to people on the streets, you'll have a bustling buisness in no time! The game has its flaws, as mentioned in other reviews, however if you enjoy a casual and relaxed game, you will adore this.
Interesting facts and Tips:
1) The fire, ice and growth potions are seasonal, so in the first ten days, you wont be able to sell ice or growth potions.
2) Scrolling the mouse wheel shows alot of different furniture types (i spent alot of time wondering why i could only use stools)
3) The skills page has multiple tabs (This is how you can increase the items you are able to buy)
4) You can kill good customers so dont shoot a thief with others in the way.
5) You can customize your main charachter in the main menu.
6) The game saves after each day when the doors close (Hitting "save shop" will not fully save the game!).
Overall the game is great, it is fun, relaxing, and quite addictive. You just have to get past the first few days to have fun! Its totally worth the price considering what most games cost nowadays, and the devs are still activly working on it, so its not done yet. The devs are also very responsive to the community and fix bugs often.
8.5/10

I've had this game on my wishlist for a while and bought it when it came out of early access.
Firstly, I would like to say that other reviewers are right in saying that the tutorial only being readable causes some problems - I got stuck at the start trying to retrieve ordered goods and then ended up buying a seasonal good that no one would buy which slowed me down a bit. That having been said, however, I actually do like this game.
I think that it would be a mistake to compare this game to Recettear and other business sims because they are different styles of game. Recettear is a strategic money making game where the pressure is on making enough money to pay the bills; in comparison this game puts the pressure on managing the actual shop floor in real time - theres a good reason its called shop keepe - and there is pressure in that you have to work out on the fly what to buy more of and what not to; it's a different kind of fun but it is very much still fun.
The biggest thing to prepare yourself for if you are thinking about getting the game is the slow start. You start with low money and nothing unlocked as expected and that means low customers and thus not much to actually do. Luckily this can be alleviated by going and selling items to people in the street but it is nonetheless initially repetitive in a boring manner. It does get better!
By far the biggest issue is the tutorial for this game and I really hope that the developers change it so that its an ingame as-it-happens tutorial rather than a text one. This could be done in a way that makes the keybinding clearer too -  like the shifts for the price changes.
Overall as long as you are prepared to play a game about being a shop keeper and not just a business simulation I think you'll enjoy it.
Update: Having played another 6 hours I can safely say that my concerns about future gameplay have been assuaged; once you get going the game gets pretty frantic. The devs continue to update at a steady pace atm with an update done today so I'm hopeful that the UI and tutorials could also be improved in the future to reduce learning curve. Overall still very much recommend.
Update 2: More improvements have happened to the game recently (June 10th was the most recent update) and increased the ease of playing a lot, also the keybindings have been made more clear in the tutorials so that the actual key that the option is bound to is mentioned rather than something like "action key".

A development team of 15 people remade Rise of the Triad and made it as face-paced, challenging, and as gory as ever. Enemies are cruel and wacky, and aren't afraid to troll you by stealing that shiny new weapon you found a few doors back. The dev team even included a metal/rock themed soundtrack that reminds me of the ol days playing Doom. Coins, easter-egg secrets, fast-paced combat, and some awesome bosses that gave me a WoW Burning Crusade feeling to them. The weapons you find are overpowered as hell, but once you see what you're up against you'll need every last rocket.
Criticisms in a more serious tone: Story and pacing of the game are hard to follow. You can easily get stuck if you're not paying attention to every little detail around you. While I think that the mobs are challenging, others can find them unfair with their super quirky movements. Multiplayer is lacking support since their community in that area practically doesn't exist. (That being said, LAN parties have been awesome, so the actual multiplayer itself isn't bad.)
Overall I found this game to be fun. It's not a perfect game, but neither is it an AAA title that will bash your face in with advertisements and microtransactions. It's a remake of a game that made most shooters the games they are today (also credited for inventing CTF) if you want to buy a piece of history, then look no further.
